## Proposal: task-linked predicate-ablation coverage, checked per lesson

Before admitting a generator version, evaluate a small set of meaningful wrong programs obtained by dropping or changing one rule condition: for this task, ignore colour equality or repeatedly apply a rule that is supposed to run once. Require an authority-verified, valid-domain counterexample to each relevant ablation, and require the actual demonstration assembly policy to expose the distinction before a query needs it. Seed, source hash, input, authority output and rival output should accompany failures.

This extends the existing semantic gate rather than introducing another morphology score. The current gate can only check the rivals a generator author remembered to declare; a shared, task-linked ablation inventory makes an omitted critical predicate visible. It must not claim to identify all possible wrong solvers.

## Reproducible failure

For baseline `f16508733f0a` SHA-256 `aa12e83d32c2fefb2bb71c71c4c5ececf166f37f26ee73386ae17c4ea4840ee1`, the majority-colour rival fits all four canonical pairs and all 108 sampled generator outputs (seeds 0–3, indices 0–8, three bands). There are zero colour-agreement witnesses in 72 three-demo windows, despite a green 12-stage battery. The original validator also rejects a small mixed-colour counterexample with genuine targets. See `checks/focused-before/report.json`, `pytest.log`, and the new regression fixture `decoy_grid()`.

The repaired generator supplies colour-agreement witnesses in all 432 tested demo windows; its 648 labels are checked through Racket. These measurements establish coverage, **not** measured Qwen quality gains.

## Possible false positive

A candidate ablation may be genuinely equivalent on the task's intended domain. A colour-equality check may be redundant when monochromatic objects are part of the problem contract. Requiring an impossible witness would force out-of-domain training examples. Therefore first exhibit a legitimate task-domain input on which the authority and ablation differ; otherwise record equivalence, an explicit restricted curriculum, or insufficient evidence rather than automatically failing the generator. Likewise, do not reject an intentionally simple early lesson whose query does not depend on the missing distinction.

## Cheapest useful test

Start with the two small local motifs and all canonical pairs, using Python for rival execution and the existing persistent Racket bridge for labels. Then test one seed, all three bands, sample indices 0–8 and all six cyclic lesson starts: 27 generated draws and 18 overlapping windows, with cached labels. Escalate only failing or underpowered cases. `workspace/review_checks.py` already implements the task-local census, live registry lookup, canonical fit and cyclic-window accounting. A shared ablation inventory is recommended, not patched outside this assignment.

# qwen9-data-value

**Question:** Based on your generator review, what one additional automated gate
would most improve Qwen3.5-9B training data quality? Name a reproducible failure
it would catch, a possible false positive, and the cheapest way to test it.

## Recommendation: check rivals on the actual assembled lesson

At automatic data generation/admission, reject or resample a lesson when a
declared plausible rival reproduces every demonstration but predicts a different
query answer. Reuse `LESSON_COMPETITORS` and `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` directly, even
when the generator has no separately written `lesson_identifiable` hook. Apply
this check after the actual examples have been accepted, ordered and assigned
to train/query roles. Individual correct labels and generator approval do not
establish that those particular demonstrations teach the query distinction.

The packet already has authoring checks for this condition. The additional
value is closing the production gap in `repo/src/arcpuzzles/worker.py`:
`lesson_check` currently invokes only the explicit hook. A generator can declare
executable rivals for the authoring gate and still receive `not_declared` in
production when that hook is absent. Shared enforcement avoids requiring each
future generator author to duplicate the same admission logic. The selected
repair also supplies its own hook, so its ordinary production lessons do not
depend on accepting the optional shared proposal.

## Reproducible failure

For `f191c16f6179`, the wrong rule “connect every pair on a 45-degree diagonal,
even when an input cell blocks its interior” matches **all three canonical
labelled pairs**. It fails the Racket-labelled blocked-diagonal fixture in
`repo/generators/f191c16f6179/counterexamples/guard_cases.json`.

That fixture has an eligible color-1 pair at `(0,0)` and `(2,2)`, and a color-4
pair at `(0,6)` and `(4,2)` blocked by color 5 at `(2,4)`. The reference changes
only `(1,1)` to 1. The rival additionally draws through the blocked color-4
diagonal, including overwriting the blocker. The retained comparison is
`checks/guard-admission-witness.json`. This is a constructed, reference-lawful
counterexample, not a claim that the original sampler generated it.

A lesson containing only the canonical clear demonstrations and that blocked
query therefore leaves this guard undecided, despite every reference label being
correct. A guard-bearing demonstration resolves the ambiguity. The repair adds
such mixed examples instead of relying on separate identity-only degenerates.

## Possible false positive and policy limit

A rival can be irrelevant to the supported task domain, malicious, stateful,
or overly specialized. Merely fitting the demonstrations is not enough reason
to declare every conceivable program a meaningful alternative. Keep a small
reviewed set of plausible mistakes, bind it to source/rule hashes, check purity,
and count execution errors separately from actual ambiguity. A rival that also
agrees on the query is harmless for that lesson and must not cause rejection.

An intentionally ordered curriculum can become ambiguous if an arbitrary
demonstration is reassigned as the query. Test rotations when that assembly is
used; do not conflate a diagnostic rotation failure with an ordinary ordered
production failure. Preserve both verdicts. Similarly, preserve explicitly
requested diagnostic examples as labelled diagnostics rather than claiming
they passed automatic training admission.

## Cheapest useful test

Start with the two existing canonical demonstrations, the retained blocked
query and one pure Python rival. Reuse their stored, source-bound Racket labels;
no model inference, GPU, or retraining is needed. Require the gate to reject the
ambiguous lesson, then add the blocked fixture as a demonstration and require it
to stop reporting that rival as query-changing. Also test a rival that is
refuted by a demonstration, one that agrees on the query, and a mutating/erroring
predictor. Cache predictions by rival identity and input hash in larger runs.

This is a task-grounded data-quality recommendation. No Qwen training run or
model accuracy improvement was measured in this review.

# qwen9-data-value

The single highest-value additional gate is a **lesson-window rival-survival gate**.

For every generator that declares `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` or `LESSON_COMPETITORS`, materialize complete demonstration windows using the real lesson assembly policy, test every cyclic start for short deterministic schedules, and require every declared wrong rule to disagree with at least one demonstration in every window. The report should bind to the final generator hash and state seeds, bands, number of windows, unique inputs, and per-rival survival counts.

**Reproducible failure it would catch.** Before this repair, every generated foreground color occurred exactly twice, so the wrong rule “draw a bar for every nonzero color” fit all examples. A weaker pooled witness-frequency test could also pass while a sampler/packer aliases the schedule: the `bab4d8f5ba7a` audit shows that stride-5 shards contain one teaching profile only and leave at least one named shortcut alive in every shard, even though contiguous five-example windows refute all of them.

**Possible false positive.** A declared rival may be answer-equivalent to the selected rule over the generator’s documented domain, or the rival implementation may be overbroad/incorrect. Symmetry-equivalent formulations can also look like distinct rules while producing identical answers. The gate should first verify that a claimed canonical shortcut fits every usable canonical pair and should classify an unseparable rival as a domain/rival-definition question rather than automatically condemning the generator.

**Cheapest test.** Run pure Python generation plus a source-bound Python rule mirror and the generator’s executable rivals; slide windows over 100 lessons per band and all cyclic starts. Use live Racket only on mirror/rival discrepancies and a small parity sample. This costs seconds to minutes and no model training, yet directly tests whether the demonstrations identify the intended rule for Qwen3.5-9B.

> Based on your generator review, what one additional automated gate would most
> improve Qwen3.5-9B training data quality? Name a reproducible failure it would
> catch, a possible false positive, and the cheapest way to test it.

## Proposed gate: query-relevant rule identifiability under a declared rival family

The highest-leverage additional gate is **episode-level distinguishing-witness
coverage**: before admitting a lesson, verify that its visible demonstrations
resolve every output-changing branch used by its actual queries, or explicitly
label the prior that makes the extrapolation intentional.

This is a priority judgment from reproduced generator failures, not a measured
Qwen training gain or a universal definition of learnability. The built tools
are:

- `repo/generators/f2dbde875127/workspace/lesson_key_gate.py` for a public lesson;
- `episode_identifiability_probe.py` for actual Racket-labeled generated episodes.

They use demonstration input/output pairs and query **inputs** only. Query outputs
are removed before analysis. For this task, the rival family is an independent
clockwise quarter-turn choice for each key, with fixed crop and floor centering.
The gate retains all key interpretations consistent with demonstrations and
requires them to predict the same interior for each concrete query frame.

## Reproducible failure it catches

Retained generator v3.2.0 SHA256:
`b10c383e8ecfbe58f04f3e0f3bee95f572e8544c97532bc6362700d4947e4831`.
Medium-band seeds **0–127**, sample indices beginning at 0, two queries:

- with three demonstrations, **69/128** lessons failed;
- with four independently keyed demonstrations, **38/128** still failed.

In every failed sampled lesson, at least one query key was absent from visible
demonstrations and admitted multiple distinct interiors. Exact examples and
rival keys are retained in `checks/round2-v32-lesson-ambiguity.json`; the
reproducer is `checks/reproduce_v32_lesson_ambiguity.py`.

This is stronger than the original single frozen lesson finding. That lesson had
three demonstrations containing keys 4/5 and an asymmetric key-3 query with four
possible outputs under independent key maps (`checks/fresh-lesson-key-gate.json`).
The generator's marginal support contained all keys and its inherited battery
was green, yet the particular lesson did not teach its query branch.

The repaired v3.3.0 source makes the teaching contract constructive: four
consecutive samples expose first-frame keys 2/3/4/5. Sixteen actual Racket-labeled
episodes, each with four demonstrations and two queries, passed the public-only
gate with zero candidate rejections or skipped indices
(`checks/round2-final-episode-aggregate.json`). This before/after result shows the
gate is actionable rather than merely diagnostic.

## Possible false positive

A curriculum may intentionally teach the arithmetic relation
`turns = key - 2` and expect extrapolation from a subset of keys. An independent-
key gate can reject such a legitimate lesson because it refuses to assume that
affine prior. The remedy is not to silently shrink the rival family until data
passes. Declare the intended prior in the lesson policy and evaluate against the
corresponding rivals.

Symmetric/no-op query objects are another edge case: an unseen key need not fail
when every surviving interpretation produces the same concrete output. The
implementation compares predicted query interiors rather than key counts, so
those cases can pass. Conflicting demonstrations or changed frame/key structure
remain hard errors.

## Cheapest reproducible test

From the extracted packet root after applying the patch:

```bash
python -m pytest -q repo/generators/f2dbde875127/tests/test_lesson_key_gate.py
python run_with_racket.py python \
  generators/f2dbde875127/workspace/episode_identifiability_probe.py \
  --count 4 --start-seed 0 --out ../checks/episode-screen.json
```

For input-only regression against a retained source snapshot:

```bash
python3 -E -s repo/generators/f2dbde875127/workspace/distribution_contract_probe.py \
  --generator checks/iterations/generator-3.2.0.py --count 128 \
  --out checks/v32-contract-replay.json
```

The lesson gate costs at most a small enumeration of quarter turns per relevant
frame and requires no model, GPU, hidden label, or extra Racket call once an
episode exists. A failed gate should retain rivals and either trigger bounded
resampling/addition of a new demonstration or attach an explicit extrapolation
label. It must never rewrite the hidden answer. A controlled Qwen ablation is
still required to quantify training benefit; none was performed here.

# qwen9-data-value

## Recommended gate: mandatory episode-level rival-survival gate

The highest-value additional gate is a **training-episode identifiability gate
that is mandatory at export time, not optional per generator**. For each
materialized lesson, run a small task-local bank of plausible wrong programs.
Reject the lesson when any rival matches every demonstration but disagrees with
the authoritative rule on the query or on a strict-canonical-like generated
counterexample.

### Reproducible failure it catches

In the baseline `f44596002946` generator, run
`difficulty=easy, seed=0, sample_index=0..3`. All four demonstrations are fit by
these wrong programs:

- connect diagonal pairs too;
- connect any aligned color occurring at least twice;
- let vertical segments always win crossings.

The only crossing occurs in sample 3 and happens to have a vertical winner, so
“vertical always wins” is not falsified. That same sample also places an
endpoint on the other segment. The existing per-grid execution and diversity
checks can stay green even though the lesson does not identify the intended
rule. A horizontal-higher crossing is a cheap authoritative counterexample.

### Possible false positive

Two programs may be genuinely extensionally equivalent over the intended task
manifold, or the generated counterexample may be outside that manifold. The
gate could then reject a valid lesson for failing to distinguish behavior that
should not matter. Require every counterexample to pass `strict_canonical_like`
and compare against the selected Racket authority; allow an explicit
answer-equivalence justification for rivals proven identical on the lawful
support.

### Cheapest test

For each generator, materialize 16–32 pinned four-demo episodes across the
three bands. Evaluate roughly 4–8 declared Python rival functions against the
demos; invoke Racket only for the query/counterexample when a rival survives.
This needs no model inference and is typically hundreds of cheap grid
operations plus a few authority calls. Fail export if a rival survives a demo
window and predicts a different lawful answer. The repaired generator's six
rivals already demonstrate the format: all 12 battery lessons refute all of
them.

# Qwen3.5-9B data-value question

## Recommended additional gate: lesson branch-mutation identifiability

The one additional automated gate with the highest expected value is a
**lesson branch-mutation gate**: for every materialized training lesson, synthesize
small plausible wrong programs from categorical semantic branches and output-code
permutations, then reject or quarantine a lesson when a mutant matches every
demonstration but changes the query answer.

This is narrower and cheaper than asking a model to solve the lesson. It directly tests
whether the examples distinguish the intended program from nearby programs that a
9B model can easily learn instead. The existing declared-rival mechanism remains useful;
the new part is automatically generating a basic rival family from branch signatures,
so quality does not depend entirely on a generator author anticipating every shortcut.

### Reproducible failure it would catch

Audit target `32d6c6648427` provides a concrete case. With generator SHA-256
`b07ae60f9e2e5ac54057a5aafc24878345d9a8fe5f5553c8a06e44240a48ccb8`, seed `0`,
medium difficulty, and sample indices `[3, 4, 5, 6]`, the three demonstrations all use
operation code `1` (AND), while the query uses operation code `2` (OR). A mutant that
maps every operation to AND matches all three demonstration outputs and differs on the
Racket-labeled query. The complete reproducer is in
`checks/audit/32d6c6648427/{probe,racket,rival,verification}.json`.

The second assigned audit shows the same failure class from a different direction:
`dfa5c1702b4c`, seed `6`, samples `[38,39,40,41]`, has demonstrations containing only
relation codes `{0,3}`; the query introduces codes `1` and `2`. Swapping the row-only
and column-only output codes is therefore invisible in the demonstrations but changes
the query. Evidence is in `checks/audit/dfa5c1702b4c/`.

### Possible false positive

An intentionally staged curriculum may be designed to introduce a new branch only in
the query, with the relevant semantics taught in an earlier lesson or supplied by a
separate instruction. A local lesson-only gate would call that ambiguous even though
the broader curriculum is intentional. Another false positive occurs when a synthesized
mutation is impossible or equivalent on the generator's declared legal domain.

The gate should therefore report the exact mutant and differing pair, honor an explicit
`ordered_curriculum`/cross-lesson policy, and require branch extractors or legal-domain
checks rather than guessing from arbitrary pixel values.

### Cheapest useful implementation

Extend the existing source-bound semantic/census path (principally
`shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` and the lesson-census materializer) with an
optional hook such as `lesson_branch_signature(input)` plus a small standard mutation
set:

1. map a query-only categorical branch to each branch seen in demonstrations;
2. swap pairs of categorical output codes not distinguished by demonstrations; and
3. collapse a multi-branch selector to the most common demonstrated branch.

Score those mutants against the already materialized Racket outputs. No model call,
new labels, or extra Racket execution is required after the lesson has been labeled.
A smoke gate can check the existing 12 lessons; the inexpensive stronger version is the
current 100-lessons-per-band census with query rotation. Store only mutants that fit all
demos and differ on the query, with source/rule hashes and replay seeds. That gives a
small, reproducible counterexample rather than an opaque scalar quality score.

> Based on your generator review, what one additional automated gate would most improve Qwen3.5-9B training data quality? Name a reproducible failure it would catch, a possible false positive, and the cheapest way to test it.

## Recommendation: recheck rival distinguishability after the actual lesson transformation

Before admitting a transformed lesson, require that every declared wrong rule
which predicts a different query answer be contradicted by at least one
**retained demonstration**. Apply this after the consumer's demonstration
selection, truncation or query-role reassignment—not only before that operation.
This is the best additional gate supported by this review's evidence; its impact
on Qwen3.5-9B learning has not been measured, and no single-model performance
improvement or universal optimality is asserted.

For rival r, with transformed demonstrations D and query q, reject when
`all(r(x) == y for (x,y) in D) and r(q.input) != q.output`.
An answer-equivalent rival is not an ambiguity for that query. The check must
use current source-bound Racket outputs and executable, domain-appropriate rivals;
no declared rivals or incomplete label evidence is not an identifiability pass.

## Reproducible failure

Audit target `ba090ac77d54`, generator SHA
`8da308ca4f853a97266e21fbfd4e3e32e8c7b93104371b1fc7a3393b5de237ee`,
rule-source SHA
`93f91c2b862dd45874908a7cdc339e282518feea043bc30f61e21e631024d9ec`.
The easy lesson at seed **3696047898**, starting sample index **0**, has four
demonstrations and one query. Move original pair **2** to the query role, leaving
pairs **0,1,3,4** as demonstrations. The declared
`euclidean_only_for_three_seeds` rival fits all four retained examples but gives
the wrong new query output. The five inputs pass the target validator; a separate
supported Racket apply agrees with all five retained labels.

The retained census covers 72 original lessons (24/band), with **zero** ambiguous
original-order lessons. Across all five possible query roles it finds **108/360**
ambiguous windows over **360 unique inputs**. This is a conditional transformation
failure, not proof that current production uses those rotations. Evidence:
`checks/audit/ba090ac77d54/verified-counterexample.json`, the complete source-bound
census, and `checks/audit/ba090ac77d54-roles-final.json`.

## Possible false positive

Rejecting a valid ordered lesson because some **unused** role permutation fails
would be wrong: all 72 actual original-order lessons passed here. Gate only
transformations the exporter truly applies; keep exhaustive role rotation as an
advisory authoring audit when roles are fixed. Bad/out-of-domain rivals can also
manufacture alarms, so rivals need domain validation and separate rationale.
Passing finite declared rivals is not a claim of unique rule identification.

`repo/generators/f47990415137/workspace/check_lesson_roles.py` already implements
the single-query role audit. It reads the retained census, checks its generator
hash and completion, evaluates actual LESSON_COMPETITORS once per pair, and reuses
those booleans for every role. No GPU, Qwen call, regenerated grid, or additional
Racket invocation is necessary. With four or five pairs and a handful of rivals,
this is a small CPU validation pass, not another training experiment.

Run from packet_root (payload cwd is repo):

redundant distinguishing examples, an equivalent rival, and fail-closed cases.

# qwen9-data-value

## Recommended additional gate: emitted-lesson rival survival

Run a gate on each **actual exported training episode**, not only on the generator-wide census. For every task-declared rival/shortcut, execute it on the episode's demonstrations. Reject or resample the episode when a rival matches every demonstration output yet differs from the intended rule on the query or on one deterministic held-out probe.

### Reproducible failure it catches

The baseline `f4a1fcdd1c8b` generator assigned a globally unique color to every component. Its three canonical examples do the same. Therefore this wrong rule survives every lesson:

> Keep every cell whose color occurs anywhere on the border.

That shortcut agrees whenever colors are globally unique, but fails when one disconnected component of a color touches the border and another component of the same color is interior. A Qwen3.5-9B fine-tune can obtain low training loss by learning global color membership instead of connected-component reasoning. A generator-wide witness rate does not guarantee that the particular demos assembled into one exported episode contain the witness.

### Possible false positive

An intentionally staged curriculum may include an ambiguous early lesson, or a task may genuinely define color globally. Blocking every ambiguous window would reject such deliberate examples. The gate should therefore evaluate only task-declared rivals and block only when the rival survives all demos **and** demonstrably disagrees with the intended rule on the episode query or a declared probe.

### Cheapest test

No model training is needed. Reuse `SEMANTIC_RIVALS` / `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` and the Python rule mirror already loaded during export:

1. For each emitted 3-demo episode, run each declared rival on the demo inputs.
2. Keep rivals that reproduce all demo outputs exactly.
3. Run survivors on the query input or one fixed counterexample probe.
4. Reject/resample only if a survivor disagrees with the intended output there.

This is a few grid-function calls per episode, deterministic, and much cheaper than a second 600-draw census or any Qwen inference. A single unit fixture using the repeated-color opposite-fate grid would have caught this review's central failure.

# qwen9-data-value

The highest-value additional gate is a **bounded-prefix rival synthesis gate for
ordered features**. Whenever the intended rule compares a full sequence (a crop,
row, contour, token list, or trace), automatically instantiate rivals that compare
only the first `k` elements and then fall back to an easy scalar such as color,
size, or input order. Require every rival that fits all canonical examples to be
refuted by at least one demonstration in every production lesson, and repeat the
check under every permitted query rotation.

**Reproducible failure caught.** In `f4a7ad69b9f2`, both
`(width,height,crop[:1],color)` and `(width,height,crop[:2],color)` fit all 4
canonical pairs and all 1,200 sampled baseline generated inputs, yet disagree
with the authority on lawful counterexamples. After fixing those inputs, the
existing four-demo schedule still produced 450 ambiguous query rotations out of
1,500 because holding out the sole lexicographic witness let the same rivals
survive. Evidence is in `checks/prefix-shortcut-before.json`,
`checks/prefix2-shortcut-before.json`, and `checks/lesson-census.json`.

**Possible false positive.** A bounded prefix may be genuinely equivalent on a
task's declared lawful domain—for example, if all legal sequences have length
at most `k`, or the validator guarantees that the first distinction occurs
within `k`. The gate should therefore accept a task-local domain proof or mark
that synthesized rival inapplicable rather than demanding an impossible witness.

**Cheapest test.** First test synthesized rivals on the canonical pairs. Only for
those that fit every usable pair, evaluate 100 materialized lessons per band and
all permitted query rotations, reusing the saved oracle labels. Add one small
constructive lawful adversary per surviving prefix depth to distinguish “the
sampler happened not to expose it” from true domain equivalence. This uses cheap
pure-Python rival scoring after the labels already exist and concentrates work on
shortcuts that are actually plausible for Qwen3.5-9B.

# qwen9-data-value

The one additional gate with the highest expected value is a **query-rotation lesson-identifiability gate over the actual assembled lesson schedule**.

It should require each task to declare executable, deterministic plausible rivals; materialize complete lessons exactly as training will assemble them; hold out each labelled pair in turn as the query; and reject a lesson whenever a rival fits every remaining demonstration but predicts a different answer for the held-out query.

**Reproducible failure it catches.** In this review, generator v3.0 produced 300/300 identifiable lessons in their original order, yet 402/1,200 query rotations were ambiguous. Removing the only partial-overlap example let `exact_span_only` survive; removing the only multicolor example let `global_frame_color` survive. The reproducer is `checks/lesson-census-final.out`, with the compressed full checkpoint at `checks/lesson-census-final.json.gz`. After adding a combined witness, the same 300-lesson/1,200-rotation run found 0 ambiguities (`checks/lesson-census-final-v3.1-r2.summary.json`). This is precisely the kind of superficially correct but weakly identifying supervision that can waste Qwen3.5-9B capacity.

**Possible false positive.** If the downstream pipeline guarantees one fixed query position and never rotates/reorders pairs, a failure that occurs only under a forbidden rotation is not a defect in emitted training data. A second possible false positive is a declared rival that differs syntactically but is answer-equivalent on the intended task domain; the gate should count ambiguity only when the rival also gives a different held-out answer.

**Cheapest test.** Run all rotations only on the small lesson window, using cached Python outputs for declared pure rivals. Reuse one authoritative label per unique input and invoke Racket only to establish/cache those labels, not once per rival or rotation. For a deterministic short schedule, exhaust all cyclic starts in task-local tests; otherwise use a small smoke sample first and escalate to 100 lessons per band only when a canonical-fitting shortcut exists or the smoke test finds ambiguity.

# qwen9-data-value

The one additional gate I would make mandatory is a **lesson-level declared-rival
identifiability gate under every allowed query rotation**.

A reproducible failure it catches is: a generator produces a discriminating
counterexample, but that example becomes the held-out query while the remaining
demonstrations all fit a plausible wrong rule. For this task, a lesson could show
only pairs where both containment tests agree; `horizontal_only` or
`vertical_only` would then fit every demonstration yet predict the query
differently. Correct labels and good marginal diversity would not catch that
teaching failure.

A possible false positive is an intentionally ordered curriculum whose consumer
never shuffles examples and whose later query position is semantically fixed. An
arbitrary rotation can remove evidence that the real ordered protocol guarantees.
The gate should therefore be required only when the training pipeline permits
query/example reordering; otherwise it should remain a separately reported
diagnostic.

The cheapest test is to reuse the existing small semantic sample: materialize 12
lessons with authoritative Racket labels, score each declared competitor on the
demonstrations, then hold out each labeled pair once. Fail only when a competitor
fits all remaining demonstrations and changes the held-out answer. This is a few
dozen rival applications, not model inference. For higher confidence before data
release, run 100 lessons per band. In this repair that larger check covered 300
lessons and 1,200 rotations with zero ambiguity, demonstrating that the gate is
both practical and directly actionable for Qwen3.5-9B data quality.

# qwen9-data-value

**Question.** Based on your generator review, what one additional automated gate
would most improve Qwen3.5-9B training data quality? Name a reproducible failure
it would catch, a possible false positive, and the cheapest way to test it.

**Answer.** Promote a **source-bound lesson/rival ambiguity gate with query
rotation** from an optional authoring diagnostic to a conditional training-data
gate whenever a declared or automatically detected shortcut fits every canonical
pair.

A reproducible failure is retained in
`checks/audit/c0aac14eef4d/rotation_witness.json`. For source hash
`6ee8b69db5fb8e1bfe688ecf5b98a0cac88731e57e6be67e2ad71ef3268955ce`,
the easy-band production sampler at seed `997599522` and sample indices 94–99
creates six lawful labelled pairs. Holding pair 3 out as the query leaves five
left-prefix demonstrations. Four wrong rules—copy-input-then-grow,
rightmost-extent, leading-run, and grow-each-marker—fit all five demos but disagree
with the Racket authority on the lawful right-edge query `[[0,0,0,0,0,9]]`.
Every input passes the task validator. Correct individual labels therefore do
not make that rotated lesson teachable.

A possible false positive is a declared rival that is actually answer-equivalent
throughout the lawful domain, or a curriculum whose downstream contract fixes a
single query position and deliberately forbids rotation. The gate should classify
those cases rather than blindly reject them: require a differing lawful query for

**Question:** Based on your generator review, what one additional automated gate
would most improve Qwen3.5-9B training data quality? Name a reproducible failure
it would catch, a possible false positive, and the cheapest way to test it.

## Recommendation: require source-bound teaching coverage against family rivals

At data admission, require a small curated rival set for each reviewed family,
then check that the actual lesson sampler supplies demonstrations distinguishing
those rivals before a query requires the distinction. Include both rivals
already rejected by the original examples and plausible shortcuts that fit all
original examples but fail on an agreed lawful domain witness. Record missing
coverage as unknown or blocked, rather than treating an absent rival contract
as evidence of successful teaching. Reuse the existing semantic gate and
lesson-census implementation; the additional gate is enforcement of this
source-bound evidence at the consumer boundary.

## Reproducible failure it catches

The baseline `fa3550d200a0` generator, SHA-256
`dbd7e8b5a46571f83a63aa4e2b8abbae691931512ff21c7775a76d5badbda782`, used eight
cardinally connected templates, all inside a marker-centered 3×3 window.
A four-connected rival matched **28/28 generated/boundary inputs** in the
retained baseline probe, but matched only **2/8 canonical appearances**
(the canonical ledger repeats four unique inputs). The canonical rule requires
diagonal connections on three of those four unique inputs. Thus correct labels
and diverse positions/colors did not teach the canonical connectivity choice.

A second rival copied only the marker's centered 3×3 window. It matched
**8/8 canonical appearances and 28/28 generated/boundary inputs**, yet a lawful
endpoint piece extending two cells from its marker separated it from the actual
Racket output. Both witnesses passed the selected validator. Their input,
Racket output, rival output and source identities are retained in
`checks/canonical-probe/before/`, especially `assessment.json`, `prepared.json`
and `racket-000.json`. These reproduce the two earlier exact-source audit leads;
they are not a claim of an independent new discovery of those leads.

The repair declares both rivals and schedules distinguishing objects. Its
final source is `c5a3a7e69f0ae05f1408fde8a7ee0fed8a10e196726efdd1438ec70b805a6a73`.
Actual final evidence includes **300/300 production lessons** and **1,200/1,200
query rotations** without detected ambiguity against the three declared rivals.
The complete materialized census is retained as `checks/lesson-census.json.gz`,
with exact raw size/hash and restoration instructions in
`checks/lesson-census.compression.json`; the summary is
`checks/lesson-census.summary.json`. This remains finite declared-rival evidence,
not proof of unique induction or measured improvement in Qwen.

## Possible false positive

A generator intentionally scoped to only cardinally connected radius-one
pieces cannot distinguish these shortcuts within that restricted domain.
Automatically rejecting it would confuse a bounded curriculum decision with
wrong labels. A separating witness may also introduce clipping, duplicate
markers or another unsupported ambiguity. Require a validator/domain verdict
and a named reviewer decision about whether the broader behavior is intended.
Do not automatically admit a handmade counterexample merely because its cells
are legal ARC colors. Here the four-connectivity distinction is already present
in canonical inputs; the endpoint extension is an explicit nearby-domain choice.

## Cheapest test

Start with the cached canonical labels and a dozen deterministic production
lessons; evaluate pure Python rivals against the already materialized Racket
labels. No model inference or training run is necessary. The provided
`workspace/probe_canonical.py` dynamically reads actual rival declarations,
deduplicates aliases, records canonical fit, and checks each query using only
the shared demonstrations. When a short teaching schedule exists, enumerate
its start residues at one fixed seed; only expand the census when a concrete
ambiguity or untested boundary remains. On this family, four start residues
across three bands produce twelve lessons and forty-eight rotations. The final
semantic battery executed that enumeration with no ambiguity; its scope is
fixed seed zero, not every seed.

The gate should retain counterexamples and source hashes and invalidate its
evidence when the generator or rule changes. It should preserve separate
canonical, prototype, ordered-production and rotation verdicts. Neither a pass
nor a successful source review should silently change protected family splits,
trajectory admission or model-performance claims.

# qwen9-data-value

## Recommended additional gate: observable-cue shortcut synthesis

The single most useful added gate would automatically test whether cheap,
observable nuisance cues can predict the output roles without performing the
intended transformation. For object tasks, the gate should extract fields already
available from `observe_overrides` or a task analysis hook—dimensions, palette
mode, object count, top-left order, absolute sizes, schedule residue—and fit a
small family of deterministic rivals such as decision stumps and two-field lookup
tables. It should then require every exported demonstration window to contain a
Racket-labelled pair on which each canonical-fitting rival disagrees.

### Reproducible failure it would catch

`fae242ae157d` 4.0.0 passed its ordinary before battery, yet 180/180 sampled
default draws had a perfect coupling:

- canonical dimensions -> ascending scan rank and areas 4/5/6;
- 11x14 -> descending scan rank; and
- 13x16 -> mixed scan rank.

A two-field rival using only scene dimensions and object top-left position
therefore reproduced the output colours without comparing areas. The final
repair's explicit probe shows the relevant denominator and source hashes in
`checks/schedule-cue-diagnostic-before.json` and
`checks/schedule-cue-diagnostic-final.json`.

### Possible false positive

Some ARC tasks intentionally use context—canvas size, palette, legend, or a
marker—as the rule selector. A generic cue-correlation warning would therefore
flag legitimate contextual-gating tasks, especially when each context selects a
different transformation. The gate must distinguish a declared answer-bearing
context axis from a nuisance axis and allow a task-local exemption backed by an
executable branch contract.

### Cheapest useful test

No model training is needed. For each difficulty band:

1. generate 6–12 deterministic samples (or one full short schedule period);
2. compute Racket outputs once;
3. enumerate one- and two-cue lookup rivals over declared observable metadata
   plus simple object order statistics; and
4. for every production lesson window, fail when a rival fits all demonstrations
   but predicts a different query output.

For this task, six schedule slots and six cyclic starts were enough; testing 12
seeds across three bands required only 216 three-demo windows. The task-local
rival can then be promoted into `SEMANTIC_RIVALS`/`WITNESS_RIVALS` for the larger
shared census. This gate would directly improve Qwen3.5-9B data value by removing
examples where a small model is rewarded for learning presentation metadata
instead of the intended abstraction.

# qwen9-data-value

The highest-value additional gate is a **source-bound lesson-window identifiability gate**, not another per-instance validity check. It should materialize the exact training unit (for this task, three demonstrations plus a query), execute the authority and declared plausible rivals, and fail when a rival matches every demonstration but disagrees with the authority on the query.

A reproducible failure it would catch is the baseline form of this generator sampling three individually valid examples that repeat one control operation, or always place both normalized masks through `(0,0)`. A fixed-union/fixed-intersection/fixed-XOR solver or an origin shortcut can then fit the full visible lesson even though it predicts a different query answer. Per-grid self-checks, diversity statistics, and canonical-profile checks all miss that lesson-level ambiguity. After this repair, the 100-lessons-per-band census found 0 ambiguous lessons among 300 and refuted all four declared rivals on every lesson (`checks/lesson-census.json`).

A possible false positive is a lawful but coincidentally degenerate lesson: for example, union and XOR can agree when the normalized masks are disjoint, or a subset geometry can make one fixed operation agree with the selected operation on the visible demonstrations. Such a lesson may be acceptable in a broader curriculum even though it is not self-identifying in isolation. The gate should therefore distinguish a hard failure for exported standalone lessons from an advisory result for intentionally mixed curricula, and it should require rivals to be task-plausible rather than enumerate arbitrary programs.

The cheapest useful test is:

1. Use fixed replayable seeds and the production lesson sampler.
2. Start with 20 lessons per difficulty as a fast CI smoke check, each with the actual demonstration/query layout.
3. Run the canonical authority once per unique input and each declared rival locally; fail only when a rival fits all demonstrations and differs on the query.
4. Escalate changed generators to 100 lessons per band and cover every residue of any small deterministic schedule.

This is inexpensive because outputs can be cached by input hash, and it directly measures the data unit seen by Qwen3.5-9B rather than inferring lesson quality from marginal sample statistics.

> improve Qwen3.5-9B training data quality? Name a reproducible failure it would

## Recommended gate: automatic simple-shortcut synthesis

Add a **canonical-to-lesson shortcut synthesis gate** to
`shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py`. Instead of checking only rival rules
that a generator author remembered to declare, the gate would enumerate a small,
task-agnostic DSL of cheap object selectors and transforms—for example color
rank, component size, bounding-box area/aspect, position/scan order, canonical
prototype membership, and common reflection/rotation predicates. It would keep
every candidate that fits all canonical demonstration pairs, then require each
candidate either to be authority-equivalent on the lawful sampled domain or to
be falsified by at least one generated demonstration before a query where it
disagrees.

### Reproducible failure it would catch

The baseline `fc41c9b3a565` declared **no semantic contract** and generated no
canonical-profile samples. A memorized-prototype rule such as “keep only the
canonical square and canonical four-cell point-symmetric shape,” or a coarse
rule such as “keep the largest/even/non-triomino objects,” can fit the sparse
canonical demonstrations yet disagree on a generalized query. Because the old
generator declared no rivals, a declared-rival-only gate had nothing to score.
The synthesized gate would discover such a fitting selector automatically and
produce the exact surviving demonstrations plus differing query as a retained
counterexample.

### Possible false positive

A synthesized selector can be extensionally equivalent to the authority on the
actual lawful domain but differ only on malformed or unreachable grids. It can
also flag a rotated-query ambiguity that is irrelevant when downstream assembly
uses a fixed ordered curriculum. The gate should therefore distinguish
`authority-equivalent on sampled lawful support`, `production lesson defect`,
and `diagnostic rotation-only ambiguity` rather than treating every disagreement
as blocking.

### Cheapest useful test

Do not invoke a model. Extract components and a compact feature table from the
four canonical pairs, exhaust a bounded selector DSL, and retain only candidates
that reproduce every canonical output. Then score those survivors on about
**20 source-bound generated lessons** (four demos plus one query) using cached
Racket labels. Escalate to the existing 100-lessons-per-band census only when a
survivor reaches the query and disagrees. This adds milliseconds to feature
mining plus the cost of labels the semantic gate already materializes, while
catching undeclared shortcut families before Qwen3.5-9B sees them.

> Based on your generator review, what one additional automated gate would most improve Qwen3.5-9B training data quality? Name a reproducible failure it would catch, a possible false positive, and the cheapest way to test it.

## Proposal: require counterevidence against a declared input-projection shortcut

Add a gate that asks whether the generated training support forces a learner
to use the intended relationship, rather than allowing a small input-only
projection to determine the answer. A projection might be red coordinates,
the presence of a particular body color, or a panel position. The gate should
retain an explicit rival and exact Racket-labeled counterexamples, then check
that the actual exported demonstrations refute it. This is one support-and-
lesson gate, with a cheap projection census followed by the existing rival
lesson machinery. It is a proposed training-quality improvement; no Qwen
training run or downstream accuracy gain was measured in this review.

## Reproducible failure it would catch

The assigned task's imported generator has 32 red coordinate layouts and
32,765 scene codes. Its candidate-relevant gray/black context was fixed for
each red key, while many changing background cells could never influence a
red-containing window. A fixed red-key-to-window dictionary consequently
solves the generated support without learning gray-window eligibility or
greedy candidate selection. Ordinary exact-grid diversity and correct Racket
labels can both pass under this construction. The retained baseline source
hash is `a971dcfa81f9aca13cb3fa186f9600f1afdfeaaac42a1c86655a5f71f75b0ba4`.
See `checks/canonical-investigation/` and the final task's structural contrast.

The repair makes 21 red keys occur with two different selected-center masks.
The production lesson schedule supplies refutations, and the final 300-lesson
census checks that the named rival is eliminated in all 1,800 held-out roles.
The projection check would also continue to warn that there are only 53
candidate contexts and fifteen scene-code bits. Fixing a single projection
shortcut does not certify broad procedural diversity.

The second audit gives a separate concrete example. In `1e92a4eef51d`, body
color 2 implies one key and body color 1 implies the other; the body palette
therefore reveals the reflection axis without consulting the key. A compact
key-ignoring rival matches all four canonical pairs and 48/48 generated Racket
cases checked. Two validator-accepted same-body/different-key inputs have
different authoritative outputs, but neither is generated because the body
lacks the palette anchor. A hook that checks only demo-fit/query-disagreement
cannot expose this shortcut while every generated query also rewards it.
Exact receipts are in `checks/audit/1e92a4eef51d/finding.json`.

## What the gate should decide

1. Deduplicate exact inputs and group them by an explicitly named input
   projection. Compare a relevant target projection such as selected centers
   or edit coordinates, not complete noisy output images.
2. Treat different target projections within one input-projection group as
   direct evidence that this projection alone is insufficient. Bind the
   witness to source hashes, legal-domain checks and executed Racket labels.
3. Treat no witnessed contrast as **unknown**, not a general proof of a
   defective or adequate generator. For a domain with an explicitly unwanted
   named shortcut, require an on-support counterexample before admitting its
   training family. A valid off-support counterexample is diagnostic, not
   proof that current generation supplies the missing evidence.
4. Once that rival is declared, use the existing production materializer and
   lesson census to require a refuting demonstration in each intended lesson
   and query-role policy. A query-only distinguishing case is insufficient.

The first audit demonstrates why the lesson step matters: hard seed 4 in
`7017b91a367d` has three demonstrations without a left-panel-only occupied
cell and a query containing one. A rival that erases just that role fits all
three demos and gets one query cell wrong. This is actual lesson ambiguity,
unlike the second audit's consistently rewarded shortcut. Both need precise
failure classifications, not a single undifferentiated diversity score.

## Possible false positive

A task may legitimately depend only on a color key or red layout. In that
case, requiring multiple answers under the same sufficient input projection
would reject correct data. An illegal counterfactual, a projection that drops
shape, or comparing complete outputs whose inert noise differs could also
create a misleading signal. Require an explicit claimed dependency, validate
the input domain, include shape in the grouping key, compare only the
task-relevant target, and keep no-contrast results as unknown. The same exact
input with conflicting labels is a data-consistency error, not useful
counterevidence, and must be reported separately.

## Cheapest test and built tool

Start with existing Racket receipts and a small batch of generated inputs.
Grouping by tuple keys and comparing center/edit coordinates uses linear
Python work in the number of cells; it needs no model call, training job, or
additional labels when receipts already exist. For the assigned task, 840
forced scene codes are enough to observe all 21 repaired same-red-key center
contrasts in the focused source probe. That finite count does not exhaust
every code. A pair of decisive inputs needs only two fresh Racket applications
to verify the projection failure; then use the already available lesson
census for teaching frequency and held-out roles.

This return includes a runnable passive prototype under
`checks/tooling/projection-collisions/`: `projection_gate.py`, focused tests,
README, an explicitly baseline/off-support Racket-backed fixture and command
evidence. It groups shape plus red coordinates, offers selected-center or
edit-coordinate targets, discounts duplicate inputs, rejects conflicting
labels and validates receipt provenance in its certifying mode. Its verdict
is bounded to supplied cases. It is a small starting point for the proposed
shared gate, not an installed shared-controller change or a Qwen benchmark.

The single additional gate I would add is an **automatic support-gap shortcut
gate**: derive simple restricted variants of the authority from canonical
features—orientation, object ordinal, border/interior position, color role, and
precondition threshold—and fail when one of those variants fits every generated
demonstration but disagrees with a lawful canonical or generated counterexample.
This complements the current declared-rival gate, because authors cannot be
expected to anticipate every easy shortcut a 9B model may learn.

generator places fillable 7-pairs only in interior columns. An
“apply the bridge rule only to interior columns” solver matched all **64/64**

train pair 0, where the authority also fills edge columns 0 and 6. The evidence
is in `checks/audit/3ecae1984445/counterexample.json`. The same gate family would
also have exposed this task's canonical-perfect `downward_only` and
`first_target_only` shortcuts before explicit rivals were written.

first-stage generator may exclude border cases because a later stage teaches
them, or deployment may explicitly exclude that branch. The gate should therefore
report the surviving shortcut with a concrete witness and allow a structured
scope/stage declaration, rather than treating every support difference as an
unconditional rule error.

band, label with the existing Racket runner, enumerate a small fixed library of
feature masks/restrictions, and compare each candidate's demo/query outputs.

counterexample when possible. This is only dozens of small-grid transformations
per lesson and can run as a preflight before the larger census or model-based

The one additional gate with the highest value would be a **canonical-fitting rival lesson-and-rotation gate**: discover or accept a small executable set of plausible rules that fit every canonical pair, then require each exported lesson's demonstrations to refute every rival that would change its query answer. For deterministic curricula, enumerate every schedule residue and every permitted held-out position; for stochastic curricula, run a pinned 100-per-band census and retain exact failing lessons.

A reproducible failure it would catch is this task's imported teaching gap. All five canonical pairs contain exactly two backslash-oriented pair colors and no decoys, so four wrong rules fit them: preserve ignored colors, fill every nonzero color's bbox, process only backslash pairs, or run only when exactly two pair colors exist. A lesson composed from similarly narrow draws can label every grid correctly yet leave Qwen3.5-9B with no evidence against those shortcuts. The final `canonical_shortcuts.json` and `reference_probe.py` show the counterexamples and the repaired schedule.

The gate should therefore report ordered-production and rotation verdicts separately, and require maintainers to mark which query policy is actually exported.

The cheapest test is mostly Python: after one Racket-versus-mirror parity check, enumerate the small deterministic schedule cycle, materialize `EXAMPLES_NEEDED + 1` pairs, and compare declared rivals against an independent oracle for every held-out position. Run the shared 100-per-band source-bound census only when a canonical-fitting rival exists or the schedule changes. This gives high leverage without invoking Racket for every sample.

# qwen9-data-value

The single additional gate I would add is a **cyclic leave-one-out lesson-identifiability gate against every declared rival**. For each materialized lesson with `N` demonstrations and one query, hold out each of its `N+1` pairs in turn as the query. A rival fails the gate when it agrees with all remaining demonstrations but disagrees with the authoritative output on the held-out pair. This checks the teaching unit that Qwen3.5-9B actually sees, not merely whether a witness exists somewhere in the generator's aggregate distribution.

**Reproducible failure it catches.** The first repaired v3.0 schedule placed one occupied-query overwrite witness in each four-sample cycle. Ordinary production lessons passed because that witness appeared among the four demonstrations. But in a five-pair window, rotating that sole overwrite pair into the query left four clear demonstrations; the plausible `skip_occupied_query` program then fit every demo and failed only on the query. The new task-local test reproduced this in easy, medium, and hard (`checks/cyclic-rotation-red-v3.0.log`). Alternating clear/overwrite in v3.1.0 fixes it, and 34/34 tests now pass.

**Possible false positive.** A fixed curriculum that contractually never rotates pair roles may be perfectly usable even though an artificial leave-one-out rotation is ambiguous. The gate could reject such data despite the production query position always being identifiable. It can also be overly strict when a surviving rival is extensionally equivalent on the intended deployment domain but differs only outside it. Therefore the result should be blocking when downstream augmentation can rotate pairs, and advisory otherwise.

**Cheapest test.** No model inference is needed. Read `EXAMPLES_NEEDED`, the generator's declared rivals, and any small deterministic schedule period. Materialize only one period plus `N` samples per band, compute authoritative outputs once, and test all consecutive `N+1` windows and all held-out positions. For this generator, parity is the schedule period, so six consecutive samples per band are enough for complete residue coverage; the retained regression uses eight starts for margin. This is far cheaper and more diagnostic than another 100-lesson random census.

**Question:** Based on your generator review, what one additional automated gate
would most improve Qwen3.5-9B training data quality? Name a reproducible failure
it would catch, a possible false positive, and the cheapest way to test it.

## Recommendation: check rival survival on the assembled lesson

Before admitting a generated lesson, reject it when a task-specific plausible
rival matches every demonstration but gives a different answer to any query.
Score the exact materialized examples, with their selected Racket labels,
source identity and accepted indices. If the intended export permits changing
which pair is the query, apply the same check to each permitted holdout.

This is a proposed use of existing shared machinery as a data-quality gate,
not a request to implement a second census. `lesson-census` and the semantic
gate already perform most of the work. The production worker currently records
only a `lesson_identifiable` hook: `src/arcpuzzles/worker.py:lesson_check` returns
`not_declared` for this repaired task even though its rival dictionaries exist.
The finished solve's generation provenance shows that distinction. Reusing the
shared rival evaluator in the data-admission path would make a missing hook
different from evidence that the actual lesson passed a rival check.

## Concrete reproducible failure

For fd68649aabf7, all eight rivals fit all four canonical pairs. In particular,
using the component centroid instead of its horizontal bbox center looks correct
on those examples. The saved 7x9 two-body query has a body centered by bbox
exactly between marker columns, but with more mass on the right. Canonical
Racket chooses the left marker; the centroid rival chooses the right. A lesson
with three canonical demonstrations and that query therefore has correct
reference labels but does not teach which of these rules to use.

I built and ran:

```bash
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 \
  generators/fd68649aabf7/workspace/check_teaching_contrast.py \
  --out ../checks/teaching-contrast.json
```

The command succeeds as a diagnostic reproduction; its proposed admission
verdict is **reject**, with all eight surviving-and-disagreeing rivals named.
The query's output comes from the retained actual Racket fixture. This is a
constructed teaching contrast, not a claim that the final sampler emits that
lesson. The repaired default sampler separately passed 300 production lessons
and 1,200 permitted holdouts against the same rivals.

Audit 677dcb71e2be shows why the rival family must also be reviewed: a fixed
palette-rank permutation matches four real generated demonstrations, while a
legal color-swap query differs under Racket. The existing hook returns `[]`
because that permutation competitor is missing. No automatic finite-rival gate
can certify against hypotheses it does not include.

## Possible false positive

An ordered lesson may intentionally reserve a harder case for the query and
never allow arbitrary pair rotations. Requiring every imaginable holdout would
reject a production policy it does not actually use. Record the assembly policy
and require only its supported query positions; keep additional rotations as
diagnostics. Also distinguish a rival that agrees on all demonstrations and all
queries (`survived_all`) from one that disagrees on a query: only the latter
is a measured ambiguous-answer finding.

## Cheapest useful implementation

Reuse already materialized reference labels and cache each pure rival prediction
by source/rival/input hash. With eight rivals and a four-pair lesson, there are
32 small Python predictions; all four holdouts reuse them and require no new
Racket calls. Run a small source-bound canary on generator changes, then check
the actual lessons selected for export. Retain one exact counterexample per
failure instead of another large green log, and reserve the 100-per-band census
for new semantic contracts or concrete uncertainty.

This would catch mislabeled *teaching assumptions* that per-grid label checks
cannot catch. I have not trained Qwen3.5-9B in this review, so the gain in model
accuracy or data efficiency remains an experimental hypothesis.

## Proposed gate: automatic lesson-level component-partition rival survival

The highest-value additional gate would automatically score a small standard family of **object-partition rivals** whenever a rule appears component-wise: same-colour 4-connectivity, same-colour 8-connectivity, colour-blind 4-connectivity, colour-blind 8-connectivity, and “merge disconnected cells by colour.” A training lesson fails when one of these alternatives matches every demonstration but predicts a different query.

**Reproducible failure it catches.** In selected baseline `fdb8815ba528`, all canonical objects have distinct colours and are separated. Consequently, “one bounding box per colour,” same-colour 8-connectivity, and colour-blind 4-connectivity all fit every canonical pair. A random lesson containing only distinct separated objects can be perfectly labelled yet teach any of those wrong programs. The retained witness at `generators/fdb8815ba528/counterexamples/current-shortcut/question_training_shortcut.json` makes all three disagree with the authority.

**Possible false positive.** Some tasks intentionally define a restricted domain where colours are guaranteed unique and objects guaranteed separated. In that case the rivals are extensionally equivalent on the intended domain, so demanding an out-of-domain contact/repeated-colour example would be inappropriate. The gate should therefore report a domain question unless the generator or canonical grammar already admits the distinguishing input.

**Cheapest test.** First run the rival functions locally on the existing labelled demonstrations and query; this needs no extra Racket calls. For any survivor that changes the query, search only 32–64 generated inputs for a lawful counterexample using `self_check`. Invoke the canonical Racket authority once for the first candidate and retain that receipt. This is much cheaper than a full model evaluation and directly measures whether the data identifies the intended partition rule.

ambiguous because a later lesson supplies the disambiguating witness. Requiring

valid sequence. The gate therefore needs an explicit ordered-curriculum

1. Run each declared rival on the small canonical set and discard any rival that
   does not actually fit every usable canonical pair.
2. Materialize a deterministic smoke sample of 12 production lessons, each with

# qwen9-data-value

The single highest-value additional gate would be a **source-bound predicate-boundary contrast gate**: for every structural acceptance predicate used by a generator, construct the cheapest local mutation that preserves the selected authority's predicate but violates a plausible stricter shortcut, then require at least one such disagreement in the generated curriculum and in a complete lesson window.

**Reproducible failure it would catch.** In selected baseline v3.0.0 for `fe0dc9f32b7b`, the authority accepts a color-8 component when its cell count equals its bounding-box perimeter. Nevertheless, every generated positive was an exact hollow outline. An `exact_perimeter_only` solver matched all 5/5 canonical pairs and all 1,000/1,000 sampled baseline inputs. Existing checks were 12/12 green because that shortcut was not declared. A single count-preserving inward swap makes the authority and shortcut disagree reproducibly.

**Possible false positive.** A selected Racket rule can be intentionally permissive outside the natural puzzle grammar. A mechanically mutated grid might satisfy the program but be visually implausible, violate the generator's documented domain, or expose an implementation accident rather than intended semantics. The gate should therefore count a contrast only when the mutated input passes `self_check`/`strict_canonical_like` (or is explicitly approved as a domain expansion) and remains within declared size/palette/component constraints.

**Cheapest test.** No model inference is needed. For each sampled qualifying object, try one deterministic local edit—for a rectangular component, move one non-corner boundary cell one step inward while preserving connectivity, bounding box, and cell count. Run the selected Racket authority and the candidate shortcut on that grid, then require one disagreement and one three-demo lesson that contains it. A tiny smoke budget—one pinned seed, the three bands, and one successful mutation per predicate—is enough for CI; the larger semantic gate can measure frequency later.

# qwen9-data-value — version 1

> Based on your generator review, what one additional automated gate would most improve Qwen3.5-9B training data quality? Name a reproducible failure it would catch, a possible false positive, and the cheapest way to test it.

## Proposed gate: mandatory rival survival on the exact assembled lesson

Add a training-export gate after demonstrations and the query have been selected. For every canonical-fitting declared or shared diagnostic rival, fail a lesson only when the rival matches **all displayed demonstrations** but predicts a different output for the actual query. When a generator claims arbitrary query rotation, test every holdout; when it declares a small schedule period, enumerate every start residue. Bind the verdict to generator hash, rule hash, accepted sample indices, sampler settings, and input hashes.

This is the highest-value gate from this review because draw-level validity and label correctness can both pass while the lesson teaches the wrong discriminant. Its expected benefit to Qwen3.5-9B is a data-quality hypothesis, not a measured model-training gain.

## Reproducible failure it would catch

At baseline generator SHA `d64cde2df0c16878e23fdfddf18d703b3de067039f8bc8cc345757ef1acc173d`, ranking objects by bounding-box area fit all five canonical pairs and 872 of 900 ordinary generated labels. For seed `947031`, easy difficulty, samples 162–164 were three demonstrations on which bbox area and cell count agreed. Sample 165 was a lawful query with component sizes `(6,5,3)` and bbox areas `(6,8,4)`; the bbox rival fit every demo but changed 11 query cells.

The exact baseline sample indices and measurements are retained in `repo/generators/fe947dc3e12c/counterexamples/review-ce35ccec4404bbb0-v0001/retained/checks/audit/fe947dc3e12c/probe.json`, with labelled lesson material beside it. A gate that only checks individual grids, aggregate witness frequency, or canonical fit would miss this episode-level failure.

## Possible false positive

An intentionally ordered curriculum may promise that only its production query position is valid, while evidence accumulates across episodes. Requiring every rotation would then reject a legitimate ordered lesson policy. A malformed or implausible rival declaration can also manufacture a needless obligation.

Control this by making the policy explicit: production-query identifiability is always checked; arbitrary rotations block only when the generator/exporter claims them. Before a rival can block, require it to fit every usable canonical pair and execute without errors on the declared task domain. A rival that also matches the query is not a failure under this criterion.

## Cheapest reliable test

Start with the generator's Python mirror and rival callables; no model inference or training run is needed.

1. Materialize one real 3-demo/1-query lesson for each declared schedule residue and difficulty band.
2. Evaluate every canonical-fitting rival on each demo and each possible held-out query required by policy.
3. Stop at the first rival that survives all demos and changes the query, retaining that small lesson as a regression.
4. Confirm only disputed inputs with one batched public Racket `apply`; use the Python mirror for the wider census after parity is established.

For this task the minimum deterministic check is six lessons (period 2 × three bands) and 24 rotations. The broader cheap follow-up is 100 lessons per band. The final repair passes both: `checks/lesson-census-period.summary.json` has 0/24 ambiguous rotations, and `checks/lesson-census.summary.json` has 0/1,200.

# qwen9-data-value

**Question:** Based on your generator review, what one additional automated gate
would most improve Qwen3.5-9B training data quality? Name a reproducible failure
it would catch, a possible false positive, and the cheapest way to test it.

## Proposed gate: effective-witness checking on each assembled lesson

Before admitting a lesson, evaluate a small, declared operation-family version
space on its demonstrations, then count the **different query answers** produced
by hypotheses that still fit. Reject or repair lessons with more than one answer;
report inconsistent labels separately. For rotation tasks, also report which
examples distinguish all, some, or none of the candidate rotations.

This repository already has semantic hooks and a semantic-gate stage. The missing
addition is a reusable operation-family adapter and an admission-time check of
the **actual assembled lesson**, including the no-contract case—not another
optional hook whose absence can remain advisory. Preparation currently records
`lesson_identifiability_checked: false`. The new task-local implementation is a
ready-to-replay rotation adapter, not a claim that the shared export/solve
pipeline has already been patched.

For this task, keep four possible turn choices for each marker-count residue.
Intersect them with each observed demonstration output; evaluate the surviving
choices on the query and deduplicate identical outputs. Add a few task-specific
rivals such as reversing direction and retaining only the largest blob. This
checks what the examples actually teach, rather than accepting a witness merely
because a named predicate is true.

## Reproducible failure and measured boundary

Baseline source `6c0b3cb57d3761838d6452b42936e2f57fb76b12717da1b0cf01b95e4f71c8d7` generates a rotationally symmetric plus at
`generate(0, 0, difficulty='easy')`, accepted by its self-check. The before census
found 40/500 easy inputs with just one distinguishable rotation, and 298/1,488
ambiguous four-demo/next-query windows across easy/medium/hard. These are seed 0,
indices 0–499 per band, with 500 within-band distinct inputs and overlapping
windows. Racket labels are correct; the teaching problem is unsupported inference,
not mislabeling. A nominal “nonrectangular” condition misses it.

Final source `389301c2c8847e304bda9a568a497bbd5ac77f06a2d15f33584a4a06770eec7c` has 0/1,488 such ambiguous windows under the same finite
hypothesis class and 0/1,500 rotationally invariant crops. Both censuses use the
same canonical rule `77da9e97370c` and actual Racket labels. Full source/label hashes,
all draws, and every failing window are in `checks/orbit-*-final/`.

A second concrete illustration is audit 033db13a9d37: three demos can lack the
later distractor needed to distinguish first-nonzero from last-nonzero behavior.
The retained counterexample shows a rival that fits all three demos and changes
the query answer. Merely declaring three examples does not supply that witness.

## Possible false positive

A symmetric query can have the **same answer under several rotations**. Rejecting
it because the rotation parameter is not unique, or because some residue lacks
a demo, would discard a perfectly determined answer. Deduplicate query outputs,
not parameter assignments. A symmetric demonstration can also be harmless if
other demonstrations supply the needed witness. The selected generator's strict
four-orbit domain is a deliberate witness policy, not a universal validity test.
A finite rival family can also be too permissive or too narrow; log the family
and disagreement rather than claiming universal logical uniqueness.

## Cheapest useful test

No model training is needed to establish this defect. First run the focused
plus-shape and missing-branch regression tests. Then run the source-bound census
on 20 indices per band (60 Racket-labeled draws, 48 overlapping windows) as a
smoke test, increasing to the retained 500-index sweep for acceptance:

```sh
# From packet_root, after applying the patch; choose a fresh output directory.
python3 run_with_racket.py python3 generators/ffcd7510821d/workspace/orbit_census.py --phase maintainer-smoke --count 20 --seeds 0 --racket --out ../checks/maintainer-smoke
```

The command above is a recommended small replay, not a claimed executed result.
Actual 500-index before/final commands and exits are in `RESULTS.json`.
Expected benefit is less ambiguous supervision and fewer learnable shortcuts;
**no Qwen3.5-9B loss, accuracy, convergence, or transfer improvement was measured**.
A matched-budget training ablation would be needed to quantify that hypothesis.

# Answer to `qwen9-data-value`

The highest-value additional gate would be an **undeclared execution-order rival
gate**. For generators whose rule applies the same operation to multiple
objects/colours in a declared order, the gate should automatically test a small,
fixed family of plausible orderings—numeric ascending/descending, row-major
first appearance, reverse first appearance, and generator insertion order—and
ask whether any rival matches every demonstration but disagrees on the query.
It should use the task's Racket outputs, not a Python mirror, and save the exact
lesson when a rival survives.

A reproducible failure is retained for audit target `b5f36515995c`. With
ordinary production generation at seed `900001`, difficulty `easy`, samples
1, 2, and 3 as demonstrations and sample 4 as query, a “process colours in
first row-major appearance order” rival matches all three Racket-labelled demos
but differs on the Racket-labelled query. The target's declared
`lesson_identifiable` hook returns no reason, because that rival is not declared.
The exact inputs, Racket outputs, rival outputs, source hashes, and comparison
are in `checks/audit/b5f36515995c/probe.json` and `racket.json`.

A possible false positive is a rival ordering that differs syntactically but is
answer-equivalent throughout the generator's documented domain—for example,
when operations commute or the generator guarantees the two orderings coincide.
The gate should therefore report a teaching defect only when it has a lawful,
validator-accepted lesson where the rival fits all demos **and produces a
different Racket query output**. Merely detecting a different internal order is
not enough.

The cheapest test is model-free: for each finite schedule period (or a small
pinned sample when no period is declared), materialize one four-pair lesson per
band, rotate every pair through the query position, obtain Racket labels once,
and evaluate the fixed rival library locally. This is a handful of deterministic
transformations and equality checks, not a Qwen inference run. It can run after
the existing semantic smoke gate and expand to the 100-lessons-per-band census
only when a rival survives.

items.text:
Make consequential-rival evidence an admission requirement

**Highest-priority shared-tool change.** Findings **M1**, **A1**, and **A2** show
why correct labels and generic validation do not ensure that a lesson supplies
the evidence needed for its query.

**Symptom and concrete evidence.** The source-bound M1 baseline contained
**41/180 ambiguous production lessons** and **182/720 ambiguous query rotations**
under seven finite rivals. Hard seed 28, indices `[0,1,2,3]`, admits the
double-swap shortcut: it fits all demonstrations, but returns `8` instead of
Racket's `0` at query cell `(6,9)`. It fits all four canonical pairs as well.
The [baseline report](checks/teaching-before/teaching_report.json) and
[exact counterexample](checks/teaching-before/hard__production__sequential_double_swap__first_failure.json)
retain hashes and labels. Final source checks found zero consequential failures
in 300 production lessons / 1,200 rotations and a separate 60-window /
240-rotation fixed-seed census; the latter contains only 50 unique inputs.
[Final random summary](checks/lesson-census.summary.json);
[fixed-seed summary](checks/schedule-census.summary.json).
Full reports are retained as [lesson-census.json.gz](checks/lesson-census.json.gz)
and [schedule-census.json.gz](checks/schedule-census.json.gz), with original
path/size/SHA mappings and `checks/restore_evidence.py` for lossless restoration.

**Affected shared paths and proposed fix.** Build on
`repo/src/arcpuzzles/worker.py:lesson_check`,
`repo/shared/tools/lesson_census.py`, and the export boundary in
`repo/src/arcpuzzles/datasets.py`. The worker already scores declared rivals and
rejects unsupported automatic lessons; it can still return `not_declared`, and
explicit demonstration requests retain diagnostics. Require a source-bound
decision for the **actual training lesson** at admission: reject a demonstrated
demo-fitting/query-wrong rival, keep missing/error contracts unscored, and bind
the declaration hashes, accepted sample indices, demonstration count, and query
policy into the receipt. Preserve an explicitly marked research route without
treating it as training admission. This recommendation does not claim that the
current shared tools lack rival checking altogether.

**Cost and false-positive control.** Reuse authoritative labels already present
in the lesson, cache pure rival predictions, and stop scoring refuted rivals.
Test rotations as a hard requirement only when the downstream assembler rotates
queries. **A1** confirms 3/3 ordered passes versus 6/15 ambiguous rotations;
rejecting the former because of the latter would apply the wrong policy.
**A2** confirms the finite-inventory limitation: a morphology/parity shortcut
matches 24/24 defaults and 0/4 canonical pairs, and gives a lawful
override query 68 wrong cells despite an accepting hook. It is not a default
query failure. See the two source-bound sections in [AUDIT.md](AUDIT.md).

**Status.** The M1 generator repair and finite rivals are included locally.
**M2** strict controls/domain validation and **M3** formatting-only authority
synchronization are separate included fixes. The two audits remain findings-only
confirmations. A general admission-policy change is proposed here, not applied
to shared production code. No Qwen learning improvement or approval is claimed.
