items.text:
Support recoverable packet subsets and deduplicated completion

**Symptom.** Initial full extraction failed with `ENOSPC` while expanding a large
file inventory; [archive-verification.json](checks/archive-verification.json)
retains that failure. The original ZIP contains **100,447 files totaling
1,651,201,819 bytes** (about 1.65 GB), so file/inode pressure matters alongside
payload size. [Full archive verification](checks/tools/packet_subset/actual-verification.json).

**Proposed fix and retained implementation.** Offer an official, recoverable
subset command based on the selected runtime closure. Journal the immutable
draw seed before extraction, validate every member hash, preserve existing
reviewer edits, and allow already assigned audit targets to be added without
redrawing. The optional implementation and tests are retained under
`checks/tools/packet_subset/`; they are a proposed utility, outside the selected
task patch and shared production runtime.

The real-archive harness verified the complete ZIP, extracted **371 files /
144,965,504 bytes**, reproduced the official pending contract, assignment and
blind selection, and verified an unchanged rerun. **12 synthetic tests passed**,
including interrupted extraction, corrupt journals, unsafe archives, edit
preservation, and deduplicated completion. The caught first compatibility failure
is retained, rather than erased. See
[actual-verification.json](checks/tools/packet_subset/actual-verification.json),
[unit-verification.json](checks/tools/packet_subset/unit-verification.json), and
[actual-verification-first-attempt.json](checks/tools/packet_subset/actual-verification-first-attempt.json).

**Packaging boundary.** A runtime subset cannot directly satisfy this packet's
official return builder, which checks the complete original repository
inventory. The helper therefore offers `complete --deduplicate` before normal
packaging: restore and verify missing originals, preserve existing selected
files, and hardlink only newly restored identical payloads with read-only modes.
Do not hardlink editable selected files to restored reference copies. The
completion dry-run and restoration instructions are retained in
[completion-dry-run.json](checks/tools/packet_subset/completion-dry-run.json) and
[README.md](checks/tools/packet_subset/README.md).

**Limits and decision requested.** The compatibility harness validates selection
and extraction, not generator/Racket execution or completed return packaging.
It does not perform disk/memory preflight or delete user files. Inode savings
from completion do not remove directory costs. Consider adopting this optional
workflow while keeping full final inventory checks and official assignment
semantics intact; the proposed helper is not itself a packaging or approval pass.

items.text:
Keep authority-sync recovery metadata outside the source inventory

The first official package attempt failed on `repo/REVIEW/.lock`. A complete
new-file inventory also found the official authority-sync transaction's receipt
and original authority JSON under `repo/var/review/authority-sync/`. These are
useful recovery artifacts created by the supported synchronization workflow,
but `review_full_return.py:build_full_return` treats them as undeclared source
files. See `checks/package-preflight.console.log` and
`checks/generated-review-metadata/relocation.json`.

The reviewer preserved all three files byte-for-byte under
`checks/generated-review-metadata/`, including the exact original authority
SHA256, then retried the unmodified official builder. No shared source gate was
relaxed. The current return retains the failed attempt and the recovery records.

Proposed shared fix: have the packet's authority-sync workflow place its
transaction receipt/backups under the workspace's `.review/` or `checks/` tree,
and keep its lock outside the source inventory as well. Alternatively, stage
these known generated records into evidence before packaging, without ignoring
arbitrary new repository files. Add one integration check that performs the
supported synchronization and then builds the return. F1 remains the highest
priority change for training-data quality; F3 removes a reproducible handoff
failure in the supported authoring workflow.

The empty lock appeared again after subsequent CLI work and caused one final
packaging retry (`checks/package-final-first-attempt.console.log`). Preserve
these generated records and perform the final cleanup immediately before the
official package command. The reviewer verified that the duplicate lock was
unheld and byte-identical to its retained copy; no source or authority bytes
were changed by this cleanup.

Symptom: the baseline `d185ceed5cc1` sampler passed rule smoke and diversity but had no semantic contract, even though its fixed full-height walls supported an obvious two-chamber shortcut that failed canonical row-local/edge-segment cases. Evidence: `checks/before/result.json` versus `checks/after/checks/d185ceed5cc1_after_semantic_gate.log` and `checks/lesson-census.json`. Suggested change: run a bounded set of pure generic rivals by default and emit a source-bound finding only when one fits every demo and changes a held-out authoritative query.

Symptom: audit target `a3c76f931ce5` accepts `anchor_corner`, `asymmetry_force`, and `palette_size` without changing output, while `palette_kind` sometimes changes hole geometry only because an unused palette shuffle consumes the shared layout RNG; the realized palette remains `[0, 3]`. Suggested change: pair each declared semantic axis with an observation hook or inferred role metric, contrast same-seed outputs, and flag both byte-identical controls and controls whose only effect is on unrelated observed geometry.

Add a large lesson-window rival-survival gate (**highest-priority shared change**)

**Symptom.** Current checks can establish valid individual inputs and frequent witnesses while still admitting an actual training episode whose demonstrations omit the exception needed by its query. Audit target `ff76baf6c2d9` supplies a concrete example: `checks/audit/ff76baf6c2d9/counterexample.json` records an always-preserve rival matching all three demos and failing the query.

**Suggested change.** Extend `generator_semantic_gate.py` (or add a publication-only companion) to assemble at least 100 deterministic lessons per band, iterate the generator's actual `LESSON_COMPETITORS`, and fail when any rival matches every demo yet differs on the query. Store survivor counts, exact sampler formulas, source hashes, and minimized lessons. Keep the present 12-lesson path as a fast smoke check.

Export staged runtime imports to subprocesses launched by task tests

**Symptom.** The reusable tool passed when imported by pytest but failed when its test launched it as a script: the script directory became `sys.path[0]`, so staged `puzzle_generators` was not importable. The retained failure is `checks/tdd-tool-green/result.json`; the task-local workaround inserts the staged root and `shared/runtime` itself.

**Suggested change.** In the task-test runtime wrapper, export `PYTHONPATH=<runtime-root>:<runtime-root>/shared/runtime` (or an equivalent documented environment variable) before invoking pytest. Subprocesses inherited from tests would then see the same portable imports as the parent test process, avoiding per-tool path bootstraps.

Emit periodic stage heartbeats and finalize lock metadata on interrupted batteries

**Symptom.** The first after battery reached defect lint after three completed stages but produced no progress for long enough that the outer execution transport terminated. Its checkpointed evidence is useful, but the live summary retained lock metadata and looked ambiguous until a separate process check. See `checks/after-1/`.

**Suggested change.** Have the battery runner update `progress.log` with stage name, elapsed time, child PID, and last-output timestamp every 10–15 seconds. On wrapper interruption, write an explicit `interrupted` receipt and clear or mark the lock stale. This would distinguish a slow defect scan from a dead process without changing gate semantics.

Report profile drift by linked semantic features, not only morphology marginals

**Symptom.** The baseline distribution gate was green even though it never generated canonical background 4 and encoded the wrong closed/open morphology. Its own log correctly warns that marginals cannot see task-linked drift (`checks/before/checks/7c7f1f574a18_before_dist_gate.log`).

**Suggested change.** Add an optional task-local feature hook returning linked tuples such as `(background, foreground_count, closed_subtypes, open_subtypes, dimensions)`. Compare coverage/support of canonical tuples rather than independent medians alone. Keep this diagnostic unless the task declares the hook, then use it alongside—not instead of—the semantic contract.

Add a preservation-coverage/destructive-rival gate to the semantic tooling

**Priority: highest shared-tool change.**

**Symptom.** A generator can produce only label-correct examples while omitting
an unchanged branch of the authority. In this review, the original
`1a58c96bb078` sampler had 0/900 inputs with a nonzero, non-cyan body cell, so a
“clear the body, then redraw mapped cyan” rival fit all generated support while
failing a canonical preserved color-6 cell. Evidence is retained under
`repo/generators/1a58c96bb078/counterexamples/review-f89bda355e4fdac7-v0001/`.

**Proposed fix.** Extend the semantic checker with an opt-in generic helper that
(a) derives unchanged canonical features or consumes task-declared feature
extractors, (b) executes simple destructive re-render rivals, and (c) requires a
lawful generated refutation for every rival that fits canonical pairs. Allow a
source-bound explicit opt-out for rules that intentionally delete unrelated
content. This would catch support defects before a model ever sees the data.

Make long check wrappers reconcile completed checkpoints after parent interruption

**Symptom.** The baseline battery and one defect-lint invocation outlived their
initial wrapper command windows even though individual stage artifacts were
being written. The aggregate could remain `running` with a live/stale lock until
manually inspected, making it easy to mistake partial evidence for a result.
`checks/before/checks/1a58c96bb078_before_battery_summary.json` is a concrete
retained example: two stages green, lint failed, nine pending, aggregate still
`running`.

**Proposed fix.** Add a heartbeat/status command and make `review.py run` reconcile
completed receipts into the aggregate when its child exits or the parent is
terminated. Content-addressed runtime reuse would also avoid rebuilding the same
isolated environment for repeated unchanged-source stage runs. Never convert an
interrupted aggregate into a pass; instead emit an explicit `interrupted` or
`reconciled-complete` terminal state.

Provide an exhaustive small-period lesson-window helper

**Symptom.** The shared rotation smoke and census hold out each pair from
materialized lessons, but they do not enumerate all cyclic starts of a
task-local short schedule. Authors currently need a custom loop such as
`test_every_four_consecutive_pairs_remain_identifying_under_query_rotation` in
this task.

**Proposed fix.** Add a helper that accepts a declared schedule period, lesson
length, rival set, and query positions, then checks every start residue and
held-out position. Retain the exact first ambiguous lesson. This would be cheap
for periods under roughly 16 and would complement—rather than replace—the wider
production census.

Native qualification distinguishes the declared parameter settings but does not test sampler shortcuts such as a fixed final direction, color-count offset, or uniquely populated ray. The task-local `audit.py` now executes those extra rivals, and its bounded lesson constructor replaces both demonstrations together when a fixed first example would make repair impossible.

Let the semantic gate consume a source-bound schedule enumeration — **highest-priority shared-tool change

**Symptom.** `repo/shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` assigns
`declared_period_not_enumerated` to every positive `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD` and
turns that warning into a failing semantic stage, but the check command has no
way to consume the separate enumeration receipt it recommends.

**Concrete example.** The repair's six-slot curriculum reached 11/12 green in
`checks/after-v2/checks/97f17772dd96_after_battery_summary.json`; the only
remaining issue was this declaration warning. The larger same-source census in
`checks/lesson-census-final.json` covers all six reported start residues in all
three bands and all 1,200 query rotations, but cannot satisfy that gate. The
final task therefore omits an otherwise truthful optional constant and retains
coverage in local tests instead.

**Proposed fix.** Add an explicit `--schedule-enumeration-receipt PATH` to
`arcpuzzles check`/`semantic_gate`. Validate generator, authority, canonical,
period, seed, bands, rotation policy, expected/completed counts, and error-free
status before marking only the fixed-seed schedule obligation satisfied. Reject
stale, partial, wrong-seed, or rotation-failing receipts; do not promote the
receipt to an all-seed or universal-identifiability claim.

items.text:
Include strict seed/sample-index probes in the adversarial audit stage

**Symptom.** The current combined audit runs task tests and the semantic gate,
but both assigned targets accepted booleans, floats, strings, and negative
sample indices. Their generated grids still passed `self_check`, so the defect
is invisible unless a reviewer manually reuses defect-lint logic.

**Concrete example.** Source-bound reports
`checks/audit/6c2353a2cdee/call-contract.json` and
`checks/audit/a338acade0b5/call-contract.json` each record 7/7 invalid scalar
calls accepted. Nevertheless, the first target's 22 task tests and semantic gate
passed, and the second target's 80 task tests passed; its semantic failure was an
unrelated schedule-declaration warning.

**Proposed fix.** Reuse the defect-lint strict-scalar probe as a small default
substage of `arcpuzzles check --stage audit`: literal-int seed, literal
nonnegative-int sample index, boolean rejection, and a malformed difficulty
probe. Keep it source-bound and report it separately from semantic correctness.

Biggest avoidable friction: wrapper-relative probe paths

An optional peer probe initially used `repo/generators/...` and `--root repo`, but payloads already run in `WORK/repo`; it exited 2 before evaluating anything. A task-bound `review.py peer-probe TASK ...` launcher, or a generated runnable probe stub with `--root .`, would remove this repeated path/interpreter guess while preserving the existing same-checkout checks.

items.text:
Biggest avoidable friction: direct pytest and staged task tests expose different import layouts

A normal pytest invocation failed before collection because the extracted checkout does not contain the generated `puzzle_generators.per_puzzle` namespace, while the supported staged task-test runner passed. Add a `python3 review.py task-tests TASK_ID` alias (or print that exact command in `duties`) so reviewers do not mistake a staging mismatch for a source failure.

Allow reviewer-supplied rivals in `lesson-census` (**top shared change**)

**Symptom.** The shared lesson census can score rivals declared inside the selected generator, but an adversarial reviewer cannot inject a one-off rival for an audit target without editing that target or writing an ad hoc scorer. For `b7e4aaffabac`, the useful reproducer was a horizontal-only rule that survived all three demonstrations in 8/128 sampled lessons; the packet's standard census interface could not directly express that audit.

**Evidence.** `checks/audit/b7e4aaffabac/audit_summary.json` and `checks/audit/b7e4aaffabac/horizontal_only_ambiguity.json` contain the source hashes, episode index, and exact survivor. The task-local preflight in `repo/generators/7f31c4f794b2/workspace/component_contract_probe.py` demonstrates the desired scoring shape but is necessarily limited to the selected task.

**Proposed fix.** Add a sandboxed option such as `lesson-census --rival-file checks/rivals.py --rival horizontal_only` (or a small declarative JSON transform DSL). Bind the rival file hash into the report, score it on canonical pairs and production/rotation lessons, and retain the first exact survivor. This would turn audit hypotheses into standard reproducible evidence without modifying immutable audit targets.

Make interrupted battery state and resume instructions explicit

**Symptom.** The first after-battery parent invocation stopped after three completed stages. Checkpoints were valid and `--resume` finished cleanly, but until resume the aggregate state was easy to mistake for a failed or still-running battery, and the progress log contains two starts in one stream.

**Evidence.** `checks/after/progress.log` shows `lint`, `selfcheck`, and `rule_smoke` before the resume marker; `checks/after-resume-console.log` shows hash verification, three source-matched skips, and completion of the other nine stages.

**Proposed fix.** When a supervising wrapper exits without a terminal aggregate, write a small `INTERRUPTED.json` receipt containing completed stages, source/runtime/checkpoint hashes, and the exact safe resume command. On resume, link the old run ID to the new terminal result in a separate field rather than relying on interleaved progress text.

## Task-local changes already included

The selected task now has portable tests plus a deterministic cyclic-lesson probe. Those changes are part of the allowed task delta and do not require a shared-tool decision. No shared checker, packet builder, approval rule, or audit target was modified.

Biggest avoidable friction: focused staged tests cannot select one node

The official staged task-test launcher supplies the required legacy namespace, but it cannot pass through a pytest node ID or `-k` selector; raw pytest then fails before the intended RED assertion. Add a selector passthrough such as `review.py task-tests TASK -- pytest-args...` so TDD can isolate one staged test without leaving the packet runtime.

items.text:
A valid multi-source shape is still a blocking “minimal impostor”

**Symptom:** the final `defect_lint` report has zero issues and one warning, but that warning fails the AFTER battery. It says that `self_check` accepts `short_line` 5/6 and `solid_2x2` 6/6 probes. Evidence: `checks/after-complete-final/checks/ee1c3a11982c_after_defect_lint.log`.

**Task-semantic evidence:** every nonzero pixel is a source under the unchanged Racket rule. A short line and a 2×2 source block inside the zero bottom/right margins are lawful. Their exact inputs, Racket outputs and validator decisions are in `checks/census-final.json` → `question_fixtures.short_line` and `solid_2x2`. The relocated probe independently executes them too. I did not suppress the warning or change the shared checker.

**Suggested change:** support a narrow task-local lawful-minimal-shape hook backed by concrete input witnesses, the active rule hash, and executed reference checks. Keep malformed cases and unknown shapes blocking. Do not accept a free-form blanket waiver. Until such evidence is reviewed, keep this return's aggregate battery status non-green. This is a domain judgment with executable support, not a maintainer-approved exemption.

items.text:
Public AFTER checks stop before revealing the other repairs needed

**Symptom:** `arcpuzzles check ... --battery --phase after` stopped at the fourth stage, so missing override provenance and low canonical-profile support were hidden. The underlying shell battery already supports `--keep-going`, but the public check route used here does not expose it.

**Built mitigation:** `workspace/run_complete_battery.py` stages the standard runtime and invokes the existing shell battery with `--fresh --keep-going`. It preserves nonzero aggregate status and adds a relocated, Python-path-isolated parity probe. Final evidence is `checks/after-complete-final/result.json`; the actual temporary runtime was `/tmp/arcpuzzles-review-full-szs63x5w`.

**Suggested change:** expose a diagnostic keep-going flag in the public CLI, without relaxing strict gate policy. Distinguish “all stages attempted” from “all stages passed” in the result schema and UI.

items.text:
Last-context provenance capture is brittle for a lesson scheduler

**Symptom:** a legitimate seed-only scheduler created its own GenCtx after the per-instance context. The checker then reported omitted provenance for dimensions/counts even though the generation context held those draws. Fixed palette counts were genuinely unrecorded too and were repaired separately. The intermediate override log documents 360 last-context provenance findings; the focused regression captures exactly the context the checker sees.

**Local fix:** construct the schedule context first and record profile-fixed palettes through `draw_int`. Final override results: 190,710 attempts, 180,930 accepted, 9,780 explicit rejections, zero findings.

**Suggested change:** identify the primary per-instance context explicitly, or inspect all captured contexts with seed/index/task identity rather than assuming the last constructed one is the generation context. Keep mismatched observable values as hard errors.

items.reason: Honest lower-bound naming and explicit singleton rejection assessed in this candidate. Declarative applicability/lower-bound axis schema needs a separately versioned checker contract; changing it now would reinterpret existing receipts.
items.text:
Bounds are not exact-value controls, and singleton separation is vacuous

**Symptom:** an integer `seed_separation` declaration was treated as an observable exact distance. The implementation promises a minimum. After renaming it `min_seed_separation`, the pairwise inertness check still reported its behavior on a pinned singleton, where all pairwise lower bounds are vacuously true.

**Local fix:** keep the old spelling as a compatibility alias, declare the minimum honestly, and explicitly reject unsupported nontrivial separation requests with `n_seeds=1` or `single_seed`. This satisfies the existing strict contract without perturbing random output solely to manufacture apparent axis activity.

**Suggested change:** permit declarative axis semantics such as `kind: lower_bound` plus a narrow `not_applicable_when` condition. Require observed constraints on applicable instances; do not require output inequality where the control has no mathematical object to constrain.

**Top shared change — probe malformed scalar types for advertised integer axes

**Symptom.** The override contract can report an exact integer axis as honored while a generator using permissive `GenCtx.draw_int` silently coerces a noninteger request. Audit target `aa14c6a9f111` accepts `grid_h=7.9`, generates a 7-row grid, reports observed `grid_h=7`, passes `self_check`, and produces a valid Racket output. Evidence: `checks/audit/aa14c6a9f111/reproducer.json` and `racket.json`.

**Affected shared paths.** `repo/shared/tools/check_generator_override_contract.py`; migration guidance can point to the existing strict primitive in `repo/shared/runtime/puzzle_generators/base.py` (`draw_int_strict`).

**Suggested change.** For every advertised `type: int` axis, add inexpensive negative probes for `True`, a nonintegral float inside or just beyond the numerical range, and a numeric string. Distinguish a documented legacy-coercion contract from an exact strict-integer contract; make acceptance of those values blocking when exact semantics are declared. Report supplied value and type beside observed value and type. This should be an override-gate improvement rather than a global behavior change to legacy `draw_int`.

The selected repair handles this locally with pre-validation and focused tests; no shared source was changed.

items.text:
Add compact or compressed output for lesson-census reports — top shared-tool request

**Symptom.** A required `lesson-census --per-band 100 --rotate-query` for this 19×19 task produced a 27,997,896-byte JSON report (`checks/lesson-census-final.json` before compression). That single source-bound report exceeded the return builder's 25 MiB expanded-size budget even though the decisive summary was only about 11 KiB.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/lesson-census-final-compression.json` records the original SHA-256 `d9b3817924f469fa205507586658547ff1193c7707b6dde8a7bf29de65332a41`, byte count, deterministic gzip hash, and restoration command. The compressed full report is 804,803 bytes and the useful aggregate is `checks/lesson-census-final-summary.json`.

**Proposed shared fix.** Add `--compact` and/or `--gzip` to `arcpuzzles lesson-census`. Compact mode should retain source/runtime hashes, sampler policy, per-band counts, rival outcomes, every ambiguous/error lesson in full, and hashes/replay coordinates for unambiguous lessons while omitting repeated full grids. Gzip mode should write deterministic `mtime=0` gzip plus a small manifest with original hash and restore command. The return builder could also transparently compress a single oversized JSON evidence file while preserving its hash binding.

Make authority synchronization safe inside a return workspace

**Highest-priority shared-tool suggestion.** The active return contract permits
the selected base JSON, but the introductory guidance describes shared paths as
immutable, and the public `authority-sync --apply` implementation creates recovery
files under `repo/var/review/authority-sync/`, outside the return allowlist.

the exact allowlist, source lines, selected file, old/new hashes, identical reader
tokens, and preserved archival source. We used the public non-applying proposal
and a checked WORK-root patch; native `--apply` was not run. The actual fix is
task-local and already included.

Proposed shared change: give `src/arcpuzzles/authority_sync.py` an explicit
review-workspace mode that emits a WORK-root patch and keeps recovery artifacts
under `WORK/checks/authority/`, while enforcing the existing exact selected-file
allowlist. Explain this narrow exception in `START-HERE.md`. No broader shared
write permission is needed. The included `checks/authority/diagnose_authority.py`
is a concrete reproducible diagnostic; no shared source patch is included.

items.text:
Add stage heartbeat and child-process diagnostics for Racket-backed checks

**Symptom.** Several source-unchanged focused stages stopped producing output or
left incomplete evidence, then passed quickly when retried/resumed. The full
before invocation was externally stopped while its summary still said
`running`; the after battery required several resumptions across Racket-backed
stages. The checkpoint mechanism recovered correctly, but it was difficult to
distinguish a slow rule process, a dead child, and stale lifecycle state.

**Evidence.** `checks/before/progress.log`, `checks/before/result.json`,
`checks/after/progress.log`, and the attempt records under `checks/after/attempts/`.

**Suggested change.** Emit a periodic stage heartbeat with child PID, elapsed
time, last stdout/stderr activity, and active sub-operation. On interruption,
atomically mark the stage interrupted and record cleanup/termination status.
This would preserve the useful resume behavior while making stalls diagnosable
without blind retries.

and 33,855 implicit directories. Extraction exhausted inodes while free bytes
remained; a partial tree then caused import and source-completeness failures.

stdlib unit tests inspect the ZIP central directory and destination filesystem
before extraction. They count implicit directories, estimate block-rounded
bytes, add reserves, and distinguish insufficient capacity from an unassessable
environment. They reject traversal, unsafe aliases/collisions, symlinks, and
unsafe destinations. The tool does not read generator contents or perform a
draw, so it can run before the required blind-solve workflow. Its estimate is
not a quota guarantee; real extraction must still handle errors.

the pre-extraction branch of
`repo/src/arcpuzzles/review_workspace_files/review.py`, before manifest/source
access. Fail with required versus available inodes and bytes, and keep the
archive untouched. The recovery finalizer included with this return shows a

items.text:
Document public rule wrapping's prepared-runtime dependency

**Symptom:** direct repository import of public rule_wrap.wrap_rule cannot
resolve its inherited scripts.comment_solutions parser dependency, producing
six failed prototype tests and one pass.

**Evidence:** `checks/parametric/initial-infrastructure.log`. The local prototype
uses public prepare_runtime/run_process before public RacketBridge/wrap_rule;
final isolated task tests pass without shared-source changes.

**Suggestion:** document that requirement beside the helper or provide a public
batch execution API that provisions it. The delivered prototype is a working
local example; its exporter is a library-layout authoring command, not a new
shared production API.

**Add a default-distribution conditional-alias gate.** The baseline `f6b9f647b109` battery was 12/12 green even though its four default slots covered only 4/16 direction × axis × distance combinations and made direction perfectly predict the other two factors. The override gate proved combinations were constructible, but did not test whether ordinary training data used them. Suggested change: census one declared schedule period (or about 64 deterministic draws), use `observe_overrides` to build pairwise/joint support tables, exclude `INCOMPATIBLE_OVERRIDE_COMBINATIONS`, and flag unexplained functional dependencies or missing constructible cells. For lesson generators, also test whether the query recombines factors instead of duplicating one demonstration's full profile.

**Run selected-task regression tests as a battery stage.** The general battery did not execute `generators/f6b9f647b109/tests/test_generator_f6b9f647b109.py`; the baseline remained all green despite lacking any conditional-support regression. The focused suite caught the defect once the desired schedule contract was encoded. Suggested change: discover and run the selected generator's test file inside the generated task runtime, and include its result in the battery summary. A missing test dependency should be a named stage failure rather than silent omission.

**Expose before/after policy differences in the summary.** The before semantic gate used `require_rival_witness=false`, while the after phase used `true`. Consequently the first after run surfaced four pre-existing unclassified positive branch witnesses even though the generator change did not create them. The strict policy is useful, but attribution is unclear. Suggested change: print a compact policy diff in the battery summary or run the strict configuration as a nonblocking shadow check during `before`, so reviewers can distinguish newly introduced failures from latent contract debt.

**Document the offline editable-install command.** In this packet, `python3 -m pip install -e repo --no-deps` still invoked PEP 517 build isolation and tried to download build dependencies, even though runtime packages were already installed. The reliable offline command was `python3 -m pip install -e repo --no-deps --no-build-isolation`. Add that exact option to `WELCOME.md`, or make the wrapper set up the local import path without an editable install.

**Provide first-class detached/polling support for the battery.** A foreground tool invocation had a shorter execution ceiling than the full battery, so otherwise healthy runs appeared hung or were orphaned before their own stage timeout. Running the documented command under a detached process and polling the evidence directory worked, and the final battery finished in about four minutes. A `--detach` mode that prints a PID, log path, current stage, and a `--poll` command would make long source-bound checks safer and clearer.

**Preserve caller `PYTHONPATH` in `run_with_racket.py`.** The wrapper currently replaces it with `src`. That made ad-hoc authority scripts unable to import `shared/runtime/puzzle_generators` or `shared/tools` even when the caller explicitly set those paths. Prepending `src` to the existing value instead of overwriting it would preserve the protected Racket setup while supporting repository tools and workspace reproducers.

**The override diagnostics were unusually actionable; retain their minimized witness format.** For `cc4d8d3dc442`, the baseline report identified exact cases such as `band=easy seed=0 overrides={'ch_h': 5}` and the unknown-key acceptance, then grouped thousands of repeats under normalized root causes. That directly led to full-domain override handling, unknown-key rejection, and the backtracking regression. A small enhancement would be to include a ready-to-copy one-line reproduction command beside each minimized witness.

**Clarify green Racket-lint stages that still contain style findings.** The final battery marks `racket_lint` green, while its log says `flagged: 1` for `dummy-let-binding`, `generated-helper-name`, and `style-eq-zero`. These are non-blocking style notes, but “flagged” can look like an unreported failure. Label them explicitly as `style advisory` and include `errors: 0, advisories: 3, verdict: pass` in the first line.

**Evidence:** this packet initially produced qualification and causal receipts under version-suffixed top-level directories and had to replay both targets into the canonical per-task layout before packaging.

**Suggested change:** have `review.py duties` emit the canonical final evidence paths as machine-readable data, and make qualification/witness commands warn or refuse noncanonical paths when an active packet contract is present.

The local tests called `generate` with keyword counts, while the native promotion worker calls `generate(seed, settings, demos, queries)` positionally; the first protected preflight therefore failed only at integration, and its wrapper hid the useful worker stdout. items.text:
Add exhaustive curriculum-start support to the shared lesson census **(top shared-tool change)

**Symptom.** `lesson-census --rotate-query` checks every query rotation within materialized lessons, but it does not enumerate every deterministic schedule start. A short-period curriculum can therefore have one bad start that random production materialization misses.

**Concrete evidence.** The selected generator has a five-slot schedule. The required production census covered 300 lessons / 1,200 rotations, while the task-local `workspace/cyclic_lesson_probe.py` separately enumerated all five starts for 25 seeds in four bands/default: 500 windows / 2,000 rotations (`checks/cyclic-lesson-probe.json`).

**Proposed fix.** Extend `arcpuzzles lesson-census` with an opt-in `--all-schedule-starts` mode. When `schedule_profile` and a finite period are exposed, assemble one complete lesson from every start, rotate every allowed query, and iterate the generator's actual `LESSON_COMPETITORS`. Record start, rotation, first ambiguous lesson, and exact source hash. Fall back explicitly to “unknown period” rather than silently claiming schedule coverage.

No shared-code patch is included because this packet permits edits only under the selected generator.

The useful root causes were only a handful: unknown-key acceptance, inert exact axes, missing observations, declared values rejected by bands, and invalid degenerates (`checks/audit/ca5dcbac0e83-override/checks/ca5dcbac0e83_after_override.log`).

Bound compact override evidence without losing root causes

A concrete mitigation is to make the lightweight rule validator also compile/evaluate each form in the same protected Racket frontend (without running task data), so macro-level syntax errors are caught before expensive preflight.

items.text:
Add a shared declared-profile realization gate

**Priority: highest; shared-tool change needed.**

**Symptom.** Current checks can validate labels and even inspect declared schedules without proving that the generated geometry actually realizes the scheduled profile. Audit target `e297c9504f64` schedules `("smallest", "middle", 0)` at seed `1`, sample index `3`, but the selected target is observed at the bottom. In `_choose_tops`, `if i == 0` shadows `elif i == below_index` when `below_index == 0`. The input is an ordinary sampler output, passes `self_check`, and has a valid Racket label, so correctness-oriented checks do not expose the curriculum drift.

**Evidence.** `checks/audit/e297c9504f64/profile_mismatch.json` contains the exact input, source/rule hashes, scheduled tuple, observed tops/sizes, Racket output, and a frequency census. Among 600 scheduled-middle draws per band, mismatches were 239 (`None`/easy), 224 (medium), and 242 (hard).

**Proposed fix.** Extend the generator contract with an optional `observe_profile(grid)` or reuse `observe_overrides(grid)`, then add a source-bound gate that compares `schedule_profile(seed, accepted_sample_index, difficulty)` with the observed profile on ordinary production draws. Record a minimal mismatch with seed, accepted index, requested/scheduled value, observed value, validator result, and source hashes. This should be blocking only when a task explicitly declares that the schedule is exact; otherwise it can remain advisory.

No additional shared-tool feedback was strong enough to prioritize over F1.

Isolate battery stages so one child cannot deadlock the full run

**Symptom.** The exact after-battery command passed lint, self-check, and rule smoke, then stalled immediately after announcing `defect_lint`. It remained stuck until an external 4,200-second timeout. The same `defect_lint` stage completed independently in 10 seconds, and every other stage also passed independently from generator hash `f41ab65c...`.

**Evidence.** [`checks/after-battery-console.log`](checks/after-battery-console.log), [`checks/after-battery-timeout.json`](checks/after-battery-timeout.json), and the twelve `checks/after-*/result.json` receipts.

**Suggested change.** Spawn every battery stage in a fresh process group with a stage-local timeout, close inherited Racket bridge descriptors, and kill/reap the whole group before starting the next stage. Emit a heartbeat containing stage name, PID, elapsed time, and last output timestamp. A stuck stage should become an `interrupted` receipt while later independent stages remain resumable.

Persist stage receipts incrementally during `--battery`

**Symptom.** When the combined process was externally terminated, the requested `--out` directory did not contain a complete structured result for the already-finished stages. The only durable combined-run evidence was captured console text, so I had to rerun stages individually to obtain hash-bound receipts.

**Evidence.** [`checks/after-battery-timeout.json`](checks/after-battery-timeout.json) records the missing terminal result; [`checks/01bb2cbe1309_final_verification_summary.json`](checks/01bb2cbe1309_final_verification_summary.json) indexes the independently retained replacements.

**Suggested change.** Write each stage result and update the battery summary atomically as soon as that stage exits, rather than primarily at parent-process completion. Add a top-level `parent_interrupted` record on signal/timeout. This makes partial batteries auditable and avoids expensive reruns.

Add automatic structural-alias discovery to the semantic gate

**Symptom.** Declared witnesses work well when the author anticipates the shortcut, as in repaired task `01bb2cbe1309`. They do not catch undeclared equivalents. items.text:
Guard irreversible solve finish after an execution error

The post-repair solve checker recorded `execution_status: error`, 0/7 visible,
with the traceback in `solve/attempts/0001/execution.json`. `finish` nevertheless
accepted a stopping reason claiming the rule matched all visible examples, and
froze the episode. The mismatch was human error, but the tool had exact evidence
to prevent it.

Proposed fix in `src/arcpuzzles/review_solve.py`: when the latest report is
`bad` because execution errored or timed out, require either another revision or

Make repeated `RacketBridge` shutdown/startup reliably terminate

**Symptom.** In one Python process, five independent bridge constructions
started, evaluated, and closed, but the sixth stalled before its startup
handshake; even an outer timeout did not return control to `review.py run`
before the 90-second command budget expired. A single caller-owned bridge
completed eight consecutive evaluations and exited normally.

`checks/tooling/racket-bridge-lifecycle/summary.json` binds the two scripts and
receipts. `repeated.stdout.txt` ends at `start 6` after five `closed` rows;
`reused.stdout.txt` ends at `done` with exit code 0. The selected task's focused
test also proves `write_evidence` honors an injected bridge rather than silently
starting another runtime.

**Suggested change.** Add a lifecycle regression that constructs and closes at
least eight bridges sequentially in one process under a hard timeout. On
shutdown, explicitly close all pipe descriptors and join stderr/stdout drain
threads before returning; ensure startup failure/timeout also reaps the child and
threads. Until that is fixed, document and expose caller-owned bridge reuse for
batch evaluators, as this task-local prototype now does.

Provide one public, packet-layout-aware Racket authority helper

**Priority: highest shared-tool change.**

**Symptom.** A task-local pytest run from the source packet can import
`puzzle_generators.runner`, but `_load_rule()` searches the materialized runtime
layout (`data/base/...`) while the packet source stores authority under
`shared/data/base/...`. `wrap_rule()` also imports
`scripts.comment_solutions`, while the packet stores that module under
`shared/tools/comment_solutions.py`. The same test passes under the portable
`task_tests` stage because that stage remaps the packet first. The initial direct
oracle failure is retained in
`checks/tdd/green-attempt-1.log` and the final
workaround is in `workspace/reference_probe.py`.

**Suggested change.** Add a supported helper in `reviewer_support`, for example
`apply_packet_rule(task_id, grids, root=find_root(__file__))`, that resolves the
packet's source layout, performs the same rule wrapping as production, and uses
the verified Racket bridge. Task tests should not need private runner functions or
synthetic `scripts` module aliases. Alternatively, make `run_with_racket.py`
export explicit source-root variables consumed by `_load_rule()` and
`rule_wrap.py`.

Make completed battery summaries clear stale lock metadata

**Symptom.** The final all-green summary still records `lock_present: true`,
`pid_alive: true`, and `own_lock: true` because the JSON is written while the
controller process is alive. When read later, those fields look like an active or
interrupted run even though verdict is `all_green` and the command exited 0.
See `checks/final-battery-2/checks/f151fbd31cb2_after_battery_summary.json`.

**Suggested change.** Finalize or rewrite the aggregate after releasing the lock,
or rename the block to `state_at_summary_write` and add an unambiguous
`controller_exit_recorded` field. This would reduce false concern during one-minute
intake.

Suppress terminal-clear noise in noninteractive wrappers

**Symptom.** Single-stage commands end with `TERM environment variable not set`
and emit an ANSI clear sequence after otherwise clean results, for example
`checks/task-tests-command.log` and `checks/lint-2-command.log`.

**Suggested change.** Guard terminal clearing with `sys.stdout.isatty()` and a
nonempty `TERM`, or let `run_with_racket.py` set a no-clear environment flag for
captured review runs.

Distinguish per-input witnesses from assembled-lesson guarantees

**Symptom.** All 12 final battery stages, including semantic_gate, are green,
but 24/60 separately audited three-demo/one-query windows permit at least one
named rival that fits all demonstrations and changes the query output.

**Concrete reproduction.** Task `5ccdbe078da6`, easy, seed 0, demonstration
sample indices 0,1,2 and query index 3 leaves `numeric_ascending` and
`ignore_lines` alive. The complete grids and Racket labels are in
`checks/verified-census.lessons.jsonl`; the summary is in
`checks/verified-census.json` → `lesson_audit`. The final battery summary is
`checks/after-final/checks/5ccdbe078da6_after_battery_summary.json`.

**Suggested change.** Expose separate coverage levels: rule parity, generator
witness support, and assembled-lesson rival separation. When no lesson hook
exists, retain `lesson_identifiability_checked=false` prominently instead of
allowing “semantic green” to be interpreted as lesson identification. The fresh
solve summary already records this distinction; surface it consistently in
training-export receipts as well.

**Built alternative.** Task workspace `lesson_cover.py` implements query-input-
only exact witness cover. `checks/teaching-lessons-final/` demonstrates 30/30
accepted pools with all six rivals refuted by demonstrations. An authorized
shared-pipeline follow-up can adopt this optional selection step without
pretending it is a universal guarantee or default-distribution evaluation.

Include newly added task tests and tools in portable staging

**Symptom.** The inherited runtime file map predates task-local additions.
Copying only its entries does not stage the newly written `tests/test_generator.py`,
`tests/test_lesson_cover.py`, or their task-local lesson-cover dependency.
A source-layout test pass is therefore not sufficient evidence of portable
execution, and adding files alone does not make the old map discover them.

**Concrete evidence.** `workspace/review_probe.py --mode portable-tests`
explicitly stages the selected task workspaces/tests after `prepare_runtime`.
It then invokes pytest from the actual directory
`/tmp/arcpuzzles-review-probe-2xgpbg3a`, not from the source tree. The full argv,
source hashes, runtime manifest hash and **59 passed** output are in
`checks/portable-final.json`. That directory was temporary and has been removed;
its exact observed path is preserved as provenance, not guessed from source depth.

**Suggested change.** Add task-scoped discovery for permitted new tests/tools,
with hashes and destinations in the staging receipt. Preserve traversal/symlink
checks and avoid copying arbitrary untracked shared files. Explicitly distinguish
new task-local tests from the root project's fixed `testpaths=["tests"]` suite.

A timeout test assumes Python startup completes within 0.2 seconds

**Symptom.** The whole repository run had 169 passes and one failure:
`tests/test_review_runtime.py::test_streaming_timeout_retains_progress_and_stops_child`.
Expected stdout was `RUN unfinished\n`; observed stdout was empty. Five isolated
repetitions also failed. Shared runtime and test source were not modified.

**Evidence.** `checks/repository-tests.log`,
`checks/runtime-reproductions.json`, and `checks/runtime-repro-1.log` through
`runtime-repro-5.log` retain every failure. `workspace/runtime_timeout_probe.py`
compares the existing runtime's streaming and nonstreaming paths without
patching it. `checks/runtime-probe-final.json` records actual commands and the
shared runtime SHA-256.

Both ordinary-startup paths were empty at 0.2 seconds; both retained output with
`python -S` at 0.2 seconds and with ordinary Python startup at one second. These
observations support an interpreter-startup sensitivity here, not evidence that
the streaming collector lost bytes already emitted. The exact site hook or
startup component responsible was not diagnosed.

**Suggested change.** Make this stdout-retention test launch a stdlib-only child
with `-S`, or use a readiness handshake before testing a deliberately short
post-startup timeout. Keep a separate test for termination of slow-to-start
children; empty stdout is legitimate when the child never reaches its print.
Do not simply suppress the failed test or claim the repository suite is green.
No shared fix is included because this assignment permits task-local changes only.

The baseline linter correctly identified the missing `RULE_HASH` and metadata-only
axes. The first repaired version's computed AXES enum strings triggered a static
literal warning; replacing them with literal strings resolved it. The final
standalone lint and full battery lint are green. No reproduced false positive
is asserted. Both failed iterations remain in `checks/`.

Provide one shared validator for public generator call arguments

The defect linter correctly found that `42a152269589.generate` accepted
malformed seed, sample-index and difficulty values. Switching all integer
overrides to existing `draw_int_strict` fixed the control layer but left 48

seeds and None difficulty. The linter was useful, not a false alarm. A shared

across generators and avoid repeated boundary code. Its contract should state
that exact integers exclude bool, that seed sign is unrestricted, and that

Top shared change — validate actual exported lesson assembly

**Symptom:** Racket-lawful labels and valid inputs do not guarantee that the
demonstrations distinguish a plausible wrong rule from the intended one. G3
reproduces this on baseline `627260bf308f`, easy seed 0, indices 7–10: the
bounding-box-area rival fits all three demonstrations and differs at 13 query

but before final example grouping/projection and training-row conversion.

disagrees on a query. Store generator/rival/rule hashes, accepted indices and the

Bind transform-code descriptions to executable examples

3 as half-turn and 4 as counterclockwise, while canonical Racket uses 1 as
clockwise, 2 as half-turn, 3 as horizontal reflection and 4 as transpose. An

allow a small executable metadata witness table. Test one asymmetric template
per opcode against the canonical rule and render the human-facing legend from

that prose matches code; a concrete transform witness can. Do not auto-edit the
canonical authority or guess an intended alternate mapping. This is a shared
metadata/documentation design proposal; the audit target remains unchanged.

## Task-local fixes and friction

G1–G3 and T1 are already delivered in the allowed task delta. The existing lint,
override, profile and authority tools were useful and did not need to be weakened
for this repair. The explicit task-test stage is essential because ordinary
root pytest does not discover generator-local tests: 82 task tests and 362
repository tests are separate reported runs.

The public `arcpuzzles check` front end does not forward the semantic script's
explicit rotation-policy flag. `checks/strict-rotations/run.py` uses the public
runtime-preparation API and the shipped script to run that flag without editing
shared sources. The retained command records its real portable cwd. One local
counterexample-reconciliation script initially used a top-level key instead of
the actual nested JSON key; its failed version/log and successful correction
are retained. Neither friction item is evidence of incorrect generator labels.

The replay helper also initially assumed one source-manifest entry per generator;
the portable task-test layout correctly has native and legacy copies. This was
my checker assumption, not a shared-runtime defect. The corrected second fresh
replay verifies both copies and passes all 82 focused tests. The failed first

Persist battery evidence incrementally at the requested output path

**Symptom.** The first foreground full-battery invocation was externally terminated after completed stages because the runner worked in a temporary directory and copied results only at command completion. The already completed lint, self-check, and rule-smoke evidence disappeared; `checks/before-command.log` ends while `defect_lint` was starting. **Suggested change.** Have `arcpuzzles check --battery --out PATH` create its journal, receipts, logs, and partial summary directly under `PATH` after each stage, with an explicit resumable status. **Symptom.** Both random audit targets advertise multi-valued controls that have no effect, yet lint does not flag those specific unused controls. For `c83b187a9e1c`, `palette_kind=warm` and `palette_kind=cool` produced byte-identical grids in 300/300 paired draws. For `24ef0b5ae2e1`, `anchor_corner=false` and `anchor_corner=true` did the same. The override stage can remain the dynamic backstop, but a static warning would identify fake controls quickly and cheaply.

`write_generator_test.py` should create the destination parent directory

**Symptom.** Running the supplied helper for the selected generator failed with `FileNotFoundError` when `generators/1e26763a6f70/tests/` did not already exist. The helper opens the requested destination in exclusive-create mode but does not create its parent. This makes the documented first-test workflow fail on exactly the common case where a generator has no test directory yet. The failed first attempt is recorded in the work history; the resulting task-local suite was then created manually and its red run is retained at `checks/tdd-red.log`.

**Suggested shared change.** In `shared/tools/write_generator_test.py`, immediately before opening the output path, call:

```python
path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
```

Keep exclusive creation for the file itself so accidental overwrites remain impossible. A helper regression test should invoke the command with a missing nested parent and assert that the parent is created, the file is written once, and a second invocation still refuses to overwrite it.

training-admission/export path, evaluate the exact displayed demo/query pairs.

`repo/generators/5c126cb64bf7/workspace/record_command.py` captures subprocess
receipts without a shell and refuses to overwrite an existing receipt prefix.

declarations, and extracts generated refuting examples. It distinguishes an

Biggest avoidable friction: authoring preflight rejects legacy singleton test mappings

`6d095613d305` stores its one canonical test pair as a mapping, while the generic base preflight iterates every split as a list and crashes before qualification. Normalize mapping-valued splits to one-element lists in the shared preflight, reusing the behavior already implemented by `reviewer_support.canonical_pairs`, so future agents do not need a task-local compatibility wrapper.

The native convenience commands still require qualification receipts, while these public creations must honestly retain authoring-preflight status. **Symptom.** The portable task runtime initially failed before executing `4512012999bb` tests because the test used `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl"`; staging changes that parent depth. **Evidence.** Replacing it with `reviewer_support.find_root` plus `canonical_path` made the same native gate pass 32/32. **Suggested change.** Add a packet preflight/static check for fixed-depth canonical ledger paths and emit the exact portable replacement, or auto-generate new tests with `reviewer_support` exclusively.

**Symptom.** A standalone witness replay could import the bridge but could not locate the packet's protected Racket binary until rerun through `review.py run`/`run_with_racket.py`. **Evidence.** The source and witness were unchanged; the wrapper-propagated environment alone resolved it. **Suggested change.** When `RacketBridge` detects a packet runtime but no selected binary, include a one-line executable replay command using the packet wrapper, or expose a small `review.py replay SCRIPT` alias that records the receipt automatically.

**Highest-priority shared-tool suggestion.** A legal-value override matrix can pass while an advertised integer control silently truncates a malformed fractional request. Audit 5d59b75cb58e accepts `side=12.75` as 12, `n_blobs=3.75` as 3, and `blob_size=5.75` as 5, although each supplied value is above its documented numerical upper bound and outside its integer domain. Affected paths: `repo/shared/tools/check_generator_override_contract.py` and the existing `repo/shared/runtime/puzzle_generators/base.py` draw helpers. Add a small separate malformed-request diagnostic for integer axes: booleans, numeric strings, interior fractional values, and fractions just beyond either endpoint. Report exact supplied/observed values and distinguish documented legacy coercion from a declared strict-integer contract. An opt-in strict declaration can make this blocking without silently changing all legacy generators. The existing `draw_int_strict` helper already provides the implementation primitive. Do not globally change `draw_int` as part of this local repair.

`tests/test_archival_reference.py::test_archival_rule_access_matches_measured_historical_pairs[defba1ab4f90]` expects pair hash `8b35cf5d019df0dad8364813e07e7cc53beb0889c77864f66251e5b4b16cfbe0`, but both the repaired checkout and a completely untouched extraction generate `b4ba8572d6971d19c012fe1d9e6c33122ab1c68d440a1a2286729fdc279c13db`. The involved test, generator and canonical file hashes match between copies. Evidence: `checks/repository/triage.json`, `checks/repository-current/pytest.log`, and `checks/repository-original/pytest.log`.

The immediate observation is a pre-existing snapshot mismatch, not proof of a wrong archival rule. Retain generator/rule source hashes alongside each historical pair digest and make the failure identify which bound source changed. A maintainer can then decide whether to preserve an old source fixture or explicitly remeasure a legitimate new sampler. Do not blindly update the digest to suppress the failure. Primitive-name lint warning conflicts with legitimate Python mirrors

**Symptom.** The first repaired generator used a local variable named `objects` in its feature extractor. The standalone lint stage warned that the identifier echoed a Racket primitive, even though the generator deliberately declared a Python `rule_mirror` for parity tests and semantic counterexamples. Evidence: `checks/round1/lint-after-1/checks/cadfb7a1ae72_after_lint.log`.

**Concrete impact.** The warning encouraged renaming an ordinary local noun but did not identify semantic duplication or mismatch. The same battery later checks declared mirror parity, so mirror support is simultaneously useful and superficially suspicious.

**Suggested change.** Scope primitive-name warnings to top-level definitions or clusters strongly resembling copied DSL code. Suppress them inside declared `rule_mirror`, `self_check`, semantic-signature, witness, and rival functions when Racket parity is exercised. Exact mirror-parity testing is a stronger safeguard than penalizing common local names.

Diversity log says “flagged” while the battery records the stage green

**Symptom.** The final diversity log reports `dup-outputs(22%)`, says `1 flagged`, and lists the task among low-diversity offenders, while the fixed battery records the stage as green. Evidence:

- `checks/round2/battery/cadfb7a1ae72_after_diversity.log`
- `checks/round2/battery/cadfb7a1ae72_after_battery_summary.json`

**Concrete impact.** A relation matrix over `{0,1,4,8}` naturally repeats outputs even when all inputs are unique and semantic coverage is strong. The linter already reports a more interpretable absolute measure: 54 distinct outputs over 144 pairs, with no warning.

**Suggested change.** Reserve “flagged” for non-green outcomes. For nonblocking observations use `noted` or an advisory status, include both absolute distinct count and ratio, and allow tasks to declare a finite structured output codomain. This prevents maintainers from mistaking a diagnostic for a failed gate.

Source-layout `rule_wrap` is not directly importable for exact-input parity checks

**Symptom.** The exact counterexample verifier imports `repo/shared/runtime/puzzle_generators/rule_wrap.py`, which imports `scripts.comment_solutions`. In the source checkout the implementation is under `repo/shared/tools/comment_solutions.py`; the `scripts` package name exists only in the prepared runtime layout. The retained verifier must synthesize a `scripts` package alias. Evidence: `checks/round2/verify_counterexamples.py`.

**Concrete impact.** Applying the selected Racket authority to one exact input requires knowledge of private staging layout rather than a stable supported command.

**Suggested change.** Move the parser into a normal importable package shared by source and staged layouts, or make `rule_wrap` use a stable package-relative import. A supported command such as `python -m arcpuzzles apply-rule TASK_ID INPUT_JSON` would be better: reviewers could retain exact Racket counterexamples without bridge/layout workarounds.

The semantic gate audits named rivals individually but not combinations

**Symptom.** The first repair declared and killed three atomic rivals, yet a newly constructed projection shortcut survived many lesson windows. More generally, two individually refuted assumptions can sometimes combine into a rule that still fits a lesson. The final task-local composed auditor enumerated 36 hypotheses, found 30 canonical-fitting rules, and had to test all 29 non-authority alternatives. Evidence:

- `repo/generators/cadfb7a1ae72/workspace/audit_hypotheses.py`
- `checks/round2/hypothesis_audit_500.json`

**Concrete impact.** `lesson_identifiable` and the generic semantic gate can report success for every declared atomic competitor without showing whether combinations of feature representation, order, and branch precedence survive.

**Suggested change.** Add an optional generator hook such as `HYPOTHESIS_FAMILIES` or `composed_competitors()` that returns named finite alternatives or factorized dimensions. The semantic gate could enumerate/filter them against canonical pairs, then report survivor counts per generated lesson. Keep it optional and bounded; the goal is interpretable interaction testing, not unrestricted program synthesis.

items.text:
Canonical-shortcut declarations need independent certification

**Symptom.** A generator can label a rival in `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`, but a later source edit may make that rival stop matching the official examples while the generated-witness checks still pass. The initial round-two auditor lacked this guard; the retained red test demonstrates the gap. Evidence:

- `checks/round2/tdd/tdd_red_audit_certification.log`
- `checks/round2/tdd/tdd_green_audit_certification.log`

**Concrete impact.** Reports can overstate canonical ambiguity and give false confidence that a witness addresses a shortcut actually supported by the source task.

**Suggested change.** In the generic semantic gate, independently run every declared canonical shortcut against every canonical input/output pair. Treat a mismatch as stale metadata and fail or clearly advise. The final task-local auditor implements this behavior and reports `all_canonical_shortcuts_fit=true`.

Make the solve-packet subprocess fixture self-contained

Symptom: the full public suite returns 165 passed / 1 failed. The failing test
is `tests/test_review_solve.py::test_duties_solve_preparation_runs_from_packet_root`;
the isolated rerun fails identically. Evidence: `checks/project_pytest.log`,
`checks/project_pytest_isolated.log`, `checks/shared_test_isolation.json`.
The miniature `library` fixture omits `src/arcpuzzles`, so a packet built from
it cannot import the API after `run_process` strips PYTHONPATH. The selected
generator is not part of that fixture; source hashes match the original packet.

Proposed fix: the CLI/subprocess packet fixture should stage the actual API
source into the fake library (or construct a complete packaged fixture) before
calling build_full_packet. Keep subprocess isolation. Do not weaken the
assertion or silently mark the test skipped. The real uploaded full packet's
solve preparation succeeds; distinguish incomplete-fixture tests from missing
API code in a production packet. No out-of-scope shared patch is included here.

Provide an official portable task-test entrypoint

Symptom: runtime-native task tests import `puzzle_generators.per_puzzle` and
`scripts`, whereas a library checkout has `shared/runtime` and `shared/tools`.
A direct pytest call failed collection for audit a16cf9241d71; using
`prepare_runtime` and copying the test into that layout produced 8/8 passes.
Evidence: `checks/audit_a16_tests.log` and
`checks/audit_a16_portable/result.json`.

Built local remedy: `workspace/run_portable_tests.py`, added by the patch.
Proposed upstream change: support `arcpuzzles test TASK_ID` with a staged task
and task-local tests, explicit cwd/runtime manifest, and normal pytest failure
propagation. Avoid advising manual sys.path guessing. Root pytest currently
does not discover task-local tests; require their commands separately.

Treat unknown axes and lawful-fixture migration as explicit contracts

Main-task R2 is repaired. The audit of db95939a5dd0 reproduced both silent typo
acceptance (15/15 calls) and lawful fixtures carrying negative metadata (four
current-linter warnings). See A2/A3 in AUDIT.md and the source-bound audit JSON.

Proposed fix: reject unknown keys at the shared caller boundary, while keeping
per-generator validation. Separate negative fixtures from lawful edge cases
in the API; retain the explicit exemption for older generators during migration.
A fixed negative fixture is not automatically an ordinary training example.
Do not mutate or relabel a working rule merely to silence a metadata warning.
For the selected main task, diagnostic palettes remain a documented follow-up:
only size controls are meaningful for fixed negative fixtures; an upstream
fixture-specific signature should reject irrelevant knobs consistently.

Measure rival survival and unique inputs, not only query disagreement

A no-op lesson-identifiability result can look healthy when both training and
query draws follow the same shortcut. Before this repair, all four tested
rivals survived 1,500/1,500 three-demo windows; none was wrong on the baseline
queries because those queries lacked contrasts too. After the repair, each
survives 0/1,500 windows. The local distribution probe reports both metrics.
Evidence: `checks/probe_before/report.json` and
`checks/probe_final_v2/report.json`.

Proposed change: report unrefuted-rival counts alongside fits-demos-but-wrong-
on-query counts, and distinguish overlapping windows from independent lessons.
Deduplicate by content across bands: this repair has 788 unique inputs out of
800 per band but only 1,586 globally unique inputs out of 2,400. A single
within-band number hides intentional cross-band anchor reuse. None of these
metrics substitutes for training a model and measuring held-out performance.

**Suggested change:** Put `--gzip` directly into the required large-census example, show how its compressed path or manifest feeds `--schedule-census`, and point readers to the existing restoration instructions. The automatic member bundle does not alone solve the expanded-byte limit, so mention both limits next to that example. This is a documentation/discoverability improvement, not a request to reimplement working compression support.

The public override checker caught the scheduled-path provenance omission, and the task-test preflight caught an editable selected-task portability defect. Those checks worked as intended; both failures and repairs are retained. No new blanket gate or frozen-file workaround is requested for them.

Highest-priority shared change — per-lesson shortcut refutation coverage

**Symptom.** A declared rival can agree with every demonstration and the query,
so a lesson is classified as non-ambiguous even though it never teaches the
operation separating that shortcut from the intended rule. Global witness
frequency does not imply that every complete lesson contains a witness.

**Concrete evidence.** The old 23a0c42b8a1c sampler always puts the target above
the marker; its first-neighbor shortcut can survive complete ordinary lessons.
The exact archived source and fresh legacy reproduction are under
`checks/baseline-source/` and `checks/legacy-shortcut/`. The a2d296c74658 audit
also gives a real three-demo/query failure for a missing cap-at-two rival in
`checks/audit/a2d296c74658/reproduced-lesson.json`. Candidate discovery and
per-lesson coverage are distinct gaps; the latter cannot compensate for an
undeclared candidate.

**Proposed fix.** Extend the existing semantic gate / lesson-census reporting
under `repo/shared/tools/` and `repo/shared/runtime/review_diagnostics.py`
with an opt-in curriculum requirement: a known nonequivalent canonical
shortcut needs a reference-validated refuting demonstration in every lesson;
arbitrary query rotation needs redundant refuting pairs. Preserve separate
statuses for ambiguity, absent teaching evidence, equivalent restricted
support, missing declarations, incomplete input and scoring error.

**Included concrete proposal.** `checks/tooling/shortcut_coverage/` contains a
standalone passive implementation and tests. It reads existing JSON/gzip
censuses, checks exact source identities, discovers declarations rather than
hardcoding names, and scores saved reference labels. It does not modify locked
shared tools or admit training data. Integrating this optional diagnostic is
the one shared-tool decision I would prioritize. See `QUESTION_ANSWER.md` for
the false-positive case and cheapest efficacy test.

Biggest avoidable friction: release evidence commands are not safely rerunnable
Receipt-backed commands and `parametric qualify` fail when their prior receipt/output path exists, but the surfaced error is often only the path; add an explicit hash-guarded `--replace`/refresh mode and an actionable “output already exists” diagnostic so exact-source release sweeps do not require manual evidence deletion.

Exhaust small exact-axis products in the shared override gate

**Priority: top shared-tool change.**

Symptom: `shared/tools/check_generator_override_contract.py` checks a useful
boundary matrix, but a compact finite surface can be proven completely at very
low cost. The baseline `d349f4dfe492` advertised `n_seeds=1..5` while its
band-specific `draw_int` ranges admitted only 2, 2–3, or 3. A sampled matrix can
also miss higher-order incompatibilities among otherwise valid individual
values.

Concrete evidence: `checks/contract-probe-v2.json` enumerates all 2,880
`(grid_h, grid_w, n_seeds, band)` combinations for the final source with zero
failures. The baseline mismatch is visible in the frozen source; the retained
before lint also shows the broader problem of an untrustworthy axis surface in
`checks/before/checks/d349f4dfe492_before_lint.log`.

Proposed fix: when the parsed finite Cartesian product is below a configurable
budget (10,000 is sufficient here), enumerate it completely in
`shared/tools/check_generator_override_contract.py`. For each unlisted tuple,
require successful generation and exact `observe_overrides`; for each declared
incompatibility, require a clear rejection. Above the budget, keep the current
boundary/pairwise matrix. Save the first failing tuple, seed, band, observed
values, and generator hash.

Let tasks provide semantic evidence for lawful minimal shapes

Symptom: `shared/tools/generator_defect_lint.py` raised
`selfcheck-minimal-impostor` for a centered one-seed grid, even though the
selected transformation is semantically defined for that grid. The warning was
reasonable because no canonical pair demonstrates the singleton domain, but the
only current resolution was to narrow the task grammar so all one-seed lessons
are border-clipping lessons.

Concrete evidence: the retained warning is in
`checks/focused-contracts/defect_lint/checks/d349f4dfe492_after_defect_lint.log`;
the clean rerun after narrowing is in
`checks/defect-lint-rerun/checks/d349f4dfe492_after_defect_lint.log`.

Proposed fix: support an optional task-local `LAWFUL_MINIMAL_CASES` or
`minimal_case_evidence(grid)` hook. The linter should still synthesize its
minimal probes, but may accept a shape only when the hook names the semantic
case and the task's `rule_mirror` produces a non-identity, source-bound output.
This preserves the warning's value while avoiding unnecessary domain
restriction when the author can supply executable evidence.

Automatically exhaust short declared lesson schedules under query rotation

**Priority: highest shared-tool change.** Affected tooling: the semantic-gate integration around `repo/src/arcpuzzles/lesson_census.py` and the `arcpuzzles check --stage semantic_gate` path.

**Symptom.** Correct labels and an ordered lesson sample can pass while the complete lesson is still underdetermined. In the intermediate `105b239cb812` source SHA `1f3602a67e8c48c22ba483003516b95b018923e4eb012d1ae1801283cdbe48b8`, the ordered 12-lesson assessment reported all lessons identifiable, but the rotation diagnostic found 6 ambiguous rotations out of 36: `reverse_pair` fit all remaining demonstrations and changed the held-out query. Evidence: `checks/semantic-gate-v1/checks/105b239cb812_after_semantic_gate.json` and the compact task counterexample.

**Suggested change.** When `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD` is declared and reasonably small, let the after/audit semantic gate automatically enumerate every cyclic start at a pinned seed across bands and hold out every pair once. Fail only when rotations are explicitly required; otherwise retain a diagnostic. For larger periods, cap and sample while stating incomplete coverage. Report lesson, pair, unique-input, rotation, rival, and source-hash counts in the main stage receipt so reviewers do not need a separate manual census to discover deterministic bad windows.

Add per-stage heartbeat and interruption provenance to the battery controller

**Symptom.** `checks/after-v2/result.json` ended with status `interrupted` while transitioning into `defect_lint`; the stage log was empty, so the receipt cannot distinguish a stalled worker, buffered output, parent timeout, or external interruption. The exact standalone defect-lint command later passed on the same final source (`checks/final-defect-lint/result.json`).

**Suggested change.** Before spawning each stage, atomically record stage name, command, start time, child PID, and source/checkpoint hashes. Update a low-frequency heartbeat and, on interruption, record whether the parent or child received the signal plus the last completed subprobe. Keep stdout unbuffered or write an initial stage banner. This would make `--resume` and reviewer diagnosis evidence-based rather than requiring duplicate standalone runs.

Make compact override reports compact by root cause, not only by case rows

**Symptom.** The audit command used `--compact-results`, yet `checks/audit/9e204e7ff3a2-override/checks/9e204e7ff3a2_audit_override_results.json` is about 7.5 MiB because it retains 10,363 individual findings even after omitting most case-result rows. That single report consumes a large fraction of the 25 MiB return budget.

**Suggested change.** In compact mode, retain one minimized witness and a small bounded sample per root-cause signature, plus exact counts, hashes, replay recipes, and an optional external/full shard reference. Keep every unique category and explicit rejection total, but do not repeat thousands of equivalent findings in the primary JSON.

Defect-lint needs lawful-canonical mutation dispositions

**Symptom.** Any two-color multicolor witness containing canonical identity color
3 or 8 necessarily causes either the modal-background or minimum-foreground
monochrome mutation to become a lawful canonical identity input. A correct
`self_check` must accept that mutation, so the generic defect linter pressures the
generator to avoid a useful counterexample.

`checks/task-tests-minimal-collapse-*` and `checks/after/`. The task-local repair
had to restrict 3/8 witnesses to counts 3..5 and carefully control non-modal
colors.

**Proposed fix.** In `repo/shared/tools/generator_defect_lint.py`, let a task
provide machine-readable dispositions for mutation classes that land on known
lawful canonical inputs. Verify the disposition through the selected Racket rule
and canonical/input hash instead of treating acceptance as an unconditional
validator failure.

Portable task tests are collected twice

**Symptom.** The selected file defines 10 test functions, but the task-test stage
reports 20 because it collects both
`generators.7a37505e7bd0.tests.test_generator_7a37505e7bd0` and
`tests.test_generator_7a37505e7bd0`. The doubled count can make review summaries
look stronger than the underlying unique suite.

**Evidence.** `checks/task-tests-final/checks/task_tests.xml` lists each test name
once under each module path.

**Proposed fix.** Adjust the task-test staging/collection logic in
`repo/src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py` to expose one canonical test root, or report both
`unique_test_definitions` and `collected_executions` in `result.json`.

Highest priority — let `package_return.py` emit the exact patch before final packaging

**Symptom.** The required fresh-extraction handoff check needs the exact final
`patches/source.patch`, but the only supported way to obtain it is to build a
provisional return ZIP, extract the patch, replay it, update `RESULTS.json`, and
then build a second ZIP. That makes the verification workflow circular and easy
to get wrong.

**Concrete example.** This return must replay the selected-task delta in a clean
Git root after all tests and counterexamples are final. The patch is generated
inside `review_full_return.build_full_return`, not exposed separately.

**Suggested shared change.** Add `python3 package_return.py --emit-patch PATH` or
`--dry-run-manifest DIR`. It should run the same path allowlist/baseline logic and
write exactly the patch bytes that a later package call will embed, without
requiring all final report fields. The final package should report and verify the
same patch SHA-256.

Gate terminal clearing on an interactive TTY

**Symptom.** Wrapper commands repeatedly print `TERM environment variable not
set` and may surface a nonzero outer-tool status even when the underlying command
and recorded `.exit` file are zero.

**Concrete example.** `run_with_racket.py` task tests and `arcpuzzles apply` in
this packet completed successfully but ended with the terminal-clear warning in
captured non-interactive logs.

**Suggested shared change.** Only clear the terminal when both `sys.stdout.isatty()`
and `TERM` are set; never let cosmetic clearing affect the command exit status.

additional shared production-code patch is bundled.
