Biggest avoidable friction: task-test output paths are interpreted from `WORK/repo`

A packet-root-looking `--out WORK/checks/...` created an accidental `repo/WORK/checks/...` tree before preflight caught it. Reject `WORK/`-prefixed output arguments at the task-test boundary, or accept/document packet-root paths and normalize them to `../checks/...`.

The baseline semantic gate was fully green—5/5 witnesses, 5/5 rival claims,
12/12 lessons—while a simple corpus-visible rival still matched every canonical
pair and 600/600 sampled generations. The gate can only test rivals a generator
already declares. Add optional generic rival probes that perturb one
precondition at a time, especially global versus line-local multiplicity,
object order, object size, and fixed-position assumptions. A useful report
would say which input features are invariant across both canonical and sampled
generated data, then propose or run small counterfactuals that preserve all
other conditions.

`python -m arcpuzzles check ... --battery --out ...` buffers the battery’s
stdout and creates the requested output directory only after the temporary run
finishes. When an outer execution cap kills the wrapper, the visible destination
is empty even though source-bound stage receipts exist in an internal temporary
directory. The underlying battery already documents detached/poll and resume
modes; expose that progress through the wrapper by printing the temporary path,
streaming stage lines, or copying receipts incrementally to a persistent output
staging directory.

The generic mutation-sensitivity report includes color-swap mutations even
for color-permutation-invariant rules. This task correctly accepts all nine
sampled color swaps, so the report shows `swap_two_colors 0/9` despite a healthy
checker. Mark mutations as expected-lawful when the task declares color
permutation invariance, or separate “semantic-preserving controls” from
“destructive mutations” in the summary.

semantic teaching gaps, but a clean line is still easy to overread. Include a
machine-readable `coverage_scope` field such as
`morphology_marginals_only` and cross-link any semantic invariant census. In
this review the morphology gate stayed clean before and after, while the actual
repair was entirely about rule identifiability.

Surface production and rotation verdicts as separate CLI exit policies

**Symptom/example.** `lesson-census --rotate-query` correctly reports `production_status=no_ambiguity_found` and `rotation_status=ambiguous`, but exits 1 under the default required-rotation policy. For an intentionally ordered curriculum, the useful production result can be mistaken for a total failure unless the JSON is inspected.

**Suggested change.** Require an explicit `--rotation-policy require|diagnostic` whenever `--rotate-query` is supplied, print both verdicts in the final one-line status, and include a named `production_exit_status` / `rotation_exit_status` in the companion. This preserves strict behavior while making ordered-curriculum evidence harder to misreport.

(runtime isolation) Make task-local protected-Racket tests purge ambient checkout modules automatically

A staged test initially mixed the packet checkout with an already imported `arc_repl` / `puzzle_generators` installation, and `_real_evaluator` correctly rejected the mixed source set. The task test had to remove those modules from `sys.modules` before importing the packet runtime. The standard task-test fixture should perform this isolation centrally so authors do not need bespoke purge logic and a green test cannot depend on ambient import order.

(authoring evidence) Add a native command that emits causal and first-turn evidence from a passed public preflight

Public creation preflight produces the exact source binding and protected execution receipt, but every author must separately recreate the same witness schema, protected replay, public-view permutation, hidden-field mutation checks, and positive control. A command such as `review_public_creation evidence TASK --preflight ... --out ...` could consume adapter hooks (`dependency`, `intermediate`, `counterfactual_program`, `public_view`, `presentation_order`) and emit the package-ready causal and export reports using the same validators as owner admission.

(generator geometry) Add a reusable component-separation assertion for constructive ARC samplers

The marker-to-line sampler initially placed a border anchor adjacent to a source body, silently merging them under four-connectivity. A small helper that checks intended object partitions, border-anchor singleton status, and minimum blank separation after construction would catch this common sampler bug before semantic tests or protected execution.

items.text:
Explain memory pressure without silently relaxing resource guards

The first disk extraction failed on capacity. The original tmpfs preflight then
blocked on strict `memory.max - memory.current`, despite substantial ordinary
file cache and reclaimable slab. Evidence is retained in
`checks/tooling/original-guard-block.json` and `extraction-recovery.json`.
A subsequent independent, bounded extraction verified all 59,878 files while
retaining the original reserve; this is not a guarantee of future capacity.

The optional standard-library tool `checks/tooling/cache_memory_report.py`
reports strict cgroup headroom, ordinary cache excluding shmem, reclaimable
slab, host caps, ancestor limits, OOM counters and filesystem capacity. An
illustrative 50% discount is labelled advisory. It does not extract, reclaim,
change limits, override the existing guard or certify available memory. Eight
fixture tests and a live report are included; the root reviewer independently
reran the eight tests successfully.

Consider adding this decomposition to the shared preflight's diagnostics so
future agents can make an informed capacity decision and retain the evidence.
No shared resource/controller code is patched in this task delta. The final
handoff runner also checks that the original archive, saved patch and running
system interpreter survive cleanup of its own reconstructible work copies.

Finalize externally interrupted check receipts instead of leaving `status: running` — highest priority shared change

**Symptom.** The first standalone defect-lint wrapper was externally interrupted.
Its durable receipt at `checks/dev-defect_lint/result.json` still says
`status: "running"`, and its lock remains, even though no process is alive. A
fresh rerun under `checks/dev-defect-lint-complete/` completed normally.

**Why it matters.** A maintainer or automation reading only the structured result
cannot distinguish a live run from a stale interrupted run without inspecting
PIDs and timestamps. This also complicates honest preservation of failed or
interrupted evidence.

**Proposed shared fix.** In the check wrapper/controller, install signal and
`atexit` handlers that atomically rewrite the receipt to `interrupted`, record
`exit_code`/signal and the last started stage, and release or mark the lock.
On startup, detect a dead lock PID and convert a stale `running` receipt to
`interrupted_stale_lock` before deciding whether to resume.

Emit a compact override evidence artifact by default

**Symptom.** The successful final override report
`checks/after/checks/3ef9eae12446_after_override_results.json` is over 300 KiB,
although the decisive result is 11,160 accepted draws, 124 cases, and zero
findings. The battery summary already carries the useful aggregate, but exact
case evidence and the aggregate are not split.

**Proposed shared fix.** Have the override gate always write a small summary JSON
with counts, root causes, boundary witnesses, source hash, and case matrix hash;
put per-draw observations in a separate optional detail file. This preserves
replayability while reducing routine return size and maintainer scan time.

Report deterministic schedule coverage directly in the semantic gate

**Symptom.** This repair needed a task-local test to prove that all six cyclic
starts of a small schedule keep a shortcut witness after any query rotation.
The public semantic smoke test and larger census sample many lessons, but neither
turns a declared short period into an exhaustive cyclic-start proof by default.

**Proposed shared fix.** When a generator declares `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD` and a
small deterministic schedule, add an opt-in semantic-gate mode that enumerates
all starts and all held-out positions. Report each start residue, surviving
rivals, and refuting demo indices. This would make the strongest curriculum
claim compact and deterministic while retaining the large census as a separate
sampling check.

Compact override evidence should be the default — **top shared suggestion

**Symptom.** The baseline override stage produced a 55.7 MB JSON report containing
roughly 94,000 repetitive findings, although a handful of minimized root causes
(`grid_h`, `grid_w`, dead metadata/provenance, unknown-key acceptance) explained the
failure. This alone exceeded the return ZIP's 25 MiB expanded-size budget.

**Concrete example.** The source report was
`checks/before/checks/60a8a9d74a75_before_override_results.json`; its hash and the
minimized roots are preserved in `checks/baseline-override-failure-compact.json`.

**Suggested change.** Make `arcpuzzles check --stage override` write a compact main
report by default: aggregate counts, all root causes, one minimized witness per
signature, and a SHA-256 for optional sharded row data. Add an explicit
`--full-rows` switch for exhaustive debugging. This would preserve decisive evidence
while keeping normal review returns within budget.

Lesson census should emit a small signed summary sidecar

**Symptom.** The required 100-lessons-per-band rotation census is valuable but its
single source-bound JSON is about 16 MB because it embeds every materialized lesson,
rotation, and runtime record. Maintainer intake usually needs only the aggregate
verdict, source hashes, sampler policy, rival list, and exact failing instances.

**Concrete example.** `checks/lesson-census-final.json` is the full report;
`checks/lesson-census-final-summary.json` is the manually derived compact view.

**Suggested change.** Have `lesson-census` automatically emit
`<out>.summary.json`, containing aggregate counts and the SHA-256 of the full report,
while retaining full lesson rows in a companion shard or evidence bundle. Successful
returns could cite both; failures would additionally embed only ambiguous/error
instances in the summary.

Add an audit helper for generated-input/authority mismatches

**Symptom.** Audit target `399643e39cf6` validated translation bounds using the
unsorted order in which two identical markers were drawn, while the authority sorted
the markers before deriving the vector. An ordinary validator-clean sample then
produced a clipped copy. Finding this required a custom scan and manual assembly of
input, generator intent, Racket receipt, and coordinate deltas.

**Suggested change.** Add a public `arcpuzzles audit-sample` helper that accepts task,
seed, sample index, difficulty, and overrides; materializes the input, runs
`self_check`, invokes the selected authority, and emits one compact JSON receipt with
source/rule hashes and optional task-declared output invariants. It would not infer
semantics globally, but it would make deterministic audit findings cheaper and more
uniform to reproduce.

Both the initial selected-task run and ticket `ticket-375a562001cf8afb` stopped before tests because the default Python lacked `pytest`; make setup report its exact interpreter and preflight NumPy/Pillow/pytest, then print a relocatable command to use one configured interpreter for wrapper and payload. items.text:
Add a manifest-bound ZIP verification and capacity report — top shared-tool request

**Affected entry points:** outer `review.py verify`, packet extraction guidance
in `START-HERE.md`, and the full-packet builder/manifest contract.

The packet has 75,893 files, 1,079,070,494 expanded bytes and approximately
48,797 required directories. Normal extraction exhausted inodes before the
assignment could be completed. The supplied directions explicitly say there is
no capacity preflight. Even file-content hardlink deduplication has a lower
bound around 106,840 inodes because of directory count and distinct hashes.
The standard builder later requires every immutable source file to exist, so
selective extraction is not a complete return workflow.

**Built optional tool:**
`checks/reviewer-tools/packet-verifier/verify_packet_zip.py` is a standalone,
standard-library, read-only streaming verifier with a JSON receipt and optional
trusted-manifest SHA-256. It checks canonical manifest encoding, exact inventory,
path safety, duplicate entries, content hashes, CRCs, actual expanded sizes and
complete DEFLATE termination. It does not import packet code, draw an assignment,
extract files, mutate the source archive or bypass the original builder.
The complete suite passes 20 test methods / 37 fixture scenarios. The final
15.305-second original-archive run verified all 75,890 manifest files plus both
outer entry files. Its code SHA-256 is
`30921e7af1419ffceb2065f25abae38b0a23dde1c7cd806248b385ff826a3f7d`.

Independent review reproduced a subtle first-version bug: ZipExtFile can stop
at a forged shorter uncompressed size and hide extra decoded bytes. The final
implementation decodes the full compressed extent and checks actual termination,
length and CRC. Four stored/deflated source/manifest regressions cover this,
along with malformed UTF-8 filenames. Their initial failures are retained.

**Requested integration:** offer the read-only verification route before
extraction and report both bytes and inode lower bounds. Consider a supported
manifest-bound selective materialization or verified immutable deduplication
workflow for constrained environments; its packager must still validate the
complete original identity. The optional tool is transported as evidence, not
silently patched into shared infrastructure. See its README, verification_runs,
issued_packet_verification and review_resolution files plus `checks/recovery/`.

This complements F1 by making the state legible even before resume.

The pinned audit replay failed before evaluation because its expected output directory did not exist, and the API probe initially assumed an optional `RULE_HASH`; retained probes should `mkdir -p` their scoped output and read optional metadata defensively (or from the pinned manifest) so bounded reviews fail only on the behavior being tested.

Both assigned homes used `tests/test_family.py`. Running the two suites together with pytest's default import mode caused a collection-time module-name collision even though each suite passed independently. `pytest --import-mode=importlib` produced the intended combined run (**60 passed**). Fix return-patch generation for missing final newlines — top shared change

**Affected path:** `repo/src/arcpuzzles/review_full_return.py`, function `_diff`.
**Status:** optional tested patch supplied; shared source remains unchanged in
this task's allowed delta.

The return builder joins `difflib.unified_diff` records directly. When an old
or new file lacks its final newline, removed and added lines can run together,
and the required Git `\ No newline at end of file` markers are absent. The
minimal before/after bytes `b"old"` and `b"new"` produce a patch ending in
`-old+new`; real `git apply --check` rejects it as corrupt. In addition, Python
`splitlines` recognizes text separators other than LF, which can make diff
line counts disagree with Git's records.

`checks/tooling-eof/regression.py` extracts the actual `_text` and `_diff`
functions from the selected shared module, generates each fixture's patch,
runs actual Git checking and application, and compares the resulting bytes.
The original implementation passes **5/20** fixtures and fails **15/20**;
the scratch-patched implementation passes **20/20**. Cases include newline
addition/removal, unterminated context, file creation/truncation, LF and CRLF,
and embedded carriage returns and Unicode separators. Retained JSON includes
the exact bytes, patch, commands, exit statuses and source hashes per case.

**Proposed fix:** use LF-delimited text records and emit the standard EOF marker
after every unterminated diff record. The small patch is
`checks/tooling-eof/optional-shared.patch`; application instructions and exact
regression commands are in that directory's `findings.md` and `commands.json`.
Its paths are relative to the repository root, whereas the task delta is
relative to the packet root. Apply and integrate this optional patch separately.

inert single-value axes. Defect lint correctly identified the ignored helpful

tests and reusable lesson probe belong to this task's source delta and do not

**Affected shared tool:** `repo/shared/tools/generator_defect_lint.py`,
the `selfcheck-power` and `selfcheck-minimal-impostor` diagnostics.

Do not add a blanket allowlist for all small grids, discard the generic test,

**Suggested change.** Make the wrapper’s process exit code mirror the retained stage exit where practical, or add explicit `wrapper_exit_code` and `payload_exit_code` fields. Avoid terminal-control calls when `TERM` is absent or output is noninteractive.

items.text:
Aggregate repetitive strict-scalar lint findings

**Symptom.** The baseline defect lint produced many near-duplicate warnings for the same root cause—coercing integer controls—making the actionable defect harder to see.

**Suggested change.** Group observations by control and coercion class, show one representative value per class, and provide a compact count plus the recommended strict helper. Keep the full cases in machine-readable evidence, not the primary diagnostic.

The ordinary focused/preflight path allowed legal `AXES` endpoints to fail when an opposing difficulty band was selected, and it missed a dense 6×6 placement-capacity corner. Add a shared preflight probe that exercises every declared endpoint across difficulty classes plus a small minimum-size/count/redundancy/layout capacity matrix before source qualification.

Battery controller must finalize completed child stages or fail loudly — highest priority

**Symptom:** The aggregate `arcpuzzles check --battery` run repeatedly stopped at the `defect_lint` handoff, left a stale/incomplete lock/summary, and did not return control before the outer execution limit. The same final source passed `defect_lint` and all other stages through isolated public `--stage` invocations. Evidence: `checks/after/result.json`, `checks/repository/aggregate-battery-stdout.log`, `checks/after-defect-lint/`, and the other completed `checks/after-*` results.

**Suggested change:** In `scripts/run_generator_battery.sh` and its controller, close inherited stdout/stderr descriptors for stage grandchildren, record the direct child PID/exit receipt atomically, and add a transition watchdog that emits the current process tree and marks the stage interrupted instead of leaving a live/stale lock. A completed receipt should be reconciled before waiting on any pipe reader.

Run Racket-heavy repository tests in isolated processes

**Symptom:** Repository-wide pytest runs stalled after a small prefix (25–77 tests) even when the next test passed in 3–4 seconds by itself. The same behavior occurred with the archival file excluded. The unrelated `defba1ab4f90` identity assertion was separately reproducible in an untouched packet, but it does not explain the later process stall. Evidence: `checks/repository/repository-pytest.log`, `checks/repository/repository-pytest-without-archival-file.log`, and the single-test logs.

**Suggested change:** Add a maintained test runner that executes Racket-bridge test files in fresh subprocesses, closes bridge processes after each file, and writes a machine-readable per-file result ledger. This would distinguish a real test failure from a leaked bridge or inherited descriptor without requiring reviewers to split the suite manually.

Surface same-source unresolved audits during assignment intake

**Symptom:** Audit target `9adaf46a8128` already had a same-source unresolved, concrete marker-4 teaching defect in its review index. The required audit still needed a fresh reproduction, which was useful, but the existing finding was easy to miss without manually opening the index.

**Suggested change:** When audit targets are drawn, print any unresolved audit whose `source_sha256` matches the current generator and label it as a lead requiring independent reproduction. This preserves independent verification while reducing duplicate discovery time.

Cross-check parsed axis domains against runtime exclusions during lint

**Symptom.** The baseline linter passed even though `AXES['left_color']['valid']` and `AXES['right_color']['valid']` said `1..9`, while generation rejected color 5 because it is reserved for the divider. The mismatch appeared only in the much more expensive override stage as 180 failures across 32,940 draws (`checks/before/checks/1ce259f214c8_before_override.log`).

**Suggested change.** For finite color domains, have lint or a cheap contract preflight enumerate each declared value once and compare acceptance with documented exclusions. At minimum, surface a lint warning when `draw_color(... exclude={...})` statically excludes a value still present in a parseable `valid` range. This would catch a contract lie before the full matrix.

Detect canonical-only spatial shortcuts even when generic semantic hooks pass

**Symptom.** The baseline semantic gate passed because every ordinary draw contained overlap, left-only, and right-only cells, yet all five canonical outputs had empty borders. The rival “XOR, then zero the complete output border” fit 5/5 canonical pairs and survived both demos in 51–74 of 300 sampled lessons per band (`checks/custom/before_shortcut_probe.json`). The baseline gate lacked a declared rival and therefore could not turn the ambiguity into a failure.

**Suggested change.** Add a generic canonical-ambiguity heuristic for invariant empty margins or active bounding boxes: when all canonical outputs have a zero perimeter, test a candidate that applies the authority only inside the canonical active bounding box. Alternatively, require a generator with spatially degenerate canonical outputs to declare `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` explicitly. A warning with an executable counterexample would have made this defect immediately actionable.

Provide one canonical whole-workspace pytest entry point for prepared runtimes

**Symptom.** The task-focused suite passes 12/12, but bare `pytest -q` is not a meaningful global verification in either prepared layout. The task-only runtime has eight collection errors because unrelated generic `gen1`/`gen3` modules are omitted (`checks/custom/runtime_full_pytest.log`). The full prepared workspace has duplicate top-level `test_generator.py` module collisions plus tests that assume source-tree paths such as `/mnt/generators` or a root `generator.py` (`checks/custom/full_workspace_pytest.log`).

**Suggested change.** Ship a documented workspace test command that selects only tests valid for the prepared manifest, or package per-puzzle tests with unique module names / package `__init__.py` files and use `--import-mode=importlib`. Normalize tests to locate sources through runtime metadata instead of hard-coded ancestry or absolute paths. The return protocol should distinguish “selected task suite” from “entire source repository suite” so agents can report both without ambiguity.

(top shared change) Gate actual production episodes against unbound control-value remappings

**Symptom.** The current generic semantic machinery can miss a lesson whose
individual labels are correct but whose demonstrations do not bind the query’s
finite control value. In `checks/audit/5faf9d5e3e6d/comparison.json`, demo keys
`[2,3,4]` leave query key `1` unseen; a one-key remapping rival fits all demos
and differs on the Racket query. The sampled key schedule showed the same
structural risk in 207/360 windows.

**Suggested change.** Extend the lesson materializer/semantic gate with an
optional finite-control extractor and prior declaration. For each materialized
production episode, synthesize the cheapest value-remapping rivals from observed
operations, score them on demos, and fail if one survives and changes a labelled
query. Implement this in the shared lesson/semantic checker rather than separately
in each generator; record the exact episode, missing value, rival mapping, and
source hashes. This is also my answer to `qwen9-data-value`.

items.text:
Make issued per-task tests resolve packet roots portably

Symptom: the frozen `generators/0bd65c18b34c/tests/test_generator_0bd65c18b34c.py` computes its canonical-data path from a fixed `__file__.parents[...]` depth. In the relocated `task_tests` runtime this points beneath the selected task, so collection stops before generator assertions run.

Evidence: `checks/main-repair/task-tests-after-v3-command.log` records the exact missing path and the staged runtime's recommended helpers. The new tests in this return use `reviewer_support.find_root`, `canonical_path`, and `canonical_pairs` and pass in the same packet environment.

Suggested change: generate or migrate issued task tests to those `reviewer_support` helpers instead of fixed parent-depth traversal. This preserves relocatability without weakening source binding.

Validate future output geometry, not only visible input separation

M1: the old self-check accepted every one of 600 sampled inputs, although actual
Racket execution showed 129 intersecting stamp layouts and 37 overwritten
markers (`checks/before_census.json`, seed 101, indices 0–199, three bands).
Add optional task-specific output-footprint/postcondition hooks to structural
checks. Do not universally require input preservation: destructive transforms
can be intentional. The delivered `workspace/review_probe.py` is a working,
Racket-backed implementation for this family and retains minimal reproducer
coordinates and full grids. The repaired validator and regression fixtures now
reject the relevant invalid clean-stamping layouts.

Add declared predicate-boundary coverage to semantic admission

A2: a strict-threshold rival matches 600/600 draws but fails all five canonical
pairs. There are no region areas 8 or 24 in the sampled stream. Finite registered
rivals alone did not encode this comparison-boundary risk. Add integer-neighbor
coverage for declared predicates, respecting domain exclusions. The implemented
`workspace/predicate_boundary_gate.py` flags the audited data and binds its
report to the source census. See `checks/boundary_gate_b28619e32f6f.json` and
`QUESTION_ANSWER.md` for false positives and the cheap replay. This is not an
automatic arbitrary-program predicate extractor.

Report cross-band uniqueness, not only per-band draw diversity

M4: the first repair passed its 12-stage battery, but shared canonical-mixture
randomness yielded only 782 unique inputs among 1,200 draws
(`checks/final_census.json`, intermediate source `c6a26dd5...`, seed 101,
indices 0–399, three bands). Add a combined difficulty-band deduplication census
with canonicalized grid hashes and source identity. The retained counterexample
regression failed at 124/180 unique inputs before the layout RNG key was salted
by normalized difficulty. Final census: 1,200/1,200 unique. Repetition can be an
intentional curriculum choice; always report it and do not count repeated grids
as new training support.

Keep canonical rejection distinct from random-generation validity

A1: all 600 generated inputs pass the `988bc6e81731` validator, but canonical
pair 2 is rejected because it has five symmetric components, while the authority
uses the first matching component. The existing profile-floor machinery is a
useful place to surface this; this audit did not establish that the target's
whole battery is green. Carry per-canonical-pair validator outcomes and authority
matches into intake so a restricted generator cannot silently redefine the task.
See `checks/audits/988bc6e81731.counterexample.json`.

Separate interpreter startup from streaming-timeout behavior in tests

H1: `test_streaming_timeout_retains_progress_and_stops_child` fails in both whole
suite runs and in isolation. It assumes a new Python process can print within
0.2 seconds. The diagnostic records first output at 0.419 seconds with a
1-second budget, and about 0.006 seconds under `python -S`. The runtime retains
that output correctly and terminates the child when it actually prints before
the budget expires. This points to environment startup rather than dropped
already-emitted bytes. Use `-S` for this stdlib-only child or explicitly
synchronize child readiness in the test. Do not relax production timeouts to
hide the issue. Delivered reproducer: `workspace/timeout_probe.py`; evidence:
`checks/timeout_diagnostic.json`. The shared test remains red in this return.

Avoid seed/index aliasing across documented schedule periods

H2: the override matrix uses seeds 0–29 and `sample_index=17*seed+3`. For a
profile `(seed+sample_index)%3`, this is always zero. Thus even 44,910 accepted
override draws fail to vary that profile-dependent branch. Explicit
`anchor_kind` overrides can still vary corners; they do not vary the aliased
profile. Evidence: `checks/override_schedule_alias.json` and the inherited
checker loop. Stratify each declared schedule residue independently of seed and
include profile coverage in the matrix receipt. The delivered task-local test
now checks all three residues for 4,050 crossed boundary tuples; the shared
sampler was left unchanged.

Highest priority — check rival survival under the actual lesson assembler

**Shared change requested:** expose a retained, source-bound lesson-coverage mode
through `shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` and the public check/export path.
The existing 12-lesson battery is useful smoke coverage; it is not a substitute
for testing schedule starts, exact override combinations and any filtering used
by the final training-data assembler. Read the actual `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` and
`LESSON_COMPETITORS` declarations and report both demo survivors and
query-changing survivors. Keep unique-input counts separate from overlapping
windows, deduplicate reference calls, and retain minimal failing lessons.
Distinguish missing rival-separating coverage from a demo-fitting rival that
changes the assembled query; the former is a distribution finding, not evidence
that a particular training label is wrong.

**Concrete evidence:** task 5dddd8d6711e's baseline area shortcut agrees with all
three originals and 60/60 distinct generated inputs. The source-bound 8x11
witness in `checks/baseline-shortcut/results/current_witness.json` separates it.
The baseline measurement demonstrates missing separation; it does not reproduce
a query-changing survivor on a baseline-supported lesson.
The new task-local probe checks 900 overlapping windows and records 1,201 unique
generated grids, not 900 independent lessons. All five declared rivals are
refuted; `checks/lesson-probe/report.json` supplies counts and receipts. The
public sampler was independently checked on 36 episodes; see
`checks/code-review/actual-sampler.json`.

**Included task-local implementation:** `workspace/maze_probe.py` and its tests.
No shared source is patched. `QUESTION_ANSWER.md` gives a cheap smoke command and
the false-positive boundary. Counterexamples outside declared support should be
coverage findings rather than mislabeled in-domain generation defects.

Preserve completed temporary evidence when output export collides

**Symptom:** one baseline invocation completed all twelve stages but raised
FileExistsError in `src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py:check` while creating its final
output directory. Only console progress survived; the temporary check tree was
deleted during unwinding. The output had been recreated externally with copies
of an earlier launch-error record. The writer remains unidentified, so this is
not claimed as an intrinsic directory-creation bug. A fresh, noncolliding rerun
succeeded unmodified and retained the complete baseline.

**Reproducer:** `checks/tooling/reproduce_output_collision.py` and its JSON result
show the unmodified function's clean/preexisting/export-time-collision behaviors
using synthetic process/preparation stubs. The distinction between the real
incident and the synthetic reproduction is in
`checks/tooling/runtime-receipt-findings.json`. The initial separate launch error
was caused by this reviewer's logger precreating the requested output directory.

**Proposed shared improvement:** reserve a staging destination or retain the
temporary evidence under a recovery name when export fails, and report that
recovery path. Continue to reject overwrites of existing evidence. Avoid printing
an unconditional successful-collection message when only runtime-local files
exist. No optional patch is included because the original collision's creator
was not established; the failure-preservation behavior is the concrete issue.

Keep conditional rivals visible when marginal modes are already covered

Audit A-0dba-1 on task 0dba62203065 found a conditional rival that fits 3/3 originals
and 300/300 unique generated inputs: use the real header if body row 1 is occupied,
otherwise reconstruct its cycle. This exploits the documented correlation
between body origin and header type. A validator-accepted 8x10 witness separates
it but lies outside the generator's explicitly declared row-2 support.

This is a previously acknowledged coverage boundary, not a newly broken label.
Add conditional combinations to future rival proposals or factor-coverage
reports, and state whether a separating case is generated, merely accepted by
self_check, or only executable by the rule. Exact evidence and qualification are
in `checks/audit/0dba62203065/finding.json` and `AUDIT.md`. No audit target changed.

## Linter feedback

The selected baseline linter's missing RULE_HASH and unprobeable-axis findings
were useful and reproducible. The defect linter also correctly caught the
ambiguous no_doors texture declaration. The final standalone lint and full
battery are clean. No linter false positive is claimed for this task.

**Top shared change — make difficulty part of keyed RNG identity or expose a band-aware helper

**Symptom.** Passing `difficulty` into `gen_ctx` did not make `ctx.draw_rng("...")`
produce band-specific draws. My first repaired version therefore generated
byte-identical easy/medium/hard samples despite forwarding difficulty, and
focused defect lint correctly reported dead bands.

**Concrete example.** The issue arose in `repo/generators/9e80ef661ecc/generator.py`
before explicit `_BAND_COLOR_SHIFTS` were added. The final rationale is recorded
under D10 in `DECISIONS.md`; focused and final defect-lint evidence is under
`checks/focused-defect_lint/` and `checks/after/`.

**Proposed shared fix.** In the `GenCtx` implementation under
`repo/shared/runtime/puzzle_generators/base.py`, either include normalized
difficulty in every keyed draw salt by default or add an explicit
`draw_rng_for_band(label)` / `band_salt()` helper. The API documentation should
state the current behavior. That would prevent a common false assumption while
still allowing generators to opt out of band variation deliberately.

Batch or cache selected-authority outputs across semantic witnesses

**Symptom.** Multiple semantic witnesses that inspect the same generated grids
can trigger repeated Racket applications, making a logically small contract
expensive. I consolidated this task's rival checks into one witness to avoid
redundant calls.

**Concrete example.** `diagnostic_profiles_refute_named_shortcuts` in the final
`generator.py` checks all diagnostic profiles and maps to all named rivals.
Before consolidation, the same profile inputs were being re-evaluated for
several narrow witnesses.

**Proposed fix.** In the semantic-gate runner, memoize authority outputs by
`(rule_hash, input_sha256)` for the duration of a stage, or batch all witness
inputs before invoking Racket. Preserve per-witness attribution in the report.

Mark interrupted battery runs conclusively and clean stale live locks

**Symptom.** An interrupted run can leave a summary showing a live lock/PID and a
stage as running even after the wrapper process is gone. This makes retained
failure evidence look ambiguous and requires a separate clean output directory.

**Concrete example.** `checks/before-interrupted/` and
`checks/before-interrupted-2/` are genuine interrupted setup attempts; the later
completed `checks/before/` run is authoritative.

**Proposed fix.** Have the wrapper install an exit/signal handler that writes an
`interrupted` aggregate verdict and removes or tombstones the lock. On the next
inspection, reconcile dead PIDs automatically and never present them as live.

Embed prior-audit counterexamples instead of only external archive paths

**Symptom.** A task's `evidence/review_index.json` can contain a valuable prior
audit description but point to absolute archive paths unavailable inside the
packet. That record is useful as a lead but not replayable evidence.

**Concrete example.** `repo/generators/1b46e014e17c/evidence/review_index.json`
described the connected-template gap and referenced files under another host
path. I had to reproduce the 1,200-input census and Racket counterexample from
scratch; the fresh evidence is in `checks/audit/1b46e014e17c/`.

**Proposed fix.** When assembling a review packet, copy each current-source
prior audit's compact counterexample JSON and analysis summary into a bounded
`evidence/prior-audits/` area, with source hashes and original return ID. Keep
large logs external, but make the decisive witness self-contained.

**Top shared change — scaffold observable override contracts

**Symptom.** The baseline advertised exact axes but several were read directly through `overrides.get`, narrowed by difficulty, semantically dead, or not recoverable from pixels. The full override checker found 2,797 issues, but authoring the corresponding `observe_overrides` function and exhaustive domain tests was entirely task-local work.

**Concrete example.** `017f1406edaf` easy-band `grid_h=10` was declared legal yet rejected, unknown keys were accepted, and requested decoys could disappear. Evidence: `checks/before/checks/017f1406edaf_before_battery_summary.json` and the 7,050-draw clean replacement in `checks/override-compact-after.json`.

**Suggested change.** Add a generator-authoring helper under `shared/runtime/puzzle_generators/` that defines an axis once (type, legal domain, default weighting, exact draw, observer) and can auto-generate override-contract tests. This would prevent AXES prose, difficulty branches, and observer semantics from drifting apart.

Preserve an explicit intermediate semantic failure summary

**Symptom.** The semantic gate correctly found a two-candidate lower-median defect (2/12 lessons unidentifiable), but a later clean rerun naturally moved the actionable details into a separate evidence directory. Reviewers need to retain and manually cross-link that intermediate report.

**Concrete example.** `checks/focused-after-semantic_gate/checks/017f1406edaf_after_semantic_gate.log` identifies the surviving rival and replay tuples; `checks/red-two-candidate-median.log` is the minimized regression.

**Suggested change.** When a later run turns green, allow the checker to emit a small machine-readable “resolved findings” link that names the prior report, minimized witness, source hashes before/after, and regression evidence. Do not overwrite the failure.

Make aggregate interruption state easier to reconcile

**Symptom.** The first after-battery controller was interrupted while a child stage was active. Its summary correctly remained `running`, but the lock metadata stayed stale until `--resume` reconciled it. The resume worked and all stages completed green, yet distinguishing a live run from an orphan required process inspection.

**Concrete example.** `checks/after-command.log` stops at defect lint; `checks/after-resume-command.log` shows source-bound resume, stage reuse, and completion.

**Suggested change.** Add a `check --status --out ...` command that performs read-only lock/PID reconciliation and prints one of `live`, `orphaned-resumable`, `stale-source`, or `complete`, without starting a new battery.

Add a canonical-data path helper for portable task tests — **top shared-tool change

**Symptom.** The portable `task_tests` stage correctly exposed a recurring path trap in audit target `8c7daa3d3cef`: 16 tests passed, but 2 failed because the test computed a repository root from `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` and then looked for `data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl` under the task directory. The staged runtime actually provides `shared/data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl` and sets `ARCPUZZLES_HOME`. Evidence: `checks/audit/8c7daa3d3cef/task-tests/result.json`.

**Affected shared paths.** `repo/src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py::_task_test_snapshot` and the templates/guidance used to create task-local tests.

**Suggested change.** Add a small public helper such as `arcpuzzles.testing.runtime_root()` / `canonical_path()` that resolves from `ARCPUZZLES_HOME`, and use it in generated examples. Add a lint warning for task tests that derive canonical-data paths from a fixed number of `__file__` parents. The runtime should not duplicate canonical data into arbitrary mistaken locations; the goal is one documented portable path and an easy API.

Expose battery resume through `arcpuzzles check`

**Symptom.** Two healthy full-battery attempts were interrupted by the outer command wrapper after several completed checkpoints (`checks/after-interrupted-outer-timeout/` and `checks/after-interrupted-outer-timeout-2/`). The lower-level shell battery supports checkpointing, but `python -m arcpuzzles check` always invokes `--fresh`; the reviewer must create a new output directory and rerun every stage.

**Affected shared paths.** `repo/src/arcpuzzles/cli.py` and `repo/src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py::check`.

**Suggested change.** Add an explicit `--resume` mode that reuses a named output directory only after validating task ID, phase, source hash, and run manifest. When an interruption is detected, print the exact safe resume command and list completed versus pending stages. Keep `--fresh` as the default so stale evidence cannot silently pass.

Provide a shared production-shaped lesson-census harness

**Symptom.** The small semantic gate is an excellent smoke test, but the assignment correctly requires at least 100 lessons per band when canonical-fitting rivals exist. Each reviewer currently has to write task-local plumbing for the production sampler, persistent Racket bridge, cyclic schedule starts, unique-input accounting, and dynamic rival declarations.

**Task-local mitigation included here.** `repo/generators/a2d8f0cb0fdb/workspace/lesson_probe.py` is a source-bound implementation, with output in `checks/lesson-probe/a2d8f0cb0fdb_lesson_probe.json`.

**Suggested shared change.** Promote the generic portions to a supported command, for example `arcpuzzles check TASK --stage lesson_census --per-band 100 --demos 3`. It should consume `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`, `LESSON_COMPETITORS`, and `SEMANTIC_WITNESSES` dynamically; label through the selected authority; report all cyclic starts when affordable; distinguish unique inputs from overlapping windows; and state that finite rival rejection is not universal induction.

Biggest avoidable friction: sequential example query counts are ambiguous
`write_examples` correctly retains four private controller queries but writes a one-query public first turn while its report says `queries: 4`; make the report distinguish `stored_queries: 4` from `public_queries_per_turn: 1`, and let the public-export helper verify that projection directly.

Biggest avoidable friction: causal witness case selection

The witness template selected a qualified nondefault pair whose source basis made the intended wrong-intermediate ablation observationally identical. Let the template accept an ablation/counterfactual candidate and search qualified pairs for the first protected output-changing case, or emit compact frame/intermediate summaries for each candidate pair.

Biggest avoidable friction: isolated task staging can silently escape to the original checkout

**Symptom:** A task-local prototype that used the repository's generic root finder passed in the working checkout but imported the original packet checkout when run by `review.py task-tests`, because the staged snapshot omitted the canonical ledger used as the root sentinel.

**Evidence:** The first isolated `public_eval_e12f9a14` run failed 17 tests while direct tests passed. Tracing module origins showed the staged adapter loading a generator/runtime outside the stage. Binding the exact adjacent `generator.py` and the runtime under the same staged snapshot made the final isolated runs pass 29/29 and 28/28.

**Suggested change:** Provide a supported `find_task_snapshot_root(__file__)` helper for relocated task tests, or copy the minimal root sentinel into the staged snapshot and assert that every dynamically loaded module remains beneath that snapshot.

Authoring preflight lacks an official one-query public-preview path

**Symptom:** `preview_public.py` accepts native qualification evidence but not source-bound public-creation preflight evidence, forcing reviewers to build a parallel exporter before they can test sequential one-query visibility.

**Evidence:** The reusable `checks/tools/public_creation_exports.py` had to bind the preflight source/program map, emit 32 content-addressed public files, verify hidden-metadata invariance, and reject visible-byte tampering. The packet's independent checker then confirmed the same 32 files.

**Suggested change:** Add an official `preview-public --preflight <preflight.json>` mode that writes one-query views while preserving `owner_accepted=false`, `verification_status=authoring_preflight_not_owner_qualification`, and exact source/content hashes.

Highest priority shared change — validate the emitted episode against declared rivals

**Symptom:** A passing generator battery does not ensure that a caller's actual
demonstration/query selection teaches the distinctions its query labels need.
`repo/src/arcpuzzles/worker.py::_generate_episodes` validates individual
generated inputs and assembles labeled pairs, but does not apply an equivalent
finite-rival check to every emitted lesson.

**Concrete example:** b985d561c63b final source
`c8acb6b749fa8817826507cfa27043773d462b7791fd50f5ffa7716d7107fc1d`,
medium/seed 140000/start 1, one demo and one query. Public generation succeeds;
three actual declared rivals fit the demo and disagree on the query.
`checks/final_probe_final/short_lesson.json` and
`checks/episode_gate/short.json` retain the real labels and counterexamples.

**Proposed shared fix:** After authoritative labeling and final pair selection,
load source-bound rival declarations, keep rivals that match every demo, and
reject/reassemble only when a survivor disagrees on an emitted query.
Record a stable named rejection reason, source hashes and counterexample.
Permit answer-equivalent survivors and an explicit diagnostic mode for
intentionally ambiguous lessons. Do not grant approval from this check.

**Built now:** `workspace/episode_gate.py` in the selected task is an executable
reference implementation, with seven tests and real pass/reject receipts.
It merges actual declarations, verifies source provenance and checks every
query. It consumes retained labels, without claiming to certify them. Shared
integration is not included in the allowed task delta; no unchecked shared
patch is offered. See [QUESTION_ANSWER.md](QUESTION_ANSWER.md).

Add feasible higher-order pin completions to override testing

**Symptom:** A large pairwise control matrix can pass while a feasible tuple
involving more axes is rejected by defaults of an unpinned axis.

**Concrete example:** First repaired source `593540b0…` passed the override
matrix but rejected an extension draw pinned to a 9×9 canvas, 4×4 template and
three targets. Four separated 4×4 slots fit exactly with one-cell gaps, but
the sampler forced positive unpinned surplus. The same issue occurred with
only row surplus or only column surplus pinned zero.
`checks/tight_geometry_before/pytest.log` records three red regressions.

**Included task-local fix:** A fallback searches zero unpinned surplus only
when explicit pins require it; all three tests now pass, with default lesson
ledgers unchanged. Tests are in
`repo/generators/b985d561c63b/tests/test_regression_smoke.py`.

**Proposed shared fix:** Supplement the matrix with a small generator-declared
set of known feasible multi-axis tuples and require successful completion of
the remaining axes. Include boundary cases where packing is exact. A structured
“incompatible” error must not count as success for a declared feasible tuple.
This is a targeted addition, not an exhaustive Cartesian sweep.

Test generated postconditions, especially bounded placement loops

**Symptom:** Returning normally and passing a permissive validator can conceal
partial construction. An attempt limit can prevent an infinite loop while
quietly violating the generated task's object-count contract.

**Concrete example:** Audit 19e8345a8f8e version 2.0.1, default easy draws at
seeds 190 and 881, index 0, return two 2×2 blobs although three are promised.
The validator accepts both. The retained 3,000-draw structural census found
2/1,000 easy failures and zero in the other bands. The real Racket rule still
returns labels, so label-execution success alone does not expose the contract
violation. See `checks/audit/19e8345a8f8e/probe.json` and [AUDIT.md](AUDIT.md).

**Proposed fix:** Require explicit object-count/shape/separation postconditions
after bounded construction. Retry the entire scene or raise a structured
generation rejection when construction is incomplete. Add these small
source-bound seeds to that task's regressions when its repair is assigned.
At shared review time, flag bounded placement loops without completion checks
as inspection leads, with explicit invariant checks as the actual gate.
No audit target edit is included in this return.

## Included handoff improvement

`workspace/replay_return.py` verifies all original manifest files, validates
the delta with the original packet's code, checks and applies the exact patch,
compares the selected source with the solve snapshot and expected hash, and
runs the task tests in a fresh extraction. Its 16 focused tests exercise
path/inventory/patch hazards. It is a reusable task-local tool, not a shared
permission or approval-policy change.

items.text:
Biggest avoidable friction: filesystem file-slot exhaustion before extraction

The first checkpoint had0 available ordinary-user bytes and only21 free file slots before this packet was extracted; the packet has9,997 files, so extraction could not start reliably. Provision a fresh filesystem with at least32,000 free file slots for each review workspace, or offer a task-private temporary filesystem; this run recovered in an isolated768MiB tmpfs without deleting unrelated work, and `checks/storage-observations.jsonl` preserves the measurements with their mount namespaces.

**A successful child receipt can leave the stage launcher alive indefinitely.** The aggregate before command and later per-stage launches sometimes failed to return even though the atomic receipt said `exit: 0` and the battery summary classified the stage green. `defect_lint` completed in about 13 seconds, and `racket_lint` completed in about 2 seconds, but a descendant retained the launcher's output pipe until the outer command cap killed the parent. Suggested change: run each stage in a dedicated process group, close inherited stdout/stderr descriptors in Racket/probe descendants, and have the launcher exit immediately after reconciling a valid receipt. The documented receipt/resume design is good; process-group cleanup should be part of the implementation rather than something reviewers must add externally.

**The semantic tooling does not propose the component-vs-color rival automatically.** The baseline generator transformed connected objects but enforced one unique color per object, making “group by color” indistinguishable from “group by component.” All baseline gates were green because competitors are manually declared. Suggested change: when a rule or mirror iterates connected components, add a generic audit that asks whether generated data ever contains two disconnected components with the same color. If not, report a `component_identity_collapses_to_color_identity` advisory and offer a standard per-color rival helper.

**The generator linter misses exact-axis no-ops in older generators.** During the random audit, task `2c904a701029` accepted undeclared overrides and accepted multiple declared overrides (`palette_size`, `palette_kind`, `density`, and others) while returning byte-identical grids. Suggested change: require every `AXES` label to appear in keyed draw provenance or a declared derived-axis observer, reject unknown overrides by default in `gen_ctx`, and run pairwise “different legal override values must be observably different or explicitly derived” probes.

**A green `racket_lint` stage can still print a flagged rule without a structured advisory in the aggregate summary.** This target reports one `dummy-let-binding` flag while the stage is green. Suggested change: preserve nonblocking findings in the battery summary’s advisory count and link the exact linter finding, so “12 green, 0 advisory” cannot be read as “the linter found nothing.”

**The battery wrapper can remain attached to a completed descendant and fail to return, even after the stage receipt says `exit: 0`.** On task `db4cb6bcf6fe`, the monolithic baseline exceeded the foreground limit, and several per-stage invocations appeared hung after the child had written a complete receipt, `.ok` marker, and final log. The behavior was most visible around Racket-backed stages and authority sync. Redirecting wrapper output and using the source-bound resumable receipts recovered the correct verdict. Suggested change: ensure the Racket bridge and every spawned process close inherited stdout/stderr descriptors before the wrapper waits; have the wrapper poll the receipt/child PID and exit once the recorded child is complete; and print a distinct “child complete, wrapper descriptor still open” diagnostic instead of looking like a test timeout.

**The output-diversity warning needs a more direct finite-codomain remediation hint.** The reviewed generator correctly has only thirteen reachable `4x4` relation matrices. Generic lint initially treated that as suspicious until `EXPECTED_OUTPUT_CODOMAIN = 13` was declared. Suggested change: when fixed-shape output diversity is low, include an actionable message such as “declare and test `EXPECTED_OUTPUT_CODOMAIN` when the task has a mathematically finite output language,” and show the observed count. That would turn a potentially confusing warning into a useful proof obligation earlier.

**Generic diversity and profile checks cannot detect the most important semantic collapse without a declared rival.** The baseline had varied-looking grids and passed ordinary distribution checks, yet all examples were rectangle corners, so raw-marker equality solved the task without closure. The semantic gate found this only after task-local `SEMANTIC_RIVALS`, witnesses, and `lesson_identifiable` were implemented. Suggested change: provide a small reusable “canonical shortcut workbench” that lets reviewers register feature projections (raw cells, bounding box, area, color histogram, component count), reports which projections fit all canonical examples, and searches generated draws for disagreements. The new focused tests in this packet demonstrate the desired interface and can serve as a seed implementation.

**Override reports are valuable but the baseline output is too large to triage efficiently.** This task produced 16,223 findings over 83,340 draws, with thousands of repeated manifestations of a few root causes. The root-cause grouping was useful, but the human-readable log still ended with more than sixteen thousand witness lines. Suggested change: default to one minimized witness per root-cause signature plus category counts, place exhaustive records only in JSON, and add a short top-level distinction among “axis cannot be honored,” “axis not observable,” “unknown key accepted,” and “negative fixture leaked into ordinary domain.”

Smoke-test composed Racket programs before long audits

**Symptom.** A composed alternate embedded the canonical lambda but did not apply it, so Python behavior was green while protected Racket received a procedure where it expected a grid.

**Evidence.** `checks/46b45dd2aff8/audit-command.json` records the failing first protected run; `checks/46b45dd2aff8/audit-command-v3.json` records the passing run after adding a direct protected-Racket regression.

**Suggested change.** The parametric adapter template or qualification preflight should execute every declared setting program on one generated grid before launching a full audit. This would surface composition/type errors immediately and give future agents a minimal source-bound failure.

Make zero-exclusion in Racket `mode` explicit in authoring guidance

**Symptom.** The Python mirror initially treated 0 as an eligible modal background, but the canonical Racket `(mode g)` excludes 0 by default. This produced parity failures only when a generated scene selected background 0.

**Evidence.** `checks/46b45dd2aff8/audit-command-v2.json` retains the failing parity run; `checks/46b45dd2aff8/audit-command-v3.json` and the new sampler regression retain the corrected contract.

**Suggested change.** Add a short authoring warning beside the parametric composition examples: mirrors of `(mode g)` must use the DSL's zero-exclusion semantics unless an explicit color set is supplied.

Bind lesson query policy into training-export validation

**Symptom:** the default semantic battery can pass an ordered lesson while leaving arbitrary query rotations unverified. In the audit of `af72e426e241`, 300/300 ordered lessons were identifiable, but 900/1,500 rotated positions raised coverage-hook warnings even though no named rival survived. Evidence: `checks/audit/af72e426e241/audit-summary.json` and `checks/audit/af72e426e241/required-rotations/`.

**Proposed shared change:** add an explicit `LESSON_QUERY_POLICY = "ordered" | "any_pair"` contract consumed by the lesson exporter and `generator_semantic_gate.py`. Require all rotations for `any_pair`; for `ordered`, report rotation diagnostics but gate the exact exported ordering. This prevents both silent ambiguity and false rejection from applying an undeclared assembly policy.

Provide a safe selected-authority synchronization command

**Symptom:** `9ce2dcf587b8` had canonical and selected active Racket programs that executed equivalently but differed in exact text. Repair required manually replacing only `racket_target.target_code` while preserving archival `raw_code`; a broad JSON rewrite risks touching unrelated provenance.

**Proposed shared change:** add an `arcpuzzles authority-sync --write-selected TASK_ID` command that writes the canonical text only to the selected active target, preserves `raw_code`, records before/after hashes, and refuses to run unless execution parity already passes. The existing authority report supplies all necessary identities.

Make portable-test legacy imports a summarized advisory

**Symptom:** the audit task `af72e426e241` passed 5/5 task tests but emitted a portability warning because its tests import `scripts.canonical_profile_gate.canonical_pairs` instead of `reviewer_support`. The warning appears before pytest output and is easy to miss in a large audit.

**Proposed shared change:** surface legacy runtime imports as a distinct field in the `task_tests` result and offer a small codemod hint to `reviewer_support.find_root` / `canonical_pairs`. Evidence: `checks/audit/af72e426e241/task-tests/result.json` and its log.

Biggest avoidable friction: output paths silently changed coordinate systems
`review.py` announces that payloads run from `WORK/repo`, but an `--out WORK/checks/...` argument was accepted and created the nested path `WORK/repo/WORK/checks/...`. Resolve wrapper output paths packet-relatively, or reject a leading `WORK/` with a message showing the correct `../checks/...` form.

**Top shared-tool change — source-bound lawful-control dispositions for generic defect lint

**Symptom.** `repo/shared/tools/generator_defect_lint.py` blocks this count-only task for accepting singleton, short-line, and solid-2×2 inputs and for accepting generic topology mutations that preserve the sole nonzero color and total count. The final stage has zero errors but two warning categories (`checks/after-final/checks/204eaaff6c24_after_defect_lint.log`), while exact current-authority execution confirms the three named controls are lawful (`checks/lawful-minimal-probe.json`). The only task-local way to make the stage green would be to invent a false topology invariant.

**Suggested change.** Add an explicit, narrow declaration such as `LAWFUL_LINT_CONTROLS`, with each entry naming a detector/control, justification, exact input, expected output, `RULE_HASH`, and optional canonical-program SHA. In strict mode the linter should execute current `self_check` and the selected canonical Racket program, verify the expected output, bind the receipt to generator/rule hashes, and disposition only that exact detector case. Do not permit free-text waivers or suppress unrelated findings. The retained `workspace/lawful_minimal_probe.py` demonstrates the minimal evidence shape but intentionally does not modify the shared linter.

items.text:
Distinguish “not requested” from “pending” in single-stage check summaries

**Symptom.** Running the required `--stage lint` command passes lint, but `checks/lint/result.json` embeds a twelve-stage battery summary with lint green and eleven stages labelled `pending`. A consumer that reads the nested battery summary instead of the top-level `stage=lint, passed=true` can misclassify a successful targeted check as an interrupted battery.

**Suggested change.** Add `selected_stages` and mark unselected stages `not_requested`, or emit a stage-specific summary without the full pending battery matrix. Keep resumable/pending only for stages that were actually requested in a battery run.

Emit progress during semantic/defect probes that invoke repeated Racket checks

**Symptom.** The defect-lint stage can be silent while many subprocess probes run; an interrupted run looked stalled until its command journal was inspected. The final run completed normally, so this is observability rather than correctness.

**Suggested change.** Append periodic case counts and the current detector name to `progress.log` (for example every 10 probes or 5 seconds), without flooding stdout. This would make genuine hangs distinguishable from slow but advancing Racket-backed checks and improve safe checkpoint/resume decisions.

Make lesson/query-rotation policy a first-class gate — highest priority

**Symptom.** Aggregate distribution checks and ordinary lesson order can pass
while a permitted query holdout removes the only counterexample to a shortcut.
The selected baseline passed its semantic smoke yet had 3 warnings in 1,200

wrapper, make the assembly policy explicit: ordered-only, diagnostic rotation,

items.text:
Give weak semantic-witness failures an actionable declaration diagnostic

**Symptom.** The first repaired source had all behavioral stages green, but the
strict semantic stage failed because five predicates were treated as weak
witnesses (`checks/after/result.json`). The useful resolution was not “invent
five rivals”: two predicates were coverage branches and three shared one honest
canonical-only rival. Discovering that distinction required reading the native
semantic report after the aggregate battery stopped at a generic failure.

**Proposed change.** In `repo/shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py`, add an
early declaration table for every witness: classified branch, mapped rivals,
missing mapping, rival callable present, canonical-fit result, and generated
counterexample result. For an unmapped positive predicate, print a concrete
suggestion to place it in `BRANCH_WITNESSES`; for a claimed rival witness,
require and display the exact rival disagreement. This would preserve rigor
while avoiding pressure to manufacture meaningless rivals merely to satisfy the
contract.

Detect advertised-but-inert axes even when their declaration is hard to probe

Clarify snapshot identity in reference-only apply receipts

## Linter / packet feedback

The selected-task linter and defect checks were useful: missing RULE_HASH, dead axes, canonical rejection and transformation drift were real defects, not false alarms. Final lint and defect-lint passed without blocking findings. The source packet has no .git metadata; both attempted git-status commands therefore failed with exit 128 before edits. [TOP SHARED-TOOL CHANGE] Add cyclic query rotation to `lesson_census.py`

**Symptom.** The shared source-bound census evaluates production lesson windows but
explicitly does not rotate every pair into the query. In this task, ordinary
semantic checks passed while a legal rotation still omitted the only same-color
tie demonstration and left `ties_always_blank` alive. The exact failure is
`checks/tdd-red-cyclic-command.log`.

**Suggested change.** Add a `--rotate-query` mode to
`repo/src/arcpuzzles/lesson_census.py`. It should read live
`LESSON_COMPETITORS`, `SEMANTIC_RIVALS`, `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`, and
`SEMANTIC_WITNESSES`; verify each claimed shortcut against all usable canonical
pairs; rotate every pair in each materialized window; and write compact exact
reproducers with generator and input hashes. The task-local
`workspace/cyclic_lesson_probe.py` is a working reference and found the defect
before the final 6,000/6,000 green run.

Make stage wrappers terminate from a completed receipt

**Symptom.** An intermediate standalone `defect_lint` invocation wrote a controller
`result.json` with `status: "running"` and no command-exit file even though the
stage had started and later focused reruns worked. The retained evidence is
`checks/stage-defect_lint-1/` and `checks/stage-defect_lint-1-command.log`. This
forced a separate rerun and makes it hard to distinguish a dead outer controller
from an active child.

**Suggested change.** In `run_with_racket.py` / the check controller, poll the
stage receipt and child PID as well as the outer process. If a terminal receipt is
present, finalize the aggregate result and exit; if the child is gone without a
terminal receipt, record `interrupted` with the last durable stage artifact.

Keep override failures compact by default

**Symptom.** A single audited generator produced more than a megabyte of override
JSON because the same band-clamping root cause was repeated per seed/value. The
human-useful diagnosis was only a handful of normalized root-cause groups and
minimized witnesses.

**Suggested change.** Make the default artifact contain grouped signatures,
counts, one minimized witness, and a small bounded sample per group. Put exhaustive
per-draw rows behind `--full-cases` or in an optional compressed attachment. This
would reduce return size without losing reproducibility.

Surface cross-band profile absence next to pooled support

**Symptom.** Audit target `04204350555e` had pooled support (1 exact and 5 envelope
hits of 60) but zero canonical-profile support in both easy and medium. A pooled
summary alone can look reassuring while two training bands never enter the public
profile.

**Suggested change.** Keep the existing per-band floor as a blocking headline in
battery summaries: print exact/envelope counts for each band before the pooled
count, and emit one minimized generated-vs-canonical profile contrast for every
zero-support band.

Biggest avoidable friction: public reviewer helper bootstrap
A copied task test can use `reviewer_support.find_root`, `canonical_pairs`, and `load_selected_generator` correctly yet still fail collection under plain `pytest` because `shared/runtime` is not initially on `sys.path`; the staged task-test wrapper masks this by supplying its own runtime path. The concrete symptom was `ModuleNotFoundError: reviewer_support` in `checks/portability-red.txt`. Generate a tiny packet-local `conftest.py`/bootstrap alongside reviewer tests, or make the public test scaffold import the helper through an ancestor search before using it.

items.text:
Make interrupted battery status more prominent at command exit

The first after-battery process was terminated by the outer execution wrapper
after several stages had checkpointed. Resume worked correctly, but a partially
written summary can look authoritative unless the reviewer notices `verdict:
incomplete` and pending stages.

Suggested change: on interruption, print one final high-visibility line naming
the summary path, completed/pending counts, source hash, and exact resumable
command. The checkpoint design is good; the discoverability of its state can be
improved.

**Top shared change — finalize a completed stage even when a descendant inherits the controller pipe

**Symptom.** A single-stage override run completed its stage work and wrote all expected receipts, but the public controller remained indefinitely at `status: "running"` with no exit code. The retained controller state is `checks/override-dev2/result.json`; the corresponding override artifacts under `checks/override-dev2/checks/` were complete. A later clean full battery passed the same override stage, so this was wrapper/process-lifecycle behavior rather than a semantic generator failure.

**Likely boundary.** `arcpuzzles check` / the generator-battery controller appears to wait on a stdout/stderr pipe that can remain open in an orphaned descendant after the stage process has produced its terminal receipt.

**Proposed fix.** Treat a source-bound terminal stage receipt plus exited direct child as sufficient to finalize the controller result, while separately reporting leaked descendants. Close inherited controller FDs before spawning grandchildren (or put the stage in its own process group and drain/terminate the group at completion). Add a regression test whose stage spawns a child that inherits stdout, writes a valid terminal receipt, and exits; the wrapper should return a completed result rather than stay `running`.

Make missing witness-to-rival mappings actionable in semantic-gate diagnostics

**Symptom.** The first semantic-contract run had valid firing witnesses and executable rivals but omitted `WITNESS_RIVALS`. The gate failed with repeated generic lines such as `witness left_align ... | no rival claim (WEAK)` in `checks/semantic-dev/result.json` and `checks/semantic-dev/checks/5b4fd0a9c80e_after_semantic_gate.log`. Adding the mapping made the next run green (`checks/semantic-dev2/result.json`).

**Proposed fix.** When witness and rival names exist but no claim mapping is declared, print a direct repair template such as `declare WITNESS_RIVALS = {"left_align": ("left_align",), ...}` and list unmapped witnesses plus unclaimed rivals. Preserve the failure, but turn the message from a policy label into a one-edit authoring instruction.

Biggest avoidable friction: portable task-test and manifest handoff
The inherited `8a802749348c` tests failed only because they guessed repository depth and imported an unavailable legacy helper, while successful staged test receipts then had to be manually compacted into task-local manifest evidence. Scaffold new task tests around `reviewer_support` by default and add a manifest option that ingests a source-bound `task-tests` receipt directly.

Biggest avoidable friction: portable task-test and manifest handoff
The inherited `8a802749348c` tests failed only because they guessed repository
depth and imported an unavailable legacy helper, while successful staged test
receipts then had to be manually compacted into task-local manifest evidence.
Scaffold new task tests around `reviewer_support` by default and add a manifest
option that ingests a source-bound `task-tests` receipt directly.

Receipt wrapper needs a completion heartbeat and child-output preservation
A round-two `review.py run --receipt ... review_base_preflight` invocation for
`02dc25c0440b` produced no terminal output and exceeded the controller timeout,
while the same command run directly through `run_with_racket.py` completed and
passed. Add periodic heartbeat output, preserve the child's partial stdout/stderr
on timeout, and record whether the child exited before receipt finalization. That
would let future reviewers distinguish a slow qualification from a launcher or
receipt-finalization stall without rerunning the full protected-Racket job.

Biggest avoidable friction: dual-language rival semantics
The Python and protected-Racket adversarial banks initially disagreed on stable-sort tie behavior, hiding a real scan-order shortcut. A shared structured rival/comparator specification that emits both implementations and minimizes surviving counterexamples would remove this drift.

**Top shared change — resumable battery orchestration

**Symptom.** The exact required `arcpuzzles check ... --battery` command was
externally interrupted after three completed stages on two attempts. Checkpoints
were preserved, but `repo/src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py` explicitly has no automatic
resume, so I had to invoke all remaining stages independently and manually
reconstruct the aggregate. Evidence: `checks/after-command.log` plus the 13
`checks/final-*-command.log` / `.exit` pairs.

**Suggested change.** Add `--resume-from OUT` (or make `--out` resumable by
default) in `repo/src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py`: validate each existing stage
receipt against the current source/runtime hashes, skip only verified completed
stages, run the rest in canonical order, and write one final aggregate summary.
The aggregate should distinguish `complete-pass`, `complete-fail`, and
`interrupted`, so an interrupted checkpoint directory can never be mistaken for
a finished battery.

Make task-test omission explicit in aggregate output

**Symptom.** The general battery intentionally excludes `task_tests`; those tests
were the only gate that exposed the selected task's non-portable canonical-data
path and incorrect raw-text rule hashing. A green battery alone would not mention
that these tests were never run. Evidence: compressed red/green records listed in
`checks/tdd-failure-compression-map.json`, and the final
`checks/final-task-tests/result.json`.

**Suggested change.** Keep `task_tests` independently runnable, but add either an
`--include-task-tests` switch or an explicit terminal aggregate row
`task_tests: NOT RUN (separate source-bound stage)`. The latter is nearly free
and prevents “all checks passed” from silently meaning “all except the task's own
regressions.” Affected code: `repo/src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py` and CLI help in
`repo/src/arcpuzzles/cli.py`.

Compact and deduplicate lesson-census rival evidence

**Symptom.** The 300-lesson report was 19,195,561 bytes even though two underlying
rival functions appeared through multiple declaration lists, producing repeated
scorer rows. It had to be retained as compressed evidence with a hash/restoration
map (`checks/lesson-census-compression-map.json`).

**Suggested change.** In `repo/shared/tools/lesson_census.py`, deduplicate rivals
by stable callable identity plus behavior hash while retaining all declaration
provenance, and add `--summary-out` or `--summary-only` for routine intake. Keep
full materialized lessons as an optional compressed sidecar when a survivor or
ambiguity is found.

Add canonical role-coverage mutants to the semantic gate — highest priority

**Symptom.** Current gates can certify internally varied lessons while missing a
canonical semantic role that the generator never emits. The two random audits
found this twice: `73500a0803e5` never emits cyan as body data, and
`4614f605ddab` never emits non-green foreground distractors. In each case a wrong
rule fits 900/900 generated inputs and fails a retained Racket-checked witness.
Evidence: `checks/audit/73500a0803e5/counterexample.json` and
`checks/audit/4614f605ddab/counterexample.json`.

**Proposed shared change.** Extend
`repo/shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` (or add a companion detector in
`generator_defect_lint.py`) to compare canonical and generated color/role support,
then test cheap mutants only for missing roles. Require an authority disagreement
before blocking, and allow task-local equivalence/exemption metadata to avoid
palette-normalization false positives. This is the shared-tool change most likely
to improve training data rather than only metadata cleanliness.

Add receipt-based `--resume` for interrupted batteries

**Symptom.** `run_generator_battery.sh` already checkpoints stage receipts, but
the packet instructions state that automatic resume is unavailable. Two full
runs in this review were interrupted by the outer execution envelope after three
completed stages; both had to restart from lint even though their completed
receipts were intact (`checks/after/`, `checks/after-r2/`).

**Proposed fix.** Add `arcpuzzles check --battery --resume --out PATH`, validate
subject hashes and run IDs, then continue only pending/interrupted stages. Never
reuse stale or mismatched receipts. This would preserve the existing conservative
verdict model while avoiding repeated Racket smoke and lint work.

Point finite structured tasks to `EXPECTED_OUTPUT_CODOMAIN`

**Symptom.** Lint correctly warned that 12 and later 18 distinct outputs were a
low ratio, but its message suggested widening unless the task was
“counting/classification.” This task has a structured but genuinely finite
18-polyomino codomain. The supported declaration solved the warning, but the
message did not mention it (`checks/lint-r2/checks/55312177dae6_after_lint.log`).

**Proposed fix.** When low output diversity is the only warning, append:
“for a complete finite structured alphabet, declare and justify
`EXPECTED_OUTPUT_CODOMAIN`.” The gate should continue verifying that the probe
covers the declared count, as it already does.
