items.text:
Semantic gate should consume a completed schedule-period census **(highest-priority shared change)

**Symptom.** The final battery reports `11 green, 1 failed` even though every semantic assertion inside the gate passed: all five canonical inputs, both declared rivals, all 12 sampled lessons, and all 60 query rotations. The only warning is `declared_period_not_enumerated`, which the gate intentionally delegates to a separate command. The required follow-up then completed cleanly at `checks/schedule-census.json` (12/12 fixed-seed cyclic starts, 60/60 rotations, zero ambiguity/errors), but there is no supported way to attach that receipt to the battery result.

**Suggested change.** In `arcpuzzles check` / the semantic-gate aggregator, accept a source-bound `--schedule-census PATH` receipt, or classify the stage as `FOLLOWUP_REQUIRED` rather than failed when all in-gate facts pass and the only unmet item is an external enumeration. Verify task ID, generator/rule hashes, declared period, seed, bands, rotation policy, and completion status before upgrading the result.

Evidence: `checks/after/checks/6be78d0010df_after_semantic_gate.json`, `checks/schedule-census.json`.

Long wrapper runs should finalize cleanly after foreground transport interruption

**Symptom.** The first after-battery foreground invocation lost its transport after three green checkpoints; the child was no longer running, but the aggregate remained `running`. The documented checkpoint/resume path correctly recovered without rerunning completed stages, so no evidence was lost.

**Suggested change.** Have `run_with_racket.py` or the public review wrapper launch long batteries under a durable driver with a heartbeat and an `atexit`/signal finalizer that records `interrupted` when the controlling transport disappears. A small status command that distinguishes “live child,” “stale running receipt,” and “resumable” would also reduce ambiguity.

Evidence: `checks/after-resume-driver/console.log`, `checks/after/progress.log`, `checks/after/result.json`.

items.text:
Audit preset should make portable task-test root failures more prominent

**Symptom.** For `2602c3d31d21`, the audit preset correctly noticed that task-local tests use a fixed `Path(__file__).parents[1]` root and therefore miss canonical data in the portable runtime. The console warning is easy to overlook because the aggregate failure is summarized primarily as a semantic-contract failure.

**Suggested change.** Include a distinct `portable_task_tests` status and the exact offending file/line in the audit summary JSON, even when another audit stage also fails. Offer the standard replacement snippet using `find_root(__file__)`, `canonical_path`, and `canonical_pairs`.

Evidence: `checks/audit/2602c3d31d21/combined-run1-command.log`.

Top shared suggestion — measure canonical component topology independently

Affected tools: `shared/tools/canonical_profile_gate.py` and the optional semantic-review tooling. Baseline70a3d3e2c975 easy/seed6/index2 matches7×9 and4 colors but has a singleton and a polychrome component; every canonical example has two monochrome components. The192-draw probe has4 coarse profile hits and0 topology hits. See `checks/coverage_before/coarse_profile_comparison.json` and the exact sample hash in QUESTION_ANSWER.md.

The selected-task implementation and reusable probe are included. A shared-tool decision remains: add an optional task-specific component-signature support check, independently computed from pixels, per band, with explicit augmentation-only exemptions. Avoid hard-coding this task's two-object signature for other puzzles. This is the one suggestion most worth promoting to shared tooling.

Probe legal scalar overrides across independent seed/index pairs

Affected tool: `shared/tools/check_generator_override_contract.py`. Its fixed seed→index schedule passed an intermediate repair while `generate(2,1,marks=15)` and `generate(2,1,marks=20)` failed from randomly undersized free geometry. Exact counts should constrain free geometry before drawing; rejection should describe a physically impossible supplied tuple, not a bad random choice.

Task-local fixes and eight regressions are included. Retained failures: `checks/scalar-feasibility-before.log` and `checks/scalar-feasibility-intermediate.log`. Suggested shared change: add a small independent seed×index sweep for single-axis extrema and a few capacity-sensitive partial tuples. Report the number of distinct seed/index pairs rather than multiplying identical geometry across difficulty bands into apparent independent coverage.

Give compatibility aliases an explicit metadata contract

Affected tool: `shared/tools/lint_generator.py`, `_check_axis_honesty` alias detection. It tells authors to collapse aliases or document why both names exist, but does not consume alias documentation. In the first repaired source, n_distinct_colors and palette_size were correctly identical, observed, and checked for conflicting requests, yet the warning remained blocking.

The task-local fix is to advertise one independent axis and retain `AXIS_ALIASES={"n_distinct_colors":"palette_size"}` as a separately validated compatibility map, with direct tests for both names. Suggested shared follow-up: support this mapping explicitly and test alias equality/conflicts without pretending it contributes another combinatorial dimension. Do not suppress genuine accidental correlations between independent axes.

Keep generated runtime staging outside source-delta scanning

Affected tool: `src/arcpuzzles/review_full_return.py`. Repository guidance places generated runtime work in ignored var/, but the return builder scans every repo file and rejects newly staged repo/var runtime files as undeclared source. The coverage probe uses public prepare_runtime; a baseline snapshot initially staged under repo/var had to be moved out before packaging.

The delivered task probe uses temporary runtime directories by default. Suggested shared fix: reconcile packager scan exclusions with the documented generated-output locations, while continuing to reject unexpected source edits. No shared packager change is included in this task-limited delta.

Reissued public work can contain a faithful prior build that lacks newer registration/resource requirements; check literal RULE_TASK_ID and isolated-folder canonical loading before expensive replay, preserving valid rule bytes. F2: The previous patch verifier assumed an existing production generator and flat inventory; `checks/verify_return_patch.py` now covers public creation and source_binding inventories with six positive/negative tests.

items.text:
Canonical-shortcut discovery should be a first-class semantic-gate output.
Symptom: the useful after report can verify declared `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`, but the baseline had none, so obvious rectangle-only and palette-only rules were invisible until manual review.  
Suggested change: auto-run a small standard rival library on canonical pairs, print which rules fit all pairs, and require either a generated counterexample, a task-specific rebuttal, or a reviewed narrow-scope waiver.

Portable runtime probes should inherit the verified Racket executable **(highest priority)

**Symptom.** A task-local probe that called `prepare_runtime(...)` and then
`run_process(...)` failed with `RacketUnavailableError` even though the packet's
verified offline Racket runtime had already been installed. Evidence:
`checks/lesson-probe-smoke.log`.

**Concrete example.** The portable child contained the selected runtime and rule
files but did not inherit `RACKET_PATH`. The same probe passed only after being
re-executed through the packet-level `run_with_racket.py` wrapper. The retained
`workspace/lesson_probe.py` now self-bootstraps as a task-local workaround.

**Suggested shared change.** Have `prepare_runtime` write the verified Racket
path into its runtime manifest and let `run_process` propagate that path, or
provide a supported `run_portable_with_racket(...)` helper. This avoids bespoke
re-exec logic and makes source-bound probes reproducible from their documented
command.

Override-contract failures should aggregate repeated cases earlier

**Symptom.** The before override stage reported the useful root causes, but also
materialized tens of thousands of repeated rejected cases; the retained results
file is about 1.1 MiB for one task.

**Concrete example.** `checks/before/checks/ebff81ea3252_before_override.log`
ends with “20972 more findings” and a count of 75,810 legacy multi-axis
rejections, all largely consequences of the same band/domain mismatch.

**Suggested shared change.** Keep exact totals, but retain only a bounded witness
set per `(axis, band, exception signature)` plus a machine-readable aggregate.
This preserves falsifiability while reducing packet size and reviewer noise.

Provide a standard source-bound lesson/rival census command

**Symptom.** The semantic gate's 12-lesson sample is intentionally a smoke check,
while duties require at least 100 lessons per band when canonical-fitting rivals
exist. Every reviewer currently has to build a bespoke probe and may accidentally
copy rival names, miss schedule residues, or use a stale source tree.

**Concrete example.** This review added
`repo/generators/ebff81ea3252/workspace/lesson_probe.py`, which snapshots the
current generator, dynamically reads its rival declarations, checks canonical
fit, uses Racket outputs, records cyclic starts, and counts unique inputs.

**Suggested shared change.** Add an `arcpuzzles lesson-census TASK_ID` command
with `--lessons-per-band`, dynamic declaration discovery, source/runtime hashes,
Racket-backed outputs, schedule-residue coverage, and a standard JSON schema.

items.text:
Promote declared-rival query rotation to a bounded blocking gate — **highest priority

**Affected tools:** `shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py`, `shared/tools/lesson_census.py`, and `shared/tools/run_generator_battery.sh`.

**Symptom.** Individually correct labels can form an underdetermined lesson. The pinned `033db13a9d37` source had a canonical-fitting `last_nonzero_seed` shortcut; a small non-rotated semantic smoke sample was not sufficient to guarantee every three-demo lesson/query position contained a distinguishing witness. Audit target `d68754fb0d84` gives another concrete case: seed 17, easy, indices 4–7 expose only codes 3/4/8 in demonstrations and put unseen codes 2/7 in the query (`checks/audit/d68754fb0d84/counterexample.json`).

**Suggested change.** When `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` or `LESSON_COMPETITORS` is nonempty, add a cheap battery stage that materializes a bounded production sample, reuses Racket labels, rotates each pair through the query slot when permitted, and fails only on a rival that fits every demo and changes the query. Distinguish advisory exit zero from semantic green in the top-level user-facing result

**Symptom.** The baseline `profile_floor` and `semantic_gate` commands exited 0 but logged `ADVISORY` / `NO_CONTRACT`, while `result.json` still has `passed: true` at the wrapper level. The battery summary handles advisory classification correctly, but a reviewer reading only the standalone `result.json` can misstate it as a pass.

**Suggested change.** Add a top-level `verdict` field (`green`, `advisory`, `failed`, `interrupted`) to every stage receipt and reserve `passed: true` for green. Preserve exit-code compatibility if needed.

The defect linter was useful; make source-sync remediation more explicit

**Affected tool:** `shared/tools/lint_generator.py` / defect-lint messaging.

**Symptom.** The linter correctly reported missing `RULE_HASH`, source divergence, weak self-check, texture overlap, and minimal impostors. For source divergence, however, it was not immediately clear whether the expected repair was canonical modification, selected base-target synchronization, or a provenance declaration.

**Suggested change.** Include the compared paths, normalized hashes, and one of three suggested dispositions: exact-sync selected target to canonical, intentionally update canonical with task-scoped evidence, or mark an approved behavior-equivalent archival source separately. The repair here used the first option and retained the previous code as `raw_code`.

items.text:
Add declared-axis effectfulness to the override gate — highest-priority shared change

**Symptom.** A generator can advertise lawful multi-valued axes that are accepted but have no observable effect, overstating data diversity and attaching misleading controls to duplicate examples.

**Concrete evidence.** In audit A2.3, `9eb815d36de7` produces byte-identical grids for `palette_kind=warm|cool` and independently for `texture=warm|cool`; see `checks/audit/9eb815d36de7/probe.json`. The strict override report contains axis-effect findings, but a small explicit liveness contract would make the failure simpler and reusable.

**Suggested change.** In the shared override checker, hold all other inputs fixed and compare two lawful values across 2–3 deterministic recipes. Require a grid delta, correctly recovered metadata, or a declared semantic witness. Allow deliberate aliases only through an explicit annotation with a reason, and retain a minimized identical-output witness on failure. This is the one shared-tool change I would prioritize most.

Run portable test files that pass preflight even when one frozen fixture blocks aggregate collection

**Symptom.** The selected task's aggregate `task_tests` stage stops at preflight because one immutable legacy fixture imports `scripts.*` and guesses a fixed parent depth. The new public-API tests are portable and pass 29/29 directly, but the aggregate receipt cannot show their execution.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/task-tests/result.json` and `checks/task-tests-command.log` show the inherited fixture blocker; `checks/parametric/focused-tests.log` shows the two valid test files passing.

**Suggested change.** Keep the aggregate verdict blocked, but preflight each file independently and still execute files that are portable. Report separate counts such as `portable_passed`, `blocked_preflight`, and `failed`. This preserves the blocker without discarding useful regression evidence from future agents.

items.reason: Retain actionable reviewer feedback/proposed tool with source-bound evidence. No shared implementation or training admission is implied. Exact retained paths: `checks/lesson-census/final.json` `checks/lesson-census/final.summary.json`
items.text:
Emit a compact source-bound lesson-census companion automatically

**Symptom.** The complete selected-task census is 18.5 MB, while normal intake needs only source hashes, invocation, sampler policy, materialized/rotation counts, ambiguity totals, errors, unique inputs, and links to retained witnesses.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/lesson-census/final.json` is the full replay artifact; `checks/lesson-census/final.summary.json` is a manually produced compact companion used in this report.

**Suggested change.** Have `lesson-census` emit `OUT.summary.json` atomically beside the full report, hash-binding it to the full file. Keep the full report for replay and bundle it automatically, while letting reviewers and intake read the companion without parsing megabytes of materialized lessons.

Validate that every declared canonical shortcut actually fits every canonical pair

**Priority:** highest shared-tool change.

**Symptom.** The baseline declared `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS =
dict(SEMANTIC_RIVALS)`, but a retained audit showed that none of those six
functions matched all five labeled canonical pairs. Even so, the baseline
semantic gate and complete 12-stage battery were green. A false declaration can
make downstream lesson evidence look stronger while obscuring the real,
undeclared canonical-fitting shortcut.

**Concrete evidence.**

- `repo/generators/8029363f9cb7/evidence/review_index.json` records the prior
  5-pair evaluation of the false declarations.
- `checks/before/checks/8029363f9cb7_before_semantic_gate.json` and the baseline
  battery summary show the shared gate accepted the contract.
- `repo/generators/8029363f9cb7/tests/test_source_launch_shortcut.py` now includes
  a task-local regression that verifies each canonical shortcut’s actual fit.
- `checks/probes/source-launch-baseline.json` demonstrates the undeclared
  nearest-frame rival that really did fit 5/5 canonical pairs.

**Proposed fix.** In the shared semantic-contract checker, execute each
`CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` callable against every labeled canonical pair using the
same source-bound canonical helper and scoring path used for lesson rivals.
Treat any mismatch or exception as a blocking contract error naming the shortcut
and first failing pair. Separately report semantic rivals that happen to fit all
canonical examples but are absent from `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`; that second check
can begin as an advisory because the semantic-rival set is not necessarily
exhaustive.

This is a shared checker change, not part of the selected task delta.

items.text:
Reconcile completed child-stage evidence when the controller is interrupted

**Priority: highest shared-tool change.**

**Symptom.** The selected task's initial before battery was recorded as interrupted in `checks/before/checks/3dc5b297cfa2_before_battery_summary.json`, even though `checks/before/checks/3dc5b297cfa2_before_lint.log` had already finished and reported 0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0. Similar audit presets reached completed child output before the parent controller was interrupted.

**Suggested change.** Make the controller journal the child exit/result atomically immediately after `waitpid`, before post-processing. On startup or signal handling, reconcile an unjournaled stage by checking the child receipt/log footer, PID liveness, and expected output hashes. Record a distinct state such as `child_complete_controller_uncommitted` instead of losing the stage result or leaving a long-running wrapper with no progress. This would preserve strict evidence semantics while making interruption recovery actionable.

Deduplicate override findings and fail fast on contract-wide dead axes

Keep aggregate counts, but cap detailed findings by axis/value/failure signature and optionally stop the stage after every advertised exact axis has a decisive result. This would make `--full-results` useful without turning obvious dead controls into large serialization and controller-recovery workloads.

items.text:
Automatically synthesize axis-conditioned lesson rivals (top shared change)

**Affected tool:** `shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` and the
`arcpuzzles lesson-census` rival layer.

**Symptom.** The semantic gate is strong once a generator author declares the
right rivals, but a missing contract can let ordinary lessons teach a simple
branch shortcut. The assigned baseline supported only left/above sources, so
`negative_side_only` fit its distribution. Independently, audit target
`cbf77aa253ac` has no lesson rival contract; seed 0/start 0 yields three
horizontal demonstrations and a vertical query, so a `horizontal_only` rival
fits 3/3 demonstrations and changes the query. The latter is canonical-Racket
verified in `checks/audit/cbf77aa253ac/racket_comparison.json`.

**Proposed change.** When `observe_overrides` exposes categorical axes,
automatically generate cheap one-branch rivals: apply the declared oracle only
for `axis == value`, otherwise identity (and the complementary branch). Evaluate
them under every query rotation and retain the first exact lesson when one fits
all demonstrations but changes a Racket-labelled query. Treat missing observable
axes or a rival that never changes any authority output as nonblocking. This
would catch common orientation/side/shape shortcuts without requiring every
reviewer to anticipate and hand-code them.

items.text:
Add a managed detached/checkpoint runner with heartbeat output

**Affected tool:** outer `review.py run` orchestration.

**Symptom.** Staging plus strict lint/task tests can run longer than an invoking
client's shell limit while producing no console heartbeat. One unchanged strict
lint invocation was externally interrupted and retained only an incomplete
checkpoint under `checks/defect-final`; the same source passed when rerun in a
manually detached process under `checks/defect-final-v2`. Full batteries already
checkpoint stages well, but reviewers must hand-roll PID/exit files to keep the
outer process alive safely.

**Proposed change.** Add an optional managed detached mode that prints a run ID,
periodically emits the current stage/progress timestamp, and provides `status`
and `wait` subcommands. It should preserve the existing source/runtime identity
checks and receipts rather than inventing a second resume format.

## Task-local fixes already included

The selected generator itself now has strict scalar validation, truthful axis
ranges, independent cycles, exhaustive small-boundary tests, executable rivals,
and a declared four-position schedule. Those do not require shared-tool changes.

items.text:
Highest priority: auto-enumerate small declared lesson periods

**Symptom.** After the semantic hook itself was correct, the normal semantic
stage returned a warning solely because `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD = 4` had not
been enumerated.  The required after-battery command in `DUTIES.md` does not
include `--enumerate-schedule-period`; the extra requirement appears later in
the return guide.  Evidence:
`checks/semantic-green/checks/71b44cea4ed1_after_semantic_gate.log`.

**Suggested change.** In `arcpuzzles check`, automatically enumerate declared
periods up to a small safe threshold (for example 32) under the strict after/audit
policy, or have the generated DUTIES command include

Keep portable-test path warnings prominent in audit summaries

**Symptom.** `7185b8225f1c`'s selected tests infer the repository root with fixed
`__file__.parents[...]` depth, so the portable audit reports a missing canonical
path before semantic testing.  The detailed warning is excellent, but the final
audit summary principally shows the semantic-contract failure.  Evidence:

the combined audit summary, even when another stage also fails, so maintainers
do not miss an independent test-portability defect.

Highest priority — add a source-bound large-lesson mode to the semantic gate

**Symptom.** The shared semantic gate checks only 12 lessons for this task. That is useful as a smoke test, but it is too small to establish that a deterministic/cyclic curriculum remains identifiable across many lesson starts, and it does not report unique-input counts or source hashes in the task-specific form requested by the review duties.

**Concrete example.** I had to build `repo/generators/ad9405621c3d/workspace/lesson_probe.py`. Its report `checks/ad9405621c3d_lesson_probe.json` checks 100 lessons per band, records the exact sampler and source hashes, counts unique inputs/pairs, checks all profile residues induced by the sampler, and verifies a Racket sample.

**Suggested change.** Extend `arcpuzzles check --stage semantic_gate` with a mode such as `--lessons-per-band 100 --racket-sample 64 --source-bound-report`. It should iterate the generator's actual `LESSON_COMPETITORS`/`CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`, record source/probe hashes, materialization policy, cyclic-start coverage, unique-input counts, per-rival survival, and finite-domain limitations. Keep the current small default for speed.

Add task-local tests as an explicit battery stage

**Symptom.** The general battery does not discover `generators/TASK/tests/`; the duties require a separate command. A return can therefore show “12/12 green” while omitting its most targeted regressions unless the reviewer remembers the extra step.

**Concrete example.** This repair's 86 task-local tests cover exact overrides, unknown controls, every four-demo start residue, canonical-fitting rival behavior, hash-seed determinism, and sampled Racket parity. None are represented by the battery stage count; the separate evidence is `checks/tdd_green_attempt1.stdout.txt` and the final replay log.

**Suggested change.** Add an optional/default `task_tests` battery stage when `generators/TASK/tests/` exists. Prepare the portable runtime with an explicit source-hash mapping, run the directory, and include test count, exit code, copied-file hashes, and skipped tests in the battery summary.

Provide an audit-counterexample evidence helper

**Symptom.** The supported `arcpuzzles apply` command correctly records authority and generator hashes, but reviewers still hand-build the companion file that combines validator status, rival output, disagreement cells, census, commands, and source identity.

**Concrete example.** `checks/audit/dc155169ea57/projection_probe.py` and `projection_probe.json` had to assemble that schema manually around `racket.json`.

**Suggested change.** Add a small command such as `arcpuzzles audit-witness TASK --input ... --rival MODULE:CALLABLE --out ...`. It should call the public apply path, optionally call `self_check`, hash the rival source, record authority/rival outputs and exact disagreement cells, and never import private runner functions. This would make audit findings uniform and much quicker to accept.

Biggest avoidable friction: native and historical prototype APIs shared one module surface

Keeping the earlier 27-setting CLI audit and the new native `program/generate` API in one `prototype.py` made monkeypatch delegation recurse through its own compatibility wrapper. Generate a standard separate legacy-module shim—or require retained exploratory CLIs to stay in a separately imported file—so native promotion cannot accidentally rebind the implementation it delegates to.

`checks/audit/d4be41674012/report.json`.

ensure replacement colors actually differ from the opposite edge, reconcile
advertised bounds with difficulty-dependent sampler bounds, and either honor

degenerates distinct from ordinary helpful-input postconditions. These are
findings-only audit targets and remain unchanged in this return.

declared range, actual draw range, exact requested override and postcondition

items.text:
Probe observable-envelope-to-label lookup shortcuts

**Symptom.** The first repair passed the declared semantic rivals, but each
`(layout_profile, palette_profile)` pair still fixed one frequency assignment.
A learner could therefore predict one of 24 output bars from shape and palette
without counting any cells. The final-review regressions and witness are retained
at `checks/anti-lookup-red.log` and `checks/anti-lookup-witness.json`.

**Suggested change.** Extend defect lint or semantic diagnostics with a generic
conditional-label probe: group deterministic draws by declared observable
controls (and optionally cheap summaries such as shape and total nonzero count),
then warn when every group maps to a single output despite the stated rule using
finer input content. Report the smallest fixed envelope, example seeds, and
whether varying an independent generator stream produces multiple labels. This
should be advisory because some tasks intentionally use profile-coded outputs,
but it would catch curriculum lookup tables that named rivals miss.

Add an automatic low-complexity shortcut miner to the semantic gate

**Priority: highest; shared-tool change.** The selected generator's baseline was
12/12 green, yet two marker-free selectors remained perfect: numeric palette
rank across generated lesson windows and canvas-dimension-to-shape lookup across
all canonical pairs. The task-local repair now declares those rivals, but other
generators will not benefit unless a reviewer happens to invent the right rival.
Evidence: `checks/red-palette-rank/result.json`,
`checks/red-canvas-shape/result.json`, and
`checks/before/checks/725513c9d0c9_before_battery_summary.json`.

Proposed change: in the shared semantic gate, extract candidate-object features
(color rank, size, bbox dimensions/area, color count, reading order, canvas
shape, coarse D4 signature) and try decision stumps plus one- and two-key lookup
tables. Report shortcuts that fit canonical pairs or complete lesson windows,
with a generated rival skeleton authors can retain. Escalate only survivors to
the expensive lesson census.

Lint task tests for portable canonical-data access

The audit target `8d45a1d4a531` has 9 passing task tests and one failure in the
required portable task-test runner. Its test computes the canonical path from
the generator directory and looks for
`generators/8d45a1d4a531/data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl`, which does not exist in
the snapshot runtime. Evidence:
`checks/audit-8d45a1d4a531-task-tests/result.json`.

Proposed change: add a test-source lint for direct `data/canonical` path
construction and suggest `reviewer_support.canonical_pairs(TASK_ID,
root=find_root(__file__))`. Optionally make the task-test runner expose a clear
one-line diagnostic when this common path pattern fails.

Make the lesson-census console summary unambiguous

The command printed only `status: no_declared_ambiguity` and the output path.
That phrase is easy to misread as “no rivals were declared,” even though the
full report contained 33 namespaced rival entries per band, 300 materialized
lessons, and zero ambiguities. Evidence: `checks/lesson-census-command.log` and
`checks/lesson-census.json`.

Proposed change: print a compact summary such as “300 lessons complete; 11
unique rivals across 3 namespaces; 0 ambiguous; 0 errors; 1,500 unique inputs.”
Reserve `no_contract` for a missing contract and label the successful status in
human-facing output as `complete_no_ambiguity`.

Diversity must distinguish color permutations from spatial support

**Symptom:** the predecessor passes the complete battery, while each fixed-size profile has only one normalized geometry across 80 seeds. Distinct palettes make raw-grid diversity look healthy. Evidence: `checks/before/checks/ecd1f88fc6d3_before_battery_summary.json`, `checks/probe-before.json` versus `checks/probe-after.json`.

**Proposed change:** allow task-declared nuisance-color equivalence and report diversity before and after normalization, conditioned on observable profile and dimensions. Preserve semantic code colors; blindly permuting all colors would be invalid here. Surface concentration as an advisory with actual exemplars, not a universal pass threshold. The local `probe_distribution.py` is a concrete implementation to adapt.

Declared rivals are an incomplete test set, even when all are refuted

**Symptom:** all predecessor semantic gates pass, but an undeclared adjacency-only rival fits all public pairs and 360/360 default-band draws. The new gate catches it only after the reviewer adds the explicit competitor. Both audit targets have analogous full-support wrong rules. Evidence: `checks/probe-before.json`, `checks/audit-probe.json`, `QUESTION_ANSWER.md`.

**Proposed change:** retain a small library of task-applicable feature-ablation rivals (ignore labels, ignore connectivity, collapse color-local geometry), with explicit applicability review. Require exact disagreement cases checked against authority and check whole lessons, not only isolated scenes. Do not present a finite named-rival pass as complete identifiability. Save whether witnesses are accepted by self-check and emitted by the generator; the audit JSON demonstrates why that distinction matters.

The packet's direct suite needs an explicit child-process import contract

**Symptom:** source tests can import `arcpuzzles` via `PYTHONPATH=src`, but the shared `run_process` deliberately strips `PYTHONPATH`; `test_duties_solve_preparation_runs_from_packet_root` then fails in a minimal copied packet's child. Relative and absolute PYTHONPATH runs both fail. Evidence: `checks/suite-command.log`, `checks/suite-absolute-command.log`. Installing the identical API locally lets the final source suite pass: `checks/install-api-command.log`, `checks/suite-final-command.log`.

**Proposed change:** document and verify installation as a suite prerequisite, or build the fixture with the required API/bootstrap resources and set an explicit supported child import path. Preserve sandbox/environment sanitization rather than weakening it globally. Add a fresh-interpreter test which is not accidentally satisfied by a developer's editable install. No shared code was altered in this task.

Source-tree success does not establish installed-wheel portability

**Symptom:** running the root suite against a locally built wheel, without the source-tree import override, produces six failures. Four cannot discover the default catalog (`No ARCpuzzles catalog at /opt/pyvenv/lib/python3.13; pass --library or ARCPUZZLES_HOME`); two fail to include `WELCOME.md` in generated packets. Evidence: `checks/suite-installed-command.log` lists every failing test, traceback and the 132-pass/28-skip totals. This wheel was built from a copied unchanged `src`, `pyproject.toml` and README; no catalog or nonpackage repository templates were installed.

**Proposed change:** distinguish a package-only install from a full library checkout. Pass or configure the library explicitly where required, and test expected option-validation behavior independently of accidental checkout discovery. Include packet-template resources through declared package data or require and validate their explicit library location. Add wheel-install smoke tests in a clean temporary environment. The missing resources were exposed by our API-only install; the logs do not prove all documented full-library installation procedures are broken.

Newly added task tests are not automatically part of runtime relocation

**Symptom:** the inherited mapping materializes 251 known files but does not automatically carry the new test/probe files added under the selected task home. A relocated run could therefore appear green while only running predecessor coverage. Evidence: `checks/portable/result.json` records `copied_new_tests_explicitly=true` and the 40-test invocation in the actual relocated directory.

A new peer audit passed when imported by pytest but failed as a standalone command because `puzzle_generators` lives under `repo/shared/runtime`, which pytest had already injected into `sys.path`. Provide a tiny documented `reviewer_support` launcher/helper for standalone task-local tools that resolves the repository and runtime roots consistently; this would prevent tools from appearing portable only inside the test harness.

Priority — cache and batch semantic authority calls

**Symptom:** semantic authoring currently encourages one Racket call per witness/rival pair. The first repair's semantic run was slow enough to be interrupted (`checks/semantic_gate-after-v1/`), and I manually bundled several rivals under one ordinary witness to make the final gate practical.

**Suggested shared change:** in the semantic gate, cache authority outputs by `(rule hash, input hash)` and evaluate all Python rivals against that one retained output. Accept a witness-to-many-rivals mapping as a first-class fast path, report cache hits, and checkpoint after each unique authority input rather than each rival. Make static `AXES` literal requirements explicit in lint diagnostics

**Symptom:** the first repaired lint failed because an `AXES[*].valid` string used `"|".join(PROFILES)`. The value was deterministic, but the checker requires an AST literal so it can inspect the contract without executing source. The reason was only clear after reading the detailed lint output (`checks/lint/`).

**Suggested shared change:** emit a focused message such as “`AXES.profile.valid` must be a literal string/list; calls such as `join()` are not statically inspectable,” and point to one passing example. Keeping the static restriction is reasonable; clearer diagnostics would save an iteration.

**Symptom:** most retained wrapper logs end with an ANSI clear sequence and `TERM environment variable not set`, even when the underlying check passed. This also caused confusing tool-level status presentation around otherwise-zero wrapper return codes.

**Suggested shared change:** call terminal-clearing code only when stdout is a TTY and `TERM` is set. Structured commands should leave plain logs and return the child's exit status without cosmetic terminal operations.

Add a portable-root lint for task-local tests and probes

**Symptom:** the first task-local probe used `Path(__file__).parents[3]`. It worked in the source tree but violated the portable runtime contract. I replaced it with `reviewer_support.find_root(__file__)` before the final source-bound task-test run.

**Symptom:** the reviewer must separately reconstruct an exact patch against the original packet, initialize an isolated Git root, run `git apply --check`, apply, compare hashes, and rerun focused tests. This is valuable but easy to perform inconsistently.

**Suggested shared change:** add an opt-in `--verify-fresh ORIGINAL_ZIP --command-from-results INDEX` mode that creates a temporary extraction, asserts its Git root, applies the exact delta the packager will emit, verifies selected source hashes, and records the command/exit evidence for `RESULTS.json`.

**Symptom:** Native qualification binds a large runtime closure, but reviewers have no compact command to confirm that a retained receipt still matches current source bytes without requalifying or writing a custom hash script.

**Evidence:** MAIN `2fb0197be694` named 148 source files in `qualification.json`; the return needed a reviewer-side comparison before packaging.

**Suggested change:** Add `arcpuzzles parametric verify-qualification ID --qualification PATH` to validate the execution hash, all bound source/executor hashes, canonical program, adapter contract, and source-drift status, emitting a compact JSON receipt.

**Symptom:** A retained test used both a fixed `__file__` parent depth and the private `scripts.generator_module_loader`, which would fail before meaningful pytest execution in the isolated runtime.

The public-export checker requires the SHA-256 to be the complete filename, so otherwise valid names such as `01-<sha>.json` fail even in per-mode directories. **Priority: highest shared-tool change.**

**Symptom.** `c24bb478ceb4`'s baseline battery was 12/12 green although a
plausible adaptive wrong rule survived 18/54 three-demo windows and disagreed on

parameter and apply it globally.” Evidence:

`generators/c24bb478ceb4/workspace/probe_first_orientation_rival.py`.

extractor. It should synthesize a first-object broadcast prediction, score it on

Both pre- and post-repair batteries have no blocking lint/defect-lint findings.

gap, outside what static syntax and declared-rival checks can infer unaided;

Evidence: `checks/audit/5b3c69ad7276/lesson-probe.json`.

**Suggested change.** When an exact categorical axis has a small enumerable domain, report for each materialized lesson which query axis values were absent from all demonstrations. Keep this diagnostic nonblocking unless a task declares semantic dependence, but make it prominent for approved generators whose canonical set also omits the value. This does not prove ambiguity by itself; it cheaply points reviewers toward the exact rival they should encode.

items.text:
Surface canonical-validator rejection as a first-class audit summary

**Symptom.** Generator `60b3a4fe8090` rejects all five of its own canonical inputs under `self_check`; pair-level error counts are 2, 2, 3, 2, and 3. Its generated distribution never emits command-colored non-command blobs, although canonical examples do, so a wrong “slide every colored blob” rule is indistinguishable on generated inputs. Evidence: `checks/audit/60b3a4fe8090/counterexample.json`.

**Suggested change.** In audit assignment setup or the standard generator summary, always print `canonical accepted / total` beside generator approval and rule-hash status. The profile gate already measures this when run; surfacing the count before manual review would make severe validator/authority drift immediately visible.

Highest priority shared-tool change — make portable task tests expose the pinned authority snapshot at legacy task paths

**Symptom.** The first source-bound portable test run executed 330 tests, but 3 failed
because the immutable retained fixture resolved
`generators/d546d87fec58/data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl` while the portable runtime
placed the same pinned snapshot at `data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl`. The failure was a
layout incompatibility, not a generator or authority mismatch; see
`checks/task-tests/result.json` (`327 passed, 3 failed`).

**Task-local mitigation included.** `tests/conftest.py` creates an ephemeral,
relative, hash-bound alias only when `ARCPUZZLES_HOME` is set, refuses an unexpected
existing path, and leaves both checkout and authority bytes untouched. The final
portable run passes 333/333.

**Proposed shared fix.** In the portable task-test runtime builder (the code that
materializes the root `data/` snapshot), create
`generators/<task_id>/data -> ../../data` for retained legacy fixtures, or migrate
those fixtures to a public authority-path helper before freezing them. The runtime
should validate that the target is its own copied snapshot and fail closed on any
other path. This removes per-task compatibility shims without weakening source
binding.

Add assembled-lesson rival coverage to the semantic gate

**Symptom.** Instance-level witness frequency and rival verification both passed, yet
the first actual 300-lesson census found 2 lessons whose four visible demonstrations
all fit `rot180_only`; only the query refuted it. Evidence is
`checks/lesson-census-ambiguity-reproducer.json`.

**Proposed fix.** Extend `generator_semantic_gate.py` (or add a lightweight companion)
to assemble the same consecutive sample-index windows used by training, enumerate all
small cyclic starts, and require each declared canonical-fitting rival to be refuted
inside the visible demo set. Keep the full source-bound Racket lesson census as a
slower audit. The task-local cyclic schedule and regression
`test_every_four_consecutive_demos_refute_rot180_only` demonstrate the intended
contract.

Surface keyed-draw provenance failures earlier for deterministic schedules

**Symptom.** A deterministic `sample_index % 3` schedule preserved semantics and
passed 11/12 final battery stages, but override checking correctly failed because the
default `mask_profile` value bypassed `GenCtx.draw_choice`. The failure is retained in
`checks/after-final/`.

**Proposed fix.** Document a small public helper such as
`ctx.record_choice(label, value, valid_options)` or show the one-option
`draw_choice(label, (scheduled_value,))` pattern in the generator specification.
That lets scheduled curricula remain deterministic while satisfying provenance and
override audits. This return applies the latter task-local fix and adds a direct
regression.

generated tiny test packets need a usable solve bootstrap

Symptom: the complete repository suite reports
`test_duties_solve_preparation_runs_from_packet_root` failing with
`ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'arcpuzzles'` inside the fixture packet's
`solve_episode.py`; no expected blocked summary is created. The same test fails
from untouched ZIP source/tests, so this is not introduced by the generator patch.
Evidence: `checks/repo-tests.log`, `checks/pristine-suite-failure.log`, and its JSON
command record. The full supplied packet's actual prepare/finish succeeded.
Suggested change: make miniature packet fixtures include the package code required
by generated wrappers, or explicitly construct a self-contained bootstrap and test
that missing prerequisites produce a retained blocked receipt. Verify after moving
the fixture and outside its parent repository's import path. Shared implementation
was not edited because this assignment permits task-local changes only.

successful Racket execution is not semantic label integrity

Symptom: original selfcheck and rule_smoke stages were green, but 198/450 actual
outputs lost colored cells; the original self-check rejected 0/900 inputs despite
696 geometry violations. Evidence: baseline battery and
`checks/path-before-comparable.json`. The bounded write behavior turns bad
placements into valid-looking grids, not runtime errors.
Suggested change: support task-specific output-invariant hooks, with exact failing
input/output retention and independent execution of the canonical reference.
Pixel conservation is appropriate here but must not become a universal ARC gate
because other tasks intentionally add/delete cells. This return supplies a working
`path_probe.py` example. Keep smoke execution and semantic integrity as separate
verdicts. The existing linter correctly caught stale axes/rule metadata; it did not
make the stronger conservation guarantee and should not be described as doing so.

make iteration labels and public phase choices unambiguous

Symptom: attempting `--phase after-synced` through the public CLI exits 2 because
only `before` and `after` are accepted. Evidence:
`checks/after-synced-command.log`. Later attempts correctly used `--phase after`
with different `--out` directories.
Suggested change: document that phase is a fixed enum and output directories carry
iteration identity, or add a separate validated run-label argument. Do not expand
an enum invisibly in one internal battery path while leaving wrapper behavior
ambiguous. This was an operator error with a recoverable documented workaround,
not a failed generator or a claim of corrupted evidence.

frozen runtime mappings omit newly added task-local test assets

Symptom: runtime preparation uses the shipped file mapping, which predates this
review's new tests and workspace probes. The portable verifier explicitly copies
those selected assets into the prepared runtime and then renames the staging tree
before checking it. Evidence: `workspace/portable_check.py` and
`checks/portable/summary.json` (252 mapped files plus explicit assets).
Suggested change: provide a scoped, validated “include current selected workspace
and tests” option, or surface omissions in the preparation manifest. Keep path
validation and a clear distinction between production-selected code and review
assets. Retain the actual runtime path and child argv, not a guessed repository
layout. The current probe verifies relocation, not filesystem isolation.

distinguish witness presence from actual rival disagreement

Symptom: the first revised semantic contract declared useful feature witnesses
but no executable linked rivals. The semantic gate correctly classified them WEAK.
Evidence: `checks/after-final-command.log` and the final green semantic report.
Suggested change: include a short task-local example in the authoring guide showing
SEMANTIC_WITNESSES, SEMANTIC_RIVALS, and WITNESS_RIVALS together, with a mismatch
regression. Also separate “fits canonical examples” from general anti-shortcut
rivals; only the former belong in CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS. This is a usability/documentation
improvement, not a request to weaken a correct gate. The completed generator is a
working example. No false positive is alleged.

Battery controller should reconcile a completed signed child receipt without waiting forever for inherited stdout handles

**Priority: highest shared-tool change.**

**Symptom:** on the final after battery, a stage child completed and wrote its `.receipt`, `.ok`, log, and report, but the outer `arcpuzzles check --battery --out ...` process remained open because a descendant still held the output pipe. This occurred after `defect_lint` and again after `override`. The completed evidence was visible under `checks/after/checks/`, while the aggregate remained `running` until the source/settings-bound resume imported the checkpoint. The same transport pattern interrupted the immutable before run at `dist_gate`.

**Concrete evidence:** `checks/after/attempts/0001/`, `checks/after/attempts/0002/`, the final aggregate `checks/after/checks/1a92a12bac06_after_battery_summary.json`, and the partial baseline `checks/before/result.json`.

**Suggested change:** in the battery controller, treat a valid signed receipt plus matching `.ok`/report hashes and a terminated direct child as authoritative stage completion. Close or redirect descendant stdout/stderr file descriptors, or have the controller poll the receipt rather than requiring pipe EOF. On timeout, reconcile completed receipts before marking the aggregate incomplete. This preserves the existing source/runtime/policy hash checks while avoiding manual checkpoint recovery.

Make the protected Racket requirement explicit or automatic in generic review runners

**Symptom:** invoking the generic packet review runner for Racket-dependent stages can produce environment failures even though the packet includes `run_with_racket.py` and a pinned runtime. The duties document the wrapper, but generic commands look otherwise valid and fail later at grammar/Racket lint rather than at dispatch.

**Suggested change:** have `review.py run` and equivalent packet helpers either delegate automatically through `run_with_racket.py` for Racket-dependent subcommands, or fail immediately with a message containing the exact wrapped command. This would separate real source failures from missing-runtime invocation errors and reduce duplicate evidence directories.

**Highest priority — ship the semantic contract document referenced by the gate

items.text: `review_base_preflight --out` raises `FileExistsError` when the destination is an already-created but empty directory. Evidence: the documented directory-shaped command failed until the empty directory was removed. Suggested change: state “output path must not exist” in `--help`, or safely accept an empty destination directory.

**The semantic gate missed a global-frequency shortcut even though the baseline battery was entirely green.** For task `38300735cc4d`, every old blocker color occurred exactly once, so `block_only_singletons` matched every generated example. Suggested change: add a blocker-frequency metamorphic probe that duplicates a blocker color in safe cells outside all semantic spans and asserts that the output is unchanged. More generally, derive count-conditioned rivals for colors that play obstruction or separator roles. Exact reproducer: `checks/38300735cc4d_counterexample.json`.

**Flag duplicate top-level semantic hooks.** Audit target `978ea94724d3` defines `self_check` twice; the second definition silently replaces the first and drops the promised left-right asymmetry check. A simple AST lint for duplicate function/constant names—especially `self_check`, `generate`, `AXES`, and semantic hooks—would catch this before runtime. Exact probe: a symmetric grid `[[1,2,1],[3,4,3]]` returns no self-check errors; see `checks/audit-probes.json`.

**Require every declared axis to be consumed and observably affect at least one valid case.** Audit target `6c894e4b9bf5` declares `n_lines` valid over `3..4`, but `generate` hardcodes three lines and never reads the override. Seed `0`, sample `0`, `n_lines=4` still yields exactly three red components and passes `self_check`; see `checks/audit-probes.json`. The override contract should fail a declared-but-unused axis even when the generator accepts the keyword.

**Expose incremental battery progress at the requested output path.** The battery takes multiple minutes, but the outer `arcpuzzles check --battery --out ...` command buffers useful status until completion. The internal runner already writes stage journals and receipts; copying or streaming those records into `--out` as each stage closes would make timeouts diagnosable and allow a caller to resume confidently. A machine-readable `--status` subcommand keyed by run ID would also help. No false-positive generator-lint finding occurred in this assignment; the standalone lint passed.

Expose required rotation checks through the public check CLI — top shared-tool change

**Symptom.** The return guide requests `--require-rotations-identifiable`, but `arcpuzzles check` has no public option that forwards it to the semantic gate. The battery intentionally runs diagnostic rotations, which do not enforce this policy. Completing the requested strict check required preparing a runtime and invoking its inherited script with a separate launcher.

**Concrete paths/evidence.** Add the option at `repo/src/arcpuzzles/cli.py`'s `check` parser and pass it through `repo/src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py` to `shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py`. The implemented workflow is retained in [run_gate.py](checks/semantic-required/run_gate.py), with the [exact command](checks/semantic-required/command.json). It passed with required rotations enabled; the manual staging is workflow overhead, not a semantic failure.

**Proposed change.** Support `arcpuzzles check TASK --stage semantic_gate --require-rotations-identifiable`, record the policy in settings/checkpoint identity, and reject incompatible stage combinations. Keep ordinary battery rotation diagnostics as the current default for intentionally ordered curricula. This makes the documented acceptance check direct and source-bound without weakening policy.

Make declared rival checks and production rejection a single review recipe

**Symptom.** The intermediate direct-window probe was clean, while the production census found a rotated teaching defect after duplicate removal: easy seed 1115388330, requested start 7, accepted `[7,8,9,11,12]`, rejected index 10. The current shared census correctly detected it; the issue is relying on a cheaper probe without the production check.

**Evidence.** [Exact counterexample](checks/rotation-counterexample.json), [initial failed census](checks/lesson-census.json.gz), and [final passing summary](checks/final-measurements.json). The task-local fix is D6/M3 and is already included.

**Proposed change.** Provide an orchestrated semantic-review recipe that runs the declared-rival canonical-fit check, a requested-start/rotation probe, and the existing production census, then renders their separate verdicts together. Include accepted indices and duplicate rejections in the compact summary. Do not collapse distinct inputs, overlapping windows and Racket-labelled lessons into one sample count. The included [probe](repo/generators/c7f337af82e5/workspace/probe_distribution.py) reads actual declarations and can supply the direct-window portion.

Preflight development dependencies under the same subprocess isolation

**Symptom.** The outer interpreter imported user-installed pytest 9.1.1, while the nested portable runner set `PYTHONNOUSERSITE=1` and correctly reported `dependency_missing`. Three root tests failed before nested collection on both the repaired and unchanged original packet.

**Evidence.** [Original-packet triage](checks/tooling-triage/REPORT.md), [initial root suite](checks/repository-tests.log), [bootstrap receipt](checks/environment/bootstrap.json), and [final root suite](checks/repository-tests-final.log): 359 passed, 3 optional torch skips.

**Proposed change.** Add a packet setup/dependency check that runs the selected interpreter with the same environment isolation and prints the exact venv-based repair command. The runtime already classifies this correctly, so preserve that behavior and `PYTHONNOUSERSITE`. An offline [bootstrap](checks/environment/bootstrap_offline_venv.py) using only installed distribution bytes is included for this environment; a normal connected setup should install the declared runtime/dev extras in a venv.

Report legacy task-test migration candidates without guessing source depth

**Symptom.** Audit target fcac68386147 still uses `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` to locate canonical data. The portable runner correctly stops at preflight because that resolves inside the generator directory.

**Evidence.** [Audit preflight result](checks/audit/fcac68386147/task_tests/result.json), actual staged cwd `/tmp/arcpuzzles-check-132heaog`, and finding A-FCAC-2 in [AUDIT.md](AUDIT.md). This is distinct from the dependency failure in F3.

**Proposed change.** Use the existing portable-path detector to list migration candidates and recommend `reviewer_support.find_root(__file__)`, `canonical_path`, and `canonical_pairs`. Migrate affected task tests under their own assignments. The selected repair already uses these helpers; no unrelated audit-target edit is proposed in this source delta.

Preserve a terminal timeout receipt when the outer check controller is killed (**top shared-tool change**)

**Symptom.** A standalone `defect_lint` check was externally terminated after its long timeout. `checks/stage-defect_lint/result.json` remained `status: "running"`, with no terminal exit code or timeout flag, even though no writer or child process remained. That state is easy to misread as active work. The same final generator later completed defect-lint normally inside the full battery, so the stale `running` record is an orchestration/evidence issue, not a generator defect.

**Suggested change.** In `src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py`, have the output checkpoint record a terminal `interrupted`/`timed_out` status from a signal-safe or parent-finally path, and reconcile any child-side stage receipt before returning. A read-only `check --status --out DIR` command could also convert a dead-writer `running` record into an explicitly interrupted receipt without rerunning the gate. Keep the original partial bytes and timestamps rather than overwriting them.

Emit a small final summary receipt for `lesson-census`

**Suggested change.** Add an adjacent `<out>.summary.json` containing task ID, generator/rule hashes, requested/materialized lessons, demonstration/query policy, unique inputs, production ambiguity counts, rotation ambiguity counts, errors, and terminal status. items.text:
Synthesize boundary-complement rivals in the semantic gate (**top shared-tool change**)

**Symptom.** The complete baseline battery was 12/12 green, yet the generator never emitted multiplicity five or above. The undeclared rival `count == 2 or count >= 5` survived 864/864 sampled three-demo windows (`checks/count-boundary-before.json`).

**Concrete reason.** `repo/shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` can verify declared `SEMANTIC_RIVALS`, but a generator author who omits the relevant upper-bound rival also omits the only check that would reveal the support gap. Exact-count tasks are especially vulnerable: observing rejection at counts 1, 3, and 4 does not establish rejection at 5+.

**Proposed shared fix.** Add an optional exact-count boundary audit that infers observed nonzero-count support and tests simple complement extensions around accepted counts—for example `accepted_counts OR count >= max_observed+1`, `accepted_counts OR count <= min_observed-1`, and parity/threshold continuations. Report these as generated candidate rivals even when they are not declared, and fail strict mode when one fits every canonical and sampled demonstration. The task-local `workspace/probe_count_boundaries.py` is a small working reference.

**Evidence:** the new `bbox_count_without_yellow` rival and `checks/87aae821984d/racket-parity.json` demonstrate the repaired schedule has zero survivors.

Direct `pytest` initially failed only because it did not inherit the packet's protected `RACKET_PATH`, while `review.py task-tests` did. Add one receipt-producing test wrapper that always establishes the protected Python/Racket environment and uses the same repo-relative path rules as preflight.

the first isolated install was blocked by network restrictions. Bundle a small
compatible pytest wheel cache, or document a verified dependency-complete
interpreter, so the existing `python-check` can lead directly to focused checks.

The bundled Racket runtime worked, but the available Python lacked pytest and
the first isolated install was blocked by network restrictions. Bundle a small
compatible pytest wheel cache, or document a verified dependency-complete
interpreter, so the existing `python-check` can lead directly to focused checks.

TOP SHARED-TOOL CHANGE — reconcile orphaned stage state after caller termination

**Symptom.** A long single-stage check can finish or be killed after the surrounding caller times out, leaving the output directory permanently marked `status: running` with a lock and no durable terminal receipt. In this review, `checks/defect_lint-v2/result.json` and its lock remained in that state after the parent execution was interrupted, even though subsequent fresh runs were healthy. The reviewer must infer that this evidence is stale and choose a new output directory.

**Suggested change.** In the shared check controller/launcher, write a small launch receipt containing run ID, child PID, source hash, start time, and intended stage before spawning. On startup/resume, reconcile `running` records: if the recorded PID is absent or its process start identity no longer matches, atomically mark the prior attempt `interrupted` and preserve its partial log. A shell `trap` for ordinary termination plus this next-run reconciliation would cover both graceful and ungraceful caller loss. This should live in the shared check runner rather than each review packet.

Add cyclic-window enumeration to the shared lesson census

**Symptom.** `lesson-census --rotate-query` correctly holds out each pair in a materialized lesson, but—as its own documentation states—it does not enumerate all cyclic starts of a small deterministic schedule. For a four-slot curriculum, checking only the starts sampled by the production assembler can miss a phase-specific demonstration gap.

**Concrete example.** The task-local `repo/generators/aea86d2776f1/workspace/cyclic_lesson_probe.py` had to enumerate all four starts, all four held-out queries, and the generator's actual rival registries. Its final report covers 300 lessons/1,200 rotations in `checks/cyclic-lesson-probe-final.json`.

**Suggested change.** Add an optional `--schedule-period N --all-cyclic-starts` mode (or a generator hook returning the finite period) to `arcpuzzles lesson-census`. Reuse the existing Racket labels and rival scorer, record start residue in each replay recipe, and keep the default behavior unchanged for nonscheduled or large-period generators.

Empty output directories should be accepted

**Symptom.** The checker rejects `--out` when the directory was created in advance, even when it is empty. My first required before invocation failed solely because logging setup pre-created `checks/before`; evidence is `checks/before_invocation_error.log`.

**Suggested change.** Accept an existing empty directory, or provide an explicit `--replace-empty`/`--resume` mode. At minimum, make the error and examples state that the parent may exist but the final output directory must not.

Semantic-gate failures need a complete compact replay list

**Symptom.** The baseline aggregate reported five unidentifiable lessons, while the human-facing log printed only three examples. Finding the other two required reading the JSON and replaying all pinned cases. Evidence: `checks/before/checks/1a4459f1a38f_before_semantic_gate.log` and `.json`.

**Suggested change.** Keep the short console excerpt, but always emit a compact sidecar row for every failed lesson: band, seed, start/sample indices, surviving rivals, and whether each rival changes the query. Point to that sidecar in the log.

Infer common sibling rivals instead of trusting declarations alone

**Symptom.** Baseline lint and defect-lint passed even though the generator's 8-neighbor moat made 4- and 8-connectivity observationally identical. The semantic gate could not test a rival the generator never declared.

**Suggested change.** Add a standard primitive-adjacent rival registry and infer checks from rule/generator features: `objects` versus `objects-8`, cell count versus bbox area, component versus color aggregation, and common ordering shortcuts. Require a generated disagreement or a reviewed opt-out. The exact proposal and false-positive policy are in `QUESTION_ANSWER.md`.

Stream or heartbeat long batteries

**Symptom.** The complete battery buffered almost all output until completion and exceeded a foreground tool window despite eventually finishing successfully. This makes a healthy long run look hung and encourages duplicate launches.

**Suggested change.** Flush a stage-start heartbeat immediately, then periodically report the active stage, elapsed time, and evidence path. Preserve the final machine-readable summary exactly as today.

The legacy e250cb77a62e test suite failed before collection because it assumed a fixed checkout depth for canonical data; the task-local repair uses reviewer_support.find_root/canonical_pairs. Reusing the same adjacent-module audit CLI across both builds reduced duplicated validation work while preserving independent source inventories and receipts.

Long override checks need visible progress or a first-class resumable mode

**Symptom.** The exact override stage for this healthy generator performs 41,310 draws and took 212.77 seconds. Caller-level 120-second cutoffs terminated initial attempts before the checker wrote its result, making a correct generator look hung and leaving child processes that had to be reconciled. Evidence: `checks/before-override/run.log` and `checks/before-override/results.json`.

**Suggested change.** Flush progress every fixed number of cases/draws and expose an officially supported shard/merge command whose merged result is semantically identical to the unsharded gate. The battery should distinguish its internal stage timeout from an outer transport cutoff in the retained receipt.

Lesson gates should report rivals that survive all visible demonstrations

**Symptom.** A hook shaped as `lesson_identifiable(demos, query)` can return no error when a competitor matches both all demos and the query. That is not evidence the lesson taught the intended distinction. This generator happened to be safe, but only the added task-local assertion proved every declared competitor was contradicted by a visible demo in all 300 sampled lessons.

**Suggested change.** Add a standard gate metric `demo_survivors`: for every declared competitor, require at least one demonstration disagreement, independent of query behavior. Keep query disagreement as a separate diagnostic.

Warn when task-local test files are not mapped into prepared runtimes

**Symptom.** A new file under `repo/generators/3ae696dbdba9/tests/` was not copied by `prepare_runtime`; only the predeclared mapped test file appeared. I merged the new cases into the existing mapped file so they would actually run. Without noticing this, a reviewer could report tests that intake never sees.

**Suggested change.** Either map every `tests/test_*.py` file under the selected task or make the packager/linter fail loudly on unmapped task-local tests, listing their paths.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/task-tests-local-after-parametric.log` and
`checks/task-tests-final/result.json`.

**Suggested change.** When direct collection fails because shared authoring
helpers are absent, print the exact repository-local rerun command (for example
`PYTHONPATH=shared/runtime:src python3 -m pytest ...`) or provide a tiny supported
test launcher. Keep the portable wrapper authoritative, but make local red/green
cycles less environment-dependent.

Biggest avoidable friction: staged tests can hide non-portable canonical-data paths
The inherited test used a fixed parent-depth path that failed only under the staged runner. Add a portability lint or template that requires `reviewer_support.find_root` / `canonical_pairs` for task tests instead of hand-built `parents[n]/data` paths.

Highest-priority shared change — expand selection-policy challenge coverage

**Symptom.** A green declared-rival result can overlook a very nearby natural rule. The initial repaired generator refuted `largest_eligible` by occupied-cell count while every teacher still fit widest bounding box and widest aspect; some teaching variants also fit sparsest bbox. Ignoring singletons or solid crops likewise rescued a smallest-object rival. The exact widest lesson in `checks/widest-counterexample/counterexample.json` has demonstration/query fit flags `[true,true,false,true]`; the independent review and red tests are in `checks/code-review.md` and `checks/review-counterexamples-red/`.

**Task-local fix included.** Five executable policies and nontrivial alternative components now join the 18-rival registry. `workspace/verify_review.py` reads actual declarations and checks canonical fit instead of copying a hardcoded list.

**Proposed shared change requiring a decision.** Add an optional reusable object-selection challenger helper to `repo/shared/runtime/reviewer_support.py`, exposed in `repo/shared/tools/lesson_census.py`: given task-supplied object/eligibility/crop callbacks, enumerate area/count/width/height/aspect/density/order variants and scalar/solid filters, first retain only canonical-fitting policies, then evaluate generated demonstration/query disagreements. Keep geometry task-supplied and report finite coverage explicitly. This prevents a single vague name such as “largest” from standing in for materially different rules. No shared source is changed in this delta, and no untested shared patch is supplied.

Validate semantic predictors on non-witness default samples

**Symptom.** All compound teachers ran correctly, but some wrong-rule predictors returned `None` on ordinary inputs with no candidate. The first complete 300-lesson census then reported 40 lesson scoring errors and 168 rotation scoring errors. See retained `checks/lesson-census.json.gz`; this was not a passing census.

**Task-local fix included.** Counterfactual predictors explicitly return a valid `[[5]]` fallback, while the authority mirror retains failure detection. A regression asserts valid grids from every actual declaration over ordinary samples.

**Proposed shared change.** Extend `repo/shared/tools/lesson_census.py` or the semantic gate with a small default-input predictor preflight. Report the first exact input, source hash, rival, return type/exception, and whether it occurred before or during scoring. Do not convert an exception or invalid output into automatic refutation; preserve the current distinction between errors and semantic success.

Make portable task-test dependencies explicit

**Symptom.** The default interpreter could import a user-site pytest, but the isolated task-test subprocess disables user sites and failed collection because pytest was absent there. Initial evidence remains under `checks/regression-before/`, `checks/regression-before-system/` and the subsequent successful local-environment runs. This cost iteration time before any task regression could run.

**Task-local workaround included.** `RESULTS.json` records the packet-local environment/interpreter used; the fresh replay provisions its own environment and records the actual temporary test directory. No environment is included in the ZIP.

**Proposed shared change.** In `repo/src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py` (the task-test controller), add a dependency preflight using the same interpreter and isolation flags as pytest execution. Emit one actionable command or document a bundled test dependency setup. An ordinary interpreter import check should not be described as confirmation that the staged runtime has pytest.

Protect solve-finish descriptions from orchestration mistakes

**Symptom.** Our own shell guard skipped a solution write when `git status` failed outside a repository, while later newline-separated commands still checked a stub and finished with an inaccurate stopping reason. The immutable record correctly retains the execution error, but a casual reader could believe the success wording. See `checks/blind-initial-orchestration-error/` and `solve-blind/attempts/0001/`.

**Reviewer correction included.** The formal blind failure remains intact; a separate corrected implementation and supplemental 3/3 visible-only result are explicitly not a replacement episode. Root reports disclose the mistake. This was a reviewer orchestration error, not a defect in puzzle labels.

**Proposed shared change.** In `repo/src/arcpuzzles/review_solve.py`, have finish print and freeze a conspicuous summary of the last actual execution/visible result alongside the free-text reason. Continue allowing wrong or blocked solves to finish. Optionally support an immutable append-only correction note after finish; never silently reopen or mutate the earlier attempt/exposure record.

Keep large source-bound evidence affordable without dropping failures

**Symptom.** Two complete 300-lesson census reports occupied 25,146,680 uncompressed bytes before any battery evidence. The packet's evidence tar bundle reduces member count but correctly still counts its expanded content against the 25 MiB limit.

**Task-local solution included.** Both JSONs are losslessly gzip-compressed with original-path/size/SHA-256 mapping and restoration instructions in `checks/COMPRESSED-EVIDENCE.*`. Complete failed and final populations are retained.

**Proposed shared change.** Teach `repo/src/arcpuzzles/review_full_return.py` to offer an explicit lossless compression option for oversized JSON evidence and generate the restoration manifest automatically. Keep the existing budget accounting and make nested compression visible; do not silently discard large failures or imply their checks passed.

Make whole-session solve rollover explicit

**Observed symptom.** A final generator edit required a new source-bound solve.
The next active public directory contained old attempts and FINISHED_NOTES,
so check numbered the new attempt0002 and finish raised FileExistsError. I
initially attributed this to incomplete cleanup. However, a subsequent helper
moved the entire public directory and verified every byte; old files still
reappeared across tool calls, causing revision0003 and another finish failure.
The latter observation disproves incomplete cleanup as the complete explanation.

**Evidence and uncertainty.** `checks/solve-archive-apply.json` records the
verified whole-folder move. `checks/solve-clean-finish.log` is the actual
second failure. `checks/prior-solve/` preserves every old/mixed public state.
Two source inspections found no restoration path in review.py, solve_episode,
review_solve, setup_racket, Catalog.generate, or run_process. An external or
cross-call writer is a hypothesis; its cause was not located. This is not an
established defect in the packet's runtime-copying code.

**Built and used here.** `checks/tools/archive_post_repair_solve.py` previews or
moves the whole public folder, rejects collisions and symlinks, and hashes all
files. All 25 fixture tests pass. A one-process archive → official prepare →
check → finish succeeds; `checks/solve-one-process/receipt.json` retains the
inventories and commands, plus exact official public bytes in `final-public/`.
No private labels or live shared sources were edited. The final package is
built against those official bytes and checked by the unchanged validator.

reject orphaned attempts/FINISHED_NOTES when preparation cannot reuse a
summary. Make the whole-session requirement explicit. Keep exclusive finish
creation and per-revision identity checks: they correctly prevent silent
