items.text:
Biggest avoidable friction: stale native-manifest diagnosis
When qualification rejected the stale prototype manifest, it did not identify the mismatched files or print the guarded manifest-replacement command. Report the exact stale paths plus the canonical `parametric manifest` invocation so the source-binding gate remains strict without requiring agents to reverse-engineer the recovery workflow.

Prevent concurrent resume workers for the same battery output (**highest priority**)

**Symptom.** While the override stage was still running, a second `--resume` invocation was able to start another override worker against the same output directory. `checks/after1/progress.log` contains repeated `RUN override` entries with different run IDs, and both processes wrote the same stage paths until one was stopped/completed.

**Risk.** Concurrent stage writers can corrupt receipts or make a later summary appear authoritative even though evidence came from competing workers. This is especially easy in environments whose foreground tool call times out while the child process remains alive.

**Suggested change.** In `scripts/run_generator_battery.sh` / the public check wrapper, acquire an atomic lock for `(task, phase, out, policy)` before spawning a stage. If the lock names a live PID with matching source/policy hashes, refuse the second run and print a copy-paste poll/status command. Only reconcile or replace a lock when the owner is confirmed dead. A `--wait-for-existing` option would be useful for automation.

Add compact/sidecar output for large lesson censuses

**Symptom.** `checks/lesson-census-final.json` is about 12.2 MB for 300 lessons because it retains every materialized grid and rotation. That is valuable evidence but consumes roughly half the return's 25 MiB expanded budget by itself.

**Suggested change.** Add `lesson-census --compact-results` that writes a small source-bound summary plus a deterministic compressed JSONL sidecar containing lessons and failures. The summary should retain generator/rule hashes, seeds, counts, rival names, unique-input hashes, and sidecar SHA-256. Failures and ambiguous lessons should remain inline even in compact mode.

Make single-stage summaries explicitly stage-scoped

**Symptom.** A successful command such as `check TASK --stage semantic_gate --require-rotations-identifiable` prints `PASS semantic_gate`, but the generated battery summary says `verdict: incomplete` because the other eleven battery stages are pending (`checks/required-rotations/checks/9f74cf8633e5_after_battery_summary.json`).

**Suggested change.** Add a `scope: single_stage` field and a stage-scoped verdict such as `requested_stages_all_green`, while retaining the full-battery completeness fields. This would let machine reports distinguish “the requested stage passed” from “the full battery passed” without interpreting console text.

Preserve stage evidence incrementally when the outer wrapper is interrupted

**Symptom.** `run_with_racket.py ... check --battery` stages evidence in a
temporary relocated checkout and copies it back only after the wrapped process
returns. An outer execution timeout can therefore discard already completed
stages. The initial baseline attempt had completed lint, self-check, and rule
smoke but was interrupted before copy-back; the retained partial recovery is
`checks/before-partial/`, with the interruption recorded in
`checks/before-partial/INTERRUPTION.txt`.

**Suggested change.** Stream receipts and completed stage artifacts back to the
requested output directory after each stage, or expose a resume token/status file
whose source hashes are validated on restart. This would preserve expensive
progress without weakening source binding.

Add automatic canonical-shortcut candidates to the semantic gate

**Symptom.** Legacy tasks without declared rivals can remain advisory even when a
simple wrong rule fits every canonical pair and the entire ordinary sampler. The
audits reproduced two such cases: length whitelist `3|5` for `d5447d3527e6` and
whole-span row filling for `26872d42d87a`; see
`checks/audit/shortcut_probe.json` and the two retained counterexamples.

**Suggested change.** Add a bounded library of cheap rival templates keyed to
common ARC operations—fixed transforms, restricted length/value whitelists,
over-broad interval fills, ignored markers, and endpoint-only rules. Fit them to
canonical pairs, then ask the generator for validator-accepted disagreements.
Treat an uncovered canonical-fitting rival as a targeted advisory/blocker with an
explicit domain escape hatch.

Permit named intermediate phases without overwriting final evidence

**Symptom.** The `--phase` option accepts only `before` or `after`. During an
iterative repair, a natural command using `--phase after1` is rejected with exit
2, while reusing `after` risks replacing the evidence intended for final intake.
The exact parser failure is retained in `checks/phase-label-probe.log`.

**Suggested change.** Separate semantic phase (`before|after`) from an optional
run label, for example `--phase after --run-label candidate-1`, while keeping
final package validation anchored to the canonical `after` run.

The final linter findings were useful; no false-positive linter finding was
observed on the repaired source.

Add a canonical-to-generated feature-support shortcut probe — highest priority shared change

**Symptom.** The intermediate repaired source passed all 12 inherited stages and
a 300-lesson declared-rival census, yet every moving cell occupied one row parity
and an even column. Existing morphology, diversity, and semantic gates had no
candidate rival for that unrequested coordinate restriction.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/parity-red/` fails all three bands against source
SHA `c0fc2e6b7f0af441079c499c8da78cd5d6425cd625db0aadc042258bd84dee66`.
The final source adds parity variation and executable parity rivals; see
`checks/after-final/checks/95b47c355ae4_after_semantic_gate.log`.

**Suggested shared change.** Extend `shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` (or
add a cheap pre-gate) to compare canonical and generated support for basic
coordinate/object predicates: row/column parity, border/interior, quadrants,
and simple count/size buckets. When generated support is a strict subset,
report a minimized witness and optionally test an operation-masked rival. Keep
this advisory by default and allow a documented task opt-out, because some tasks
make those features semantic. This targets a training-data shortcut that pure
input uniqueness and declared-rival checks cannot discover on their own.

Biggest avoidable friction: hand-built causal witness schema

The native executor returns a full Racket runtime identity, while the sequential-witness validator requires exactly the two-field backend/protected object. Expose a native witness writer/validator helper so future reviewers can retain the full identity separately and produce the required source-bound artifact without recreating this contract; this return's task-local `audit.py witness` now does that.

Biggest avoidable friction: visible coverage did not establish taught behavior

Boundary contacts and matching query pairs were easy to count without checking whether the demonstrations taught their consequences. Require the selected demonstration output to distinguish edge and overlap rivals; this return implements those checks and repairs both gaps without increasing the demonstration count.

Declared-setting qualification alone does not catch a plausible ceiling-threshold rival when all teaching maxima divide evenly; the runnable task-local verifier now retains the exact counterexample and checks nonintegral cutoffs. Reuse that finite-rival check alongside native qualification for future input-derived threshold families.

Biggest avoidable friction: unregistered public-family causal evidence and public exports needed repeated task-local glue. Add a first-class preflight-aware witness/export command; the included authoring_tools.py demonstrates source-drift rejection, protected replay and private-order-independent public writing without claiming owner acceptance.

Reject staging-dependent fixture paths during packet construction

`a02bd9f85082`’s portable baseline test failed before reaching semantics because it derived `data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl` from a fixed `Path.parents[...]` depth beneath the task home. The packet already exposes `reviewer_support.find_root` and `canonical_path`, which work in the isolated task-test staging tree.

Add a packet-build/static preflight that rejects task tests resolving canonical or runtime fixtures from hard-coded parent depths and points authors to the portable `reviewer_support` API. This would turn a reviewer-time baseline repair into an author-time lint failure.

Reviewer authoring guidance permits `var/`, but the return builder rejects new `repo/var/` files; direct transient probes to `WORK/checks/` or outside `repo/`, as the retained audit tool does, or explicitly exempt declared scratch output.

items.text:
Top shared-tool change — make interrupted battery recovery explicit

**Symptom.** A fresh twelve-stage battery process was externally interrupted
after `lint`, `selfcheck`, and `rule_smoke`. Its retained `result.json` and
battery summary still said `running`, with a stale controller PID/lock, even
though no process remained. The public `--resume` path worked correctly and
hash-safely reused the three completed stages, but diagnosing whether the run was
alive versus abandoned required inspecting process state and retained internals.
See `checks/after/attempts/0001/result.json`, its `progress.log`, and the resumed
`checks/after/result.json`.

**Suggested change.** Add a public `arcpuzzles check --status/--recover OUT`
(or equivalent behavior before `--resume`) that: (1) reports controller PID
liveness, source/settings compatibility, completed journaled stages, and first
safe resume stage; (2) converts a dead `running` receipt to an explicit
`interrupted` snapshot without discarding it; and (3) prints the exact supported
resume command. This would reduce guesswork while preserving the existing strong
hash checks and attempt archive.

items.text:
Add a fast authoring preflight for profile support plus provenance

**Symptom.** A repair could satisfy ordinary generation and focused boundary
checks yet still fail the full battery's pinned profile floor or the interaction
between canonical anchoring and keyed override provenance. In this review, one
iteration had zero exact canonical-profile hits in medium/hard; another improved
support but exposed an override/provenance integration failure. The decisive
reports are `checks/after/` and `checks/after-final/`.

**Suggested change.** Provide a lightweight author-facing preflight that runs the
same pinned 20-draw-per-band profile sample together with named-axis provenance
and explicit-override bypass checks. It should print the exact canonical profiles,
per-band hits, envelope rate, and whether anchors used keyed context draws. This
would not replace the battery; it would make the distribution contract cheaper
to iterate on and easier to cover test-first.

The generator linter itself did not produce a false alarm on the final source.
Its baseline findings correctly pointed to missing authority binding and dishonest
axis behavior; task-local fixes are already included in this return.

Biggest avoidable friction: ready-result transcription is manual

After qualification, manifest creation, witness replay and public verification,
`RESULTS.json` still requires manually duplicating paths and the four causal
descriptions.  Add a `review.py summarize-ready TASK_ID` command that reads the
current source-bound receipts and emits a validated repair-target row; this
would reduce copy errors without weakening owner acceptance.

Make actual-lesson rival refutation a source-bound acceptance artifact

R2 and A2 show why marginal morphology and per-grid branch occurrence are not
sufficient. Main baseline: 55/390 lessons have a demo-fitting rival that differs
on the query. Echo audit: boundary scenes exist, but four complete lessons
still fail to distinguish wrapping. Require actual-runner lesson traces, demo
refutation versus query-equivalent survival versus query ambiguity, source/rule
hashes, and all cyclic starts for small schedules. Verify each declared
canonical shortcut against every usable canonical pair before counting it.

Delivered concrete implementation: task `workspace/lesson_probe.py`, complete
before/final archives, and `workspace/audit_targets.py`. Import rival declarations
instead of maintaining a duplicate name list. Keep finite-domain caveats and
independent training approval. See `QUESTION_ANSWER.md` for cheap smoke/full paths.

Do not print “ALL stages green” for a baseline with advisories

`checks/before/result.json` and its console transcript end with
“ALL 12 stages green”, even though the same run's authoritative battery summary
is **10 green, 2 advisory, 0 failed**, and its intermediate lines correctly mark
both advisories. A consumer reading only the last line receives the wrong
quality conclusion. Build the final CLI sentence from the summary's verdict
and green/advisory counts. Regression: a synthetic baseline with one
nonblocking advisory must exit 0 but must not say all-green. No shared-script
patch was made because this assignment forbids it.

Compute frozen-fixture counts rather than hard-coding success prose

The untouched main-task fixture prints “128 mixed override cases checked”,
but its loops are 3 bands × 2 heights × 2 widths × 2 counts × 4 profiles = **96**.
`checks/portable-fixture.json` retains its real output and actual runtime path;
`REVIEW.md` reports the discrepancy rather than repeating it. Increment and
print a counter inside the loop, preferably include it in machine-readable
results. The new tests independently cover 288 mixed cases over three schedule
positions. Preserve frozen fixtures during a review; fix this upstream.

Audit `8c069ab108a1` supplies an exact case where a first-write-wins rival fits all three canonical pairs and three generated demonstrations, then differs from the Racket query by 12 cells (`checks/audit/8c069ab108a1/rival_analysis.json`).

Make production ordering and rotation policy explicit so intentionally staged curricula are not falsely rejected. This adds no extra Racket calls after materialization.

Make override-contract failures available as a compact machine-readable summary

**Symptom:** the pristine `bf8910eef99b` override gate correctly found dead axes, undeclared incompatibilities, and an accepted unknown key, but the log contained more than a thousand repeated rows. Audit `03909f3e98e7` similarly has several distinct control-contract classes that are easier to act on when grouped.

items.text:
Detect active-authority source divergence before the expensive battery

**Symptom:** `bf8910eef99b` had behavior-equivalent but textually different active Racket sources. The full baseline battery did not report this until its final `authority_sync` stage.

**Suggested change:** add a cheap preflight that hashes active canonical/selected source groups and prints divergence before launching expensive stages. Execution parity can remain in the normal authority stage; the early hash check would shorten the feedback loop without weakening the final gate.

items.reason: Retain bounded profile-conditioned hybrid rival construction as a shared semantic-gate proposal, with explicit predicates and exact demo/query fit vectors.
items.text:
**Priority shared change — synthesize profile-conditioned hybrid rivals

**Symptom.** The selected baseline passed the standard semantic gate even though a strong rival fit every demonstration and disagreed on the query. The rival applied the intended rule on strict-canonical or same-foreground inputs, then switched to count-only placement on the held-out distinct profile. Exact evidence: `checks/selected/profile-gated-count-shortcut-before.json`.

**Suggested change.** Extend `scripts/generator_semantic_gate.py` (or its shared rival evaluator) with a bounded hybrid construction: for every canonical-fitting rival `R` and every declared/profile extractor `P`, test `intended if P(input) else R(input)` and the converse across each materialized lesson and query rotation. Keep the search explicit and capped; report the predicate, base rival, fitting demo indices, and differing query. This would catch evidence segregation without asking every task author to anticipate the exact hybrid manually.

Validate `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` against canonical pairs

**Symptom.** The baseline set copied all seven declared rivals, but only `equal_cells` actually fit every canonical pair. False canonical-fit claims make witness reporting noisy and can hide the shortcuts that truly require counterexamples.

**Suggested change.** During semantic preflight, execute every declared shortcut on every usable canonical pair. Fail or warn with an exact fit vector when a claimed shortcut does not fit all pairs, and separately list undeclared `SEMANTIC_RIVALS` that do fit all pairs. The task-local probe demonstrates the desired report in `checks/relation-curriculum-probe-final.json`.

Distinguish feature counters from rival-refuting witnesses in the schema

**Symptom.** Two intermediate witnesses merely detected strict or broadened profiles and had no `WITNESS_RIVALS` binding. The shared semantic gate called them weak, but this distinction is currently conventional rather than structural.

**Suggested change.** Split the contract into `SEMANTIC_FEATURES` for distribution observability and `SEMANTIC_WITNESSES` for executable disagreements, or require every semantic witness to bind at least one rival. Dedicated profile-floor/diversity stages can consume feature counters without presenting them as evidence that a rival is refuted.

Preserve the helpful portable-test preflight diagnostic

The audit of `c1fd38e5812b` shows the current preflight catches fixed-depth canonical paths before pytest and gives an actionable replacement API. Evidence: `checks/audit/c1fd38e5812b/task-tests/result.json`. This behavior is useful and should remain; no change is requested beyond making the same diagnostic available from ordinary repository pytest where feasible.

Add semantic support-signature probes to the standard battery

**Symptom.** The original generator passed all 12 stages while its decisive mapping axis covered only nonzero cyclic rank shifts: 1/2 `K=2`, 2/6 `K=3`, and 3/24 `K=4` signatures. Ordinary diversity was high because grid sizes, positions, and palettes changed.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/before/checks/e1e7c467196f_before_battery_summary.json` is all green for generator SHA `e4bb6edd…`, while `checks/final-pairing-coverage-before.json` shows the support collapse and absence of two canonical signatures.

**Suggested change.** Let generators declare a small finite `semantic_signature(grid)` hook plus legal/support expectations by band. Have the semantic or distribution gate enumerate signatures, report missing canonical signatures, and optionally require minimum support. For legend tasks, the signature is the source-rank→target-rank permutation; other families could expose object-count, orientation, topology, or ordering signatures. This catches semantic mode collapse without hard-coding task-specific logic into the core linter.

Execute generator-local tests as an explicit battery stage

**Symptom.** The assignment requires new tests under `generators/TASK/tests/`, but root pytest is configured with `testpaths = ["tests"]`; the generator-local file is not part of the normal root suite or the 12-stage command journal.

**Concrete evidence.** `repo/generators/e1e7c467196f/tests/test_generator_e1e7c467196f.py` contains 10 regressions and passes through `workspace/run_task_tests.py` (`checks/final-task-tests.log`), but the battery summary has no task-test stage.

**Suggested change.** Add a `task_tests` stage that builds the same runtime overlay as the checker, discovers `generators/<task>/tests/test_*.py`, and records the exact pytest command and result. A missing test directory can be advisory; discovered tests should be blocking.

Expose a supported rule-evaluation helper for audit reproducers

**Symptom.** Adversarial audits need exact Racket outputs for custom inputs, but the public wrapper is optimized for battery commands. A standalone script must reconstruct the runtime overlay and internal `scripts.comment_solutions` alias before `puzzle_generators.rule_wrap` can execute canonical rules.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/audit_reproducer.py` contains an `install_comment_solutions_alias()` compatibility shim solely to evaluate two hash-bound audit witnesses.

**Suggested change.** Provide a stable command such as `python3 -m arcpuzzles eval-rule TASK_ID --input JSON` or a documented public Python helper that loads the selected authority, applies it through the protected Racket bridge, and returns rule/source hashes with the output. This would make audit counterexamples shorter and less coupled to checker internals.

Make interrupted reviewer launchers resume from completed child evidence

**Symptom:** a high-level `review.py task-tests` invocation can be interrupted by the host command window after its pytest child has already produced JUnit/source-binding files, leaving no final `result.json`. The exact payload then has to be rerun even though most work completed.

**Evidence:** the final successful receipts are `checks/public_eval_4c416de3-tests/result.json` and `checks/public_eval_97d7923e-tests/result.json`; each was obtained by invoking the documented payload directly after an earlier high-level launch left only partial files. The same packet also produced complete preflight payload JSON before some outer receipt invocations returned cleanly.

**Suggested change:** make `review.py` persist a small in-progress command identity before spawning, then atomically finalize or resume from valid child outputs after interruption. Ensure the launcher owns and reaps the whole process group, and distinguish “payload completed but wrapper receipt missing” from a semantic test failure.

Promote the bounded public-family audit pattern into a shared command

**Symptom:** `review_public_creation preflight` correctly verifies official labels and finite setting identification at the qualification demo count, but public-family authors still need task-local code for the required 2–6-demo sweep, shortcut rivals, public/private leakage, prefix stability, stress metrics, and hash-named one-query exports.

**Evidence:** the byte-identical task-local tools at `repo/generators/public_eval_4c416de3/workspace/parametric/audit.py` and `repo/generators/public_eval_97d7923e/workspace/parametric/audit.py` implement the same reusable harness. Their outputs are `checks/public_eval_4c416de3/adversarial/audit.json` and `checks/public_eval_97d7923e/adversarial/audit.json`.

**Suggested change:** add a shared `arcpuzzles.review_public_creation audit` command with plugin hooks for task-specific rival predictors. Standardize counts, protected-rival receipts, presentation manifests, public-byte hashing, and leakage controls so future agents only supply the semantic rival set rather than copying the harness.

Compare executable identity after path normalization in the prerequisite test

`tests/test_task_test_prerequisites.py::test_preflight_matches_isolated_test_interpreter` compares the parent's literal `WORK/repo/../.venv-review/bin/python` with the child's normalized `WORK/.venv-review/bin/python`. **Proposed shared change:** normalize equivalent path spellings while preserving the identity of the virtual-environment executable; do not blindly resolve symlinks to a base interpreter and accidentally equate different environments. The concrete strings and failing assertion are retained in the repository-suite analysis. This test-only shared fix is deliberately outside the task-scoped source patch.

## Scope of remaining reports

Two other original-packet failures concern historical reference fixture expectations and one concerns the Racket-setup diagnostic regex. Their exact node IDs and repeated assertion evidence are in `checks/repository-suite-analysis.md`; no cause beyond those observations is assumed here. The two assigned generator audits are fully reported in `AUDIT.md` with exact inputs, source/rule hashes and public reference receipts. Their target source files were not edited.

Biggest avoidable friction: complete copied-runtime dependency list
The first isolated smoke copy omitted `shared/tools/comment_solutions.py`, which the Racket wrapper requires outside `shared/runtime`; the preflight source binding already named it, and copying it fixed the run. Expose a small public-creation runtime-closure materializer based on that binding so new unregistered families can be smoke-tested without hand-selecting dependencies.

Verify every firing witness against its rival, not only a capped prefix

**Symptom.** The repository semantic gate was fully green on 12/12 lessons and
reported 60/60 checked firings for the three-occurrence witness, yet the broader
independent audit still found 3 failing windows out of 540. A triple's implied
span crossed an active segment, and paint order erased the rival's extra pixels.
The failed report is
`checks/a3086dea6cff_curriculum_after_attempt1.json`; RED/GREEN regression evidence
is in `checks/witness-rival-{red,green}.log`.

**Suggested change.** For each sampled scene in which a declared witness fires,
assert that every mapped `WITNESS_RIVALS` program actually disagrees with the
intended output, or use stratified/adversarial sampling until each interaction
class (including overlap and overwrite) is covered. Keep the existing cap only
for expensive reporting, not for the correctness assertion.

Stream battery stage completion and long-stage progress

**Symptom.** The battery wrapper buffered its output until the entire command
finished. The override stage took about 121 seconds and exercised 8,100 draws,
so an interactive reviewer could not distinguish healthy progress from a hung
process without detaching it and polling internal status files. The final timing
is recorded in
`checks/after/checks/a3086dea6cff_after_battery_summary.json`.

**Suggested change.** Flush each `RUN/PASS/FAIL` line immediately and expose a
stable live progress record for long stages, for example completed cases / total
cases plus the current axis and band. This would preserve deterministic logs
while removing the need for reviewer-written process supervision.

Add a cross-object latent-coupling gate

**Priority: top shared-tool change.**

**Symptom.** The baseline generator passed all 12 battery stages, but both colors had identical scatter counts and branch histograms in 1,800/1,800 sampled inputs. Canonical examples contradicted that equality. Evidence: `checks/scatter-profile-before.json`.

**Suggested change.** Add an optional task hook such as `observe_roles(grid) -> list[dict]` plus role-equivalence metadata. A lightweight shared stage should detect perfect equality or deterministic dependence across roles when canonical evidence refutes it. Keep it advisory unless the task declares the roles interchangeable and supplies canonical/authoritative counterevidence. The task-local `workspace/probe_scatter_profiles.py` is a concrete prototype.

Lint portable test paths before staging the runtime

**Symptom.** Both the selected task's inherited tests and audit target `158efba9f453` used fixed `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[...]` assumptions. The official task-test stage correctly caught the problem, but only after building a full isolated runtime. Audit evidence: `checks/audit/158efba9f453/finding.json`.

**Suggested change.** Extend the source linter/preflight to scan task tests before runtime materialization for fixed-depth canonical paths and emit an autofix-ready message showing `reviewer_support.find_root`, `canonical_path`, and `canonical_pairs`. This would make the failure faster and more actionable while preserving the authoritative isolated-stage check.

Check witness-to-rival discrimination during ordinary lint

**Symptom.** An intermediate generator declared `main_diagonal_pair` as a semantic witness, but the witness had no associated rival whose prediction changed. The semantic gate rejected it only after several earlier stages had run. Evidence: `checks/after-intermediate-weak-witness/checks/49c16a3506ab_after_semantic_gate.json`.

**Suggested change.** Add a static or cheap dynamic lint that requires every declared witness to name at least one live rival and verifies on one retained example that the rival and authority predictions differ. This would catch decorative witness hooks before the full semantic stage.

Add intra-stage progress/checkpointing for large exact-override matrices

**Symptom.** The final override audit grew to more than 18,000 draws and took about 64 seconds. Battery-level resume worked well, but an interrupted override stage restarts that entire stage and gives little indication of which axis combination is slow.

**Suggested change.** Have the override stage periodically record completed cross-product shards, current axis tuple, accepted/rejected counts, and source hash. Resume only complete shards when policy/source hashes match. This would also make exponential construction regressions easier to localize.

Emit a compact before/after distribution-delta template

**Symptom.** The useful finding here lived outside the standard battery, so the reviewer had to build a task-local probe and manually connect before/after hashes and denominators.

**Suggested change.** Provide a small helper that runs a task-declared observer on baseline and candidate bytes with the same deterministic seed recipe and writes a source-bound delta report. It should report denominators, exact feature frequencies, and canonical comparison without deciding whether a difference is good. This would reduce clerical work while keeping task semantics local.

Validate that every declared `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` program actually fits canonical pairs — highest priority

**Affected tool:** `shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py`

**Symptom.** Audit target `8029363f9cb7` declares six programs as `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`, but direct evaluation shows that **none** reproduces all five labeled canonical pairs. For example, `treat_every_mirror_as_backslash` already disagrees on train pair 0. The current semantic gate auto-includes these declarations as lesson competitors without first enforcing the defining “canonical-fitting” premise, so a generator can receive shortcut-counterexample credit for defeating a rule the public examples already defeat.

**Evidence.** `checks/audit/8029363f9cb7/probe.json`, `racket.json`, and `verification.json`; reusable probe: `checks/audit/run_audit_probes.py`.

**Suggested change.** When canonical data is available, evaluate each `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS[name]` on every labeled canonical pair before lesson scoring. Emit a blocking finding (or at minimum a distinct `misdeclared_canonical_shortcut` result) for any mismatch, with the first pair and differing output. Only canonical-fitting entries should contribute to “canonical shortcut killed” metrics. Add a shared regression based on a deliberately misdeclared shortcut.

Cross-check `schedule_profile` outputs against the public axis and exact override replay

**Affected tools:** `shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` and/or `shared/tools/check_generator_override_contract.py`

**Symptom.** Audit target `806425ca81b3` declares/schedules `canonical_anchor`, but `AXES["scene_profile"]["valid"]` contains `canonical_rows`. `schedule_profile(0,0,"medium")` returns `canonical_anchor`; passing that exact scheduled value back to `generate(..., scene_profile=...)` raises `ValueError`. Default generation hides the mismatch by translating through a private `_scheduled_defaults` path.

**Evidence.** `checks/audit/806425ca81b3/probe.json`; the same reusable audit script derives values from the target rather than hard-coding them.

**Suggested change.** For every sampled `schedule_profile` result, require: (1) membership in `SCHEDULE_PROFILES` when declared, (2) membership in the corresponding advertised axis domain, and (3) successful exact replay as an override with matching observed provenance. Report the scheduled value, band/index, and rejection text.

Make stale `arcpuzzles apply --out` evidence harder to compare accidentally

**Affected command:** `python -m arcpuzzles apply`

**Symptom.** The command safely refuses to overwrite an existing output, but a caller that continues after the nonzero exit can accidentally compare a new input/probe with stale Racket JSON. This occurred during the final shortcut witness refresh; the explicit source-hash assertion caught it, and the failed artifact was retained under `checks/shortcut-witness/prior-source-158189/`.

**Suggested change.** On an existing output, print the existing record’s input hash and generator hash alongside the requested input hash, or provide an explicit `--replace` flag that atomically archives/replaces the file. This keeps refusal safe while making stale-evidence mismatches immediately visible.

Biggest avoidable friction: causal-witness recipe plumbing

`review_witness template` produces a useful source-bound draft, but a reviewer must manually import task code in the packet runtime to construct the intermediate and counterfactual program. A task-local factory hook executed through the same protected wrapper would remove this environment-sensitive glue while preserving the existing qualification binding.

add an immediate protected-Racket one-pair smoke check

- **Symptom:** The Python mirror and 19 semantic tests for `b765f6c9ebeb` were
  green, but the first protected execution rejected `build-grid` because this
  DSL macro takes `(r c)` binders rather than a lambda.
- **Evidence:** The focused Racket test failed before any semantic comparison and
  passed after only the macro-call shape was corrected.
- **Suggested change:** Add a lightweight `parametric smoke ID` command, or make
  qualification run one smallest pair before source freezing, with diagnostics
  that distinguish parse/macro errors from label mismatches.

provide a portable helper for arbitrary repository data fixtures

- **Symptom:** Both pre-existing task suites used fixed `__file__.parents` depths;
  one warned and the other failed in the copied runtime. `canonical_path` solved
  the ledger lookup, but the c1 base fixture still required a hand-written
  `data/...` versus `shared/data/...` branch.
- **Evidence:** Initial portable task checks failed for `c1ee27b39d13` and emitted
  a diagnostic for `b765f6c9ebeb`; after switching to `find_root`,
  `canonical_path`, and `load_selected_generator`, the suites passed 26/26 and
  28/28.
- **Suggested change:** Add `reviewer_support.data_path(root, relative)` with the
  same bounded two-layout resolution as `canonical_path`, and update the static
  diagnostic to recommend it.

Its linked-profile repair preserves role/order structure and documents finite coverage; this is high-value but review-expensive evidence (`repo/generators/fcabbbbdfc11/generator.py`, `tests/test_generator_fcabbbbdfc11.py`, `evidence/associated_notes.jsonl`).

- `bf47583ab6e3` is unapproved/unverified with no tests and no retained notes. The first bounded peer-ticket probe failed before touching the target because `review.py run` stages the selected task but not the pinned peer module under `puzzle_generators`; the source-bound retry had to discover `reviewer_support.load_selected_generator` manually. Generate ticket probe scaffolds with that helper (or expose a peer-source loader command) so the single-probe budget is spent on the requested behavior rather than import plumbing; evidence is in `checks/tickets/ticket-e182b62e08764a97/command.log` and `direct-command.log`.

items.reason: Default public task-test stdout is compact, with receipt/log paths; --full-json retains optional complete output. Full on-disk evidence is unchanged. Evidence: shared/tools/evidence/packet-maintenance/pass-45/manifest.json
items.text:
Add a compact staged-test stdout mode
The staged runner now correctly supports unregistered public homes, but its default stdout repeats the complete source binding. A --summary mode reporting status, test counts, and receipt paths would avoid that duplication while preserving every hash in source-binding.json.

Biggest avoidable friction: task-local executable drift is not checked by preflight
The inherited `78ab57735469/workspace/parametric/verify.py` had silently fallen behind the prototype API. Require each executable promotion resource to have one focused current-contract smoke test, or have preflight execute declared task-local verifier entry points before source binding.

items.reason: Accepted finite-map ambiguity tool for explicitly declared mapping tasks. Preserve exact generated counterexample and declared constraints; do not impose bijection semantics on unrelated puzzles.
items.text:
Add a finite-map lesson ambiguity gate (top shared-tool change)

**Symptom:** pair-level label parity and self-checks can pass while the demonstrations leave the query underdetermined. `generic_dense_field_gen1`, easy seed 11960, has two query colors absent from every demonstration; an alternate bijection fits all training pairs and changes 165 query cells. Evidence: `checks/audit/generic_dense_field_gen1/counterexample.json`.

**Proposed fix:** add a reusable finite-relation competitor to `repo/shared/tools/lesson_census.py` (or a small helper called by semantic gate) that extracts observed symbol mappings, enumerates remaining bijections/functions, and emits the first demonstration-fitting/query-differing rival. Allow task code to declare an explicit global constraint that removes a candidate. This is the shared change most likely to improve Qwen3.5-9B data value.

items.reason: High-priority repeated follow-up: atomically mark dead-owner aggregates interrupted using PID/start identity. Existing source-bound resume works; report-read reconciliation remains unimplemented.
items.text:
Make interrupted battery terminal state explicit

**Symptom:** an externally terminated full battery left `result.json` at `status=running` with a stale live-lock snapshot after three completed stages. `--resume` recovered correctly and preserved the first attempt under `checks/after-v1/attempts/0001/`, but a reader could mistake the stale aggregate for a live job.

**Proposed fix:** on controller startup/status read, verify the recorded PID plus process start identity; when dead, atomically rewrite the top-level state to `interrupted` before presenting resumable stages. Preserve the current archive-on-resume behavior.

items.reason: Accepted small reporting change: explicitly say task-local tests were not included in the 12-stage battery and print the supported task_tests command.
items.text:
Keep task-test discovery warning prominent

**Symptom:** the general 12-stage battery intentionally does not execute task-local tests. That separation is documented, but it is easy to report “all green” without the selected tests.

**Proposed fix:** print a final battery note such as “task-local tests not run; invoke `--stage task_tests`” whenever `generators/TASK/tests/` exists. The current portable task-test stage itself worked well and recorded copied-source hashes and exact counts.

Highest priority — broaden ordering-rival discovery before declaring lesson success

**Affected tools:** shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py and the shared
lesson-census authoring workflow. This is a proposal for author assistance,
not a new routine maintainer intake gate.

**Symptom and exact evidence:** the intermediate c6a453e86480 source
ba7abb90aa3a4ba27c42c7e6dbe958801fdbb6a7dd92d1d80f38f77fcd599522
passed all 12 after stages and required rotations against its ten declared
competitors. A bottom-row-column ordering rival, absent from those declarations,
fit all three canonical pairs. At seed 12, indices 8..11, it fit all three demos
and changed the query. Public Racket confirmed [true,true,true,false]; see
checks/intermediate-bottom-row-ambiguity.json and the retained intermediate
source. The generic checker behaved correctly for its declared hypothesis set;
the missing hypothesis was the limitation.

**Suggested shared improvement:** provide an opt-in component-ordering candidate
inventory that can score first/last occupied-row anchors alongside min/max/
centroid/bbox/area/width/row-major candidates against the actual canonical pairs.
Keep canonical-compatible candidates and source-bound disagreement examples
visible to the author; do not call such an inventory exhaustive or automatically
approve a generator. It should reuse existing canonical and Racket APIs and
respect fixed colors rather than assume generic color symmetry.

**Included task-local implementation:** bottom_row_column was added to the
actual rival declarations, the teaching shape was repaired, and the retained
workspace/probe_rank_distribution.py dynamically inspects those declarations,
checks the full joint override matrix, and compares witnesses to public Racket
outputs. Its final report is checks/authoring-probe-final.json. No shared checker
or runtime patch is bundled, and no shared change needs to be accepted to use
the repaired generator.

## Other observations

The isolated pytest preflight correctly refused to call a missing prerequisite
a generator failure and provided an actionable remedy. Its failed receipt and
the successful new-environment receipt are retained; no checker weakening was
needed. Initial archive extraction exhausted filesystem inodes despite available
bytes; extraction to a filesystem with sufficient inodes solved that environment
issue without omitting or changing packet content. The linter identified real
missing-rule-pin/dead-control defects and raised no final false alarm.

Add an early protected-Racket setting smoke check

**Symptom:** The first projection/bridge draft passed its Python mirror and construction tests, but a misplaced Racket parenthesis left Stage B inside the object loop. The defect appeared only when the exact alternate program was executed.

**Evidence:** `generators/bdcb4c9eb6bd/tests/test_parametric_projection_bridge.py` now contains the protected-Racket regression; the corrected exact program is `generators/bdcb4c9eb6bd/workspace/parametric/project_then_bridge.rkt`.

**Suggested change:** Add a small `arcpuzzles parametric smoke ID` command that executes one demonstration and one query for every declared setting through protected Racket, validates grid shape/integer colors, and reports the exact setting/program hash. Running it immediately after adapter creation would catch parser/scope mistakes before broad Python curriculum sweeps.

Separate immutable source inventory from mutable check annotations

**Symptom:** The native manifest correctly inventories source without executing it, but its free-text `reported_checks` said qualification was pending after qualification had completed. Refreshing that sentence rewrote the manifest even though no inventoried source changed.

**Evidence:** The final task-local manifests retain identical source file hashes but replace only the author-reported check summary after native qualification and witness replay.

**Suggested change:** Keep the hashed source inventory immutable and store reviewer check annotations in a sibling receipt, or add an `annotate` command whose output is explicitly outside qualification source binding. This would reduce harmless post-qualification manifest churn while preserving provenance.

items.reason: Expose battery stage transitions and durable final state.
items.text:
The aggregate `--battery` command can remain silent for the whole
multi-stage run. In this review the first after-battery invocation produced no
incremental console evidence before the execution wrapper stopped observing
it, even though the individual stages were diagnosable and a later aggregate
run completed. Please line-buffer/flush each stage start and finish and update
the summary JSON after every stage, so an interrupted caller can distinguish a
slow stage from a dead process and resume from durable evidence.

items.reason: Make grouped override root causes the default console view.
items.text:
The override gate found the right root problem, but the failing baseline
expanded it into 238,230 draws, 156,958 unstructured rejections, 12,521
findings, and a 2.2 MB result. Once a declared axis value is rejected in a
band, or a negative `texture` is found in the ordinary domain, the tool could
minimize and cap equivalent descendants while still retaining counts. An
early root-cause table plus a representative witness would make the report
much faster to inspect without losing diagnostic value.

items.reason: Add grammar-preserving region-ablation counterfactuals to supplied rivals.
items.text:
The semantic gate is strong when a generator declares rivals and
witnesses, but the baseline received only `NO_CONTRACT`; it did not itself
show that three consecutive seed-0 examples in every band had blank top and
bottom halo segments, allowing the shortcut “pad the gray crop with zero
rows.” Add a low-cost automatic counterfactual/region-ablation pass for common
transformation families, and use declarations to extend or waive it rather
than making all shortcut detection author-supplied.

items.reason: Provide an explicit dry-run authority sync that preserves archival source and metadata.
items.text:
`authority_sync` was useful and correctly separated selected active text
from archival `raw_code`. Its error could be even more actionable by naming
the canonical source field and emitting a ready-to-review normalized diff for
each divergent selected `target_code`; execution parity alone did not explain
which text should become authoritative.

Reuse declared-rival scoring at the actual data-admission boundary — highest priority

**Symptom:** public generation's `src/arcpuzzles/worker.py:lesson_check` checks
`lesson_identifiable` only. A task with SEMANTIC_RIVALS/LESSON_COMPETITORS but no
hook gets `not_declared`, even after a successful rival census. The finished
`solve/summary.json` is an exact example on final source 43366acb... . Conversely,
audit 677dcb71e2be has a hook returning `[]` while an unlisted fixed palette-rank
rival survives four demonstrations and disagrees on a legal color-swap query.

**Evidence:** `checks/teaching-contrast.json` reproduces all eight canonical-fitting
rivals surviving a constructed lesson; `checks/audit/677dcb71e2be/reference.json`
and `finding.json` retain the actual generated-demo counterexample. The repaired
main task's real default lessons are separately checked in `checks/lesson-census.json`.

**Suggested change:** reuse the shared lesson-census rival evaluator in export
or data admission on the exact selected pairs, with an explicit query policy,
source/rival hashes, accepted indices and `refuted` / `survived_all` /
`query_ambiguous` outcomes. Keep absence of a rival contract unknown. Do not
describe any hook or finite rival set as a universal proof. Add task-specific
palette-order competitors when color-role permutation probes expose them.
This shared change is a proposal; the allowed patch adds executable rivals,
the local contrast tool and its witness only for fd68649aabf7.

Test advertised degenerate geometry, not just its label

**Symptom:** baseline fd68649aabf7's `equidistant_marker` fixture has markers at
2 and 8 and a body spanning 5..6, so its actual center is 5.5 rather than the
tie location 5. The defect linter correctly flags that the supposed degenerate
passes self_check, but the texture name itself does not establish the geometry.

**Evidence:** `checks/diagnostic-independent/baseline-probe.json` and
`authority-probe.json`; baseline defect-lint log. The selected repair replaces
the old case with an ordinary lawful bbox-tie witness and a Racket-labelled
minimal regression in `counterexamples/joint_witness.json`.

**Suggested change:** where authors declare named semantic textures, permit a
small observed-geometry predicate and report whether it actually fires on the
materialized texture. Do not impose a generic distance or shape rule across
tasks. The current linter raised a useful true positive here; no linter false
positive is claimed from this review.

owner_tool_review.reason: Static review found system_site_packages=True: imports borrow the host environment. No fresh-destination guard before provisioning. This cannot establish packet isolation; use declared dependencies in a clean environment.

items.text:
Include large near-miss negatives for exact-shape tasks

**Symptom:** audit 54875f792be0 constructs complete frames against solids,
strips and tiny L-shapes. Both a coarse area/non-solid predicate and an any-hole
predicate fit all canonical pairs and all 12 checked generated pairs. A frame
with one missing corner or an irregular enclosed loop defeats them under the
unchanged Racket rule.

**Evidence:** `checks/audit/54875f792be0/reference_witnesses.json` and
`mixed_reference_witness.json`, including the in-bounds two-object scene.

**Suggested change:** add a review prompt or task-level witness checklist for
large structurally close negatives: missing corners, gaps, interior additions,
and shapes with the right perimeter count but wrong occupied positions. Keep
this an authoring aid, not a universal input mutation; derive each label from
the selected rule. The audited target was not changed in this return.

## Runtime note

The isolated task-test preflight correctly caught user-site-only pytest and
did not misreport it as a failed generator test. A temporary venv was provisioned
offline from installed distribution files; `checks/runtime/setup_isolated_runner.py`
and `setup.json` make that repair reproducible in this environment. A normal
networked installation can use a clean venv plus pip install numpy Pillow pytest.
The initial preflight and one relative-interpreter launch failure are retained;
no isolation setting or shared tool was weakened.

Add a public-authoring sequential-witness command

**Symptom:** The native witness tooling is centered on already-qualified catalog tasks, while a new public-evaluation family has only an authoring preflight and is intentionally unregistered. This forced a task-local witness builder even though the required schema and protected evaluator already exist.

**Evidence:** `checks/tools/build_public_witness.py` binds an exact case from `checks/public_eval_b99e7126/preflight/preflight.json` or `checks/public_eval_a6f40cea/preflight/preflight.json`, executes correct and wrong-intermediate programs through protected Racket, writes the standard witness schema, and independently replays it.

**Suggested change:** Add `arcpuzzles.review_public_creation witness TASK --preflight ... --out ...` that selects an exact preflight case, verifies current source binding, emits the standard sequential witness, and performs replay. This would reduce duplicated security-sensitive orchestration while retaining the same owner gate.

Make bounded protected audits checkpointable

**Symptom:** The a6 family’s 32-seed protected audit exceeded the controller budget even though per-seed work was deterministic and earlier seeds had completed. The final source-bound run had to restart at a smaller 18-seed bound.

**Evidence:** `checks/public_eval_a6f40cea/audit/audit.json` records the completed 18-seed audit, including 36 episodes, 1,620 rival checks, 144 public views, and 60 protected evaluations. The b99 family completed the same audit shape at 32 seeds, showing that cost varies substantially by rule complexity.

**Suggested change:** Let the audit runner atomically checkpoint each seed with source hashes, support `--resume`, and optionally stop on `--max-seconds` while producing a valid explicitly bounded receipt. A resumed receipt should reject source drift and duplicate seed records.

Record immutable-label extension assumptions structurally

**Symptom:** A public parent can contain an apparent label convention or anomaly not uniquely supported by the remaining examples. Prose notes are necessary but difficult for owner reconciliation and later overlapping returns to compare mechanically.

**Evidence:** `public_eval_a6f40cea` requires an orientation-dependent checkerboard phase extension to reproduce all immutable labels; the assumption is documented in `repo/generators/public_eval_a6f40cea/notes.md` and covered by `test_documented_wide_stripe_phase_extension_matches_immutable_pair`.

**Suggested change:** Extend the public-creation inventory with an optional `inferred_extensions` list containing a stable ID, exact parent-pair locator/hash, concise assumption, alternatives considered, and covering test/evidence paths. Preflight should preserve this metadata without treating it as owner approval.

**Top shared change — add a realized-structure contract gate

**Symptom.** `be5d9fa6fec1` could produce Racket-correct labels while violating its own latent block grammar: the frozen sampler realized fewer than five groups in `332/1000` easy, `103/1000` medium, and `39/1000` hard draws, and produced mixed `1/8` rows. Existing label parity and permissive self-checking did not directly compare sampled intent with final pixels. See `checks/baseline-structure-probe.json`.

**Proposed fix.** Extend `repo/shared/tools/check_generator_override_contract.py` (or add a neighboring battery stage) with an optional `observe_structure(grid) -> dict`/`STRUCTURE_INVARIANTS` contract. On a small deterministic cohort, compare task-declared pixel-observable structure to recorded draw metadata and emit a minimized mismatch; exact declarations block, heuristic observations remain advisory. This would generalize beyond numeric AXES to blocks, objects, holes, components, periods, and relations.

Make interrupted-battery state less ambiguous

**Symptom.** The first after battery checkpointed valid green stages but its outer wrapper ended while `result.json` still said `running`; a resume completed all 12 stages. The retained evidence is clear only after inspecting the aggregate, journal, lock, and wrapper logs (`checks/after/attempts/0001/result.json`, `checks/after-resume-driver.log`, and final summary).

**Proposed fix.** In `repo/shared/tools/run_generator_battery.sh` and the Python check controller, trap parent termination and atomically write `status: interrupted`, last completed stage, and a ready-to-copy resume command. On startup, treat a dead PID lock as stale without presenting it as a live run. This is a reporting/UX change, not a task-local source change.

Offer a safe source-synchronization mode for equivalent authorities

**Symptom.** Defect lint correctly found that the task-specific base JSON and canonical ledger had different Racket text but sampled execution parity. Repair required manually replacing two JSON fields while carefully avoiding label changes (`checks/before/checks/be5d9fa6fec1_before_defect_lint.log`).

**Proposed fix.** Add an opt-in `authority-sync --write-selected TASK` command that first proves execution parity on canonical plus generated witnesses, then updates only the selected base `raw_code`/`target_code` to canonical text and prints the exact diff. It should refuse any output mismatch or unrelated row change.

Report legal joint-axis coverage as a first-class audit metric

**Symptom.** Audit target `016795030ca2` declared a Cartesian axis domain of 768 combinations, but 301 combinations raised incompatibility errors and no `INCOMPATIBLE_OVERRIDE_COMBINATIONS` contract existed. A single-axis check can miss this; the direct reproduction is `checks/audit/016795030ca2/joint-axis-probe.json`.

**Proposed fix.** Have the override checker summarize `accepted / declared Cartesian combinations`, require declared incompatibility predicates for deterministic rejections, and sample pairwise or exhaustive combinations when the product is small. Accepted combinations should still be checked through `observe_overrides`.

Highest priority — expand semantic-gate adversarial templates beyond declared rivals

**Affected path:** `repo/shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` and the lesson-census rival discovery/diagnostics.

**Symptom:** the first repair correctly declared and refuted `most_frequent_color`, so its semantic checks passed, but a stronger conditional rule—“when the top color is disconnected, choose the second color”—still fit every canonical example and every generated lesson. It was found only during manual self-review (`checks/stronger-rival-red.log`, `checks/shortcut-probe-first-repair.json`).

**Suggested change:** add generic adversarial templates for object-vs-color tasks: aggregate by color, largest component of the top color, conditional rank changes when the top color is split, and “ignore colors with multiple components.” Report candidate rivals that fit canonical pairs even when the generator has not declared them. Keep the task's own declarations authoritative for gating, but surface undeclared canonical-fitting templates as warnings with concrete witness requests.

Add conditional support matrices for schedule leakage

**Affected paths:** semantic gate, profile-floor report, and `lesson-census` summary.

**Symptom:** an intermediate curriculum alternated witnesses correctly but tied witness type to exact dimension/profile; another tied target size to schedule position. Ordinary aggregate coverage passed. Regressions `checks/profile-decouple-red.log` and `checks/size-decouple-red.log` caught the leakage.

**Suggested change:** when a generator exposes schedule profiles and semantic witnesses, report a matrix of witness counts and key semantic values conditioned on each advertised axis/profile. Warn when any profile has zero support for a witness or a semantic value is deterministic from schedule rank. A machine-readable `conditional_support` section would make this reusable at intake.

Improve static evaluation of literal-equivalent AXES metadata

**Affected path:** `repo/shared/tools/lint_generator.py`.

**Symptom:** a valid computed AXES string produced `WARN AXES is not a literal — can't validate type` and failed the lint despite 20/20 runtime validations (`checks/lint-static-failure-run.log`). I simplified the task source to a literal, so this is not a blocker.

**Suggested change:** evaluate safe constant expressions such as `"|".join(CONSTANT_TUPLE)` or downgrade this specific finding when runtime axis validation proves all values/types. The message should include the AST form it could not evaluate.

Add generic audit probes for connectivity and morphology support restrictions

**Affected path:** shared reviewer/audit helpers.

**Symptom:** both assigned audits had validator-accepted/canonical cases outside ordinary generation: task `9d0a6f959321` excluded diagonal contact and therefore taught 8-connectivity; task `2361d6aa42c3` generated only straight paths although bent paths were canonical and accepted. Evidence is in `checks/audit/`.

**Suggested change:** provide optional source-bound probes that compare 4- versus 8-connectivity rivals and classify generated components as straight, bent, branched, holed, or irregular. The tool should distinguish “generator support restriction” from “rule/validator defect” and emit a minimal accepted counterexample when possible.

Biggest avoidable friction: staged tests need portable roots and realistic timeout tiers

Two issued canonical tests assumed the shared data tree lived beneath the selected task home, and the ray task’s exhaustive suite could not finish within the wrapper execution window. Standardize `reviewer_support.find_root` / `canonical_path` in frozen tests and expose separate fast semantic and exhaustive test tiers with checkpointed progress.

items.reason: Added opt-in labeled_only canonical reading for census rival scoring; absent query outputs skip, malformed present values and zero labeled pairs still fail. 53 related CPU tests passed.
items.text:
**Highest priority — lesson census should ignore unlabeled canonical queries only for rival-fit scoring

**Symptom.** The source-bound census completed 300/300 lessons, 1,200 pair
applications, and 1,200 query rotations with zero ambiguity, warning, or scoring
error, but returned status `error` because
`reviewer_support.canonical_pairs()` attempts to normalize the missing output of
the normal ARC test query. Evidence:
`checks/lesson-census.json` (`canonical_read_error` is exactly
`ValueError: Expected a nonempty grid`) and
`checks/lesson-census-verified.json`.

**Affected paths.** `shared/runtime/reviewer_support.py` and
`shared/tools/lesson_census.py`.

**Suggested change.** Add an explicit `labeled_only=True` option to
`canonical_pairs()`. Keep the current strict default so malformed or missing
outputs are never silently ignored by general callers. Have the census use the
option only for canonical-rival-fit scoring, because a rival can be checked only
where a reference output exists. Error if no labeled pairs remain.

**Optional patch.** `checks/feedback/F1-lesson-census-unlabeled.patch` implements
that narrow API plus a regression test. It was not applied to shared source, and
`git apply --check` succeeds from `repo/`.

No other shared-tool change is requested by this return.

items.reason: Accepted as scoped follow-up: evaluate actual materialized lessons and declared competitors, bind sources and explicit ordered/arbitrary query policy. Finite rivals are not universal identifiability. Current intake implements the task repair, not a new corpus-wide admission gate.
items.text:
Make canonical-compatible rival rotation checks an admission gate (highest priority)

**Affected tools:** `shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py`, the lesson-census path, and training-admission policy.

**Symptom/example.** In `b1e6ee6856bf`, `erase_one_bottom_cell` fits all 4 usable canonical pairs but is wrong on a lawful three-cell column. Marginal diversity, correct labels, and even canonical parity do not establish that a 3-demo/1-query lesson distinguishes it. The repaired task required an explicit larger census; final evidence is `checks/lesson-census-final.json` (300 production lessons, 1,200 required rotations, 0 ambiguity).

**Suggested change.** When `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` contains a callable that fits all canonical pairs, automatically require production-bundle identifiability and `--rotate-query` before a generator can be training-admitted. Run the current 12-lesson check first; escalate to 100 lessons/band only for surviving canonical-compatible rivals. Allow an explicit source-bound ordered-curriculum exemption rather than silently treating diagnostic rotations as a pass.

**Why shared.** The defect is at the lesson unit consumed by a model such as Qwen3.5-9B and recurs across tasks; task-local sampling tests cannot enforce corpus-wide admission semantics.

items.text:
Retain exact accepted grids for defect-lint minimal-impostor warnings

**Affected tool:** `shared/tools/generator_defect_lint.py`, detector `selfcheck-minimal-impostor`.

**Symptom/example.** The intermediate run reported only `full_one_color 3/6, solid_2x2 6/6` in `checks/defect-lint-after/checks/b1e6ee6856bf_after_defect_lint.log`. It did not retain the exact accepted grids, modal-background construction, or a replay command. I had to reconstruct the fixtures before writing the failing regression.

**Suggested change.** For each accepted impostor family, save one minimized record containing task/source hash, exact grid, family/variant, validator return, background inference, and a one-line replay command. Keep the concise aggregate log, but place exact fixtures in a JSON sidecar.

**Why shared.** This would shorten root-cause work and make lint warnings independently reviewable without changing detector policy.

items.reason: Accepted into the current shared-tool request list with source-bound evidence. Reuse existing public helpers, preserve isolation/authority checks, and qualify any shared implementation separately. Task-local repair accepted on reviewer-reported evidence.
items.text:
Add optional canonical structural-feature support checks

**Affected tools:** canonical profile floor and generator authoring contract.

**Symptom/example.** The two assigned audits expose gaps invisible to shape/palette marginals: `1409f5f7af2e` generated 0 shared-endpoint target chains in 8,000 samples although 3/5 canonical pairs contain them; `677dcb71e2be` generated 0 noncorner components in 8,000 samples although 5/5 canonical pairs contain them. Evidence: `checks/audit/1409f5f7af2e/probe-report.json` and `checks/audit/677dcb71e2be/probe-report.json`.

**Suggested change.** Support optional task-local structural observables, for example `CANONICAL_FEATURES = {name: extractor}`, and compare canonical feature values with generated support by band. Report absent canonical values as an advisory unless the task opts into a strict floor. Keep this separate from generic morphology marginals to avoid pretending there is one universal feature set.

**Why shared.** This provides a reusable way to detect relation/location shortcuts while avoiding brittle global heuristics.

items.reason: Accept lazy rule_wrap missing-dependency fix request; retain checks/tooling/ including actual traceback and source bindings. Task-local narrow verifier workaround is integrated; no general parser/shared runtime fix selected.
items.text:
Make `rule_wrap` self-contained in stripped runtimes **(top shared-tool change)

**Symptom.** `repo/shared/runtime/puzzle_generators/rule_wrap.py::convert_for_shorthand()` imports `scripts.comment_solutions`, but the review packet's stripped runtime does not contain a `scripts` package. Calling `wrap_rule()` on a rule containing `for/list` exits with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scripts'`.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/tooling/rule-wrap-missing-dependency.json` records the exact command and exit code; the traceback is in `checks/tooling/rule-wrap-missing-dependency.stderr.log`. This initially blocked use of the generic wrapper in the parametric verifier. The task-local workaround in `generators/92f4d4eb0dbb/workspace/parametric/verify.py` avoids the parser for known generated programs, but that is not a general fix.

**Proposed fix.** Move the parser/AST types needed by `convert_for_shorthand()` into the packaged `puzzle_generators` runtime (or vendor a minimal self-contained parser there), and make both authoring and stripped runtimes import that same implementation. Add a stripped-runtime test that calls `wrap_rule("(rule! (for/list (x (list 1 2)) x))")`; importing the module alone is insufficient because the missing dependency is lazy.

items.reason: Accept public source-bound arbitrary Racket program execution request; the task-local verifier and four exact programs are integrated. No new public apply-program command or variant approval selected.
items.text:
Add a public, source-bound verifier for arbitrary proposed Racket programs

**Symptom.** `arcpuzzles apply TASK_ID` verifies catalog authorities, but a task-local parametric proposal has four newly instantiated programs rather than catalog IDs. The prototype therefore uses the lower-level Racket bridge in `workspace/parametric/verify.py` to obtain exact execution evidence.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/parametric/92f4d4eb0dbb-midpoint.json` records four program hashes and exact outputs over 16 unique inputs, but this required custom bridge orchestration.

**Proposed fix.** Add a supported command such as `arcpuzzles apply-program --program PATH --input PATH --out PATH`, capped at a small batch (for example 64 grids). Its receipt should bind program bytes/hash, runtime hash, input/output hashes, command, cwd, timeout, and validation status. This would let future agents verify proposed variants without private imports or duplicated wrappers.

items.reason: Accept human-readable census progress request; deterministic checkpointing remains unchanged and no liveness claim follows from sparse console output.
items.text:
Emit periodic human-readable progress during long lesson censuses

**Symptom.** The 300-lesson, 1,200-rotation census checkpointed its report, but `checks/lesson-census-final.log` showed only wrapper setup until the final summary. During a long run, an agent cannot tell whether materialization, Racket scoring, or rotation checking is advancing from the console log alone.

**Concrete evidence.** Compare the sparse `checks/lesson-census-final.log` with the completed source-bound report `checks/lesson-census-final.summary.json`.

**Proposed fix.** Print periodic counters such as `materialized/requested`, `rotations_checked/expected`, errors, ambiguities, and checkpoint path. Keep the existing deterministic checkpointing; this is only an observability improvement.

Expose the exact selected canonical program in the packet contract. The archival base-solution text and Catalog-selected `program_solution` were execution-equivalent but byte-different, causing a protected-worker rejection; include the authoritative source/hash or a one-command pin check before authoring.

Make demonstration identifiability a first-class check

The native preflight correctly establishes that declared settings produce different labels, but that does not show the demonstrations teach the intended setting. In both assigned families, simple non-declared selectors could fit every demonstration and fail a query.

Add an optional adapter hook for a finite, task-authored rival family and require a demonstration-only survivor report. The retained implementation in this return provides a concrete pattern:

- `TEACHING_SELECTORS`
- `teaching_certificate(train, settings)`
- independent recomputation in `probe.py`

Seed sweeps can retain large grids through memoized helpers and make a correct sampler appear unstable or hang under a long-lived worker. items.text:
Highest-priority shared change — replayable joint-override seed probes

**Affected path:** `repo/shared/tools/check_generator_override_contract.py` and
the public override-check command that invokes it.

**Symptom and evidence:** The intermediate repaired generator passed all 12
battery stages in `checks/after-1/result.json`, including override checks, but
still violated exact palette conservation. With seed114, index 0, difficulty omitted (None),
8x8, five zero-bearing rows and columns, palette10, density0.4 and scatter,
a late witness write erased the last occurrence of one color. The final grid
had nine colors. The battery's bounded seed set did not exercise this case.
This is a concrete finite-coverage gap, not evidence that the battery claims
an exhaustive proof. The failure and intermediate source remain in
`checks/palette-probe/`; the focused regression is in the task patch.

**Built proposal:** `checks/tooling/exact_override_probe.py` accepts explicit
override cases and a replayable seed range, records the generator/tool/cases
hashes, checks validation and observable exact axes, and distinguishes declared
incompatibilities from errors. `cases.json`, `README.md`, command receipts,
`intermediate_failure.json` and `final_success.json` demonstrate it on 128 seeds
times four cases. The intermediate source has exactly one failing acceptance
at seed114; the final source has none. Each run contains 384 returned grids and
128 declared incompatibilities. Those incompatibilities are not passed grids.
The tool uses the public generator interface and portable root/catalog helpers,
not private Racket runner functions. It produces strict JSON with complete
failure recipes and input hashes. It is passive until deliberately invoked.

**Proposed shared fix:** Add an explicit cases file and seed-start/seed-count or
seed-list input to the existing override gate, plus exact-axis re-observation
after all generation writes. Preserve explicit incompatibility/error counts and
source-bound replay recipes. Use a modest maintained bank of joint boundary
cases; avoid unbounded Cartesian expansion by default. The prototype is useful
now and can be adapted without replacing the shared runtime. Wider numerical
coverage remains finite and does not replace semantic lesson checks.

Expose isolated test prerequisites before a long review run

**Symptom:** `checks/task-tests-final/result.json` reports infrastructure failure
and dependency_missing; no test count is available because pytest was visible
to an ordinary interpreter but absent when user-site imports were isolated.
This became apparent after substantial generator work. The gate correctly
refused to label this a test pass.

**Evidence and recovery:** `checks/runtime-setup.json` retains an initial setup
attempt that did not fix isolated imports. `checks/runtime-setup-verified.json`
records the successful isolated import check after installing locally rebuilt
pure-Python dependency wheels in a task environment. The fresh gate in
`checks/task-tests-verified/result.json` passes all54 tests with copied source
hashes and import diagnostics. Installed environments are not shipped.

**Proposed fix:** Surface the same read-only prerequisite preflight in packet
setup/start, naming the actual interpreter and isolated import mode. For offline
packets, optionally include a small hash-pinned test dependency wheel bundle or
document an available local bundle. Preserve the existing gate's infrastructure
failure status and require its real rerun after setup; do not fall back silently
to user-site imports or report missing tests as passed.

Provide a standard compact transport for large census evidence

**Symptom:** One 300-lesson source-bound census is roughly24.5MB as pretty JSON,
close to the complete return's25MiB expanded budget before before-check failures,
tests or audit evidence are added. Native bundling solves the member count but
still accounts for the bundle's expanded contents. Discarding the only retained
failure or the exact lesson instances would make replay materially worse.

**Proposed fix:** Add a documented compressed-census representation containing
the untouched raw report in gzip, its original path/size/SHA, a compact readable
summary, and a verified restoration command. The return uses this permitted
evidence-compression pattern with restoration instructions, retaining every
reported failure and full instance. A shared implementation would avoid each
reviewer inventing naming and restoration conventions. Compression does not
change whether the census passed, which source it measured, or its finite scope.

Keep query-rotation and rival-set limits prominent in teaching claims

**Evidence:** `checks/audit/4c4f94e7d611/counterexample.json` shows a canonical-
fitting undeclared rival surviving four rotated demonstrations while changing
the query, although all currently declared rivals are refuted. For
`0c1bec3fcbdc`, `findings.json` records a rotated ambiguity that the existing
guard correctly rejects. Their nominal ordered lessons have different verdicts.

**Proposed practice:** Retain the current separate production and rotation
statuses, and place the rival-set scope beside them in summaries. Add newly
reproduced rivals to each task's teaching contract and ensure repeated decisive
controls where rotations are supported. The main repair implements that local
choice with two rich slots in a four-slot cycle. A finite declared-rival pass
should never be presented as uniqueness against arbitrary hypotheses.

**Example:** `checks/task-tests/result.json` reports the preflight error at `generators/78143e5d7ed1/tests/test_generator_78143e5d7ed1.py:17`; `checks/review-tests/pytest.log` records the independent portable suite. The relevant shared code is `repo/src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py`, where any `preflight_errors` bypass pytest for all discovered tests.

**Proposed fix:** make preflight per-file. Retain every invalid fixture as a hard reported failure, but run pytest on the remaining portable files and report both result sets. The aggregate can remain non-passing while still producing counts and regression evidence. Add a test with one frozen bad-path file and one portable passing file; assert that the bad file is reported, the good file executes, and the aggregate remains failed.

items.text:
Add automatic semantic-clause ablation rivals

**Symptom:** the baseline semantic gate did not synthesize the exact omitted-height alternative that made a query rotation underdetermined. It could report nominal profile coverage while a simpler legal sort key fit all demonstrations.

**Example:** `checks/before-audit-reproducer/78143e5d7ed1/stdout.json` records `(area,width,color)` fitting all four demonstrations and changing the held-out height query. The separate `4201f3b3ea1b` audit shows the same class of problem for a local-only motif hypothesis.

**Proposed fix:** extend the semantic tooling with an opt-in declaration of semantic clauses/features and small rival factories: delete one sort key, remove one filter, localize one selected set, ignore one alignment step, or replace tight crops with filled boxes. Evaluate them under the declared query policy and retain the first exact survivor. This should remain finite-rival evidence, not an identifiability proof.

items.text:
Let the audit preset consume or run declared-period enumeration

**Symptom:** `b88894a36787` has a declared period of four and task-local tests that exhaust every query rotation, yet `--stage audit` exits 1 solely with `declared_period_not_enumerated`. The warning is valid for the random smoke test, but the preset offers no integrated route to satisfy it.

**Example:** `checks/audit/b88894a36787/full/result.json`; the target notes report a separate fixed-seed period census, while the audit semantic gate still remains warning-only.

**Proposed fix:** when `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD` is positive, either run a bounded fixed-seed enumeration automatically or accept a source-bound census receipt after validating generator/rule hashes, period, bands, expected lesson count, rotation policy, and zero errors. Keep fixed-seed coverage distinct from all-seed or universal claims.

items.text:
Emit a compact census summary alongside large lesson evidence

**Symptom:** the complete `lesson-census` report is valuable but can be tens of megabytes because it embeds every grid. A maintainer checking counts must parse a large artifact, and return-size pressure encourages reviewers to discard useful exact instances.

**Example:** `checks/lesson-census.json` is about 14 MB for 300 lessons, although the acceptance facts are a small set of hashes, counts, statuses, and replay coordinates.

**Proposed fix:** always emit a companion summary JSON containing source/rule hashes, sampling recipe, per-band counts, production/rotation verdicts, rival totals, errors, and pointers/hashes into the full report. Preserve the full report for replay, but let routine intake read the compact summary.

Biggest avoidable friction: legacy “public” payloads can include hidden parameters

Run the current strict public serializer/checker before native promotion of historical prototypes; this packet's mirror prototype labeled a parameter-bearing report as public. Keep legacy aliases private to authoring and export only content-hash-named, input-only query views.
