Suggested change: after retaining that failure, optionally run generic advertised-axis observability, strict-scalar, and repeated-window code/branch coverage probes so an audit receives more actionable evidence by default.

Biggest avoidable friction: generated task tests assumed a fixed repository depth.
The baseline suite failed only because canonical/source paths were derived from `__file__.parents`; scaffold future task tests with `reviewer_support.find_root`, `canonical_path`, and `load_selected_generator` so the same tests run in repository, packet, and staged layouts.

Add optional cyclic query rotation to the shared lesson census — highest-priority shared change

**Symptom.** The production 300-lesson census passed while the first schedule still depended on which generated pair occupied the query slot. A task-local test that rotated each of four consecutive pairs into the query position then failed 4 tests: `first_two_special_rows_only` survived all demonstrations whenever the sole third-special example was withheld as query.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/cyclic-red/result.json` shows 4 failed/61 passed. After hardening the schedule, `checks/cyclic-lesson-probe.json` shows 480/480 rotations passing.

**Proposed shared fix.** Add an opt-in `--rotate-query` mode to `arcpuzzles lesson-census` / its lesson assembly path. For each materialized N-demo + 1-query window, evaluate all N+1 choices of query, report each declared rival’s survival by rotation, and retain one compact failure record per distinct survivor. Keep the current default for cost compatibility, but let review assignments require rotation when the sampler has a short deterministic schedule.

Fail fast in override checks when required generator contract hooks are missing

**Symptom.** Audit target `ee602abaa45a` failed lint immediately for missing `RULE_HASH` and `self_check`, yet a subsequent generic override-stage invocation remained at `RUN override` until the outer 10-minute shell timeout. A direct reproducer established the actual defect in under a second: requesting 8×12 returned 13×18 because the source samples dimensions with `rng.randint` instead of the keyed exact-control API.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/audit/ee602abaa45a/lint-driver.log`, `checks/audit/ee602abaa45a/override-driver.log`, and `checks/audit/ee602abaa45a/ignored-overrides.json`.

**Proposed shared fix.** Give each override matrix case a bounded generation attempt/time budget and preflight required hooks before expanding the matrix. If `self_check` or `RULE_HASH` is absent, return a structured contract failure rather than entering the full override probe. Also print the current case key before generation so a stalled axis/value is visible.

Biggest avoidable friction: owner admission assumes three demos

`repo/src/arcpuzzles/review_parametric_admission.py` calls native `qualify` without passing demo counts, so a correctly declared family requiring four demonstrations would be retried with the default three and fail owner admission. Select a bounded count from the promotion contract (prefer three when supported, otherwise its declared minimum); this family supports three and is not blocked by that issue.

Cache or expose the prepared check runtime.** `python3 ../run_with_racket.py python3 -m arcpuzzles check 557449d8b860 --stage lint --phase after ...` spent more than six minutes before producing a receipt, although the underlying lint stage later completed in 18 seconds. The expensive repository staging should be cached by packet/source hash, and the CLI should print the prepared runtime path so all twelve per-stage invocations can reuse it safely.

Make stage completion coincide with parent-process exit.** Several per-stage runs printed `PASS` and had complete `.ok` and `.receipt` files, but the parent shell remained alive long enough for the command transport to time out. The stage runner should close inherited descriptors and exit immediately after atomically publishing its receipt; rebuilding the aggregate summary can be a separate `--status` operation.

Keep successful override evidence compact by default.** The repaired override stage had zero findings but wrote a 2.1 MB `override_results.json` for 21,150 accepted draws. Retain the case manifest, aggregate counts, and a deterministic hash by default; make the full per-draw trace opt-in or compressed. That would reduce return size without losing reproducibility.

Separate structural and palette-symmetry mutations in `self_check` reporting.** Swapping two foreground colors is lawful for this color-symmetric gravity task, while blanking the grid is not. The current combined mutation-sensitivity total is useful as a smoke signal but can be misread as a target rejection rate. Report structural, palette, and geometry mutation classes separately and never imply that a palette-symmetric generator should reject color renaming.

The static linter findings were actionable and accurate here.** It correctly identified the missing `RULE_HASH` and the unprobeable single-token axes before expensive execution. No linter false positive was found for task `557449d8b860`.

items.text:
Let lesson-census emit a ready-to-commit first counterexample

**Symptom.** The census correctly retained a large report, but turning the first 29-KB ambiguity record into a focused regression required manual extraction and normalization. The resulting task-local witness is `repo/generators/97bcb3b9194e/counterexamples/review-5dbe0af1a8250935-v0001/lesson-ambiguity-before.json`.

**Suggested change.** Add `--emit-first-counterexample DIR` to `lesson-census`. Write the four complete pairs, exact generation recipe, source/rule hashes, rival name, demo-fit verdict, differing canonical/rival query outputs, and a tiny replay script. This would make failed curricula immediately actionable for future agents.

Biggest avoidable friction: staged task tests retain a full runtime copy

Each `review.py task-tests` run left an approximately 6.9 MB `checks/.../task-tests/runtime/` tree even though the compact result, source binding, log, and JUnit XML were sufficient for the return. Have the staged runner delete or place that runtime outside retained `checks/` after completion; this avoids manual pruning and accidental transport of a duplicated runtime.

Biggest avoidable friction: obsolete native prototype inventory status

The retained prototype used `reviewer_reported_with_independently_exercised_public_identifier_correction`, which the current native promotion reader rejects; rebuild such inventories with the existing manifest helper during packet preparation, or surface that exact incompatibility in `review.py start` so the reviewer can repair it immediately.

Biggest avoidable friction: public-creation preflight has no first-class sequential public-projection/privacy gate.
Each task required a nearly identical source-bound audit for one-query views, hidden future queries, private settings/programs/answers, and first-turn invariance. Add a reusable `review_public_creation projection-audit` command that consumes `preflight.json` and an adapter, emits the standard receipt, and tests total-query-count independence plus private-field mutations.

Ignore runtime caches when computing resumable battery subject hashes — shared-tool change most needed

**Symptom.** Running focused Python tests created cache artifacts under the selected task. The generator file remained byte-identical at SHA-256 `33ec3a6cd523fc37a16a282f83ca44f7c26d7f081cf5bf561f1394e63405ac72`, but battery summaries moved from subject `af9768a8da117b11` to `5fce2a3f3ceecab3`, making otherwise valid checkpoints non-resumable/noisy. Compare `checks/retained/subject-af9768a8da117b11.json` with `checks/final-battery/checks/bbbec840ce41_after_battery_summary.json`.

**Proposed fix.** In the source-manifest/subject hashing path used by `arcpuzzles check`, whitelist source-bearing task files or at minimum exclude `__pycache__/`, `.pytest_cache/`, `*.pyc`, and `*.pyo`, matching the exclusions already used by the return packager. Keep the generator-file hash and a separate declared-source hash in receipts so cache cleanup cannot invalidate semantic evidence.

Add `--resume` to `lesson-census`

**Symptom.** The census checkpoints completed lessons internally, but the public command has no resume interface. A single all-band 300-lesson rotation run can outlive a caller window; this review had to retain three separate 100-lesson files (`checks/lesson-census-easy.json`, `-medium.json`, and `-hard.json`) even though the logical job was one census.

**Proposed fix.** Add `lesson-census --resume --out PATH`. Bind the checkpoint to generator hash, authority hash, rival/hook hash, seed, per-band count, difficulty selection, and rotation policy. Resume only unfinished lessons and preserve prior failures. This would reduce duplicated materialization and make large identifiability gates easier to run reliably.

Make canonical semantic-support absence a blocking or waivable gate

**Symptom:** `scripts/check_canonical_profile_floor.py` currently emphasizes
coarse profiles such as dimensions and palette size, while the semantic gate
relies on task-authored hooks. The imported `7b0c20fe6f33` therefore had no
blocking automatic check for its most important distribution defect: 300/300
natural samples had four green cells and only four short vectors, whereas every
canonical example had a three-cell object and a much larger marker vector.
Baseline evidence is in
`checks/before/checks/7b0c20fe6f33_before_profile_floor.log` and the prior audit
record in `generators/7b0c20fe6f33/evidence/review_index.json`.

**Suggested shared fix:** extend the profile-floor tool (or add a neighboring
`canonical_semantic_support` stage) to compare canonical and generated support
for generic object/component counts, displacement vectors between singleton
colors, bounding-box shapes, and output-change counts. Merge task-provided
`observe_overrides`/`semantic_observables` when available. Report exact missing
features and require either support in each intended training mix or a reviewed
waiver. Start as advisory to tune role-extraction false positives, then make
unwaived total absence blocking.

This is the highest-priority shared change; the task-local repair and tests are
already included in this return.

public-creation test dispatch

The packet requests `task-tests` for new public IDs, but the wrapper resolves only owner-registered catalog entries and fails with `Unknown puzzle`; both actual failures are retained. Add a source-home test-dispatch path for unregistered public-creation assignments, or explicitly document the direct task-local pytest command used here. Do not require reviewers to register owner authority merely to execute tests.

Separate presence coverage from rival-bearing semantic witnesses — **top shared-tool change

**Symptom.** `SEMANTIC_WITNESSES` currently treats every entry as if it should have a `WITNESS_RIVALS` claim. Legitimate presence/coverage probes—canonical-profile frequency, no-clipping coverage, and shift-quadrant coverage—produce `WEAK` warnings, and the semantic stage exits 1 even when all lessons and required query rotations are unambiguous. The concrete intermediate report is `checks/required-rotations-final/checks/ae7376fe4957_after_semantic_gate.json`: 0/48 ambiguous rotations and zero errors, but six presence-only warnings made the stage non-green.

**Proposed fix.** Add a separate public declaration such as `COVERAGE_WITNESSES`, or allow per-witness metadata like `{"predicate": fn, "kind": "presence_only"}`. Keep rival-bearing `SEMANTIC_WITNESSES` strict, but report declared presence coverage without a blocking weak-witness warning. I removed the six presence-only entries locally and retained direct task-test coverage, but this distinction belongs in the shared contract.

stdout tail as well as stderr in the command receipt/error. The worker emits structured

retain the partial receipt and bounded child diagnostics. This would distinguish a

Biggest avoidable friction: qualification summary omits execution counts

**Priority: highest shared-tool change.** The public override stage can emit
multi-megabyte JSON with tens of thousands of repeated findings. Audit targets
`d9829b956366` and `8c73e339d80e` produced 13,595+ and 14,073+ findings, plus
22,410 and 28,380 legacy multi-axis rejections; see
`checks/audit-*-override/`. The documented compact mode exists only through a
separate prepared workspace script.

Suggested change: add `--compact-results` (and optionally `--max-examples-per-root-cause`)
directly to `arcpuzzles check --stage override` and battery runs. Preserve exact
totals, provenance, and one or a few representative cases per normalized root
cause while omitting repetitive successful/failed case rows. This would make
baseline batteries faster to retain and easier for future agents to inspect
without weakening the contract.

Make wrapper-relative path mistakes fail before invoking pytest

`run_with_racket.py` correctly announces that payload paths are relative to
`repo/`, but a natural command using
`repo/generators/96c1983b6cb5/tests/test_generator.py` still launches pytest and
returns “file not found.” The preserved harness-only error is in
`checks/tdd-green-attempt1/pytest.log`.

working directory is already `repo`, print a targeted correction and exit
before launching, or safely strip one leading `repo/` for path-valued arguments.
The current notice is useful but easy to miss in long autonomous runs.

Distinguish completed interrupted batteries in the top-level `result.json`

After an externally killed/resumed baseline run, `checks/before/result.json`
remained `status: running` even though no process remained and useful stage
receipts had been checkpointed. The detailed battery summary and live-lock data
allow reconstruction, but the top-level state is easy to misread.

Suggested change: on the next status/read operation, detect a dead recorded PID
and rewrite or overlay the verdict as `interrupted_resumable`, preserving the
last completed stages and original run ID. This would reduce accidental claims
that a partial battery either passed or is still active.

items.text:
Reconcile completed child receipts before reporting controller interruption

**Symptom.** A check controller can time out or receive termination just after a
child stage has already written a complete failing receipt. The outer result is
then labelled `interrupted`, forcing a reviewer to inspect multiple files to
recover the actual verdict.

**Concrete example.** In
`checks/audit/f3672f3f540b-defect-lint/`, the stage log and receipt show a
completed defect-lint failure (`1 issue`, `232 warnings`, detector counts
`strict-scalar=228`, `texture-dead=4`, `texture-domain-overlap=1`). However,
`result.json` says `status: interrupted` because the Python controller received
signal 15 after the receipt was present. The battery summary reconstructed the
stage as failed, but the top-level status remained interrupted.

**Suggested shared-tool change.** In the check controller’s timeout/termination
handler, after stopping or observing the child, atomically reread the stage
receipt and journal. If they prove that the requested stage reached a terminal
state for the same run/source hash, synthesize `status: completed`, preserve the
controller interruption as a secondary diagnostic, and return the stage’s real
exit code. Only use `interrupted` when no source-bound terminal receipt exists.
This would make automation and human intake agree without weakening timeout
safety.

items.text:
Aggregate repetitive defect-lint scalar findings while retaining raw rows

**Symptom.** The baseline focused defect lint produced 228 strict scalar findings,
many repeating the same range/profile problem across seeds and bands. The full
rows are useful evidence, but the console/log makes it harder to identify the
few root causes: oversized dimensions, object-count fragmentation, palette
mismatch, and ignored overrides. Evidence is retained in
`checks/before-defect-lint/`.

**Suggested shared-tool change.** Add a compact summary grouped by check ID,
axis, observed range, and representative seed/input hash, with counts per band.
Keep the complete machine-readable rows unchanged in JSON. The human-facing log
could then lead with four or five causal groups while preserving every witness
for replay.

Check canonical admission before trusting generator coverage

**Symptom:** A1: `d414585aa873` rejects canonical train examples 1 and 3 because its moat restriction excludes overlap. Yet all 600 generated pairs are validator-accepted and Racket-correct. A per-generated-case gate misses the omitted canonical branch.

**Evidence:** `checks/audit_probe.json`, target `d414585aa873`, `canonical`; `checks/counterexamples/d414585aa873_canonical_overlap.json`.

**Proposed change:** Add a canonical-input validation/admission stage, distinguish strict canonical from intentionally narrowed generation domains, and require a reviewed exception rather than automatically classifying rejected canonical cases as invalid. Also compare a branch-sensitive rival on canonical and generated cases. The task-local audit tool already emits this distinction; it is a reusable prototype, not a shared-policy change.

Evaluate query-changing rivals per lesson and count unique scenes

**Symptom:** M2: two wrong rules fit all canonical and 900 baseline synthetic pairs. B1: `4199aa353fa1` has an unresolved control rival that changes the query in 116/360 four-demo/query windows despite 600/600 individually valid draws. M5: an intermediate main candidate passed the usual battery but repeated scenes across bands (492/900 unique).

**Evidence:** `checks/census_before.json`, `checks/census_final.json`, `checks/census_final_v2.json`, `checks/cross_band_before.log`, and `checks/counterexamples/4199aa353fa1_unidentified_control.json`.

**Proposed change:** Report explicit candidate-family coverage at the episode level: rival fits all demos AND changes query. Separate draws, unique inputs, unique outputs and overlapping windows; never imply overlapping windows are independent. Include deterministic cross-band duplication checks. The new `workspace/review_probe.py` implements source-bound real-Racket census and saved rival witnesses; its finite scope is explicit. Do not relabel a no-rival task “identifiable” merely because there are no registered candidates.

Test override effects and whole-input grammar, not successful calls

**Symptom:** M3's old advertised controls were inert/misleading; A2's `rect_min_h=6` produces two height-5 rectangles. B2 accepts a required-anchor deletion and Racket silently returns a nonempty output. Generic successful-call coverage alone is insufficient.

**Evidence:** `checks/before/checks/11ebef5b0986_before_override_results.json`; `checks/counterexamples/d414585aa873_ignored_rect_min_h.json`; `checks/counterexamples/4199aa353fa1_missing_anchor_passes_validator.json`.

**Proposed change:** Require axis-specific measurable postconditions, full legal ranges independent of difficulty defaults, infeasible-combination errors, unknown-key rejection, and negative structural mutations. Remove no-op axes rather than inventing unrelated visual effects. The main task now has explicit regression coverage for these contracts. The existing override and authority gates caught real main-task issues and should not be weakened.

Decouple timeout-retention tests from ordinary interpreter startup

**Symptom:** T1: the root suite has 169 passes and one failure in `test_streaming_timeout_retains_progress_and_stops_child`; the isolated test also fails. Its 0.2-second timeout expires before this environment's ordinary Python interpreter emits its first line.

**Evidence:** `checks/repo_suite.log`, `checks/repo_timeout_isolated.log`, `checks/runtime_timeout_diagnostic.json`. Three normal startup trials produced first output at 0.423–0.451 seconds; all three original-timeout trials had no output. All three `python -S` timeout trials retained the expected line; all three one-second normal-Python timeout trials also retained it. The shared runtime/test hashes match the original packet.

**Proposed change:** Use a controlled lightweight child (for this stdlib-only test, `sys.executable, "-S", "-c", ...`) and separate “process is forcibly stopped” from “already-emitted progress is retained.” A startup handshake or a generous outer deadline can make the retained-progress prerequisite explicit. Do not loosen production timeout handling or classify genuinely lost emitted output as harmless. The read-only diagnostic script is included; shared source remains unmodified and the original suite failure remains reported.

Normalize canonical pair encodings and stage real runtimes in probes

**Symptom:** The first reusable-probe attempt could not import `scripts.comment_solutions` from the shallow shared-runtime layout. A further regression exposed both list and single-dict canonical `test` encodings. Hand-written direct imports and assumed schemas make otherwise useful audits brittle.

**Evidence:** `checks/probe_smoke.log` (retained failed attempt), `checks/probe_smoke_fixed.log`, `checks/tools_tests_before.log`, `checks/task_tests_final_v2.log`, and `checks/census_dict_encoding.json` (30 real-Racket draws and five canonical pairs for `4199aa353fa1`).

**Proposed change:** Offer a shared, validated canonical-pair iterator and a small probe API built on `Catalog` plus `prepare_runtime`, with actual runtime location and source hashes in every receipt. The task-local tool now does this without patching shared code. Preserve failed setup evidence separately from semantic generator failures, and avoid asserting output correctness from a Python mirror without independent Racket execution.

Biggest avoidable friction: public creation IDs cannot reach ordinary generation

The creation API issues `public_eval_<8hex>` identifiers but the shared runner's
hex-only rule-ID guard rejects them even after registration; admit precisely that
namespace and add a copied-runtime public-creation regression before issuing new
packets. A minimal proposed patch and RED/GREEN 22-case reproducer are included
in checks/, with no shared-source edit or owner-approval claim.

Emit controller heartbeats and flush stage progress during long checks

**Symptom.** Several foreground check invocations appeared stalled because controller output was not flushed while a native stage was running. The surrounding execution harness terminated the controller session, even though stage subprocesses/checkpoints were healthy. The repair was recoverable through hash-verified `--resume`, but distinguishing “quiet, running stage” from “hung process” required inspecting PIDs and checkpoint files.

**Concrete evidence.**

- `checks/after-controller-resume.log`
- retained interrupted attempts/checkpoints under `checks/after/`
- the final summary correctly reports no interruption only after the resumed unchanged-source run completed

**Suggested change.** While a stage is alive, write a timestamped heartbeat to both stdout and `progress.log` at a modest interval, including stage name, elapsed time, remaining allowance, and child PID. Use line-buffered output or explicit flushes after `RUN`, `LIMIT`, checkpoint-save, and heartbeat records. This would help interactive agents avoid killing healthy work and would make checkpoint resume less dependent on low-level process inspection.

items.text:
Surface source-bound check summaries in a compact machine-readable index

**Symptom.** The decisive facts for a return are spread across battery summary, stage JSON, portable task-test `result.json`, census companion, solve summary, and controller logs. The packager validates evidence, but reviewers still need custom parsing to assemble final hash, test count, profile count, lesson count, and rotation verdict.

**Concrete evidence.** The maintainer brief in `REVIEW.md` required values from `checks/after/checks/...battery_summary.json`, `checks/task-tests/`, `checks/lesson-census.summary.json`, and `solve/summary.json`.

**Suggested change.** Add an optional `arcpuzzles review-summary TASK --checks-root ...` command that emits one JSON object with source/rule hashes, final battery counts, task-test collected/passed/failed counts, profile support, lesson/rotation counts, solve binding, and links to the original evidence. It should copy—not reinterpret—the source reports and mark missing values unknown.

Expand the generic semantic-rival library

**Symptom.** An official all-green intermediate battery did not detect that
“choose the red object with maximum bounding-box area” fit every canonical pair
and could survive a generated lesson. The semantic gate can only test rivals a
generator author already declared.

**Evidence.** The exact canonical-fitting rival and final counterexample are in
`repo/generators/db98b701e5bb/counterexamples/largest_bbox_area.json`; the
supported authority output is `checks/shortcut-counterexample-final/racket.json`.

**Suggested change.** For object-selection tasks, automatically fit a small
shared library of pure candidate rules against canonical pairs—scan rank, size,
width, height, bounding-box area, perimeter, compactness, and color rank. Report
canonical-fitting candidates and require either a declared rival/witness or an
explicit task-specific rejection. This should be advisory until domain typing is
reliable, but it would surface missed shortcuts before a reviewer has to invent
them.

Make long battery/census execution first-class resumable jobs

**Symptom.** Long commands can outlive an interactive tool-call transport even
though the underlying checker is healthy. The checker has excellent stage
checkpoints, but callers currently need to launch a detached process and poll
logs manually to avoid mistaking transport interruption for test failure.

**Evidence.** The retained interrupted attempts under `checks/before/` and
`checks/after/` are distinguishable from the completed final run under
`checks/after-v31-final/`, but reaching that state required manual process
management.

**Suggested change.** Add `review.py start-job/status-job/wait-job` wrappers that
persist PID, exact argv, source hash, output directory, and final exit status.
They should expose the current stage and reject source drift before resume.

Surface comment-only authority divergence more directly

**Symptom.** `defect_lint` and `authority_sync` correctly failed, but the root
cause was an active archived target string differing from canonical only by a
comment. The actionable diagnosis was buried among broader source checks.

**Suggested change.** When parsed behavior/rule hash matches but exact text does
not, emit a dedicated “comment/whitespace-only selected-authority drift” finding
with both JSON field paths and whether the assignment permits synchronization.

Shared canonical-pair decoding should be a public helper (highest priority)

**Symptom.** The first source-bound lesson probe treated compact string rows as
already-decoded grids.  Its canonical-fit precheck therefore produced a false
failure even though 300 generated lessons and Racket execution were otherwise
clean.  Evidence: `checks/lesson-probe-failed-v1.json` and
`checks/lesson-probe-tdd-red.log`.

**Suggested change.** Add one public normalization function in the shared
`arcpuzzles` canonical-data API that returns every train/test pair as
`list[list[int]]`, and have semantic-gate/probe templates consume it.  This
would eliminate repeated ad hoc `if isinstance(row, str)` decoders and make
canonical shortcut checks less error-prone.  No shared patch is included here
because this assignment permits only the selected task delta.

Semantic gate should distinguish “missing proof” from “bad distribution” and scaffold the proof surface

**Symptom.** Both audit targets fail `semantic_gate` only with “no semantic
contract declared.”  For `dc657616ec21`, an independent probe then found a
specific canonical-fit bbox-radius rival surviving 15/400 easy, 35/400 medium,
and 66/400 hard cyclic three-demo windows.  The generic message does not guide
a maintainer from missing hooks to that lesson-level risk.  Evidence:
`checks/audit-stage/dc-semantic/` and
`checks/audit/dc657616ec21/rival_probe.json`.

**Suggested change.** When no contract exists, emit a compact scaffold naming
expected hooks and a machine-readable template for at least one rival, witness,
and `lesson_identifiable`.  Optionally run a small library of clearly labeled
diagnostic rivals (bbox side, area, color, object count) without treating them
as task truth.

Authority-sync could offer a safe comment-only normalization patch

**Symptom.** The baseline authority-sync failure was caused by one comment in
one active Racket copy; executable behavior and whitespace/comment-stripped
forms agreed.  Repair required locating the duplicate and deleting the comment
manually.

**Suggested change.** When exact text differs but comment-stripped normalized
hashes and execution parity agree, print both paths and offer a generated
comment-only synchronization patch.  Keep the stage blocking, but make the
safe resolution explicit.

Override reports need root-cause compression for audit use

**Symptom.** The `b45771715d10` audit produced 16,000+ displayed findings and a
results file with 4,860 override mismatches, 1,260 generation errors, and
10,530 self-check findings.  The useful causes are simple—ignored code axes,
difficulty-clamped declared domains, singleton/inert axes, and unknown-key
acceptance—but they are buried in repeated cases.  Evidence:
`checks/audit-stage/b45-override/checks/b45771715d10_after_override_results.json`.

**Suggested change.** Keep the full case file, but make the console and summary
rank one representative per `(axis, category, root cause)` with counts and a
minimal replay.  This would preserve rigor while making adversarial reviews
much faster to triage.

**Symptom.** In this environment, the after battery twice stopped producing controller output while a short stage was running. The first call ended after starting `defect_lint`; the first resume ended after starting `diversity`; the second resume ended after `racket_lint`. **Suggested change.** Have the public battery controller emit a timestamped top-level heartbeat while each child stage runs (for example every 10–15 seconds), atomically record the child PID and last-output time, and on controller teardown write an explicit interrupted attempt receipt before releasing the lock. On the next `--resume`, report whether the prior child is alive, stale, or completed-but-unjournaled in one concise line. This is a shared runner usability improvement; no shared patch is included in this task-local return.

**Symptom.** The current semantic framework primarily evaluates per-grid rival
functions. `d62a0e470ae8` passes all 12 battery stages, including its declared
semantic competitors, while a learner can ignore the corner key: for each fixed
lesson seed, both `key` and `n_distractors` advance with the same sample-index
coefficient modulo four. Four demos reveal the offset, and distractor count then
predicts the query transform.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/audit/d62a0e470ae8/probe.json` evaluates 300
five-pair lessons and every query rotation on source SHA
`ec7545cf16e4e43fe7bdc944b4799d6773ced15f4db69c34bb2db37ee84a07dd`;
the adaptive proxy matches 1,500/1,500 Racket-labelled queries. A lawful
counterfactual changes only the key and breaks the proxy. The ordinary battery
summary in `checks/audit/d62a0e470ae8/battery/` is nevertheless 12/12 green.

**Proposed fix.** Extend `shared/tools/lesson_census.py` with either (a) an API for
competitors that receive demonstrations before predicting the query, or (b) a
generic scheduled-axis leakage diagnostic. For every observable axis pair, fit a
small deterministic mapping on demos and test whether it predicts a semantic
query control; report perfect/near-perfect within-lesson predictability and retain
a lawful counterfactual. Keep it diagnostic by default because correlated axes
can be intentional.

The reusable reproducer `checks/audit/d62a0e470ae8/probe_distractor_proxy.py`
shows the minimal interface and counterfactual record needed.

battery fails only `semantic_gate` because it declares no strict hook, witnesses,

changes the query in 74/900 production-shaped lessons and 354/4,500 rotations.

generator whose current source has `NO_CONTRACT` under the required semantic

special-case rival, `LESSON_COMPETITORS`, and a task-local rotation test from the
existing `rule_mirror`. This turns a loud battery failure into an actionable
repair rather than a status mismatch.

items.text:
Add an optional finite schedule-phase enumerator to `lesson-census`

**Symptom.** The shared census samples consecutive starts and reports residues,
but explicitly does not enumerate every cyclic start. For a generator with a tiny
declared period, reviewers still need a task-local script to prove every phase can
start a complete lesson.

**Concrete evidence.** This return adds
`repo/generators/ff5eb7af92e7/workspace/probe_schedule_phases.py`; its report
`checks/schedule-phase-probe.json` covers 3 bands × 3 start phases, 36 Racket
applications, and every query rotation.

**Proposed shared fix.** Support an optional generator hook such as
`SCHEDULE_PERIOD` plus `schedule_profile`, or a CLI option like
`lesson-census --enumerate-schedule-period N`. The output should keep the current
finite-scope warning, iterate the generator's declared rivals, and bind labels to
the public Racket authority. This would remove repeated bespoke probes without
pretending to enumerate all seed identities.

Add an optional observed-witness gate for canonical-fitting rivals

**Priority shared-tool improvement.** Add an opt-in mode alongside the public `arcpuzzles check --stage semantic_gate` workflow, using the included task-local probe as the concrete implementation example.

**Symptom.** Successful generation and positive examples can leave simpler predicate alternatives indistinguishable from the selected rule. This creates a concrete support gap even when reference labels are correct.

**Evidence.** The reusable [predicate witness probe](repo/generators/7494855fa379/workspace/probe_predicate_witnesses.py) found four simple rivals fitting all three canonical labels for `7494855fa379`. Across 72 baseline direct generation inputs, none was refuted: twelve required per-band unknown/gaps; optional gate exit 1. The preserved intermediate repair, source `cfcace6a4a3363bd49a6db129eb2521db8bd170c02a322c38a23c305295a0c70`, refuted each rival on 16/24 inputs in each band with no gaps. Five retained first witnesses were executed through actual Racket and matched the mirror. These intermediate counts belong to their recorded source. The final version 3.2 [predicate report](checks/predicate-probe/repaired-final.json), bound to source `e8a0b3d73133b90b1fb605adc877d638413533391b8994e9891355425403985f`, records **72 draws**, **12/24 refutations per simple rival in each band**, **zero gaps/errors**, and **five selected actual Racket witnesses**, all agreeing with the mirror. Its [command receipt](checks/final-verification/probe-final.receipt.json) records exit 0. The final period-2 schedule changes the finite contrast rate; this does not itself measure learner value. Receipts are [baseline.json](checks/predicate-probe/baseline.json), [repaired.json](checks/predicate-probe/repaired.json), and [commands.json](checks/predicate-probe/commands.json).

Separate final [lesson-census evidence](checks/lesson-census-final.json) records 300 materialized lessons, 1,200 rotations and 809 unique inputs with no measured ambiguity or errors. The [fixed-seed schedule census](checks/schedule-census-final.json) covers starts 0 and 1 at seed 0 in all bands: 6 lessons, 24 rotations and 11 unique inputs, with `complete_fixed_seed` coverage and no measured ambiguity or errors. Both bind the final generator hash. Their finite lesson-level results remain distinct from the direct-draw witness gate.

The independent `54875f792be0` audit also confirms a retained unresolved canonical-fitting shape shortcut on unchanged source. A fresh validator-accepted equal-perimeter nonrectangular closed loop separates it from the actual reference. See [AUDIT.md](AUDIT.md).

**Proposed fix.** Retain the runnable task-local tool and consider an opt-in observed-witness check: canonical fit, per-band refutation counts, exact first witness, source/rule hashes, replay settings, and explicit unknown/gaps. Separate Python-mirror diagnostics from actual reference labels. The implementation uses public helpers/source loading and `Catalog.apply`, without private runner imports; copied runtimes without a Catalog library report reference execution as skipped/unknown.

Keep the gate optional. Small ranges, rare support, intentional schedules, and answer-equivalent declarations can create false alarms. A finite pass does not prove complete coverage, identifiable materialized lessons, approval, or value for a particular learner. It introduces no mandatory intake or battery stage.

Provision isolated task-test prerequisites in the selected interpreter

**Symptom.** A task-test command can fail before collecting tests because the exact isolated interpreter lacks a required package. Imports in another environment do not establish the child interpreter's prerequisites.

**Evidence.** [The initial task-test receipt](checks/task-tests/result.json) records `status: infrastructure_failed`, `test_status: dependency_missing`, missing `pytest`, exit 2, and unknown test counts. The interpreter was `/opt/codex/runtimes/codex-primary-runtime/dependencies/python/bin/python3`. This was an infrastructure failure, not a generator test failure.

After using a provisioned isolated interpreter, [the final receipt](checks/task-tests-final/result.json) records successful prerequisite preflight, `test_status: executed`, **98 passed, zero failed/errors/skipped**, and exit 0. The selected interpreter was `/dev/arc-review-task-tests/venv/bin/python`, with pytest, NumPy, and Pillow present.

**Proposed fix.** Make packet setup expose a straightforward command to create a review environment and install the documented prerequisites into the interpreter that will run the tests. Route that interpreter consistently through the wrapper and its test child. Keep isolation enabled and preserve the existing public preflight's actionable infrastructure classification. Check prerequisites before staging an expensive runtime or interpreting any absent test results as code failures.

The repair resolved this run's prerequisite problem. This feedback concerns setup ergonomics and reproducibility; it does not request weaker isolation or a new generator acceptance gate.

items.text:
Make long battery progress visible through the wrapper

**Symptom.** Full batteries can spend several minutes inside a stage. Stage
checkpoints are excellent, but the wrapper's foreground output may remain static,
which encourages accidental relaunches or premature timeout assumptions.

**Suggested change.** Echo a periodic elapsed/stage heartbeat from the existing
checkpoint state and atomically write the wrapper PID/final exit status beside
`progress.log`. A client could then attach to an existing source-bound run instead
of launching a duplicate.

Add bounded composite-rival mining to the semantic gate

**Top shared-tool change.** `repo/shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` and `repo/shared/tools/lesson_census.py` currently score declared rivals well, but they do not discover small conjunctions of otherwise visible features. In this task, the unary `bbox_missing_interior` shortcut was declared and refuted, yet `bbox_missing_interior AND cell_count >= 8` fit 4/4 canonical pairs and every 600/600 plus 720/720 retained generated pair. Evidence: `repo/generators/629ec8fd452e/counterexamples/review-6260ee24a1c08425-v0001/resolution.json` and the two imported audit directories.

Proposed fix: add an optional public hook that exposes a finite set of named object-level Boolean/numeric features, then let the shared semantic gate enumerate unary thresholds at observed values plus pairwise Boolean conjunctions/disjunctions. Candidates that fit all demonstrations but disagree on a lawful query should be reported with the first source-bound instance and Racket label. Keep the search bounded and advisory unless the generator declares that feature grammar authoritative; this limits false positives and cost. The task-local `workspace/probe_final_support.py` demonstrates the evidence shape, but the synthesis belongs in the shared gate.

Extend strict-scalar linting to all top-level generator arguments

`repo/shared/tools/generator_defect_lint.py` / `repo/shared/runtime/review_diagnostics.py` caught invalid `sample_index` and override scalars in the assigned generator, but the audit of `a06827026857` shows a remaining blind spot: bool/float/string seeds, `True`/`False`/negative sample indices, and unknown string/integer difficulty values were all accepted and returned self-check-clean grids. Its existing task tests still passed 64/64. Evidence: `checks/audit/a06827026857/scalar-contract-report.json`.

Proposed fix: make the strict-scalar detector always probe `seed`, `sample_index`, and `difficulty` in addition to declared axes. Require literal integer seed, literal nonnegative integer sample index, and either `None` or a declared difficulty enum. Report each accepted invalid value under the same `strict-scalar` category so a generator cannot pass by validating only `**overrides`.

Provide a standard source-bound semantic-support probe template

Reviewers repeatedly need the same compact report: selected source SHA, canonical shortcut fit, validator errors, witness support, rival disagreement, role/size overlap, and strict-call rejection. Reconstructing that logic task by task increases inconsistency and makes future agents miss checks.

Proposed fix: add a small public helper or documented template beside `reviewer_support` that accepts a task ID and draw count, resolves the selected generator in repository or staged layouts, and emits a stable JSON schema. The new task-local `repo/generators/629ec8fd452e/workspace/probe_final_support.py` is a concrete working example. It sampled 192 scenes and made the repaired curriculum's support and limitations visible in one report (`checks/repair-probe-rerun.json`).

Biggest avoidable friction: stale parametric manifests do not identify the changed inventory rows

Symptom: native qualification stopped with only `evidence_changed_or_missing`
after the adapter and prototype changed. Determining whether the blocker was the
current generator, rule binding, evidence receipt, or one of many inventoried
files required manually reading the readiness code and comparing hashes.

Evidence: the retained manifest for `8291f3ee7e54` contained 24 bound files and
an external-correction hold. After archiving it and rebuilding a current 11-file
inventory from the focused tests and self-audit, the same qualification command
passed four jobs without any adapter change.

Suggested change: when `_prototype` finds a stale inventory, report the first few
missing or hash-mismatched paths and the current manifest hash, then print the
safe `parametric manifest ... --replace <hash>` shape (or say that a pending hold
must be archived/resolved first). Keep qualification fail-closed, but make the
repair source-specific instead of requiring code archaeology.

Make the battery controller resilient to a closed stdout pipe

**Priority:** top shared-tool change.

**Symptom:** the aggregate battery completed ten source-bound stages, then the controller process terminated with `BrokenPipeError` while emitting progress for `racket_lint`. All completed stage receipts were valid, and an exact `--resume` skipped those ten hashes and completed the remaining two stages. The retained resume trace is `checks/after-final/progress.log`; it shows the first run reaching `RUN racket_lint`, followed by `RESUME`, ten hash-matched `SKIP` records, then green `racket_lint` and `authority_sync`.

**Proposed fix:** in the controller behind `review.py check`, treat EPIPE/BrokenPipe on user-facing stdout as a reporting-channel failure rather than a child-stage failure. Continue writing progress/result/journal files through a file handle, finalize the current stage receipt and battery summary in `finally`, and suppress further console writes after the first EPIPE. This would make long checks robust to notebook/container transport limits without changing stage semantics.

Promote low-complexity shortcut mining to a shared approval gate

**Symptom:** all canonical outputs for this task were also explained by “recolor a size-two component.” Correct labels, morphology marginals, and canonical support did not reveal that lesson-level ambiguity. The exact reproducer is `repo/generators/d93294819fca/counterexamples/fixed-size-two.json`; the source-bound lesson evidence is `checks/lesson-census-100.summary.json`.

**Proposed fix:** extend the semantic gate or `lesson-census` to automatically synthesize a bounded library of rank/size/color/bounding-box/partial-edit rivals that fit canonical pairs, then require query-rotation refutation for any rival that changes a lawful query. Retain a minimal witness and distinguish “equivalent on declared support” from a blocking ambiguity. This should be shared rather than copied into each generator.

Include exact task-test counts in the aggregate battery summary

**Symptom:** `task_tests` is a separate stage from the 12-stage generator battery. Intake therefore has to combine `checks/after-final/checks/d93294819fca_after_battery_summary.json` with `checks/focused-task_tests-after3/result.json` to learn that 109 tests passed.

**Proposed fix:** allow the aggregate summary to reference the latest source-matched task-test receipt and report its pass/fail/count without treating it as one of the generator gates. That keeps the concise maintainer brief source-bound and reduces manual evidence stitching.

items.text:
Make the fresh-packet `git apply` command prefix-safe

**Symptom:** With the isolated Git root initialized at the packet root and the
command run from `WORK/`, plain `git apply --check source.patch` and `git apply
source.patch` returned exit 0 while skipping every `repo/...` path. The generator
remained at its baseline hash and the newly added test file was absent.

**Evidence:** `checks/fresh-handoff/attempt-1.md`. The successful replay in
`checks/fresh-handoff/replay.log` uses `git apply --check --directory=WORK` and
`git apply --directory=WORK`, then obtains the final generator hash and 69 passing
tests.

**Suggested change:** Update `RETURN-GUIDE.md` to either initialize the isolated
Git root at `WORK/`, or show `--directory=WORK` explicitly when the root is the
packet directory. Also require a post-apply changed-path or source-hash assertion,
so an all-skipped exit-0 apply cannot masquerade as a replay.

Estimate and bound override-matrix cost before execution

**Symptom.** The first repaired contract used integer dimensions `12..18`. The
override checker expanded each seven-value range and then exercised pairwise
cross-axis combinations, yielding 147 cases. The foreground wrapper ended before
that stage completed even though the contract was valid. The retained attempt is
`checks/override-after/`; the same generator design with explicit values
`12|13|18` completed 59 cases and 5,310 draws in
`checks/override-after-v2/` with zero findings.

**Suggested change.** During lint/planning, print the exact case count and
estimated draw count. Support an axis-level `probe_values` field or an explicit
endpoint/representative policy for large exact ranges, and automatically shard a
matrix above a configurable cost threshold. Exact observability should remain
strict; this only controls which legal values are crossed pairwise in one run.

Reconcile checkpoint state when the foreground driver is interrupted

**Symptom.** Long battery stages outlived the tool transport. The parent command
was interrupted while its checker child continued as an orphan and eventually
wrote valid stage evidence; `progress.log` still showed `RUN` until a later
`--resume` invocation imported or reran the stage. This occurred during the
final battery and required process polling before it was safe to resume.

**Suggested change.** Have the driver trap termination, either terminate the
child process group cleanly or remain in a lightweight polling/reconciliation
mode until the child receipt is committed. On the next invocation, reconcile a
finished stage report/receipt before printing `RESUME-IMPORT: no completed-but-
unjournaled stage evidence found`. A stable machine-readable driver-status file
would also avoid confusing a transport timeout with a checker timeout.

Make portable test-root helpers mandatory at collection time

**Symptom.** Audit target `48fee61713bb` has an extensive test file that passes in
its original repository layout but the public portable task-test stage fails
before collection because it derives canonical data from a fixed
`Path(__file__).parents[...]` depth. Evidence:
`checks/audit/48fee61713bb/task-tests/result.json`.

`reviewer_support.find_root`, `canonical_path`, and `canonical_pairs` should be a
blocking preflight for selected-task tests before a generator is marked

can migrate without hand-rewriting path logic.

Surface canonical-structure mismatches as a first-class semantic diagnostic

**Priority: highest shared-tool change.**

**Symptom:** Audit target `afa7a3af9331` is not merely weakly sampled; its generator implements and documents a different task from the pinned authority. The generator creates an `(0,0)` op marker plus color-2 and color-3 operands and describes a set operation painted color 4. The canonical rule instead takes exactly two normalized objects, overlays them, preserves their colors, and paints overlaps color 8. In 600 ordinary draws, 596 had three disconnected nonzero objects and four had two only because the op marker accidentally merged into an operand. All 600 passed the task's current `self_check`.

**Evidence:** `checks/audit/afa7a3af9331/sample_probe.json`, `checks/audit/afa7a3af9331/counterexample.json`, and the supported apply record `checks/audit/afa7a3af9331/racket.json`.

**Suggested change:** Extend the shared defect/semantic lint to compare basic canonical structural signatures against ordinary generator support—at minimum nonzero object-count range, shape-changing versus shape-preserving behavior, output palette roles, and persistent marker cells. When generator `SUMMARY`/`INVARIANTS` imply a conflicting transformation or no ordinary sample enters any canonical coarse profile, emit one explicit “generator/authority semantic mismatch” finding with a representative input and Racket output. Existing rule smoke proves that the authority executes; it does not by itself show that the generator samples the intended task manifold.

No other shared-tool change is requested. Battery checkpoint/resume, source-bound task tests, supported apply records, and the lesson census all provided useful, replayable evidence in this review.

# Feedback to Codex

The inherited strip-task test used a task-relative canonical path and a legacy import, preventing portable staged collection; it also equated archived formatting with live selected-source bytes. Prefer the public `reviewer_support` root/canonical/generator APIs and an AST-level archive-provenance check, while keeping the live rule hash and native default byte-exact.

The aggregate battery wrapper can look wedged after children finish.
The required high-level before command produced no terminal output or parent
receipt within the execution window. A three-stage after loop likewise remained
open long after `lint`, `selfcheck`, and `rule_smoke` had complete child
receipts. `--status` correctly recovered them, and one-stage invocations exited
normally. Suggested change: make `arcpuzzles check --battery` stream stage
starts/finishes immediately, close inherited child descriptors, and return once
the receipt is durable. Printing the exact `--status` recovery command before
launch would also reduce uncertainty.

The documented per-stage path is reliable but the top-level command does
not automatically explain the fallback.** The comments inside
`run_generator_battery.sh` are excellent, but a reviewer must discover them
after the wrapper appears silent. Suggested change: have the CLI detect a
non-interactive environment and print the per-stage or detached-and-poll recipe
up front.

Semantic rival verification caught a genuinely noncausal witness.** The
first after run minimized a short-gap/crossing case where the only short interior
cell was overwritten, so the declared rival still matched. This was the most
valuable check in the packet. Suggested change: save the authority output,
rival output, and a cell-level diff next to the minimized witness in the JSON
report; currently the grid and counts are present, but reconstructing the output
difference requires rerunning the task.

Override output is too large for interactive diagnosis.** The selected
baseline emitted 16,793 findings, and audit target `406739865b43` emitted
20,522. The grouped root-cause header is useful, but the log still expands tens
of thousands of repetitive examples. Suggested change: cap the text log to the
first 2–3 examples per normalized group and put the full records only in JSON.

Standalone lint labels its phase `before` even when invoked as the final
required lint check.** The exact documented command writing to `../checks/lint`
created files named `c831492f416e_before_lint.*`. It passed, but the phase name
is confusing in a return that already has a real baseline. Suggested change:
accept `--phase lint` or derive the phase from the output directory for
single-stage invocations.

Racket-lint stage wording can be misread.** The stage passed while saying
`flagged: 1` for two style-only categories. Suggested change: use separate
labels such as `style notes`, `warnings`, and `errors`, then print `PASS (style
notes present)` explicitly.

Full repository tests need an environment hint.** Running bare `pytest`
with only `PYTHONPATH=shared/runtime` failed collection because `src` was absent;
`PYTHONPATH=src:shared/runtime pytest -q` passed 104 tests. Suggested change:
put the canonical test command in `AGENTS.md` or configure pytest's Python path.
With bundled Racket on `PATH`, the full suite exceeded ten minutes after five
tests, so a documented fast/unit subset plus a separate integration command
would make completion status clearer.

Add a semantic counterfactual de-correlation gate **(highest-priority shared change)

**Symptom.** Current semantic checks establish that declared rivals lose on sampled lessons, but they do not detect deterministic correlations among witnesses or semantic roles. A generator can therefore be perfectly labeled and pass its named rivals while teaching a global switch instead of the intended compositional rule.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/audits/assigned-shortcuts.json` contains two source-bound examples:

- `3f93d8860778`: a `has_same_colour_triple` switch matches 5/5 canonical pairs and 2,000/2,000 generated samples, because all negative column types are bundled.
- `d8ce64d73f8a`: “if not largest, paint largest non-main” matches 2,000/2,000 generated samples, because smaller pockets are never seeded; canonical pair 3 refutes it.

**Proposed fix.** Extend the semantic gate with an optional task hook such as `semantic_facts(grid) -> dict[str, hashable]` and `semantic_counterfactuals(grid) -> iterable[grid]`. Over one schedule period, report deterministic fact implications and require at least one lawful intervention for any declared independent fact pair. A lightweight first pass can use witness incidence only; only flagged relations need Racket labeling. This belongs in the shared semantic tooling rather than in each task's bespoke tests.

Task-local defects for `98c4483164f7` were repaired in this return; no additional shared-tool blocker remains for accepting that task.

Expose a cheap keyed-draw honesty preflight

**Symptom:** my first sampler repair returned valid profile geometry but
overwrote already-recorded default axis draws. The full override stage found
the drift, which ordinary grid-validity and explicit-override tests missed.

**Evidence:** `checks/after/checks/2bb81826c18d_after_override.log`,
`checks/keyed-draw-red.log`, `checks/intermediate-generator.py`, and the new
task regression using public set_ctx_observer/recorded_draws. The final fix
chooses domains before recording values; the full final override stage passes.
**Suggested change:** provide a small public draw-provenance stage before the
larger override matrix. The regression is already built locally; no shared
implementation is required to accept this task repair.

add conditional-shape redundancy rivals, not just area/position baselines

Symptom (G1): the original 12-stage battery passed, yet each two-row matcher was
perfect on all 360 baseline draws. All shapes had total area six, making the third
row derivable from the other two. Evidence: `checks/before-census/census.json`.
A large count of unique grids or a failed area-only rival does not establish that
all represented features matter.

Built here: three input-only row-omission rivals, exact oracle-backed witnesses,
and an independent cut census in `workspace/run_review.py`. Suggested shared
extension: conditional feature-ablation probes for parameterized shape families,
with witnesses that preserve all but one decision-relevant feature. Generalize
only where an independent feature decoder is available; do not invent a universal
ablation that changes the puzzle's grammar.

support exact enums larger than sixteen without falsely calling them unparsable

Symptom (G4): a valid 32-value scene domain first hit the nonliteral AST warning;
a literal domain then failed because the boundary parser caps enums at sixteen.
Evidence: `checks/after/` and `checks/after-final/`, lint/override logs.

Built here: an explicitly manual scene probe, complete literal domain, a test
binding enum strings to runtime names, and exhaustive 96-combination testing.
The final lint log explicitly reports the exemption; no automatic coverage is
claimed. Suggested shared fix: accept explicit probe values independently of the
full domain, or deterministically sample large finite enums with coverage metadata.
Distinguish “parseable but beyond budget” from malformed metadata. Keep unknown-key
checking and exact observer checks; do not globally suppress the warnings.

discover new task-local tests when staging a runtime

Symptom: the packet's static runtime file mapping does not automatically discover
newly added test files. The repository's own test suite also uses a different test
root. A passing battery/root suite could omit the regression that justified a patch.
Evidence: `checks/final-tests-v3/run.json` explicitly lists both staged test hashes
and the actual pytest command.

Built here: `workspace/run_review.py` copies only the selected task's test files to
a clean runtime and runs them explicitly. Suggested shared fix: permit a bounded,
validated task-test manifest or discover `generators/<id>/tests/test_*.py`, recording
all source hashes. Never silently broaden execution to arbitrary repository files.

separately measure input validity and demonstration identifiability

Symptom (G3): initial v4 passed its oracle/input probes and fifteen local tests,
but 2/12 lessons left a query-changing rival consistent with all demonstrations.
Evidence: `checks/after/checks/54a83e6bbc20_after_semantic_gate.json` and
`checks/curriculum-red/tests.log`.

Built here: three-slot identifying anchors and 1,095 overlapping-window
regressions. Suggested process: every distribution expansion should run both
individual-input checks and lesson-level alternative-rule survival tests, across
multiple window starts. Report surviving-but-query-equivalent rivals separately
from genuine ambiguity. Report overlapping windows separately from unique inputs.
The existing semantic gate caught a useful defect; preserve that check rather
than weakening the identifiability threshold to make a broader sampler pass.

remove Python site-initialization speed from the 200 ms streaming test

Symptom (T1): `tests/test_review_runtime.py::test_streaming_timeout_retains_progress_and_stops_child`
fails in the full suite and isolated retry because the child is killed before its
first print. The full suite reports 169 passed / 1 failed; the module retry is
7 passed / 1 failed. Evidence: `checks/logs/repository-tests.log`,
`checks/logs/runtime-tests-retry.log`, and `checks/runtime-startup.json`.

the original 0.2-second timeout, and ordinary Python with a 2-second timeout, both
capture the expected progress and still terminate the sleeping child. Suggested
fix: launch a minimal `-S` child for this standard-library test or separate startup
readiness from the intentional sleep deadline. Keep assertions for timeout,
process termination, and retained output. No shared runtime/test patch is included;
the original suite remains red in the report.

correct Racket outputs, so semantic checks alone miss the caller-contract defects.
Evidence: `checks/audits/*_ignored_palette_override.json` and

items.text:
Biggest avoidable friction: output paths cross two working directories

`review.py task-tests` is launched from the outer packet while its `--out` value resolves from `WORK/repo`, which caused otherwise-correct runs to fail on paths such as `WORK/checks/...`. Normalize the path at the wrapper boundary, or print the resolved destination before refusing it, so future agents can use one packet-relative convention.

# Feedback to the next builder

Two reusable task-local audit entrypoints were added. They execute every retained
setting through protected Racket, compare against an independent Python oracle,
check demonstration-only setting identification, attack named shortcuts, verify
query-prefix stability, and preserve a causal witness candidate:

- `generators/70a3d3e2c975/workspace/parametric/audit.py`
- `generators/75be7448827f/workspace/parametric/audit.py`

For sequential public bundles, each saved public file is one model turn and thus
contains exactly one query. Run `check_public_exports.py` with `--queries 1`, even
when the private qualified episode contains four total queries.

The clean follow-up is owner-side exact-source intake. Do not repin either source
inventory after edits; any source change requires a new manifest, qualification,
and causal witness.

Highest priority — add a counterfactual role/order leakage gate

**Symptom.** `shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` can score declared competitors, but it does not generically test whether placement order, color rank, or full-border geometry is a proxy for the intended measurement. In the selected task’s old source, a scan-order/solid-border rival matched 12/12 generated Racket outputs even though a validator-accepted rearrangement refuted it.

**Evidence.** `checks/final-counterexample/counterexample.json`, `checks/task-tests-red/pytest.log`, and the prior retained audit named in `REVIEW.md`.

**Suggested change.** Add an opt-in counterfactual provider API to the semantic gate: generators declare preserved invariants and legal role/placement permutations; the tool runs a small generic rival family, validates the counterfactual, obtains a source-bound authority output only for surviving candidates, and retains a minimized witness. Keep an explicit “position/color is semantic” declaration to avoid false positives. This is the shared change most likely to improve training-data value.

Shard and checkpoint the exhaustive override matrix

**Symptom.** The final override stage took 144 seconds for 53,730 draws. During an earlier combined invocation, the shell wrapper timed out while the child continued and completed in a temporary directory, requiring manual discovery/recovery. A long monolithic stage makes evidence easy to orphan.

**Evidence.** `checks/after/checks/5a01897eb8be_after_override_results.json` and the final battery journal/summary.

**Suggested change.** In `shared/tools/check_generator_override_contract.py`, make case shards first-class, write the aggregate incrementally after each shard, and expose a resume command tied to source/settings hashes. Have the wrapper forward termination to the process group and copy any completed child report before returning a timeout.

Materialize rotated lessons explicitly in semantic reports

**Symptom.** Rotation reports retain the original `instance` and separately provide `train_indices` and `query_index`. During the `c09f9e692978` audit, reading `instance.train` as the rotated demonstrations initially appeared to contradict the rival verdict; reconstructing indices showed the report was correct.

**Evidence.** `checks/audit/c09f9e692978/required-rotations/checks/c09f9e692978_audit_semantic_gate.json` and `checks/audit/c09f9e692978/rotation-counterexample.json`.

**Suggested change.** In `shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` and `shared/tools/lesson_census.py`, retain `rotated_train` and `rotated_query` (or source-pair indices embedded beside each pair) in ambiguity examples. Preserve the compact original instance for deduplication, but make a witness directly executable without manual reconstruction.

Turn portable-root preflight guidance into an authoring lint/fix template

**Symptom.** `c09f9e692978` has substantive tests, but they cannot collect in the staged runtime because `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` points beneath the task and the file imports a private `puzzle_generators.per_puzzle` alias.

**Evidence.** `checks/audit/c09f9e692978/combined/result.json`; failing lines 13–24 are quoted in `AUDIT.md`.

**Suggested change.** Extend lint to flag fixed `parents[...]` repository-root guesses and private per-puzzle imports before the expensive portable stage. Generate a ready-to-copy header using `reviewer_support.find_root`, `canonical_pairs`/`canonical_path`, and `load_selected_generator`.

Surface and optionally enumerate the generator-declared lesson schedule period **(top shared-tool change)

**Symptom.** `generators/63a780e1d475/generator.py` declares `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD = 20`, derived from a four-slot semantic cycle and five-slot shape cycle. However, `checks/lesson-census.json` records `sampler.period = 6` with `enumerate_schedule_period = false`; the six appears unrelated to the declared generator period. A reviewer could mistakenly believe the census covered all cyclic starts when it sampled consecutive starts under a different residue summary.

**Concrete effect.** I had to add a task-local loop over all 20 starts to substantiate the claim that every query rotation retains the required witnesses. The public census still cannot report that exact schedule coverage, even though the generator supplies the period explicitly.

**Suggested change.** In the lesson-census controller, read and validate an integer `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD` when present, report it separately from lesson/window length, and add an option such as `--enumerate-schedule-period`. That option should materialize every declared start residue for each band (or clearly report rejected residues), then summarize coverage as `covered/declared`. Preserve the current sampled census as the broader stochastic check.

Add an authority-sync diagnostic/autofix for comment-only duplicate-source drift

**Symptom.** The baseline authority-sync stage failed because the selected bank entry’s nested `racket_target.target_code` and `raw_code` differed only in comments, while execution parity already passed. The report classified the divergence accurately, but resolution required manually locating and copying the corresponding field.

**Evidence.** `checks/before/checks/63a780e1d475_before_battery_summary.json` reports `diagnostic_divergence` with `execution_parity=PASS`; the final report under `checks/after/` is synchronized after a byte-for-byte field update.

**Suggested change.** Keep exact equality as the gate, but print the precise JSON pointer(s) and offer a non-default command such as `arcpuzzles authority-sync TASK --copy raw_code-to-target_code --check/--write`. For comment-only or whitespace-only drift, the diagnostic should say that executable behavior agrees and show the exact safe synchronization direction. This would reduce accidental edits to the wrong authority copy without weakening the check.

Expand the audit preset to include lint and defect-lint

**Symptom.** `--stage audit` ran task tests plus the strict semantic gate, but it did not expose the most actionable defects on either drawn target. `19ba16363b7f` passed semantics while defect-lint found five invalid scalar cases; `eed263bf30fc` lacked a rule hash, had an unprobeable axis, and accepted ten invalid scalar cases.

**Example/evidence.** `checks/audit/19ba16363b7f-combined/`, `checks/audit/19ba16363b7f-defect_lint/`, `checks/audit/eed263bf30fc-combined/`, `checks/audit/eed263bf30fc-lint/`, and `checks/audit/eed263bf30fc-defect_lint/`.

**Suggested shared change.** Make the audit preset include at least `lint` and `defect_lint`, or print a prominent follow-up command when those stages are omitted. Audit conclusions would then be less likely to report a semantic pass while missing a broken public API contract.

**Top shared change — finalize interrupted batteries and support receipt-based resume

**Symptom.** An aggregate battery can be terminated by an outer execution cap while `result.json` remains `status: "running"` and the lock remains the only indication that the controller disappeared. This occurred for the baseline (`checks/before/result.json`) and once on the final source (`checks/after-interrupted-final/result.json`). The isolated stage then passed, and a clean rerun completed 12/12 green.

**Suggested change.** In the battery controller, trap `SIGTERM`/`SIGINT` and atomically finalize the aggregate as `interrupted`, naming the active stage and preserving its receipt state. Add `arcpuzzles check ... --resume <out>` to reuse hash-matching completed stage receipts and rerun only incomplete stages. Refuse resume when source or authority hashes differ. This would preserve the current evidence model while avoiding both stale “running” reports and expensive full reruns.

Add cyclic query rotation to `lesson-census`

**Symptom.** The shared census explicitly reports that it does not rotate pairs into alternate query positions. The first repaired schedule passed the standard 100-per-band census but failed one task-local cyclic rotation: the sole opposite-side witness became the query, leaving three demonstrations that all fit the rival. Evidence: `checks/tdd/cyclic-rotation-red.log`.

**Suggested change.** Add an opt-in `--cyclic-query-rotations` mode that, for every materialized lesson, scores each pair once as query and the others as demonstrations. Report ambiguous rotation count and residues separately from the standard sampler. The task-local final regression demonstrates the desired calculation.

Expose one canonical grid-normalization helper in the public review API

**Symptom.** `shared/data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl` can store grids as compact digit strings, while generated/runtime grids are lists of integer rows. A first version of the independent probe passed strings into `self_check`, causing three misleading cross-reference failures before the data-shape boundary was traced (`checks/tdd/focused-green-attempt1.log`).

**Suggested change.** Export a small documented helper that returns normalized integer-grid train/test pairs and the canonical program text/hash. Keep it separate from private labels and make its use safe outside solve episodes. This would reduce duplicated loaders and correlated parsing mistakes across task-local probes.

# Tooling and process feedback

## 1. Preflight Racket before launching a battery

The packet clearly documents that Racket is required, but the battery still spends time starting multiple stages that can only report the same missing-runtime cause. Add a single preflight receipt with three states: available, unavailable-but-static-fallback-supported, and unavailable-blocking. Downstream summaries should reference that receipt instead of making each stage rediscover the dependency.

The setup path also assumes outbound package access. This host had neither Racket nor working DNS. A small version-pinned runtime archive in the packet, or an explicit offline cache hook, would make reviews reproducible.

## 2. Do not mark diversity green when no input/output pairs materialize

The baseline diversity log reported no usable pairs because Racket was unavailable, yet the stage was counted green. “No pairs” is neither evidence of diversity nor a generator failure; it should be an explicit `blocked_dependency`/`unmeasured` state and excluded from green counts.

## 3. Separate static generator lint from rule-execution validation

`lint_generator.py --validate` bundles static metadata/axis checks with runtime generation through the protected rule path. Once `RULE_HASH` was added, the inherited lint stage failed solely because Racket was missing even though direct static lint had zero findings. Emit separate static and execution receipts so a reviewer can show that source structure is clean without laundering the missing authority check.

## 4. Provide a source-checkout loader fixture for task tests

Per-puzzle modules are importable as `puzzle_generators.per_puzzle.<id>.generator` only after runtime staging. A test written in the source tree therefore fails collection unless it manually loads the selected file. Provide a shared pytest fixture such as `load_candidate_generator(task_id)` that preserves the runtime imports while loading the candidate source path.

## 5. Expose progress from the wrapper command

`python -m arcpuzzles check ... --battery` buffers almost all useful stage output until completion. The underlying battery has detailed journals, but the wrapper gives no visible progress and is easy for a constrained shell to mistake for a hang. Stream stage start/end lines or provide a documented `--follow` mode.

## 6. Give full-battery outputs an explicit phase

The wrapper always invokes the inherited shell battery with phase `before`, even when the caller writes to `checks/after`. That makes filenames and strictness policy look like baseline evidence. Add `--phase before|after` to the Python wrapper and make the duties use it, or derive phase from an explicit argument rather than the output directory name.

## 7. Preserve strict-profile threshold diagnostics in one place

The initial controlled-breadth design provided one canonical anchor per four profiles, but the pinned census produced `13/60` rather than the intuitive `15/60`, just below the 25% strict threshold. The gate behaved correctly, but the sampling/index schedule was not obvious from the worker instructions. Document the exact pinned sample-index sequence or expose a small `explain-census TASK` command.

## 8. Distinguish lawful diagnostic overrides from ordinary training mass

The generic minimal-impostor warning treats the exact `n_seeds=1` override as evidence that `self_check` is too broad, even though ordinary draws are constrained to three or four seeds and the one-seed case is lawful under the selected rule. Detectors should report both ordinary-draw support and override-only support, or let a generator declare `ordinary_domain` separately from `override_domain`.

## 9. Keep the strong parts

The immutable baseline hashes, source-scoped return builder, strict unknown-key probe, canonical profile floor, named semantic rivals, schedule coverage, and requirement to retain failures all materially improved review quality. The task-local return ZIP validation is especially useful: it prevents accidental workspace dumps and makes the review delta auditable.
