items.text:
Authority synchronization diagnostics were useful; retain the exact-text/execution split

The authority checker correctly distinguished a semantic failure from the
actual issue here: execution parity passed, while two active selected strings
were not byte-identical. That prevented an unjustified Racket rewrite. The
current diagnostic categories should remain separate, and the final report
should continue stating whether a repair changed semantics or only normalized
selected authority text.

**Persist battery evidence directly to the requested output directory.** The first direct full-battery command exceeded the outer command lifetime. Because `arcpuzzles check` stages into a temporary directory and copies evidence only after its child returns, all completed stage receipts from that invocation disappeared. I had to use `workspace` plus a detached `run_generator_battery.sh` process and poll its persistent receipts. Suggested change: add `check --persistent-workspace DIR` or make `--out` the live stage directory, with resumable per-stage copying rather than end-of-run copying.

**Show canonical target profiles and nearest misses in the profile-floor log.** The useful failure said medium had zero exact hits, but the human-readable log did not list the canonical `(height,width,palette)` targets or representative medium profiles. Those details were available only by opening JSON and tracing the pinned seed formula. Suggested change: print target profiles, per-band exact/envelope counts, and the three nearest misses whenever a band fails.

**Offer a generic shortcut-correlation diagnostic before a semantic contract exists.** The baseline morphology and diversity gates were clean even though every key/query pair was aligned by column and the semantic gate had no contract. Suggested change: compute simple role-to-position and answer-to-position correlations (same row/column, nearest key, fixed reading-order mapping) and emit candidate rivals that the reviewer can promote into executable hooks.

**Keep the linter's actionable strictness.** For this task it correctly exposed two constant axes and the missing `observe_overrides`; defect lint separately caught 33-wide boards and dead/degenerate textures. That division was useful. A small usability improvement would be for the linter to print a one-line scaffold for `observe_overrides()` listing the exact axes it expects, so the remediation path is immediate.

**Cap repetitive override detail in the text log while preserving the full JSON.** The baseline had 8,495 findings. Root-cause grouping was excellent, but the text log still contained thousands of near-identical provenance/bound messages before suppression. Suggested change: default to the minimized root-cause table plus per-category counts in `.log`, with every raw case retained only in `_override_results.json`; add `--verbose-findings` for expansion.

**Surface intermediate-after status as a first-class artifact.** The first rebuilt source had 11/12 green stages and one profile failure. Retaining that failed attempt was valuable because it proves the final profile fix was evidence-driven. Suggested change: let the battery accept an attempt label and write immutable `after-attempt-N` directories and source hashes automatically.

Make canonical-fitting rival coverage blocking when a rival is known

**Priority: highest shared-tool change.**

**Symptom:** The imported `4e05481a2c21` sampler produced correct labels but
only rectangular holes.  `fill_hole_bbox`, `largest_region_only`, and
`all_bbox_zeros` fit every labeled canonical pair; the first also fit every
baseline generated lesson.  Because the module declared no rivals, the
baseline semantic stage was advisory rather than a blocking teaching failure.

**Suggested change:** When a task declares a rival that fits all usable
canonical pairs, require every production lesson—and every supported query
rotation—to refute it.  If no executable rival contract exists, surface a
blocking “semantic coverage unknown” result for training admission rather than
counting correct labels as sufficient.  Start with the existing 12-lesson smoke
sample, then automatically request the 100-lessons-per-band census only for
canonical-fitting rivals.

**Possible false positive:** A deliberately ordered curriculum may rely on a
fixed query position, or a genuinely underspecified task may not have a known
witness within its lawful domain.  Permit an explicit diagnostic-only rotation
policy or documented domain exception, but keep the uncertainty visible.

the supported report actually stores each output under `results[*].output`.
The Racket execution itself succeeded, but the avoidable parser mismatch cost a
rerun.

**Suggested change:** Add a minimal report-schema example to the apply-command
documentation, including `results`, `executed_rule_hash`, and
`generator_sha256`.

**Evidence:** The corrected retained report is
`checks/selected-witness-parity/racket.json`.

Direct task-local `pytest` did not inherit the packet's bundled Racket even after setup, while the same command passed through `review.py run`. Print the exact wrapper command beside setup output, or export the runtime path into the packet shell, so agents do not misclassify a harness-path issue as a test failure.

Make aggregate battery progress and termination robust

**Symptom.** The exact supported aggregate command completed lint, selfcheck, and
rule smoke, printed `RUN defect_lint`, then did not return within the outer
1,200-second harness. The same `defect_lint` stage passed in an isolated wrapper
invocation, and all 12 stages subsequently passed individually.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/after-command.log`,
`checks/after-command-status.json`, and
`checks/after-per-stage-summary.json`.

**Proposed fix.** Have the aggregate runner persist/copy each stage receipt as
soon as that child exits, close inherited stdout/stderr descriptors explicitly,
and add a watchdog that reports the child PID, elapsed time, and last completed
receipt. On timeout, emit a resumable summary rather than leaving the caller
with only the last `RUN` line.

Deduplicate the runtime manifest in per-stage result files

**Symptom.** Every `checks/after-*/result.json` embeds the same large runtime
manifest. In this packet each result is roughly 68 KiB, so a 12-stage fallback
repeats source metadata hundreds of kilobytes even though the generator and
runtime are identical.

**Concrete evidence.** The 12 result paths and their hashes are listed in
`checks/after-per-stage-summary.json`; each contains a repeated
`runtime_manifest` block.

**Proposed fix.** Store one content-addressed runtime manifest per check batch
and have individual stage results reference its path and SHA-256. This preserves
source binding while reducing return size and review noise.

Emit a compact override-contract failure summary before detailed witnesses

**Symptom.** The baseline override gate produced 23,641 findings over 146,340
draws plus 76,200 legacy-accepted multi-axis rejections. Its human-readable log
is dominated by repetitive per-seed provenance lines, while the most actionable
root causes are the missing observer, dead aliases, out-of-range declarations,
and silently accepted unknown key.

**Concrete evidence.**
`checks/before-manual/d57b7deebba2_before_override.log` and
`checks/manual-before/override-command-rerun.log`.

**Proposed fix.** Print the grouped root-cause table, minimized witness, finding
counts, and top remediation hints first; cap repetitive examples per signature
in the text log while retaining the full machine-readable JSON. This makes a
large failure diagnosable without losing evidence.

items.text:
Portable task-test roots
The issued task test imported a staged `puzzle_generators.per_puzzle` namespace and used a fixed parent-relative canonical path, so it failed outside one runtime layout before reaching assertions. Scaffold reviewer tests with `reviewer_support.find_root`, `load_selected_generator`, `canonical_path`, and `canonical_pairs` by default.

TOP SHARED — add operation-visibility support to lesson census

**Symptom.** `repo/shared/tools/lesson_census.py` can prove that declared rival programs are refuted, but it cannot detect when the semantic edit classes themselves are visually masked by the query. Audit target `8a851bf5cdd7` produced a validator-clean, in-distribution identity output at seed 1006/sample 6 even though its latent transform had one addition and three deletions; neither operation was visible. The pinned frequency probe found 18–92 identity outputs per 1,000 draws depending on band. Evidence: `checks/audit/8a851bf5cdd7/probe.json` and `racket.json`.

**Proposed fix.** Add an optional `LESSON_EFFECTS`/`observable_effects(input, output)` contract with per-effect policy (`required_per_lesson`, `conditional`, `identity_allowed`). Have the existing census evaluate effect coverage across cyclic query positions and retain the smallest counterexample. This is the highest-value shared change because it catches weak supervision that ordinary validity, parity, diversity, and rival checks can all miss.

make interrupted battery runs resumable and stale-lock-aware

**Symptom.** Two externally interrupted controllers (`checks/after-v4/` and `checks/after-v5/`) left source-bound checkpoints plus lock metadata but no finished aggregate. The current instructions correctly say that automatic resume is disabled, so a reviewer must create a new output directory and rerun already-green stages. In long override/census workloads this multiplies runtime and evidence volume.

**Proposed fix.** Add `arcpuzzles check --resume OUT_DIR` that validates the generator/authority subject hashes, reuses only finished receipts from the same run subject, clears a lock whose PID namespace/heartbeat is stale, and starts at the first incomplete stage. Keep the final summary explicit about reused versus freshly run stages.

emit a compact final evidence index and help prune superseded successes

**Symptom.** A serious review naturally accumulates a before run, genuine failed intermediates, a final battery, task-test snapshots, census files, and audit evidence. `package_return.py` bundles members when needed but does not identify duplicate successful snapshots; the reviewer must manually decide what to retain while preserving failures.

**Proposed fix.** Have packaging print a source-hash-grouped retention plan: keep every failure/interruption, the newest complete success for each command class, and any artifact referenced by reports/`RESULTS.json`; flag other successes as optional duplicates. Generate a compact `checks/EVIDENCE_INDEX.json` with command, source hash, status, and canonical evidence path.

items.text:
Biggest avoidable friction: repeated single-query export plumbing

Native qualification retains four-query episodes, while the reviewer handoff needs one-query views with current source checks and private ordering. The tested task-local `repo/generators/699479899861/workspace/parametric/export_qualified.py` now provides export/verify commands using the native receipt validator and public serializer; promoting this bounded projection into a common helper would save future reviewers from rebuilding the same privacy and source checks.

Deduplicate lesson-census rival aliases and offer compact evidence output

**Priority: top shared-tool change.** The affected path is the shared `arcpuzzles lesson-census` report builder. A callable can be declared under `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`, `SEMANTIC_RIVALS`, and `LESSON_COMPETITORS`, so the report records and scores it under three labels even when all labels point to the same function. In `checks/lesson-census-final.summary.json`, five semantic rival names expanded to 14 aliases; the full 300-lesson JSON was 14,128,283 bytes, much of it repeated grids and alias status.

Proposed change: identify rivals by a stable callable/source digest, retain all declaration names as provenance aliases, execute each unique rival once per input, and aggregate per-band results by semantic rival ID. Add `--compact` or `--evidence-dir` so the main JSON stores hashes/seeds/results while full materialized instances are content-addressed once. This would make reports smaller, faster, and less misleading without losing reproducibility.

Add safe battery resume/reconciliation for interrupted wrapper lifetimes

The first after battery at `checks/after/result.json` finished lint, self-check, and rule smoke, then the outer caller ended while the aggregate remained `running` with a live-lock snapshot and nine pending stages. An isolated defect-lint run passed, and both later full batteries completed green. The current correct procedure is to retain the interrupted result and start a new output directory, but it duplicates work and leaves stale lock interpretation to the reviewer.

Proposed change: add `--resume` that verifies the subject/authority hashes, reconciles completed stage receipts and journals, detects whether the recorded PID is actually alive in the current namespace, marks orphaned running stages interrupted, and executes only missing stages. Never silently turn a partial aggregate into a pass; emit a new final aggregate with explicit provenance linking reused receipts.

Green structural checks can conceal composed semantic shortcuts

Symptom: original `d9d4f0ebb48b` passes all 12 battery stages, including lint and semantic checks, while a palette-filtered component-bbox rival and an area-filtered bbox rival both survive all 192 sampled four-demo lessons. Existing rivals tested bbox filling without the additional cheap palette/area condition.

Evidence: `checks/before/checks/d9d4f0ebb48b_before_battery_summary.json`, `checks/counterfactual-baseline/palette.json`; findings G1/G2.

Suggestion: compose a bounded family of simple nuisance filters with existing transformation rivals, and require a matched reference-backed counterexample in the visible lesson. Report both pair accuracy and complete-lesson survival. Gate only declared semantic distinctions; preserve color constants where the authority requires them. See `QUESTION_ANSWER.md` for the single proposed gate and false-positive example. Added task-local rivals implement this now; no shared linter changes are included.

New task tests need explicit portable-runtime discovery

Symptom: the imported runtime file map lists the original test file; adding `tests/test_palette_roles.py` does not automatically prove that the battery or repository suite will run it. A broad green result could omit the most important new regressions.

Evidence: `checks/task-tests-final/receipt.json` names both exact test files and records `/tmp/arcpuzzles-palette-sa847fl9` as the actual runtime cwd. Its run log shows 79 passed.

Suggestion: include an intake inventory of selected-task tests and compare it to the files actually staged/executed. Make omitted new test files an explicit warning or error. The supplied `workspace/review_checks.py` stages all task `test_*.py` files and runs an explicit list, without modifying the shared import map.

Negative fixtures must change their source before testing rejection

Symptom: after changing palettes/layout RNG consumption, the inherited “extra same-color spur” fixture repainted an existing arm near the border. A purported negative input remained valid. Its name alone did not establish a counterexample.

Evidence: `checks/palette-green/run.log`, then the added mutation-change regression in `tests/test_palette_roles.py`; finding G3.

Suggestion: fixture APIs should retain the source input/hash and assert nonidentity before using rejection as evidence. Test the claimed semantic mutation separately from the expected validator response. The selected task now chooses an empty in-bounds spur cell and derives corruption colors from the actual shape.

Separate process startup from the streaming timeout being tested

Symptom: repository suite: 169 passed, one failed. `test_streaming_timeout_retains_progress_and_stops_child` expects a first print from an ordinary new Python process within 0.2 seconds. A standalone retry fails too. In this environment, five normal interpreter starts had median 0.812 seconds; `-S` had median 0.0105 seconds. Normal Python at a one-second deadline and `-S` at 0.2 seconds both preserve streamed output and terminate the sleeping child.

Evidence: `checks/repo-tests-console.log`, `checks/repo-timeout-retry.log`, `checks/runtime-timeout-diagnostic.json` and the task-local diagnostic script. Shared runtime SHA256 is retained there; shared source was not changed.

Suggestion: start the timeout after a child-ready handshake, or use `-S` for this stdlib-only child and test startup behavior separately. Do not silently inflate production deadlines or mark the test passed based on the diagnostic. This return leaves the actual failure visible and makes no shared-source patch.

Hash the immutable executed source, not the mutable editor copy

Symptom in **our new local runner**, not an accusation about the pre-existing product: `checks/palette-before/receipt.json` hashed the home generator after the worker completed while an edit had already occurred. Its hash conflicts with the worker's correctly frozen original hash in `palette.json`.

Suggestion and implemented fix: hash the staged source before starting the process; include actual cwd and explicit source selection; make baseline replay use an immutable file. The bad receipt is retained and labeled, not overwritten. Superseding checks are `checks/palette-baseline` and `checks/counterfactual-baseline`, whose source identity agrees with their workers. Intake should flag receipt/report hash disagreement rather than merging those runs.

Cross-check realized placement and overrides, not only planned geometry

Symptom: audit target `2fb8d019f6ca` emits overlapping stamped pixels in 12/192 draws while accepting all 192; `bc005ea27dae` emits fewer than three objects in 7/192 and tied perimeter maxima in 7/192, also all accepted. Both targets ignore advertised override inputs in saved counterexamples. These counts may overlap within a target and must not be added as independent failures.

Evidence: `checks/audits/2fb8d019f6ca.json`, `checks/audits/bc005ea27dae.json`, `AUDIT.md`; findings A1/A2.

Suggestion: calculate post-placement observable features from the actual grid, enforce the requested/declared contract, and resample or raise explicitly if allocation fails. For stamps, reserve all future painted cells symmetrically, not just anchor cells. Distinguish a broad Racket-valid domain from a narrower promised training distribution. These audit targets are unchanged in the delta.

## Friction and alleviation

The packet's isolated runtime and source-bound return format are useful. The main friction was that test discovery, immutable source identity and process-startup assumptions were not obvious from a single green command. The supplied scoped runners leave reproducible argv/cwd/hash receipts and retain failing intermediate evidence; no installed runtime tree or duplicate repository is returned. Subsequent reviewers can replay the focused tests and counterfactual probe without reconstructing the temporary layout manually.

**Top shared change — add cross-split rival-survival to the semantic gate

**Symptom.** Pair-level correctness and ordinary witness counts can pass while a complete generated lesson still permits a cheaper wrong rule. `generic_slot_match_gen1` seed 46 supplies two training pairs that both support “take the first matching object's color,” although the intended rule is the modal color; the rival fails on `test[1]` at two cells. Add source-bound resume to the battery controller

**Priority: top shared-tool change.**

**Symptom.** The first final battery invocation was interrupted by the outer tool
after it had already completed and checkpointed lint, self-check, rule smoke, and
defect lint. The retained directory `checks/after-interrupted-r1/` has valid
stage receipts, but the controller has no automatic resume path; the assignment
itself warns that resume is not enabled. The only safe option was to start the
full 12-stage battery again, which repeats expensive Racket and distribution
work.

completed `checks/after/checks/`. The former contains four completed receipts
bound to the same repair phase, while the latter had to rerun those stages before
reaching the remaining gates.

2. rejects running, malformed, stale, or mismatched receipts;
3. reuses only completed green stages and reruns failed/interrupted/pending ones;
4. writes a new aggregate journal entry identifying every reused receipt; and
5. produces a final summary whose verdict is based on the merged, hash-consistent

checkpointing useful in constrained agent runtimes. No shared-tool patch is

TOP SHARED CHANGE — mine undeclared canonical-consistent shortcuts

**Affected tool:** `shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py`.

**Symptom.** The semantic gate is strong against rivals a generator author
already named, but it cannot detect a simple omitted rival. In task
`0bb8813a21dc`, rarest-row-color fits all four canonical pairs. The first repaired
draft declared several strong alternatives but omitted this one; the omission was
found only in a separate self-review. Evidence: `checks/tdd-rarest-red.log` and
the final canonical-fit regression in
`repo/generators/0bb8813a21dc/tests/test_generator_0bb8813a21dc.py`.

**Suggested change.** Add a bounded library of generic pure candidate programs
(position extrema, frequency extrema, global/local scope, connected components,
fill span/row/column, identity). Run them on canonical pairs, retain candidates
that fit all labels but disagree somewhere with the selected rule, then require
those candidates to be declared/refuted or explicitly waived with an executable
domain/equivalence reason. Start with 20 deterministic draws per band and one
four-pair rotation window; escalate survivors to `lesson-census`.

low-description-length rule that is perfectly consistent with canonical examples.
Checking only author-declared rivals creates a blind spot exactly where author
intuition failed.

**Task-local mitigation already included.** The final generator declares the
rarest-color shortcut, every generated input refutes it, and
`workspace/lesson_probe.py` checks all declared rivals over 300 cyclic windows.

Top shared suggestion — make battery checkpoint completion atomic and visible to the wrapper

**Affected tool/path:** `arcpuzzles check --battery --resume`, the portable
controller/wrapper, and stage checkpoint synchronization under `checks/<run>/`.

**Symptom.** The first after-battery invocation completed lint, self-check, and
rule smoke, then the outer call was interrupted after roughly an hour. A resume
completed through semantic gate, then appeared to stall at diversity; isolated
`defect_lint` and `diversity` runs both completed quickly, and later source-hash-
checked resumes finished all 12 stages green. Evidence is retained in
`checks/after-command-attempt1.log`, `checks/after-resume-command.log`,
`checks/after-diversity-command.log`, `checks/after/attempts/`, and the final
summary. The final source was not the cause, but a reviewer cannot easily tell
whether a completed child stage is waiting to be journaled, copied, or observed
by the outer wrapper.

**Suggested change.** After each child stage exits, atomically write and fsync a
small controller-level checkpoint containing stage name, source/runtime/settings
hashes, child PID/exit, evidence hashes, and UTC completion before any expensive
copy/aggregation. Emit a heartbeat that distinguishes `child-running`,
`collecting-evidence`, `checkpoint-written`, and `finalizing-summary`. On resume,
import a hash-valid completed stage even when the prior wrapper died between
child completion and journal update. This would turn an apparent hang into a
clear resumable state and avoid rerunning already completed work.

items.text:
Separate Python-only review execution from the fixed Racket readiness gate

**Highest-priority shared-tool suggestion.** A Python-only payload launched with `review.py run` cannot start until `WORK/run_with_racket.py` calls `ensure_racket()`, which executes the fixed 20-second readiness probe in `WORK/setup_racket.py::_probe`. During the loaded portion of this review, that probe repeatedly timed out before pytest started. These are infrastructure failures, not generator or regression-test failures.

### Concrete evidence and reproduction

The two attempts recorded in `checks/diagnosis/portable-tests-repair-evidence.json` used this exact command from the outer extraction directory `/workspace/scratch/d14ef4c3c21a/review_work`:

```bash
/workspace/scratch/d14ef4c3c21a/review_work/WORK/.venv-review/bin/python review.py run /workspace/scratch/d14ef4c3c21a/review_work/WORK/.venv-review/bin/python -m pytest -q generators/2b34f380ed25/tests/test_generator_2b34f380ed25.py
```

Both exited 1 before the payload. The full tracebacks are retained in `checks/diagnosis/portable-tests-pytest-after.log` and `checks/diagnosis/portable-tests-pytest-after-retry.log`. Each contains:

```text
subprocess.TimeoutExpired: Command '['/workspace/scratch/d14ef4c3c21a/review_work/WORK/.review/racket-runtime/racket/bin/racket', '-e', '(require json racket/list) (displayln "RACKET_READY")']' timed out after 20 seconds
RuntimeError: Racket probe timed out after 20s; stdout=''; stderr=''
```

The intended payload cwd was `WORK/repo/`. The wrapper sets `PYTHONPATH` to `WORK/repo/src:WORK/repo/shared/runtime`, sets `ARCPUZZLES_HOME` to `WORK/repo`, and supplies the selected `RACKET_PATH` and its directory on `PATH` after readiness succeeds. On these failures, readiness stopped execution before that payload environment and cwd were installed. The full inherited `PATH` and other ambient variables were not snapshotted. The inherited test file exercises Python generation, mirrors, and retained authoring data; it does not execute Racket.

Running that inherited file directly from `WORK/repo/` with `PYTHONPATH=src:shared/runtime`, the explicit repository `ARCPUZZLES_HOME`, and the same venv interpreter passed all nine tests in 68.77 seconds: `checks/diagnosis/portable-tests-pytest-direct-after.log`. Its command, actual exit 0, source hashes, and before/after evidence are recorded in `checks/diagnosis/portable-tests-repair-evidence.json`. A separate root regression attempt also stopped at the wrapper probe; its actual argv and exit 1 are retained in `checks/diagnosis/root-contract-wrapper-timeout.json`.

Recovery evidence is separate from these failures. The parametric test payload initially hit the same readiness timeout (`checks/parametric/tests-v2.json`) and subsequently passed all eleven tests in a serialized run using explicit venv interpreters for wrapper and payload (`checks/parametric/tests-v3.json`). The interpreters differ between those two receipts, so this is a successful retry of the test payload, not a claim that the complete command/environment was identical. The direct root regression also passed seven tests and 679 subtests (`checks/diagnosis/review-contract-after-direct.log`; actual exit 0). Host load is a plausible contributor to the readiness timeouts; these records do not establish a particular operating-system or Racket defect.

### Proposed shared fix

Provide a supported Python-only execution path that installs the documented repository cwd/import environment without starting Racket. Keep reference execution and Racket-dependent checks on the verified Racket path. For commands that require Racket, make readiness timeout configurable and report a distinct infrastructure failure with `payload_started: false`, the probe argv, selected interpreter/runtime, and bounded stdout/stderr. Preserve archive/hash verification. This would let reviewers retain accurate failing evidence and rerun the correct layer without treating a Python regression as a Racket availability check.

No wrapper or shared runtime change is included in this task delta.

## Task-owned portability observation: repaired in this return

The inherited `generators/2b34f380ed25/tests/test_generator_2b34f380ed25.py` used a private `puzzle_generators.per_puzzle` import and a fixed-depth task-local root for canonical/base data. The repository-layout import failure is retained in `checks/diagnosis/portable-tests-unittest-before.log`. This is a task-owned test defect, not a new shared-tool finding.

The included migration uses public `load_selected_generator`, `find_root`, `canonical_path`, and `canonical_pairs`, retaining the original first canonical variant. The base authority path derives from the canonical data directory. All nine inherited test methods and all 49 assertion calls remain unchanged. They pass in direct repository execution and in the supported copied task-test runtime; see `checks/diagnosis/portable-tests-repair-evidence.json` and `checks/portable-tests-fixed/result.json`. These portability checks used inherited generator SHA-256 `b04d2f58c34c7c47940fcd87c8cfedc9024f759347c88c091b92dd57d9ccac1f`. That intermediate aggregate receipt also retains the then-failing newly authored review-contract tests and eleven Racket startup errors; it is not a final aggregate pass or verification of later generator bytes.

There is no second shared-tool suggestion supported by sufficiently specific new evidence. Missing pytest was correctly reported as an infrastructure prerequisite failure in `checks/task-tests-before/result.json`, and was resolved by selecting a review venv with pytest and the existing NumPy/Pillow available. The parametric prototype's earlier padding/query defect was local to that prototype and is documented with its failed iteration and repair in `checks/parametric/final-summary-v2.json`.

Run a metadata-only byte/inode preflight before full packet extraction.

`checks/environment.json`. Consumer: review packet launch/extraction tooling.

Add a checkpoint-aware controller mode for long battery runs **(top shared-tool change)

**Symptom.** In this review the battery correctly wrote stage receipts, but the foreground wrapper detached while the deep scan was running. `checks/after/result.json` remained `running` until I manually resumed from matching checkpoints; the completed result later reused only hash-compatible receipts and finished 12/12 green. The same issue affected a standalone long probe: a valid receipt existed while the shell no longer represented the job state. Evidence: `checks/after-resume-driver.log`, `checks/after/progress.log`, and `checks/after/result.json`.

**Proposed fix.** Add `arcpuzzles check --resume-until-complete` or `--yield-after-stage`. The controller should execute one pending stage, atomically write its receipt and aggregate status, then either exit with a machine-readable `next_stage` or continue in a child-independent loop. Reuse the existing source/runtime/checkpoint hashes; the missing piece is a foreground-safe orchestration mode, not a new evidence format.

Provide a source-bound audit-rival helper that emits a compact reproducer

**Symptom.** Both assigned audits required custom scripts to answer the same questions: does a rival fit every canonical pair, how often does it fit generated samples, what exact input separates it from the authority, does that input pass `self_check`, and what generator/rule hashes produced the result? The reusable logic is visible in `checks/audit/9f74cf8633e5/overlap_shortcut_probe.py` and `checks/audit/287967e33b21/validator_override_probe.py`, but each reviewer currently rebuilds the receipt format.

**Proposed fix.** Add a command such as `arcpuzzles audit-rival TASK --probe PATH --input INPUT.json --out reproducer.json`. It should call public generator hooks, invoke the supported Racket apply path, and emit canonical-fit counts, generated sample coordinates, validator verdict, rival/authority outputs, first differing cell, and all source hashes. Keep the rival implementation task-local; standardize only execution and provenance.

Surface declared schedule period automatically in the default lesson-census summary

**Symptom.** The required random census command reported a default sampler period of six even though this generator declares `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD = 4`. The explicit `--enumerate-schedule-period` run correctly used period four and covered all 12 band/start combinations. Nothing was mislabeled, but the two reports are easy to compare incorrectly without reading their sampler sections. Evidence: `checks/lesson-census.json` and `checks/schedule-census.json`.

**Proposed fix.** When a generator declares `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD`, print both `random_window_period` and `declared_schedule_period` in the top-level summary, and suggest the exact enumeration command. Do not silently replace one with the other; they answer different coverage questions.

Validate every retained Racket resource before witness construction

**Symptom.** The second target’s normal behavior tests and copied-runtime suite passed while its task-local counterfactual program still lacked the outer `rule!` closing parenthesis. The stricter complete-form validator caught it only when run explicitly.

**Evidence.** `checks/95be702ec4db/program-syntax.json` records the failure; `checks/95be702ec4db/program-syntax-v2.json` and `checks/final-program-syntax-command.json` record the corrected pass. The retained regression is in the target’s parametric test module.

**Suggested change.** Have the native preflight validate every `.rkt` file named by the adapter, promotion resources, audit, or causal recipe—not only programs exercised in qualification jobs—before producing a ready receipt.

Split base-review and parametric Racket evaluation counts in execution receipts

**Symptom.** Each qualification reports `racket_evaluations: 40`, while the four visible parametric jobs account for 28 labels. The remaining base-review evaluations are legitimate but require reading nested receipt details to explain the total.

**Evidence.** `checks/f2e717c7c250/qualification/execution.json` and `checks/95be702ec4db/qualification/execution.json` each contain the aggregate count and four seven-label job checks.

**Suggested change.** Add explicit `base_review_racket_evaluations` and `parametric_racket_evaluations` fields while retaining the aggregate. This makes reviewer summaries auditable without inference.

A semantic hook can report “identifiable” while naming zero competitors

**Symptom.** The baseline semantic artifact for `a4f0ea66fd65` reports 12/12 lessons identifiable, but `competitors_declared` is empty and every witness has no rival claim. A signed/oriented 2×3 shortcut nevertheless matched 432/432 sampled scenes and survived 216/216 four-demo windows.

**Evidence.** `checks/before/checks/a4f0ea66fd65_before_semantic_gate.json`, `checks/a4f0ea66fd65_before_vector_shortcut_audit.json`.

**Suggested change.** On baseline runs, make `lesson_identifiable` plus an empty `LESSON_COMPETITORS` list a prominent advisory, not just a buried field. Add a standard library of proposed task-agnostic rivals and task-family rivals; for vector tasks, include exact-distance quantization and fixed-vector hypotheses. The after-phase strict mode correctly verified the declarations once present.

Run task-local pytest files as an explicit battery stage

**Symptom.** The twelve-stage battery does not execute `generators/TASK/tests/`. This task's focused tests contained a schedule-dependent mutation fixture that became valid after profile reordering, and the test root path was not portable to a staged runtime. Neither issue was visible to `generator_selfcheck.py`.

**Evidence.** Manual staged-runtime red/green logs: `checks/a4f0ea66fd65_tdd_red_pytest.log` and `checks/a4f0ea66fd65_after_focused_pytest.log`; final source test file `repo/generators/a4f0ea66fd65/tests/test_generator_a4f0ea66fd65.py`.

**Suggested change.** Stage task-local tests into the independent runtime and add a bounded `pytest -q` stage. Expose the runtime root and protected Racket path through fixtures so individual tests do not reinvent discovery. Keep generic self-check and pytest separate: they catch different defect classes.

Stream battery stage progress to the caller

**Symptom.** The first full-battery invocation produced no stdout before the outer tool timeout, even though the battery was progressing and retaining stage receipts. This made a healthy run indistinguishable from a hang until the temporary runtime was inspected.

**Evidence.** `checks-before-console.log` is empty; `baseline.full.log` and the final before receipts show all stages completed. The detached after run likewise wrote detailed stage logs in its temporary runtime before the wrapper emitted its summary.

**Suggested change.** Flush a one-line `RUN/PASS/FAIL` record when each stage starts and ends, and mirror the current receipt path. Preserve the final JSON summary, but do not buffer all user-visible progress until completion.

Distinguish positive branch witnesses from rule-discriminating evidence in summaries

**Symptom.** v3.0.0 had nine witnesses that fired across the census, but none was bound to a rival. A reader could reasonably mistake “9/9 witnesses firing” for evidence that the rule was identified.

**Evidence.** Baseline semantic JSON and log; after semantic log now explicitly reports five verified rival claims and six declared branch witnesses.

**Suggested change.** Put three counts on the main summary line: branch-only witnesses, rival-claim witnesses, and verified rival claims. When all witnesses are branch-only, state “no rule-discriminating witness declared” even in non-strict baseline mode.

The generator linter was clean but cannot detect this data-value defect

**Symptom.** Running the linter alone produced no false alarm and no usability problem. It also could not detect that every “generalized” vector remained in the same 2/3 magnitude family; that is outside its structural/static scope.

**Evidence.** `checks/lint_after/checks/a4f0ea66fd65_after_lint.log` and the before/after vector-shortcut audits.

**Suggested change.** Keep the linter narrowly structural. Link its success message to the semantic/lesson gates rather than expanding AST lint into behavioral inference. The missing protection belongs in the declared-rival sliding-window gate proposed above.

Add a static portability lint for task-local canonical-data access **(highest priority)

**Symptom.** Audit target `97e1d2aa0bc3` imports successfully in the repository
but its portable task-test stage fails before pytest because
`Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl"` points
beneath the staged task directory. Evidence:
`checks/audit/97e1d2aa0bc3-task-tests-console.log` and
`checks/audit/97e1d2aa0bc3-task-tests/result.json`.

**Suggested change.** Extend the task-test preflight or generator/test lint to
flag fixed `__file__.parents[...]` canonical paths and private per-puzzle imports.
The diagnostic should prescribe `reviewer_support.find_root(__file__)`,
`canonical_path`, `canonical_pairs`, and `load_selected_generator`. The existing
runtime error is good, but a static authoring-time failure would prevent broken
tests from reaching review packets.

Separate rotation hook warnings from “ambiguous” counts in the semantic summary

**Symptom.** The strict semantic console for `97e1d2aa0bc3` says
`0/48 ambiguous` while failing because six rotations produced
`lesson_identifiable` warnings. A reader can easily interpret the zero as a
semantic pass even though the hook found a named rival that fits all demos and
changes the query. Evidence:
`checks/audit/97e1d2aa0bc3-semantic/checks/97e1d2aa0bc3_audit_semantic_gate.log`.

**Suggested change.** Report a combined primary count such as
`rotation failures: 6/48 (0 provider ambiguities, 6 hook disagreements, 0
errors)` and label the overall rotation status `failed_identifiability` rather
than `warning` whenever `--require-rotations-identifiable` is active. Preserve
separate provider/hook fields in JSON.

Promote witness-to-rival binding omissions to a focused contract hint

**Symptom.** `97e1d2aa0bc3` declares four useful `SEMANTIC_WITNESSES`, but no
`WITNESS_RIVALS`; the gate therefore calls all four weak even though its private
lesson hook contains related competitors. This splits one semantic contract
across naming conventions and makes the report harder to act on.

**Suggested change.** When a witness name or docstring appears related to a
`lesson_identifiable` competitor but `WITNESS_RIVALS` is absent, emit a single
focused suggestion showing the expected declaration shape. Do not infer the
binding automatically; require the author to confirm that the rival actually
disagrees on witness-positive inputs.

Make portable task-test root mistakes an immediately actionable audit finding

**Symptom.** Audit target `cfadc43e5098` has a substantial independent-oracle suite, but the public task-test stage cannot collect it because line 15 sets `ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]`, then looks for `ROOT/data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl`. In the portable runtime that resolves beneath the task package. Evidence: `checks/audit/cfadc43e5098/task-tests/result.json` and its runtime manifest; generator SHA `13aa933b5b692a34d03098576a485d8f9c857af2182371d316c3def109fdc12b`.

**Suggested change.** The stage already prints the right migration advice; also emit a small machine-readable finding containing the offending file/line and a ready replacement using `reviewer_support.find_root(__file__)`, `canonical_path`, and `canonical_pairs`. That would let intake route a mechanical test-only repair without reading a large JUnit or runtime manifest.

Stage launchers can outlive successful child receipts

**Symptom.** The full battery launcher and several per-stage launchers remained alive after their child check had already written a green `.receipt` and `.ok`. This occurred reproducibly around `profile_floor` and `grammar`; logs showed `PASS`, while the wrapper process lingered until terminated. The source-bound receipt and final summary reconciled correctly.

**Suggested change.** After a receipt is atomically written and reconciled, explicitly close inherited descriptors and terminate any teardown helper. The parent should exit based on the receipt rather than waiting on unrelated descendants. A documented `--resume` command that consumes existing source-bound receipts would also make this recovery path obvious.

Generic destructive-mutation scoring misclassifies lawful seed deletion

**Symptom.** `selfcheck` rejected 39/45 destructive mutations. The six survivors were mostly “drop minority color” mutations that turned a valid four-seed input into a valid three-seed input. This generator intentionally accepts both counts, so rejection is not the correct oracle for that mutation.

**Suggested change.** Let generators declare which structural dimensions are unions of lawful classes, or classify a mutation as destructive only after confirming it leaves the declared grammar. Report “mutated into another lawful profile” separately from “validator missed malformed input.”

Racket style findings are correctly nonblocking but could be clearer

**Symptom.** `racket_lint` exits green while reporting `style-not-eq` and `style-eq-zero` in the unchanged canonical rule. The rule executes correctly and all authority/parity checks pass.

**Suggested change.** Label these explicitly as “style advisory” in the stage summary, separate from semantic or safety findings, so a reviewer does not need to infer why a flagged stage is still green.

Generator lint was useful and raised no generator false alarm here

The generator lint correctly accepted the selected implementation. Its structured diversity, override, and source-binding evidence was useful; I found no generator-specific false positive or missed defect in this task.

items.text:
Make authority-sync provenance explicit in its primary receipt

**Symptom.** Exact selected-authority divergence and intentional archival `raw_code` divergence are easy to conflate. The baseline failed because selected `target_code` was whitespace-divergent; after repair the correct state is `selected_synchronized_archival_divergent`, with execution parity passing.

**Concrete change.** Have `authority-sync --selected-only` emit a compact patch receipt listing each mutable selected field, old/new hashes, canonical source hash, and each preserved archival field. Put the selected-vs-archival verdict near the top of the log and use distinct severity labels. This would make safe normalization reviewable without opening all authority JSON files.

Validate or preserve extra result metadata instead of silently dropping it — top shared-tool suggestion

**Affected shared path:** `src/arcpuzzles/review_full_return.py`, `build_full_return`, the construction of the returned `results` object.

**Symptom:** source inspection shows that the builder reconstructs `RESULTS.json` from a fixed set of accepted keys. Additional reviewer keys such as `source_bindings`, `counts` or `solve_summary` are omitted without a warning. A reviewer can believe final-source metadata was saved while it is absent from the returned machine-readable summary. This was found by inspecting the actual builder during handoff preparation; it is not described as an observed corrupted archive.

**Concrete response in this return:** source hashes and denominators are stored inside retained verification-command entries and compact evidence receipts, which the builder preserves. `REVIEW.md` identifies the final source in its opening lines. No unsupported extra top-level metadata is relied upon.

**Proposed shared change:** define/document an extension namespace whose contents are preserved and hash-bound, or reject unknown keys with an error listing them. Add one round-trip test: supply a source hash under an extension key, package, and verify either that it survives exactly or that packaging fails clearly. Silent omission is the behavior to remove. This is a proposal requiring shared-tool ownership; no shared patch is included in the assigned delta.

Check test dependencies under the same isolated interpreter used by task tests

**Symptom and evidence:** direct pytest worked, but the first `task_tests` stage failed with `No module named pytest` because the staged runner uses `-E -s` and pytest was installed in the user site. See `checks/task-tests/result.json`, `checks/test-environment-install.log` and `checks/environment-receipt.json`.

**Local action already completed:** created a task-local environment outside the repository and made the existing pure-Python pytest dependencies available to its isolated interpreter. The final staged test run executed 52 cases with no failure or skip. Neither shared source nor frozen tests were edited.

**Proposed shared change:** setup/preflight should run the actual selected interpreter with `-E -s` to import the dependencies needed by the task-test runner, and give a matching installation command when imports fail. A successful user-site import is not sufficient evidence for that stage. Preserve dependency errors as infrastructure failures, separately from test assertions.

Promote schedule shortcuts found by the audits into reusable coverage probes

**Symptom:** both audited generators produce lawful individual outputs while excluding a useful counterexample family. In A1, target selection excludes the largest room. In A2, interior routes are always Manhattan-shortest. Their current validators accept the retained counterexample queries, and their lesson hooks do not expose these rivals. See `AUDIT.md` and `checks/audit/f86f870eb9f2/finding.json`, `checks/audit/ad9405621c3d/verification.json`.

**Proposal:** task owners should add the retained rival as an executable competitor, generate the missing contrast, and rerun complete-lesson checks before accepting a repair. Shared tooling can help by summarizing covariation between semantic target choice and nuisance properties (area rank, boundary depth, monotonic path distance), but should not impose those task-specific assumptions globally. This is follow-up for the two audit owners; their sources are deliberately unchanged in this assignment.

Keep the new task-local oracle probe reusable, with its limits visible

**Delivered:** `generators/80f776fb3ce5/workspace/probe_local_contract.py` plus four tests. It enumerates all binary neighborhoods, adds selected palette cases, calls the public Racket authority API, reads actual rival declarations, and returns source-bound minimal witnesses. It explicitly separates validator acceptance from emitted support. `checks/local-contract-verified.json` records 568 authority comparisons, zero predicate disagreements and scoped rival refutations.

**Recommended use:** adapt this small probe for other local predicates, using each task's own domain and fixed color semantics. Do not copy the selected task's predicate or enumerate palette permutations when colors are semantically fixed. Do not replace complete-lesson tests with local parity. No new shared API is required for this utility.

Preserve checks that caught restrictions introduced by a repair

**Useful existing behavior:** the battery caught ineffective controls, canonical rejection, fragmentation, and missing explicit shortcut-witness links. The first two repair versions and their failing evidence are retained. A separate support regression then caught a limitation the green battery did not cover: diagonal counts one and two had disappeared after connecting rims (`checks/red-diagonal-support.xml`).

**Proposal:** encourage authors to state support sets that should survive distribution edits and test those sets directly, alongside existing aggregate gates. Passing broad counters does not guarantee that a specific legal contrast survived. This return includes that task-local regression; no universal diagonal-count requirement is proposed for other tasks.

**Top shared-tool change — make lesson census cyclic-query aware

**Affected path:** `repo/shared/tools/lesson_census.py` and its CLI/report schema.

**Symptom.** The stock census correctly verifies declared rivals on the one
assembled query position, but its own report states that pairs are not rotated.
A schedule can therefore pass ordinary windows while depending on the held-out
query itself to provide the only counterexample.

**Concrete evidence.** The retained prototype
`repo/generators/1f9fef86a482/workspace/lesson_probe.py` imports the source's
actual `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`, `LESSON_COMPETITORS`, and `SEMANTIC_RIVALS`, verifies
canonical-shortcut fit, and rotates every member of each four-pair block.  Its
final run covered 1,200 query rotations with zero ambiguity
(`checks/task-local-cyclic-lesson-probe.json`).  The stock census explicitly
lists lack of rotation as a limit in `checks/lesson-census-final-v2.json`.

**Proposed fix.** Add an opt-in `--query-rotations all` mode (or an assembly-policy
JSON input).  Cache the four materialized pairs, score each three-demo/one-query
split against declared rivals, and report survivor counts by rotation.  Keep the
current mode for arbitrary/expensive episode structures.  The task-local probe is
a small working prototype, kept separate from shared source as required by this
assignment.

Persist terminal interruption state and recover stale battery locks

**Affected paths:** `repo/shared/tools/run_generator_battery.sh`, the `arcpuzzles
check` wrapper, and lock/receipt handling.

**Symptom.** When the outer execution process was killed, isolated `defect_lint`
and `grammar` runs retained `result.json` with `status: running` and a lock rather
than a terminal interrupted status.  A reviewer cannot tell from that file alone
whether work is active, killed, or resumable.

**Concrete evidence.** See `checks/final-defect_lint/result.json`,
`checks/after-grammar-v2/result.json`, and
`checks/after-final-interrupted/result.json`.  Fresh repetitions and the final full
battery later passed both stages (`checks/after/...battery_summary.json`), so the
stale status was a harness-lifecycle issue, not a source defect.

**Proposed fix.** Store controller PID/start time in the lock, trap termination to
write `status: interrupted`, and on startup mark a lock stale when its PID is
absent or start identity differs.  A `--resume` invocation should consume green
receipts and rerun only interrupted/pending stages.

Enforce exact runtime types for exact override axes in the shared context

**Affected path:** `puzzle_generators.base.gen_ctx` draw/override validation.

**Symptom.** Generators can cast values before or during draw handling, causing an
exact integer axis to accept a float or string alias.  This produces duplicate
scenes and hides caller mistakes.

**Concrete evidence.** Audit target `4629b6d55040` accepts `n_blobs=3.9` and
`n_blobs="3"`; both become observed integer 3 and are byte-identical to the
lawful `n_blobs=3` draw (`checks/audit/4629b6d55040/finding.json`).

**Proposed fix.** For a declared `type: int` exact axis, require
`type(value) is int` (and explicitly decide whether booleans are forbidden)
before range checks or coercion.  Apply analogous exact checks to bool and enum
strings.  The override contract can then test the shared behavior once while
retaining task-local observability checks.

Distinguish semantic mask repetition from input collapse in diversity reports

**Affected path:** shared diversity gate/reporting.

**Symptom.** This task's final distribution has 100% unique inputs but 36% unique
outputs, so the report prints “worst offender” even though repeated masks follow
from a small set of graph-degree answer shapes.  The battery correctly leaves the
stage green, but the wording makes an informational signal look like a defect.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/after-final/checks/1f9fef86a482_after_diversity.log`.

**Proposed fix.** Report input duplication, output duplication, and paired
(input, output) duplication separately; make only the paired/input-collapse
threshold blocking by default.  Allow task contracts to declare a finite output
shape family, then annotate rather than flag expected mask reuse.

Biggest avoidable friction: `audit-status` writes an unpackageable retained-evidence file

Running `review audit-status` retained the source-bound assessment in `notes.md`, but it also rewrote `generators/<task>/evidence/review_index.json`; `review.py package` then rejected that path as outside the allowed task scope. Stream battery evidence directly to the requested output directory

**Priority: top shared-tool change.**

**Symptom.** `arcpuzzles check --battery` builds stage evidence in a temporary runtime and copies it to `--out` only after the wrapper returns. If the outer process is interrupted, completed stage logs can disappear with the temporary directory.

**Concrete example.** A redundant final rerun reached three green stages and began defect lint, but the outer command window ended. `checks/final_battery_console.log` shows the progress; no corresponding stage directory was recoverable under `checks/final_battery/`. Earlier baseline runs had the same failure mode and had to be replayed stage by stage under `checks/before_stages/`.

**Proposed fix.** Pre-create a run directory under the requested `--out`, write each stage log/receipt there atomically as it finishes, and keep a `.partial` journal/lock until the summary is finalized. Prepared-runtime files can remain temporary; durable stage evidence should not. An optional small patch would route `run_generator_battery.sh`’s `OUT_DIR` to a caller-owned staging directory and rename it on success rather than copying at process end.

Add progress receipts and bounded work to the override stage

**Symptom.** On the baseline generator, the override stage appeared idle for a long interval with no visible case count, current axis combination, or partial result. It was impossible to distinguish expensive enumeration from a stuck subprocess.

**Concrete example.** `checks/before_stages/override_console.log` contains only the stage start before the run was stopped. The repaired generator’s final override stage completed normally, but the baseline diagnostic path remained opaque.

**Proposed fix.** Emit the planned case count before execution, append a receipt every fixed number of cases, record the current combination/seed, and apply a per-case or per-shard timeout. On interruption, preserve completed case rows and the next resume cursor.

Document the exact portable-runtime command and make task tests portable by default

**Symptom.** Review instructions refer to preparing a runtime by internal function/module language, but the supported user-facing command is `python3 -m arcpuzzles workspace --id TASK --out ...`. Task-local tests also need source-layout aliases for `scripts` and the selected per-puzzle generator, whereas prepared runtimes expose different import paths.

**Concrete example.** `tests/test_generator_df5e596e5e96.py` needs a small bootstrap to run unchanged both from the source tree and the prepared runtime. `workspace/semantic_census.py` similarly contains layout detection. The final portable smoke verifies the tool works, but every reviewer should not have to rediscover these path differences.

**Proposed fix.** Put the exact CLI in `DUTIES.md`, and provide one shared test bootstrap/helper that resolves the selected generator and `shared/tools` package consistently in source and portable layouts.

Promote canonical-fitting rivals to a generic lesson-value gate

**Symptom.** Existing gates separately check validity, diversity, and a small semantic sample, but they do not generically require a complete training lesson to refute executable rivals that still fit all canonical examples.

**Concrete example.** The baseline `df5e596e5e96` passed superficial generation requirements while the cell-count shortcut fit both all canonical and all generated pairs. The task-local census in `repo/generators/df5e596e5e96/workspace/semantic_census.py` demonstrates a generic contract shape.

**Proposed fix.** Add a shared gate that discovers `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`, filters to rivals fitting every canonical pair, assembles lessons using `EXAMPLES_NEEDED`, and calls `lesson_identifiable` or a standard equivalent. Report rival-by-rival witness coverage and distinguish query-equivalent rivals from blocking query-divergent rivals.

Several valid multi-program checks exceeded the foreground client window after emitting only partial progress; add periodic structured heartbeats plus built-in shard/resume support to qualification and `task-tests` so long protected-Racket batches stay observable and unambiguous.

# Reusable reviewer tooling

## Keep native test snapshots out of compact returns

The current public-task test runner writes a complete isolated runtime under
`checks/TASK/family-tests*/runtime`. The native return builder includes the
checks tree, so those useful local snapshots become copied runtimes in the
return and consume its expanded-byte budget. This conflicts with the packet's
explicit compact-delta requirement. Removing them in an earlier tool process
was also unreliable in this workspace: previously materialized files could
reappear when another payload started.

Implemented `checks/tools/package_delta.py` as a narrowly scoped wrapper around
the **unchanged** native `arcpuzzles.review_full_return.build_full_return`.
It recognizes native stages from their result and source-binding schemas,
verifies the exact snapshot inventory and bytes, preserves test reports and
bindings, and renames verified snapshots and generated caches to a new
packet-local stash outside checks. Because original paths were observed being
materialized again even during a same-process build, it now creates a fresh
work view under that stash. Every retained file has an independent copy with
verified hash, size and mode; complete source/destination inventories are
compared. Unexpected source and evidence files are retained for native
validation, rather than silently filtered. The original and copied checks both
receive the exclusions and compact view-binding receipts.

The unchanged native builder receives this fresh view. Its source validation,
archive budgets and approval boundaries stay intact. The wrapper rejects
changed bytes, symlinks, unsafe destinations and stale output paths; a failure
leaves its stashed bytes and view recoverable.

Thirty-two focused orchestration/refusal/recovery/archive/copy tests pass. They use
synthetic snapshots, real ZIP fixtures and explicitly labeled mock builders.
Because copied files were observed reappearing during one packaging attempt,
native success now also requires a postflight scan of the actual ZIP and native
evidence manifest. Any `runtime` path component under checks or generated cache
component causes rejection, including a retry with an empty cleanup plan. The
ZIP and stashes are preserved on rejection. Run final packaging without other
processes inspecting or materializing the staged snapshots.

The final packet build is the
separate native integration check; its result and exclusions receipt are not
replaced by those unit tests. Three independently reviewed wrapper defects
received failing regressions before their fixes. The source and tests are
included for future agents to reuse. Owner integration into the shared packager
is a proposed follow-up, not a shared-runtime change made by this return.

## Preserve full audit evidence with compact JSON

`checks/tools/finite_rival_audit.py` now writes compact grid-heavy episode and
harmful-case JSON while keeping the summary readable. It drops no programs,
grids, predictions, query executions or source bindings. A focused round-trip
fixture reduces grid artifacts from 3,700,004 to 415,398 bytes (88.8%); the
complete fixture audit shrinks from 3,709,448 to 424,842 bytes. Unicode and CRLF
program bytes, every query prediction and both harmful cases are retained.

The current helper suite passes 61 tests; the packaging wrapper separately
passes 32 tests. These are distinct recorded runs. The earlier 16- and 25-test
wrapper results remain historical evidence. Mock finite-audit fixtures prove orchestration and serialization;
the assigned-family reports supply actual protected Racket execution evidence.
Current source hashes, exact commands, red/green receipts and limits are in
`checks/tools/validation.json` and `checks/tools/README.md`.

No allocation, approval, runtime, raw-data, publication or training policy was
changed. These improvements make the existing review workflow easier to run and
transport without weakening its checks.

## Check native return metadata before packaging

The first native packaging attempts caught two transport-format mistakes in the
return metadata: task-local deliverable paths lacked the `repo/` prefix, and
command working directories were absolute. Both are corrected; no family code
or label needed changing. The exact original command receipts remain intact.

The reusable `checks/final-review/check_release.py` now applies the unchanged
native `validate_target_outcomes` and `_intake_summary` gates before packaging,
in addition to its source/evidence consistency checks. Ten pure metadata tests
cover the valid return, each of the six missing-prefix mutations, an absolute
command directory, and protection of an existing report. Reports use a fresh
explicit `--out` path so earlier evidence is never overwritten.

For future packet instructions, distinguish these two path bases explicitly:

| Field | Path base and example |
| --- | --- |
| `RESULTS.json` prototype/promotion/inventory paths | Relative to WORK: `repo/generators/TASK/workspace/parametric/...` |
| `promotion.json` adapter/resources | Relative to the repository: `generators/TASK/workspace/parametric/...` |
| Verification command `cwd` | Packet-relative, normally `repo`; the command receipt retains its original absolute environment. |

items.text:
Add a generic component-vs-color grouping rival to the semantic gate

**Top shared-tool change.** The semantic gate can thoroughly test declared
rivals but cannot notice a plausible rival that the generator author failed to
declare. An intermediate version of this repair used only distinct component
colors and still received semantic status `PASS` with 600/600 strict draws,
because its declared witnesses covered only `fill_bbox` and
`outline_over_input`; see
[`checks/intermediate-distinct-only-after/checks/6347dcb736b5_after_semantic_gate.json`](checks/intermediate-distinct-only-after/checks/6347dcb736b5_after_semantic_gate.json).
Yet the canonical demonstrations all permit the stronger
`global_color_bbox` shortcut, and a distinct-color generator can never refute it.

Proposed change: in `scripts/generator_semantic_gate.py` (or a reusable ARC
geometry rival library), add an opt-in/auto-suggested probe when a task contains
same-color connected components and the canonical set never shows one color in
multiple components. Compare component-wise and color-wise grouping transforms,
or at minimum emit a loud advisory: “canonical colors are one-component-only;
consider a disconnected same-color witness.” The exact selected-task witness in
[`checks/shortcut-counterexample/counterexample.json`](checks/shortcut-counterexample/counterexample.json)
shows the class of missed defect: the two rules differ at 14 cells while the rival
fits 3/3 canonical pairs.

This should remain a suggestion unless a task-specific oracle can be constructed
safely; automatic rival synthesis must not claim universal semantics from color
statistics alone.

items.reason: Accepted shared-tool follow-up; not implemented in this task-only intake: Include representative seeds and observed profiles in profile-floor failures
items.text:
Include representative seeds and observed profiles in profile-floor failures

The profile-floor report correctly caught an intermediate regression: after
adding repeated colors, the easy band had **0/20 exact** canonical-profile hits
while medium/hard had support. The report in
[`checks/repeated-profile/checks/6347dcb736b5_after_profile_floor.json`](checks/repeated-profile/checks/6347dcb736b5_after_profile_floor.json)
shows aggregate counts and the canonical profiles, but not the twenty observed
profiles or a smallest seed/sample witness. Diagnosing that the anchor confused
object count with palette size required a separate task-local reproduction.

Proposed change: when a band has zero exact support, retain a compact histogram of
observed `(height,width,palette-size)` signatures plus the first seed/sample index
for each signature. This would make “wrong dimension,” “wrong palette accounting,”
and “anchor never selected” distinguishable directly from the gate output without
inflating successful reports.

Make canonical parametric source bytes unambiguous

Symptom: the task archive exposes both archival `raw_code` and canonical `target_code`; copying the plausible larger field produced a 30,826-byte default that direct Racket tests could execute, but native qualification rejected it because the true catalog authority is the 1,720-byte `target_code`.

Evidence: the accepted canonical program SHA-256 is `514c258ab731e4505bfca2101754e3b65d525218243f63ac16632c6b87ef2744`; the regression in `test_parametric_adapter.py` now compares the adapter default directly to catalog `target_code`.

Suggested change: add a read-only CLI/helper that materializes the exact canonical program for a task, or expose the canonical field name, byte length, and SHA-256 in the authoring handoff. On mismatch, report expected and actual hashes/lengths.

Preserve worker diagnostics on qualification failure

Symptom: the initial native qualification surfaced `Parametric worker failed:` with an empty stderr tail, while the useful default-program mismatch was only visible after reproducing the disposable worker manually.

Evidence: the failure occurred before the canonical-source correction; the same qualification then passed six jobs and 78 protected-Racket evaluations.

Suggested change: have `parametric_worker` emit a structured error object and make `_execute` include both stdout and stderr tails, exit code, timeout state, and request/job index in the raised diagnostic.

Biggest avoidable friction: parametric qualification floods stdout with the complete shared-runtime source binding
The useful result was only job status, survivor counts and Racket-evaluation counts, but each qualification printed hundreds of dependency hashes. Add a `--summary` mode—or make concise stdout the default while retaining the complete source-bound receipt on disk—so reviewers can preserve full provenance without burying the decision signal.

Biggest avoidable friction: native parametric worker failures hide their structured error

Symptom: `parametric qualify` raised only `Parametric worker failed:` because the worker writes its JSON error to stdout while `_execute` appends only stderr. In this review, an invalid 40×40/50×50 output was therefore invisible until the worker request was replayed directly.

Evidence: the direct worker reported `A grid must be rectangular 1..30 with exact integer cells 0..9`; the added output-bound test then reproduced the defect deterministically.

Suggested change: when the worker exits nonzero, include bounded tails of both stdout and stderr in the qualification exception, or emit the worker’s error JSON on stderr.

Any source edit invalidates the manifest, qualification, witness, preview, and privacy receipts separately; add a source-hash-aware `refresh-evidence` orchestration that rebuilds this dependency chain atomically and refuses mixed-source receipts.

The packet required separate manual test, manifest, qualification, witness, projection, and privacy commands, making mixed-source receipts easy. This return adds task-local `refresh_evidence.py` orchestration that binds one source snapshot, rejects mismatches, and publishes the chain transactionally; this should become a shared packet command rather than duplicated reviewer code.

Packet-local Racket can be installed and verified yet remain unavailable to direct Python API calls because activation is process-local. Expose one shared `activate_packet_racket()` helper/context and have all review APIs use it, so CLI wrappers and direct callers receive identical protected-Racket behavior.

Ordinary exception rollback does not cover SIGKILL or host timeouts. Evidence publication should ship with a standard durable journal/recovery primitive for manifest-plus-output transactions, including safe path validation and startup recovery, rather than relying only on `with` cleanup.

Highest-priority shared decision — distinguish lawful mutations from invalid inputs

**Symptom:** the repaired 84def340ce03 fails shared/tools/generator_selfcheck.py with “ACCEPTANCE-ONLY: 0/53 destructive mutations rejected.” shared/tools/generator_defect_lint.py adds selfcheck-power and selfcheck-minimal-impostor warnings. Blank fills, color replacement, dropping a minority color and repeating a row leave this task's even integer grid domain intact. A correct validator must accept them.

**Evidence:** checks/after/checks/84def340ce03_after_selfcheck.log and the matching defect_lint log; checks/domain-probe/ provides source-bound public Racket outputs and literal expected outputs for lawful low-information cases, plus true malformed cases. The separate strict_canonical_like gate measures teaching support at 557/600 and rejects uninformative cases without falsifying validity.

**Proposed shared fix:** make mutation classification task-aware and report validity sensitivity separately from information/teaching sensitivity. Evaluate explicit malformed fixtures and independently verified lawful contrasts. Preserve the generic default for structured-object tasks; do not add a blanket bypass or equate accepting a blank grid with a universal defect. This policy decision is the remaining acceptance blocker. No shared gate was weakened in this return.

Optional tested patch — label source and callable hashes explicitly

**Symptom:** public Catalog.apply names a hash rule_text_sha256, but it hashes the runtime callable, not the exact stored canonical source. Both the new lesson probe and audit 9a9025a8556a initially compared it with a raw source hash and stopped. The task's exact canonical source SHA begins 62c5fc04; the callable SHA begins fb16aadc; both refer to rule e27cc4c77443.

**Evidence:** checks/lesson-probe/DIAGNOSIS.md and retained failed revision; checks/audit/9a9025a8556a/; checks/optional-shared/verification.json.

**Built proposal:** checks/optional-shared/rule-hash-fields.patch adds rule_source_sha256 and rule_callable_sha256 to src/arcpuzzles/worker.py and src/arcpuzzles/runtime.py while retaining the old field. It is separate from the allowed task patch. Public apply was tested before/after in a disposable copy: seven assertions pass, outputs and existing fields are preserved except elapsed time. Archival mode and strict downstream schema consumers were not separately tested. Maintainer decision required for this optional shared change.

Additional training gate — check whether semantic input channels are observable

**Symptom:** the original task generator made three of each tile's four pixel roles unobservable. Canonical inputs need all four roles, yet a top-left-only rival matches every original generated lesson in the retained sweep.

**Evidence:** checks/lesson-probe-final/report.json: the canonical ablation changes 3/3 unique outputs, baseline 0/600 per band, repaired 555/600 per band. All six declared rivals are eliminated in 300/300 tested lessons per band.

**Built task-local fix:** workspace/lesson_probe.py adds complete-lesson and ablation measurements through public Racket execution. QUESTION_ANSWER.md gives the cheapest shared rollout and the intentional-uniform-example false positive. No Qwen performance claim is made.

## Already handled locally

The actual quadrant distribution, canonical profile support, false override controls, unknown-key swallowing, malformed input validation and active authority text drift are repaired in the task delta. The two audit targets remain findings-only. The full results preserve all genuine failures and identify the two unresolved generic gates.

Runtime preparation is silent long enough to look hung.** Running the required standalone lint produced no console output for several minutes while `prepare_runtime` copied the snapshot; the actual lint then passed quickly. Emit a progress line before/after snapshot creation, or expose a `--reuse-runtime` option with manifest/hash validation.

`--out` creates a surprising nested `checks/` directory.** The command `--out ../checks/lint` writes evidence under `checks/lint/checks/...`. Either write stage files directly under the requested directory or document that the requested path is a result bundle containing a nested inherited `checks` tree.

The self-check stage can be green with extremely weak mutation sensitivity.** Baseline `selfcheck` passed although only the blank-grid mutation was rejected (15/60 mutations); `defect_lint` later caught the minimal-impostor problem. Promote a minimum mutation-rejection contract into `selfcheck`, or make its green status explicitly advisory when sensitivity is below threshold.

Canonical-profile matching is too coarse for semantic fidelity.** `(height, width, palette-size)` support can be 100% while object count, object sizes, row origin, and header grammar are wrong. Allow a task hook such as `canonical_profile_signature(grid)` or include common morphology fields in the strict profile floor.

“Canonical demonstrations” and “all canonical pairs” are conflated in shortcut analysis.** For this task, the row-major-first-cell rival fits both training demonstrations but is refuted by the held-out canonical query. `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` currently evaluates train and test pairs together, so it does not report that genuine demonstration ambiguity. Report two statistics: train-demonstration ambiguity and all-public-pair ambiguity.

Baseline completion left the battery lock looking live.** The completed before summary recorded `lock_present=true`, `pid_alive=true`, and `own_lock=true` even though all 12 stages had final receipts. Finalization should remove the lock or mark it closed so later tooling does not mistake completed evidence for an active run.

Profile-floor failures need per-draw diagnostics **(top shared-tool request)

**Symptom:** the intermediate source failed only because medium had 0/20 exact profiles, while the log reported aggregate `7/60 exact / 41/60 envelope` and the starving band. To identify why, I had to reproduce the private pinned-seed formula and print all 60 `(seed, sample_index, observed profile)` rows manually.

**Evidence:** `checks/after/checks/529bd4803bcc_after_profile_floor.log` and `checks/profile-floor-red/`.

**Suggested change:** in `shared/tools/canonical_profile_gate.py`, include a compact machine-readable per-band draw list in the JSON report: index, pinned seed, sample index, observed `(h,w,palette)`, exact/envelope booleans, and exception. On failure, print the first few nearest profiles. This would turn a probabilistic-prior diagnosis into a direct one-command result.

Provide a semantic-contract scaffold when `rule_mirror` exists but hooks do not

**Symptom:** both random audit targets have substantial rule mirrors and focused tests but fail `semantic_gate --require-contract` with `hooks=none`. One already emits a useful irregular-block counterexample yet has no declared rival/witness linking it to lesson identifiability.

**Evidence:** `checks/audit/520fe6e64fb6/battery/checks/520fe6e64fb6_after_semantic_gate.log` and the parallel f687 log.

**Suggested change:** have the semantic-gate failure print a small task-local scaffold showing required names and signatures (`SEMANTIC_RIVALS`, `SEMANTIC_WITNESSES`, `WITNESS_RIVALS`, optional branch witnesses), plus a command that validates one candidate. This keeps the strict policy while reducing repeated contract boilerplate and accidental no-contract returns.

items.text: (task-test templates) Normalize Racket source according to the authority-hash convention before source-sync equality checks. The selected task’s base solution stores compact Racket while the canonical row stores pretty-printed Racket; byte equality produced a false failure although normalized SHA-256 values were identical. Evidence: `checks/main/task-tests-direct.log`; suggested change: expose/use one shared `normalize_racket_source()` helper in generated source-sync tests.
