items.text: (outer review wrapper) Make `python3 review.py check --help` hide the positional task ID that the outer wrapper already injects. The current inherited help advertises `id`, so supplying it causes `arcpuzzles: error: unrecognized arguments`. Evidence: `checks/main/task-tests-portable-v1-console.log`; suggested change: custom outer help or an explicit “omit ID” line before the inherited parser output.

Promote cyclic declared-rival coverage into a compact standard gate

**Affected tool/path:** the semantic-check/lesson-census path under `repo/src/arcpuzzles/` and the standard reviewer battery.

**Symptom.** A generator can pass source parity and produce only correct labels while still teaching a shortcut. In `c2fb0e01a539`, six wrong rules fit all canonical pairs. The existing small semantic smoke is useful, but the decisive evidence came from exhaustive cyclic starts in the task-local probe and the 300-lesson query-rotation census.

**Suggested change.** When `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` or `LESSON_COMPETITORS` is declared, add a cheap compact stage that materializes one full schedule cycle per band, verifies each canonical-shortcut claim against all canonical pairs, and fails if a rival survives the demonstrations but changes the production query. Offer query rotation under an explicit `require|diagnostic|off` policy. Emit only source hashes, seeds/sample indices, survivor names, and the first reproducer unless a failure requires full grids. This is the shared change that would most improve training-data quality.

Add a cheap exact-axis endpoint smoke before the full override matrix

**Affected tool/path:** generator linter / override-contract checker.

**Symptom.** Audit target `3f9bb51d528b` advertises `palette_kind=default|warm|cool|varied`, yet seed 17/sample 0 produces the identical grid hash for all four values. It also advertises dimension domains wider than the actual per-band `draw_int` calls accept. The full override checker can find these, but it is expensive.

**Suggested change.** Before constructing the large cross-product, probe each exact axis independently at its endpoints (and each enum token) for two fixed seeds in every band. Require either an observable pixel difference, an exact observed value, or an explicit incompatibility/rejection. Minimize failures into one case before continuing to the full matrix.

Add compact mode to `lesson-census`

**Affected tool/path:** `python -m arcpuzzles lesson-census`.

**Symptom.** The final 300-lesson report is about 12.9 MB even though it contains no ambiguity. That is valuable forensic detail but dominates the return package and forces evidence bundling.

**Suggested change.** Add `--compact-results`, analogous to the override checker. Retain generator/rule hashes, requested/materialized counts, accepted sample indices and input hashes, unique-input count, rival/rotation totals, checkpoint state, and every ambiguous/error reproducer, but omit full grids for clean lessons. Keep full mode available for authoring investigations.

The morphology failure was correctly actionable

The intermediate repair failed with generated object-count around seven versus canonical median two and maximum component size below the canonical range. The defect and distribution reports pointed to the same root cause, and the minimized metrics made the repair straightforward. No linter false positive was observed on the selected final source.

Persist completed battery stages incrementally

**Symptom.** The requested full before battery ran long enough to complete several stages, but the caller timeout terminated the wrapper before it copied the temporary check directory to `--out`. All completed stage receipts vanished, so I had to rerun source-bound stages individually under `checks/before-*`.

**Concrete example.** The retained baseline evidence consists of separate `checks/before-lint/result.json`, `checks/before-selfcheck/result.json`, `checks/before-defect_lint/result.json`, `checks/before-dist_gate/result.json`, and `checks/before-profile_floor/result.json` rather than one resumable `checks/before` battery.

**Suggested change.** Create the requested output directory before launching the battery and copy/flush each stage log, receipt, and journal entry as soon as that stage finishes. On interruption, write an `interrupted` summary with completed/pending stages and the source hash. A retry should resume from those receipts rather than discard them.

Add selected-generator task tests to the official battery

**Symptom.** The 12-stage official battery does not execute new tests under `generators/<task>/tests/`. A return can therefore be all green while its task-local regressions were never run unless the reviewer records a separate command.

**Concrete example.** `checks/after/checks/8a2e39528187_after_battery_summary.json` is 12/12 green but has no pytest stage. The separate `checks/task-local-tests.log` is the only evidence that all 50 new tests passed.

**Suggested change.** Add a `task_tests` stage that discovers the selected generator's `tests/` directory, runs it in the same relocated runtime used by checks, and records the generator hash and exact test paths. Keep it absent/green when no task tests exist, but never silently ignore tests that do exist.

Support audit/run labels distinct from `before` and `after`

**Symptom.** The check CLI restricts `--phase` to `before|after`. Required adversarial audits therefore have to masquerade as `after`, and their internal filenames say `*_after_*` even when written under an audit evidence directory. Repeated exploratory runs can also collide semantically with the actual repair's final after evidence.

**Concrete example.** `checks/audit-df53944d9b47-selfcheck/result.json` is an audit-only run, but its command/report phase is `after` and its inner log is named `df53944d9b47_after_selfcheck.log`.

**Suggested change.** Separate comparison semantics from run identity: keep an optional `--comparison-phase before|after`, and add a free-form validated `--run-label audit-df53944d9b47` used in filenames and receipts. At minimum, accept `audit` as a non-admission phase.

Synthesize a connectivity-vs-global-color rival for component tasks (top priority)

**Symptom.** An intermediate version of `515cca15a0b7` passed the full 12-stage
battery, its 300-lesson census, and a cyclic declared-rival probe, yet every
canonical and generated scene used a distinct color per 4-connected component.
The undeclared rule "union all cells of each color before testing border contact"
therefore fit everything. The failure was found only in manual final self-review;
the retained prior-source evidence is under `checks/prior-f3615f0496e3/`, and
the reproducing red tests are `checks/red-split-color-tests.log`.

**Suggested change.** In `repo/shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py` (or a
small companion structural-rival library), add an opt-in/generic probe for rules
that reason over monochrome connected components: compare the declared rule
mirror with a variant that aggregates disconnected pieces by color. At minimum,
warn when no sampled grid contains the same nonzero color in two disconnected
components with different semantic outcomes. This would catch a broad class of
object-segmentation shortcuts without requiring each author to imagine and
hand-code the rival.

Balance profile-floor samples across deterministic schedule residues

**Symptom.** A valid four-position schedule deliberately supplied one exact
canonical-profile layout per period (25%), but the profile-floor sample happened
to draw only 13 exact hits out of 60 and failed. Evidence:
`checks/split-profile_floor/checks/515cca15a0b7_after_profile_floor.json`. The
repair increased support to 40%, which is healthier here, but the tool's random
residue imbalance made the boundary behavior hard to interpret.

**Suggested change.** In the profile-floor runner, distribute each band's sample
indices deterministically across small schedule residues (for example modulo
2..8, as the semantic gate already reports), or report both empirical support
and exact residue coverage before enforcing a fraction. Keep the requirement for
at least one hit per band; make a fraction threshold reproducible rather than
sensitive to a small random draw.

Print the direct portable task-test reproduction environment

**Symptom.** Running the task test path directly from `repo/` failed collection
unless `shared/runtime` was manually added to `PYTHONPATH`, while the supported
`--stage task_tests` command passed and correctly assembled the portable runtime.
This is not a generator defect, but it slows test-first iteration.

**Suggested change.** Have the task-test stage print a copy-pastable direct
command (including its runtime directory or `PYTHONPATH`) in `result.json` and the
console footer. That would make focused red/green loops match the final portable
stage more easily.

items.text:
Top shared-tool change — make public check orchestration controller-safe

**Symptom.** A foreground `review.py run ... check` can be terminated by the outer controller while the inner stage is healthy, leaving `result.json` permanently at `status: "running"`. In this review, `checks/final-defect-lint/result.json` and `checks/after-full/result.json` are stale running receipts for the final source, while the managed/checkpointed run against the same final bytes completed all 12 stages green in `checks/after-final-managed/checks/42fb6b33deea_after_battery_summary.json`.

**Concrete impact.** The public command accepted a long inner timeout, but the foreground wrapper stopped earlier and did not rewrite the result as interrupted. This looks like a generator hang and forces reviewers to discover and invoke lower-level detached/checkpointed machinery.

**Suggested change.** In the public `review.py run` / check wrapper, either detach long batteries by default or propagate a controller deadline into the inner runner and checkpoint. On wrapper termination, atomically mark the current stage `interrupted` with controller reason, elapsed time, and a resumable command. Print both effective wrapper and inner timeouts before execution. Expose the existing managed/check-run path through one documented public flag so ordinary reviewers do not need internal orchestration knowledge.

**Symptom.** `checks/lesson-census-final.json` is about 10 MiB even though all 300 lessons and 1,200 rotations are clean. Most bytes are repeated full grids, which pushes a small source repair toward evidence bundling and makes manual inspection slower.

**Suggested change.** Add `lesson-census --compact-results`: retain source/runtime hashes, exact command/configuration, seeds and accepted indices, aggregate/per-band counts, all ambiguous/error lessons in full, and a deterministic clean sample; replace other clean grids with input/output hashes and a hash of the omitted canonical result stream. Keep full mode available for deep investigations.

Unregistered public-home task-tests now work through the provided copied-runtime wrapper, removing the previous catalog barrier; keep this path documented. Retain compact receipts outside staged runtime trees when packaging so temporary checkout copies do not enter the return.

Strict semantic checks should not pass an entirely weak, rival-free contract **(top shared change)

**Symptom.** The baseline `1d26c382ab68` semantic stage reported `require_rival_witness: true`, nine witnesses, and status `PASS`, while `weak_witnesses` contained all 9/9 names, `rival_claims` was empty, and no lesson competitors were declared. The public pairs also shared a fixed left answer, but that task-domain shortcut was invisible until it was explicitly declared. Evidence: `checks/before/checks/1d26c382ab68_before_semantic_gate.json`.

**Suggested shared change.** In `repo/shared/tools/generator_semantic_gate.py`, make strict/required-rival mode fail (or at minimum emit a blocking warning) when semantic witnesses exist but all are weak and neither `SEMANTIC_RIVALS` nor `LESSON_COMPETITORS` supplies an executable hypothesis. Keep task authors responsible for the rival definitions; the shared tool should not invent domain semantics. A useful message would name the weak witnesses and show a minimal declaration template.

**Task-local repair already included.** Four rivals and seven concrete witness bindings now produce zero weak witnesses and verified disagreement evidence. No shared file was changed.

Run the portable canonical-path preflight earlier or offer an autofix hint

**Symptom.** Both the assigned task and audit target `f7c6c7bbc781` used `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "data/canonical/puzzles.jsonl"`. In the copied runtime this points under the task directory and fails before pytest. Evidence: `checks/task-tests-before/result.json` and `checks/audit/f7c6c7bbc781/task-tests/result.json`.

**Suggested shared change.** Extend the regular lint stage to scan selected task tests for fixed `parents[...]` canonical paths, or add a copyable autofix snippet to the existing preflight diagnostic:

```python
from reviewer_support import canonical_pairs, find_root
pairs = canonical_pairs(TASK_ID, root=find_root(__file__))
```

The current diagnostic is already precise and actionable; moving it earlier would prevent a late handoff failure.

Keep query-rotation status prominent in the compact battery summary

**Symptom.** Ordered production lessons can pass while a different query position remains ambiguous. The detailed semantic JSON records rotation results, but the battery summary only says the stage is green.

**Suggested shared change.** Add compact fields such as `lesson_rotations_checked`, `lesson_rotations_ambiguous`, and `rotation_policy` to the battery summary. This would let maintainers distinguish an ordered-only pass from required arbitrary-query support without opening the large semantic report.

**Top shared change — remove the universal `EXAMPLES_NEEDED >= 2` semantic warning

**Symptom.** `scripts/generator_semantic_gate.py` exits nonzero for audit target `d7b84df5a06a` solely because `EXAMPLES_NEEDED=1`, with the claim that one demonstration cannot refute a rival. That statement is false for structured examples containing multiple independent subproblems. The task's one four-chamber pair fires all eight witnesses, refutes every declared rival, agrees with Racket, and passes its own `lesson_identifiable` hook. See `checks/audit/d7b84df5a06a/semantic/checks/d7b84df5a06a_after_semantic_gate.log` and `checks/audit/d7b84df5a06a/one-demo-proof/evidence.json`.

**Suggested change.** Permit any positive integer `EXAMPLES_NEEDED`. Determine vacuity from behavior: for each query-disagreeing rival, require at least one demonstration on which the rival differs from the true output. Warn only when no actual refutation exists, or when no rival can disagree on the sampled query. Keep a separate optional pedagogical-size advisory if desired, but do not conflate example count with logical identifiability.

Continue the override matrix for probeable axes after metadata failures

**Symptom.** The override checker for `c868b0210c96` correctly found three unprobeable declarations, then fail-fast stopped at 0/0 draws. `command`, `n_panels`, and `palette_size` had enumerable domains, but the checker did not directly exercise them. A manual source-bound reproducer shows `command=0` is silently ignored and materially changes Racket output (`checks/audit/c868b0210c96/counterexample/evidence.json`). The report still caught missing observers, but not the simplest per-axis mismatch.

**Suggested change.** Preserve fail-fast for the invalid axes while running an explicitly labelled **partial matrix** over independently probeable axes. Report both totals: `unprobeable_axes` and `tested_axes`. This would surface ignored controls without making an invalid declaration look globally healthy. The current `--no-fail-fast` option is useful, but a bounded automatic partial pass would provide better default evidence.

Add a controller heartbeat / abandoned-run marker at battery stage boundaries

**Symptom.** The final selected-task battery was externally interrupted three times between otherwise short stages. Each standalone stage passed quickly, and `--resume` eventually produced a source-matched 12/12 aggregate, but the intermediate summary remained `running` with pending stages and a stale controller identity until another resume. Evidence is retained under `checks/after-final/progress.log` and the archived resume attempts in the same check directory.

**Suggested change.** Write a small heartbeat containing controller PID, process start time, and monotonic timestamp; on status/resume, distinguish an alive matching process from PID reuse or an abandoned controller. At stage start, also flush a structured `stage_started` record immediately. This would make external harness timeouts easier to diagnose and would reduce uncertainty about whether a stage itself hung.

Positive result — source-bound portable task tests worked well

The `task_tests` stage copied the selected tests, workspace oracle, canonical data, and public API into an isolated runtime and recorded every source hash. It caught both implementation and portability issues without requiring a sibling repository. The final result (`checks/task-tests-final2/result.json`) is unusually easy to audit: 32 passed, zero skips, and the runtime manifest binds the exact generator/workspace bytes. Retaining this stage as a required handoff check is strongly recommended.

ordinary diversity can miss a closed translated bank (D1)

**Symptom:** before distribution/diversity checks pass, but the whole input
support is 199 grids and ten normalized layouts. In every band, a 300-row prefix
covers all 300 normalized signatures in the next seed window.
**Evidence:** `checks/baseline_exact_capacity.json`,
`checks/baseline_census.json`, and the before battery's structured summary.
**Change:** add a task-calibrated, transform-normalized support/seed-prefix gate.
The assigned workspace's `review_probe.py` and `fixed_bank_capacity.py` implement
repeatable probes, source hashes, failed-sample retention, and an opt-in local
threshold. The corresponding final census passes. Do not generalize this task's
40% cutoff or translation normalizer to every task without reviewing its grammar.

synthetic solve packets need their own importable source (T1)

**Symptom:** the whole repository suite has one failure:
`tests/test_review_solve.py::test_duties_solve_preparation_runs_from_packet_root`.
The subprocess's generated packet cannot import `arcpuzzles`; copying only a tiny
synthetic library omits the source that an actual packet carries.
**Evidence:** `checks/logs/repository_tests.log`; pristine reproduction and proposed
fix in `checks/fixture_import_repair.json`.

packet. `workspace/verify_fixture_repair.py` applies that exact proposal only in
an isolated temporary tree: pristine target fails; the proposed version passes
all 21 tests in `test_review_solve.py`. The report includes the ready-to-apply
unified diff. Shared source was not changed by this assignment; its repository
suite remains 165 passed / 1 failed until the maintainer integrates the repair.

shell success text should agree with structured stage counts (D2)

**Symptom:** the successful before invocation prints “ALL 12 stages green”, while
its structured summary says 11 green and 1 advisory. `semantic_gate` is
`NO_CONTRACT`, not a semantic pass. This is a misleading aggregation message, not
a failing selected-task output.
**Evidence:** `checks/logs/before.log` and
`checks/before/checks/17b682bce66f_before_battery_summary.json`.
**Change:** derive the console ending from the structured counts/verdict; keep
exit-zero advisory outcomes distinct from semantic passes. The task-local exact
canonical hook fixes the missing contract here, but not the shared console text.

public lesson ambiguity should be surfaced, not counted as a solved rule (S1)

**Symptom:** the final generated lesson has three visible pairs compatible with
four tested collision policies. These policies make two different predictions
for its second masked input. A 3/3 visible score consequently does not identify
the behavior the query asks for. No hidden label is required to witness this.
**Evidence:** `solve/public_probe.py`, `solve/public_probe.json`,
`solve/SOLVE_NOTES.md`, and `solve/summary.json`. Challenge SHA-256:
`7712c9226c81736a5fccd04a4ac1657acbdfdf7af28f8e51c1b31ea05d7374fb`.
**Change:** for this task, include a collision-disambiguating demonstration when
queries exercise collisions, or flag the lesson for review. The supplied public
probe is a small starting hypothesis class, not a proof of identifiability when
it finds no ambiguity. Its rejected controlled candidates are intentional
teaching negatives, not claimed accidental model mistakes. Keep the exposure
record and masked-correctness withholding; do not inflate visible fit into
blind-solve accuracy or automatically admit this exposed episode to training.

Make declared query-order support an intake gate

**Priority: highest shared-tool change.** The ordinary baseline battery for
`06b4c496c6cf` was green even though the same source failed 38/72 arbitrary
held-out-query positions. Evidence:
`checks/before-required-rotations/checks/06b4c496c6cf_before_semantic_gate.json`
and the compact reproducer `checks/rotation_ambiguity_before.json`.

Suggested change: add an explicit generator declaration such as
`QUERY_POLICY = "ordered" | "arbitrary_rotation"`. When it is
`arbitrary_rotation`, the normal semantic gate should automatically enforce
`--require-rotations-identifiable`; when ordered, retain the current rotation
report as diagnostic. This prevents reviewers from accidentally accepting a
fixed-order pass for data that downstream tooling later rotates.

Run portable task tests as part of the standard after handoff

The 12-stage battery does not execute selected task-local tests. This task's
baseline tests used a fixed `Path(__file__).parents[...]` layout and failed in
the isolated task-test runtime even while the main battery passed. Evidence:
`checks/task-tests-before/result.json`; the repaired portable run is
`checks/task-tests-final-2/result.json`.

Suggested change: have `package_return.py` or the final handoff validator require
a successful `task_tests` receipt whenever task tests exist, and lint new tests
for direct canonical path guesses. The documented `reviewer_support` helpers
already provide the correct replacement.

Emit a compact override report by default for audit-only targets

Audit batteries produced tens of megabytes of successful override case rows
while the actionable result was a small set of repeated mismatch categories.
For example, `1d8a1c70332a` produced 73,914 findings, mostly duplicate
`override_mismatch` rows. The originals are retained as deterministic gzip
artifacts with hashes in `checks/EVIDENCE-COMPRESSION-MANIFEST.json`.

Suggested change: default audit-only batteries to compact override receipts,
retaining all failed *equivalence classes* plus a bounded number of examples per
root cause. Preserve an opt-in full matrix for generator authors who need every
row.

items.text:
Biggest avoidable friction: review-time single-query projection

Reviewers need to inspect four qualified queries as separate public turns before owner acceptance; this currently requires a task-local exporter. Consider promoting the included `export_qualified.py` projection and its rejection tests into a shared native command that keeps qualification evidence distinct from acceptance and training admission.

Preserve payload exit status when clearing noninteractive terminals — highest-priority shared change

**Symptom:** `run_with_racket.py`/the review wrapper emits `TERM environment variable not set` and terminal-clear output after otherwise successful commands. In a compound shell, the clear operation can become the wrapper's observable status instead of the payload status. The clearest reproduction is `checks/tdd-green-counterexample.log`: pytest reports `43 passed`, but the enclosing tool call was marked failed after the terminal-clear step. The final task-test driver reached exit 0 but still appended the same warning (`checks/task-tests-final-driver.log`).

**Suggested change:** in the shared wrapper path, clear only when `stdout.isatty()` and `TERM` is set to a usable value, or make clearing best-effort while explicitly returning the saved payload exit code. A minimal pattern is `payload_rc = ...; if isatty and TERM: clear(); return payload_rc`. This prevents false failures in agents, CI, pipes, and redirected logs without changing interactive behavior.

Automatically compact very large override failures by root cause

**Symptom:** the baseline override gate produced 14,773 findings plus 15,180 legacy multi-axis rejections. The compact rerun was useful, but the first full report/log was noisy enough to obscure the three actual causes: band-incompatible declared ranges, validator-incompatible degenerate textures, and accepted unknown keys. Evidence: `checks/before/checks/fea6a4ce763f_before_override_results.json` and `checks/before/checks/fea6a4ce763f_before_override.log`.

**Suggested change:** when finding count crosses a threshold, automatically print only minimized root causes and per-category counts while still retaining the complete machine-readable case shard. Keep `--compact-results` as an explicit override, but make pathological matrices readable by default and include the command needed to inspect the full shard.

Add a one-command source-bound semantic witness exporter

**Symptom:** retaining a proper shortcut witness currently requires three steps: generate/write an input, call `arcpuzzles apply`, then merge the Racket receipt with rival output and generator metadata. This review kept those intermediate files under `checks/question/`, but the procedure is easy to perform incompletely.

**Suggested change:** add an `arcpuzzles witness TASK --seed ... --sample-index ... --difficulty ... --rival NAME --out FILE` command that loads only a declared rival, generates the input, validates it, obtains the canonical Racket output through the public runner, computes the rival output, and writes one source/rule-hash-bound JSON artifact. It should refuse undeclared rivals unless an explicit unsafe flag is supplied. The desired schema is exemplified by `repo/generators/fea6a4ce763f/counterexamples/most_frequent_color_split_distractor.json`.

Promote declared-period query rotation into the shared semantic gate

**Symptom.** The regular semantic smoke check and a random lesson census can miss a bad cyclic start. A generator may contain one distinguishing witness per period, pass ordered production examples, and fail when that witness is held out as the query.

**Concrete evidence.** The selected task needed a separate `lesson-census --enumerate-schedule-period` run (`checks/schedule-census-final.json`) and a task-local probe (`repo/generators/1acd7639146e/workspace/probe_schedule.py`) to establish every start/holdout. The audit reproduction at `checks/audit/0846393acd63/report.json` shows a three-demo local shortcut followed by a rectangular query.

**Suggested shared change.** In the shared semantic stage, when `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD` exists and `--require-rotations-identifiable` is active, automatically enumerate every residue for one fixed seed in each band and make any unrefuted query-changing rival blocking. Report start residue, held-out index, rival name, and refuting demo indices. This is the highest-priority shared-tool change.

Report transformation-effect and informative-example rates

**Symptom.** A valid generator can emit many labels where output equals input, which teaches an identity shortcut even though the Racket rule and self-check both succeed.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/audit/81f7234dc4a2/report.json` found 31/1,000 default draws with no color-1 body cell below a marked header column. The retained seed 730015/sample 200 has ten body cells, but none selected; the canonical Racket output exactly equals the input.

**Suggested shared change.** Add an advisory distribution metric to `dist_gate`/`lesson-census`: fraction of pairs with changed output, and per-lesson counts of rule-activating versus no-op demonstrations. Allow task-local opt-outs because identity examples can be pedagogically intentional; flag only high no-op rates or lessons with no activating demonstration.

items.text:
Make schedule enumeration diagnostics self-explanatory and composable

**Priority shared-tool change.** `arcpuzzles check --stage audit --enumerate-schedule-period` failed for `cf6ef609da0d` with “Enumeration requires the matching staged runtime manifest; use arcpuzzles check,” even though the command was already executed through `arcpuzzles check` and its staged audit runtime. Evidence: `checks/audit/cf6ef609da0d-audit-stage/result.json` and its semantic log. The full battery on the same source successfully enumerated and passed semantics, so the combined `audit` preset and standalone semantic path disagree about manifest plumbing.

Suggested change: have the `audit` preset pass its freshly created runtime-manifest identity into the semantic stage exactly as the battery path does, and add an integration test for `--stage audit --enumerate-schedule-period` on a generator with `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD`.

Explicit enumeration requires a valid period; missing declaration alone is not a wrong-label or observed lesson-ambiguity claim.
items.text:
Distinguish “no declared period” from semantic ambiguity

For `fb413112b7c8`, requesting enumeration fails the semantic stage because `schedule_profile` and a four-item `SCHEDULE_PROFILES` exist but `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD` is absent. Evidence: `checks/audit/fb413112b7c8-battery/checks/fb413112b7c8_audit_semantic_gate.log`. The message is technically correct, but the aggregate failure obscures that ordinary witness/rival checks ran and produced useful counts.

Suggested change: report a dedicated contract finding such as `missing_schedule_period_declaration`, preserve the non-enumerated semantic verdict separately, and state the one-line remedy (`LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD = len(SCHEDULE_PROFILES)`). In diagnostic mode, consider skipping enumeration while marking schedule coverage unknown; strict mode may still fail.

items.text:
Lint portable tests before staging them

`fb413112b7c8`'s test uses a fixed `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "data/canonical/..."`, which breaks in the portable runtime. The task-test preflight catches it, but only after staging. Evidence: `checks/audit/fb413112b7c8-task-tests-final/result.json`.

Suggested change: extend the task-test linter to flag fixed parent-depth canonical paths and recommend `reviewer_support.find_root(__file__)`, `canonical_path`, and `canonical_pairs` before launching the isolated runtime. This would turn a runtime-only failure into an immediate actionable authoring diagnostic.

items.text:
Keep strict-scalar detector summaries machine-readable

The defect linter correctly found 204 strict-scalar cases for `fb413112b7c8` and 39 for `cf6ef609da0d`, but the concise human log only prints the final representative case. Evidence: the two audit battery defect-lint logs and `checks/audit/contract-probes.json`.

Suggested change: always retain a small JSON summary grouped by call argument/axis and invalid type, with one replay tuple per group. This would reduce the need for reviewers to build an additional probe merely to distinguish seed, index, difficulty, and override failures.

Validate every executable rival's output before semantic scoring — **highest priority shared change

**Symptom.** A declared orientation rival returned `[]` as a sentinel on one branch. The battery's semantic smoke stage did not reject that declaration, but `lesson-census` later produced 300 production scoring errors and 1,200 rotation scoring errors. Evidence: `checks/lesson-census.json`; corrected evidence: `checks/lesson-census-v2.json`.

**Suggested change.** In the shared semantic-gate/lesson-scoring path, invoke each live `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`, `SEMANTIC_RIVALS`, and `LESSON_COMPETITORS` callable on at least one lawful input per declared branch, then validate that the result is a nonempty rectangular integer grid. Fail with the declaration name and sample identity before lesson aggregation. This should be a contract failure, not an ambiguity result.

A task-local regression demonstrating the desired behavior is `generators/ebe355c22d70/tests/test_generator.py::test_every_declared_rival_returns_a_well_formed_grid_on_lawful_inputs`.

Add an opt-in exhaustive gate for small finite lesson schedules

**Symptom.** Random lesson smoke tests do not establish that every cyclic schedule start remains identifiable after every possible query rotation. The intermediate generator also declared a sixteen-member output codomain while ordinary scheduling reached only four members; the official linter found that particular issue, but it did not combine schedule coverage with rotated lesson identifiability.

**Suggested change.** When `SCHEDULE_PROFILES` is finite and below a configurable cap, enumerate each cyclic start for every difficulty band, use the live competitor declarations, rotate each pair through the query position, and compare the observed output signatures with `EXPECTED_OUTPUT_CODOMAIN`. Keep it opt-in or diagnostic for intentionally ordered curricula.

The reusable prototype is `generators/ebe355c22d70/workspace/probe_schedule.py`; `checks/schedule-probe.json` records 48 starts, 192 rotations, 1,536 rival checks, and 16/16 output profiles.

Ensure the battery wrapper exits after a child stage checkpoints completion

**Symptom.** On this packet, the outer battery process repeatedly remained alive after the current child stage had finished and written a valid receipt. The supported `--resume` flow recovered correctly, and the final aggregate is complete, but reaching 12/12 required segmented invocations. Evidence: `checks/after-final/progress.log`, `checks/after-final/attempts/`, and final `checks/after-final/result.json`.

**Suggested change.** Audit process/pipe shutdown at each stage boundary: close inherited stdout/stderr handles, reap the bounded child, and have the controller automatically convert a completed receipt plus a nonterminating wrapper into an interrupted-but-resumable state. An optional `--max-stages-per-invocation` would also make long batteries predictably resumable without relying on an outer execution limit.

items.text:
Make battery process ownership and interruption state self-healing — highest-priority shared change

**Affected tool/path:** the `arcpuzzles check --battery` controller/resume path and `scripts/run_generator_battery.sh`.

**Symptom/example:** the first completed-source v3.0 battery ran lint, self-check, and rule-smoke, then its wrapper detached/was killed while the child state and lock remained. `checks/after-final/progress.log` stopped at the next stage and `checks/after-final/result.json` remained a non-final running aggregate; recovery required launching a separately supervised process and explicitly using `--resume` (`checks/after-final-resume.out`). The resumed receipts were sound, but determining whether the original parent, child, or lock was authoritative required manual process inspection.

**Suggested change:** have the controller record its PID, process-group ID, heartbeat, and an atomic final exit marker. On startup/resume, detect a dead owner, mark the attempt `interrupted`, archive the stale lock, import intact completed receipts, and continue automatically. The wrapper should forward termination and wait for the process group so an outer harness losing its pipe cannot leave a misleading `running` result.

items.text:
Promote held-out-query rotation to an optional semantic gate

**Symptom/example:** the fixed-query 12-lesson semantic smoke test passed the v3.0 curriculum, but the production-shaped census found 402/1,200 ambiguous rotations (`checks/lesson-census-final.out`). Per-witness frequency was not enough: one held-out position removed the lesson's only counterexample.

**Suggested change:** when a task declares `LESSON_COMPETITORS` and downstream assembly permits pair rotation, add a bounded `--rotate-query` semantic mode that tests every pair in each sampled lesson as the query. Report separately: rival fits demonstrations, rival differs on query, query index, replay seed/sample indices, and source hashes. Keep this optional because fixed-order training pipelines can legitimately disallow rotations.

items.text:
Run the unknown-override-key probe before the full override matrix

**Symptom/example:** audit task `a631936f7715` required 60,750 matrix draws before reporting a one-call contract defect: `**overrides` silently accepted `__override_contract_unknown_axis__`. The minimized reproducer is `checks/audit/a631936f7715/unknown-override.json`.

**Suggested change:** make unknown-key rejection a constant-cost preflight before estimating/running the Cartesian matrix. Fail fast on acceptance while still optionally running the matrix under `--keep-going`; this gives authors an actionable result in seconds and avoids spending most of the gate on a generator already known to violate the public contract.

**[TOP SHARED TOOL CHANGE] Migrate legacy frozen fixtures before packet staging

**Symptom.** The required portable task-test run passes all 18 tests, but the
issued frozen fixture
`repo/generators/a9f315ca9cc7/tests/test_generator_a9f315ca9cc7.py` imports
`scripts.canonical_profile_gate`. Portable execution warns that this is a legacy,
layout-dependent helper. The reviewer duties correctly forbid editing the frozen
fixture, so the warning cannot be repaired in the allowed task delta.

**Concrete evidence.** The fixture’s final SHA-256 exactly matches the issued
baseline (`cd988c6c…`), and the portable run is green in
`checks/task-tests/result.json` and `checks/task-tests/checks/task_tests.xml`.
Earlier red/green snapshots demonstrate that new tests can use portable
`reviewer_support` helpers without modifying the inherited file.

**Suggested change.** In the packet builder or pre-staging validator, scan the
fixture that will be frozen for imports from `scripts.*` and migrate supported
canonical/profile calls to `reviewer_support` before computing the assignment
baseline. Where migration must be deferred, mark the diagnostic explicitly as
an inherited non-actionable warning so reviewers do not have to choose between
violating the freeze and returning noisy evidence.

items.text:
Make the audit preset retain defect-lint evidence even when semantic contract is missing

**Symptom.** `arcpuzzles check TASK --stage audit` fails immediately at the
missing semantic contract for both drawn audit targets. That is correct, but it
leaves the remaining source-quality checks pending. To obtain the actionable
strict-scalar, dead-texture, and domain findings, I had to run `defect_lint`
separately and reconcile two evidence trees.

**Concrete evidence.** See
`checks/audit/e71b8db9e07b-combined/result.json` versus
`checks/audit/e71b8db9e07b-defect-lint/`, and
`checks/audit/7f2dafa2bee4-combined/result.json` versus
`checks/audit/7f2dafa2bee4-defect-lint-v2/`.

**Suggested change.** Let the audit preset run independent static/source stages
with keep-going semantics even when semantic-gate setup fails, or emit a compact
aggregate receipt that includes both the missing-contract verdict and standalone
defect-lint summary. Do not convert either to advisory; the goal is one
source-bound audit receipt with all independent findings, not a weaker gate.

items.text:
Make declared-rival lesson identifiability an admission gate

**Priority: highest; shared-tool change needed.** The task baseline reached the
training-data path with `NO_CONTRACT`, so correct Racket labels and diverse grids
could still encode a positional shortcut. `checks/qwen-gate-reproducer.json`
contains a deterministic 3-demo/1-query case where every label and uniqueness
check passes, but `crop_top_left_block` survives all demonstrations and fails the
query.

Proposed change: in `src/arcpuzzles/worker.py::lesson_check` and the dataset
admission path, require a source-bound `passed_declared_hook` result for every
query when a task declares `LESSON_COMPETITORS`; treat a missing contract as an
explicit review warning/waiver rather than ordinary success. Reuse Racket labels
already produced for the episode, retain the first counterexample seed/input
hash, and keep generic searched rivals advisory. The task-local reproducer and
one-test RED/GREEN harness under `checks/tools/` are a small executable spec for
the shared behavior.

items.text:
Randomized allocation/data-quality audit — separate evidence tier from nominal weight

Seed:
`fa92ffbfd8368c880d209c78bf5533415e01b485f3dfed29d4f239e0f67fb4ad`.
Sampling exactly
`random.Random(int(seed,16)).sample(sorted(PACKET-MANIFEST.json["all_ids"]),3)`
selected `1520a56aa617`, `26b41ff6047f`, and `5875afa30211`. The reusable extractor,
its four tests, and the source-bound report are in
`checks/tools/allocation_audit_extract.py`,
`checks/tools/test_allocation_audit_extract.py`, and
`checks/allocation-audit.json`.

Observed current allocation:

- all three records are internal-bank provenance, unapproved, absent from the
  252-ID normal authoring pool and 254-ID main pool, yet each retains nominal
  dataset sampling weight `1.0`;
- all three catalog rows are lint warnings, so equal nominal weight does not
  encode review quality;
- `5875afa30211` has a retained unresolved exact-axis contract defect;
- `1520a56aa617` has reach `0.687`, four locked axes, and only its canonical
  4-train/1-test supervision; `26b41ff6047f` has reach/diversity `1.0` but still
  lacks approval evidence in this packet;
- the sample contains no ARC-GEN or RE-ARC item, so it cannot support a source
  ranking. Internal provenance also did not guarantee quality.

The actual authoring policy remains distinct: 90% uniform over the normal pool
and 10% public-evaluation focus, with 120 anchors but only one mapped task and two
eligible related generators in this packet. Do not infer authoring probability
from `generator_weights.json`.

Concrete alternative for a bounded **review-allocation** pilot, without changing
the 10% focus or training boundaries: allocate 60% of review slots to
high-reach items with unresolved source-bound findings, 30% to approved/all-green
items filling underrepresented source/difficulty cells, and retain 10% uniform
sentinels. Training admission remains approval-gated; nominal dataset weights do
not override it. Compare this with uniform review allocation on 30 items per arm
(90–120 generated episodes per arm), measuring accepted identifiable four-query
lessons per 1,000 Racket calls, unique-input rate, critical defects, ambiguity,
and deduplication loss. Stop the harmful arm after at least five critical defects
or >10% ambiguity; otherwise stop at 30 items/arm, or early when the Wilson 95%
lower bound shows a >10 percentage-point advantage in usable lessons per cost.
This is an estimate/proposal, not a measured corpus-wide result.

Coverage limits: source-only bounded inspection; no model job, corpus-wide
rerun, or new Racket work; no sampled ARC-GEN/RE-ARC record; stored weights may be
candidate metadata rather than actual admitted-training probabilities.

Let portable task tests run even when one frozen legacy fixture fails path preflight

`checks/task-tests/result.json` stops before collection because the inherited
frozen `test_generator_4d5bb3c0250b.py:30` guesses a canonical path using fixed
`parents[...]` depth. The new portable tests are valid but the stage never runs
them, so one legacy-path diagnostic masks all task-local regression evidence.

Proposed change: make task-test preflight report each nonportable file as a
separate failed case while still collecting unaffected test files, or stage a
read-only compatibility adapter generated by the runner. Do not silently create
filesystem shims. The final verdict should remain failed until the legacy file is
migrated, but the receipt should include real pass/fail counts for portable tests.

items.text:
Add a compact-success option to the required lesson-census recipe

The successful 300-episode census produced a 19,226,496-byte JSON report, and the
full override stage produced an 11.7 MB success matrix. Both are useful for deep
forensics but exceed the complete return budget when combined. The lesson summary
already contains counts, source hashes, accepted indices, error totals, and the
full-report hash.

Proposed change: expose `--compact-results` for `lesson-census`, retaining all
failures/ambiguities, first witnesses, replay recipes, source bindings, and
aggregate per-band/rotation counts while omitting successful grids. This mirrors
the override check's compact mode and would avoid reviewer-side pruning of large
all-green evidence.

Let a declared lesson schedule be verified in the same strict battery

**Priority shared-tool change.** The semantic gate marks an otherwise fully
passing generator `WARN` solely because `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD` is declared but
has not been separately enumerated. Under the required after policy, that keeps
the battery from being all green even when 12/12 lessons and all 60 query
rotations are identifiable.

**Concrete example.** With period 4 declared for `03000b260ae0`, the gate reported
`declared_period_not_enumerated (period=4)` while recording strict 600/600,
canonical 5/5, witnesses 3/3, rival claims 3/3, lessons 12/12, and rotations 0/60
ambiguous. Evidence: `checks/intermediate-schedule-period/03000b260ae0_after_semantic_gate.log`. The reviewer either has to run a separate enumeration and somehow
bind it back to the gate, or omit the useful declaration. The final task therefore
keeps `SCHEDULE_PROFILES` and exhaustive cyclic tests but cannot publish the
reserved period constant without losing a clean gate.

**Proposed fix.** Add a battery option that automatically enumerates a declared
period (fixed seed, all configured bands) and lets that source-bound result
satisfy the warning in the same output. Alternatively, treat the missing
enumeration as a clearly reported advisory that does not prevent the strict
semantic stage itself from passing when required rotations are already green.
The separate `lesson-census --enumerate-schedule-period` should remain available
for deeper evidence.

Normalize wrapper output paths to the workspace

**Symptom.** `review.py run/check` executes payloads from `WORK/repo`. A caller at
the packet root who naturally passes `--out WORK/checks/name` gets evidence under
`WORK/repo/WORK/checks/name`, while console logs are often stored under
`WORK/checks`. This split is documented, but it is easy to create nested evidence
that then must be copied into the return.

**Concrete example.** The decisive battery initially landed at
`WORK/repo/WORK/checks/after-final2-battery`; its console was
`WORK/checks/after-final2-battery.console.log`. I copied the source-bound reports
to `checks/final-battery/` for a coherent handoff.

**Proposed fix.** Have the outer `review.py` wrapper accept workspace-relative
`--out` paths and rewrite them for the repo-cwd payload, or print the resolved
absolute output path before launch and reject accidental `WORK/repo/WORK/...`
paths. This would reduce duplicate evidence and packaging mistakes without
changing the inner CLI.

Add a structured sequence-level curriculum gate

**Symptom.** `80271cb9b303` declared `4, 3, then 5..6`, but the third slot drew
`3..6`. The normal battery was green because it checked samples and a small set
of identifiable lessons, not conformance to the declared slot schedule.
`checks/before-curriculum-contract.json` reproduces 112 violations.

**Suggested fix.** Permit generators to expose a machine-readable
`CURRICULUM_CONTRACT` describing slot constraints, cyclic assembly, and required
support. Add a fast source-bound gate that samples each slot, checks observed
axes, and evaluates all cyclic starts. Do not infer hard contracts from prose.

Make long battery execution resumable without orphan ambiguity

**Symptom.** The exact all-stage command exceeded the caller's single-command
execution window while a child battery process continued normally. Stage-local
commands passed, and a detached uninterrupted replay was needed to capture the
full result. The first partial attempt is retained in `checks/after-command.log`.

**Suggested fix.** Have `arcpuzzles check --battery` immediately write a stable
run ID and PID/heartbeat receipt, plus an explicit `--resume RUN_ID` or
`--follow RUN_ID` command. That would distinguish an actual gate timeout from a
front-end transport timeout and avoid duplicate stage execution.

Supply an official source-tree runner for frozen task fixtures

**Symptom.** The frozen baseline `test_generator_80271cb9b303.py` imports the
materialized runtime module and assumes a runtime-relative canonical path, so
plain `pytest generators/80271cb9b303/tests` from the source tree fails during
collection. The fixture is correctly immutable, but the packet does not expose
a one-command adapter for it. Evidence: `checks/task-tests-before.log`.

**Suggested fix.** Add a repository command that materializes the selected task
runtime and executes frozen fixtures there, while separately discovering new
source-bound tests. This preserves fixture immutability and gives reviewers one
reproducible test command.

items.text:
Make query-policy-aware rotation identifiability an export preflight **(top shared change)

**Symptom.** A generator can have correct labels and an ordered lesson that
refutes its rivals, yet become shortcut-teachable when the exporter chooses a
different pair as query. Audit target `bc5e668b7668` passes the intended ordered
idea but fails required rotations in 9/60 cases; see
`checks/audit/bc5e668b7668-rotations/checks/bc5e668b7668_after_semantic_gate.json`.

**Suggested change.** In the lesson exporter / `arcpuzzles check semantic_gate`,
bind a declared query policy into the artifact: `fixed_last`, `arbitrary_rotation`,
or a concrete allowed-index set. Automatically run the existing rotation scorer
over exactly those positions and block shard export only for supported positions
that remain ambiguous. This avoids both shortcut-contaminated data and false
positives for intentionally ordered curricula.

items.text:
Emit a compact companion summary for large lesson censuses

**Symptom.** The decisive census for this small task is 5.9 MB because it retains
all materialized lessons and replay evidence (`checks/lesson-census.json`), while
routine intake needs only the source hashes, counts, status, per-band totals, and
paths/hashes of exact failures.

**Suggested change.** Have `arcpuzzles lesson-census` additionally write
`<out>.summary.json` containing the top-level provenance and aggregates plus a

Surface source-matched resume as the primary recovery command

**Symptom.** The first foreground after-battery process ended while a long stage
was still running, but stage receipts were intact. The source-matched `--resume`
path safely reused the first three completed stages and finished 12/12 green.
Evidence is under `checks/after/attempts/0001/` and the final aggregate under
`checks/after/checks/`.

**Suggested change.** When an output contains a running/interrupted checkpoint,
print a single copy-pastable resume command prominently at the end of `progress.log`
and CLI output, including any policy flags bound into the checkpoint. This reduces
the chance reviewers accidentally restart or misreport a partial run.

Highest-priority shared change — compare canonical behaviors with ordinary generated support

The old d7f13ee34d85 labels were reference-lawful while its fit restriction made negative centering impossible, despite that behavior appearing in three of four canonical pairs. Scalar size/palette profiles and generator-declared witnesses cannot discover every omitted behavior when the old generator declares no contract. Add a task-justified canonical feature-support extension to `shared/tools/canonical_profile_gate.py` / `generator_semantic_gate.py`, preserving source/rule hashes, ordinary-versus-forced sampling, unique inputs and per-lesson exposure. Missing extractors should remain unreviewed, not green.

The task-local implementation is included at `generators/d7f13ee34d85/workspace/canonical_behavior_gate.py`, with four focused tests. It fails the original source and passes the repaired source. `QUESTION_ANSWER.md` describes the cheap budget and false-positive policy. No shared source was changed; generalizing the extractor/policy requires a maintainer decision.

Blind preparation exposes solver hints through provenance

`solve-blind` preparation automatically prints named competitors and their refutation status before the solve is finished. In this round these included all-left/all-right and closure-related alternatives. The post-repair preparation likewise prints frame-height/perimeter/clamping names. This metadata can prime a solver even when rule source and private labels remain closed.

Keep the public dimensions/grids and execution feedback, but withhold semantic rival names and statuses from visible-only preparation until finish. Retain complete provenance for later scoring/intake. Both solve notes here explicitly record the automatic metadata exposure; this is not evidence of deliberate reference consultation. Relevant paths: `src/arcpuzzles/review_solve.py` and the public prepare presentation.

Source heuristics conflate harmless identifiers and safe ancestor searches with defects

The first repair's linter warned because a lambda argument was named `objects`; it was only a list argument in a diagnostic rank comparison. Renaming it removed the warning without changing behavior (`checks/after-1/`). The task-test preflight also flags an unbounded, `find_root`-bounded ancestor search as a fixed parent-depth guess; the exact portable task tests still pass 27/27. See `checks/task-tests-v42-command.log`.

Make the identifier check sensitive to call/import context, and make the path check distinguish indexed `.parents[n]` guesses from a search constrained to the nearest canonical root and the selected task. Preserve warnings for real authority duplication and runtime path escapes. No checker was disabled or patched to get a pass.

Keep accepted lesson evidence and sampling coordinates visible in schedule diagnostics

The first repair had 300/300 ordered lessons pass but 167/1,200 rotations fail. Its successor's `(seed+index)%2` phase collapsed every `generate(sd,sd)` call to the canonical profile; the existing defect linter correctly caught this. Final source separates seed mixing from index progression and uses two teaching roles, with the runtime checking materialized demonstrations after any rejections.

Extend schedule reports to show paired `(seed,index)` conventions, profile exposure, accepted-index gaps and rotation policy together. An ordinary-sample histogram or raw cyclic proof must not be reported as accepted-lesson coverage. The retained failures and final required-rotation census provide regression fixtures. Both audit targets add actual production examples of missing teaching support: an unseen code in 727667a2d7b7 and a canonical-fitting nearest-seed shortcut in e58b545527d3. Their existing rule labels are correct; the unrefuted lesson alternatives are the problem.

Biggest avoidable friction: Python and Racket rivals can encode subtly different orderings

The Python “bottom-right” selector and a reversed Racket bounding-box comparator initially represented different rules, allowing a real latest-top-left-anchor shortcut to hide. Add a small parity helper that executes each declared Racket rival on one fixture and requires it to match its Python semantic counterpart before large sweeps.

The main's retained source-bound learnability audit already identified row-copy
and side-only shortcuts, but its current review index had no audits and its notes
were blank. Surface unresolved retained findings in the current task index so
the next author can reuse the counterexamples directly.

items.text:
Support source binding for generic generators whose program is produced by a callable

**Symptom.** The source-bound battery helper for `generic_dense_motion_gen3` could not inspect the task because it requires a literal module-level `PROGRAM`, while this generic generator constructs its Racket program dynamically through `_program`. The lint failure was therefore about representation, not the reproduced semantic defect.

**Concrete evidence.** `checks/audits/generic_dense_motion_gen3-lint-r2.console.log` and `result.json` retain the failed source-binding attempt. Independently, `checks/audits/generic_dense_motion_gen3-parity.log` reports 123/123 Racket parity, and the public generated episode in `checks/audits/generic_dense_motion_gen3/racket-generated.jsonl` records executed rule hash `3df5cf16ac58` and generator SHA `6d4b39fd529f04aed087eb640d87750165c4fe635730061402873ccb04616bc0`.

**Proposed fix.** Let the battery subject resolve a standardized zero-argument/static program provider, or define a generic-generator provenance hook that emits the exact program template and parameter binding used for each episode. Hash the resolved text and parameters into the receipt. Continue rejecting arbitrary unbound dynamic code; the goal is an explicit supported interface, not a lint bypass.

Biggest avoidable friction: completed Racket stages can be stranded by the battery controller

The persistent-bridge battery sometimes finished a stage or stalled before writing the outer receipt, forcing manual checkpoint inspection and isolated reruns. Persist each stage receipt atomically as soon as the child exits, and have resume automatically restart only the first receipt-less stage with a fresh bridge.

Task-local regression tests are not automatically discovered by the inherited battery

**Symptom.** The generator battery can be 12/12 green while newly added tests under `generators/TASK/tests/` have never run. This assignment explicitly required those tests, so I had to retain a separate command and log (`checks/task-tests-final.log`).

**Suggested change.** Add a source-bound `task_tests` battery stage that discovers only the selected generator's `tests/` directory, builds the same staged runtime, and records the exact test paths and source hash. Keep repository-global pytest separate so a distant failure cannot obscure the selected task result.

The high-level check wrapper needs durable resume semantics across parent termination

**Symptom.** Expensive stages write child receipts, but when a front-end command is terminated, the Python wrapper can lose the staged runtime/output handoff even though the shell battery has durable journal concepts. Reviewers then rerun stages individually and manually reconcile evidence.

**Suggested change.** Expose `--resume` and `--status` on `arcpuzzles check`, keep the prepared runtime at a user-visible path until finalization, and reconstruct `result.json` from matching source-bound receipts after a parent restart. A command should either resume the same hash or loudly reject stale evidence.

Authority-sync failures should emit an exact patch target

**Symptom.** Baseline authority sync correctly reported two active exact-text groups, but the reviewer still had to locate which JSON fields were selected `target_code` versus archival `raw_code` and determine the safe synchronization direction.

**Suggested change.** Include a machine-readable list of JSON files/pointers, role (`canonical`, `selected`, `archival`), exact hashes, and a proposed patch that copies canonical text only into selected fields. Explicitly state which archival fields must remain untouched.

Promote the large lesson-window census from assignment prose into a reusable gate

**Symptom.** The inherited semantic gate used 12 lessons, while the assignment separately required at least 100 per band when canonical-compatible rivals exist. Without a standard tool, each reviewer can accidentally use a different seed policy, omit cyclic starts, hard-code rival names, or report overlapping windows as unique inputs.

**Suggested change.** Add a configurable `lesson_census` stage that dynamically unions `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` and `LESSON_COMPETITORS`, verifies canonical fit, follows the actual training sampler, reports per-band unique inputs and domain limits, and distinguishes demo survival from query disagreement. The retained `workspace/lesson_probe.py` demonstrates the minimum useful schema.

**Symptom.** A sound prototype required task-local code for program instantiation, protected Racket execution, public/private episode separation, label receipts, parameter-coverage checks, and no-overwrite evidence. **Top shared-tool change — distinguish advisory from passed in stage results

**Symptom.** `arcpuzzles check 8c6b703c91e5 --stage semantic_gate` printed
`ADVISORY` / `NO_CONTRACT`, and the battery correctly did not count it green, but

`checks/audit/8c6b703c91e5/semantic_gate.console.log` and its stage log.

**Suggested change.** In the shared check runner, emit a status enum such as
`green|advisory|failed|interrupted`; reserve `passed=true` for green, or add an
explicit `green` field and require callers to use it. Keep exit 0 for advisory if

additional cases in machine-readable JSON.

**Symptom.** The semantic gate evaluates declared rivals well, but a plausible
rival remains invisible until an author names it. For `f891d1ff5dd8`,

continuation-rival family for periodic or iterative rules. Given a task-local
period detector or declared period, synthesize stop-after-1-period,
stop-after-2-periods, and stop-after-max-demonstrated-extent transforms. Retain
only candidates that fit canonical pairs, then test them against the actual
lesson and allowed query rotations. Emit the smallest survivor with exact
inputs and query disagreement. This should be a shared-tool feature because the
failure pattern recurs across generators and cannot be repaired reliably by

**Shared-tool priority — add cyclic query-position shortcut checks to lesson census

**Symptom.** `repo/shared/tools/lesson_census.py` correctly reports that its current census “does not rotate every pair into alternative query positions.” A lesson can therefore contain a valid shortcut-refuting pair only in the masked query while every visible demonstration still supports the shortcut. Pair-level witness frequency and whole-lesson “somewhere refuted” counts are not sufficient for few-shot training quality.

**Concrete example.** For `5d3738a6b89c`, the canonical-fitting `first_anchor_per_key_only` rival is wrong only when a key repeats. The baseline could emit one anchor per key. A future sampler with only one repeated-key pair per four-pair lesson could pass a coarse lesson check but become ambiguous when that pair is the query. **Suggested change.** Add `--cyclic-query` (and a cheap `--preflight-per-band 8`) to `repo/shared/tools/lesson_census.py` / `repo/src/arcpuzzles/lesson_census.py`. For each materialized lesson, rotate each pair through the query position, iterate the generator’s actual `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` and `LESSON_COMPETITORS`, and record whether each rival is refuted by at least one visible demonstration. Save rival name, band, seed, start residue, query index, and the smallest ambiguous lesson. Reviewed curriculum exceptions should be explicit and hash-bound.

**Symptom.** The required before battery checkpointed several completed stages under `checks/before/` but the outer execution was interrupted before an aggregate verdict. The packet correctly warns that automatic resume is unavailable, so the only supported path is rerunning all stages. items.text:
**Top shared-tool change — provide one canonical Racket-program execution helper

**Symptom.** Task-local authoring code repeatedly strips `(rule! ...)`, binds a grid, and calls the bridge. It is easy to evaluate the enclosed lambda itself rather than apply it to the grid; the bridge then returns a procedure descriptor instead of a grid. The parametric prototype’s first execution test exposed exactly this integration mismatch before the executor was corrected to evaluate `(<lambda-body> g)`.

**Concrete example.** See `repo/generators/57799de7f990/workspace/parametric/prototype.py::execute` and `repo/generators/57799de7f990/tests/test_parametric_axis_mode.py::test_racket_labels_match_canonical_and_all_axis_modes_diverge_on_one_input`. items.text:
Auto-enumerate small declared lesson schedules in the prescribed final battery

**Priority: highest shared-tool change.**

**Symptom.** `DUTIES.md` prescribed the standard after battery, but strict after policy rejected the otherwise-clean semantic stage solely because `LESSON_SCHEDULE_PERIOD = 3` had not been explicitly enumerated. The retained run at `checks/after/` finished 11/12 green: all 12 sampled lessons and 48 diagnostic rotations were identifiable, yet `declared_period_not_enumerated` made the stage exit 1. Re-running the same source with `--require-rotations-identifiable --enumerate-schedule-period --schedule-seed 0` produced 12/12 green at `checks/after-enumerated/`.

**Suggested change.** When strict after policy sees a valid declared period below a conservative cap such as 16 or 32, have the battery automatically enumerate all starts at the documented fixed seed and bind that census into the semantic-stage receipt. Alternatively, generate the required command in `DUTIES.md` rather than the known-to-fail default. Keep explicit flags and diagnostics for large periods or custom ordering policies. This preserves the strict standard while removing a predictable failed full-battery iteration.

Make native qualification reject trailing Racket syntax

**Symptom:** `parametric qualify` successfully executed a `(rule! ...)` source
with one unmatched trailing `)`, because the rule-wrapper extraction stopped at
the first complete wrapper and ignored the suffix. The later causal-witness
builder uses `parse_all` and correctly rejected the same source as
`Unexpected )`.

**Evidence:** the first qualification passed, while
`checks/e64c021e29ad/causal-build-command.json` records the strict-parser
failure. After removing the trailing delimiters and adding
`test_every_authored_racket_source_is_one_complete_expression`, the corrected
source requalified and the witness replay passed.

**Suggested change:** before executing any setting program in native
qualification/acceptance, parse the full source and require exactly one complete
`rule!` or `lambda` expression, using the same validation path as
`arcpuzzles.review_witness`. This prevents qualification and witness validation
from disagreeing about the exact program bytes.

Exit-zero advisories must not print “ALL 12 stages green”

**Symptom:** `checks/before/result.json` has authoritative counts 10 green,
2 advisory and verdict `passed_with_advisories`, but its captured stdout ends
“ALL 12 stages green for 6d19cd1698b1 (before)”. The detailed JSON is already
correct; the terminal summary is misleading and can contaminate handoffs.
**Suggested change:** derive the final human message from `battery_summary`
counts/verdict, with distinct all-green versus advisory language. Add a CLI
regression with one zero-exit advisory and assert it cannot print all-green.
**This return:** reports the structured status and keeps the conflicting
stdout as evidence. No out-of-scope shared-script patch was made.

Make declared-control coverage and canonical admission first-class audits

**Symptom:** audit `3f600d3093b8` rejects a canonical one-row-marker example,
omits matrix color 8 despite canonical outputs containing it, advertises a
6..16 height range but enforces 8..12, and silently ignores several declared
controls. Audit `281f59ba6a02` returns the identical 16x17 input when explicitly
asked for a 10x10 single-plus scene and specific colors.
**Suggested change:** systematically compare declared integer bounds to actual
accepted boundaries, verify outputs using an observed-grid function, require
unknown-key rejection, and run self_check on every canonical input variant.
Avoid inferring compliance from non-crashing calls or deterministic equality.
**Evidence:** `checks/audit-evidence.json`; reproducible using `checks/audit_probe.py`.

Require distinguishing examples, not just canonical parity

**Symptom:** version 2.0.0 had correct Racket labels and substantial diversity,
yet every generated case fit both color-envelope and first-two-runs shortcuts.
Canonical parity alone could not expose the missing semantics.
**Suggested change:** use the existing SEMANTIC_WITNESSES / SEMANTIC_RIVALS /
CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS / WITNESS_RIVALS interfaces when plausible rivals are known.
Report actual Racket disagreements, per-band support and exact replay cases.
Do not add a redundant approval flag that bypasses these hooks.
**Built here:** two counterexample families, those hooks, and a source-bound
before/after probe. It deliberately does not claim lesson identifiability.

Document complete relocated-runtime staging for standalone tools

**Symptom:** initially importing `shared/runtime` failed with
`ModuleNotFoundError: scripts` because required helper modules are housed in
`shared/tools` and are relocated by the staging API. RACKET_PATH alone also
left 28 repository tests skipped because their guard checks PATH.
**Suggested change:** include one minimal documented `prepare_runtime(Catalog,
destination, task_id)` example and emphasize using `run_with_racket.py` for
repository tests. An ad hoc PYTHONPATH shim is not an equivalent runtime.
**Built here:** the probe stages a complete temporary runtime and includes a
source-layout launch regression; red and green logs are retained.

Keep per-band canonical-scale coverage separate from semantic stress

**Symptom:** adding valid new rule witnesses still failed strict profile_floor
because medium/hard retained no canonical-scale support. Easy-only overlap did
not suffice. Formal-rule stress grids alone would hide this training mismatch.
**Suggested change:** retain separate canonical admission/scale and semantic
contrast gates. Report the band-level floor before expensive downstream stages;
do not treat formally legal large grids as evidence of canonical relevance.
**This return:** fixed the generator mixture, not the acceptance threshold;
retains the failed strict run and reports the resulting 3/20, 7/20, 3/20 exact
size/color-profile hits. These frequencies are measurements, not approval.

Make actual lesson sufficiency mandatory at supervised admission (R2)

Symptom: the original generator's semantic stage was advisory with no contract, while real assembled lessons admitted shortcuts. The larger source-bound probe retained 35/360 baseline episodes whose named rival fit every demonstration but failed the query. See `checks/before/checks/f7e325967ea1_before_semantic_gate.log` and `checks/lesson-probe.json`.

Change: reuse the existing semantic hooks, verify canonical-fit claims, and require the ordinary admission path to check actual assembled lessons against declared rivals. Preserve failing full episodes and distinguish surviving-but-query-correct rivals from wrong-query survivors. Use at least 100 lessons per band for final review when canonical ambiguity exists; keep the small battery as smoke coverage. Intentional exploration data needs an explicit separate policy. `workspace/lesson_probe.py` provides a reusable implementation, without patching shared tooling.

Exact controls must be observed jointly, including inverse combinations (A1)

Symptom: audit task 28ad783a6a98 silently substitutes the second transform for 70/490 explicit transform requests. Every generated scene passes its own validator. Example: seed 0 / start 0 / r1 then r3 produces r1 then atr. Evidence: `checks/audits/28ad783a6a98-counterexample.json` and `checks/audits/report.json`.

Change: require output-derived joint control observations, not just valid grids or independent per-axis probes. An inverse composition is lawful and still maps a wide input to one output panel; it is not raw identity degeneracy. If any combination is excluded, fail explicitly and declare the incompatibility. Keep override correctness separate from Racket-label correctness.

Preserve partial override results and explain nested time budgets (R1)

Symptom: the full before command requested `--timeout 4000`, but the override stage hit its separate 300-second budget and returned 124. The retained battery correctly records failure, but the per-stage stdout log has no useful final result. See `checks/before/checks/f7e325967ea1_before_battery_summary.json` and its command journal.

Change: print effective stage budgets at launch, checkpoint each completed override case to JSONL, and retain a last-completed-case/timing summary on timeout. Never turn a timeout into a semantic pass or lose the already discovered mismatches. A rerun into an existing output directory currently rejects before work starts; report the conflict without encouraging users to delete sole failure evidence.

Report cross-band uniqueness alongside coverage (R2)

Symptom: the repaired generator has 480/480 distinct input observations within each band, but only 612 distinct inputs among all 1,440 observations. All named-rival lesson tests still pass. A coverage-only report could imply 1,440 independent training examples. Evidence: `checks/lesson-probe.json`.

Change: hash inputs across bands, across overlapping lesson windows, and before train/validation splitting. Report observations and global distinct inputs separately. The retained probe does this already; incorporate the counters into admission evidence and deduplicate exported datasets. Exact-grid dedup alone still cannot eliminate scaffold-family leakage.

Keep linked profile floors separate from lawfulness and morphology (A2/R1)

The existing profile-floor gate usefully caught A2: pooled support exists, but medium and hard each have 0/20 exact hits. Meanwhile a broad rule-domain validator can accept every canonical input and every generated sample without recovering canonical visual support. R1's `strict_canonical_like` intentionally has that broad domain meaning.

Change: present three separate labels in intake: rule-domain valid fraction, per-band linked height/width/palette support, and morphology diagnostics. Do not describe a 100% rule-domain fraction as exact canonical-distribution fidelity. Preserve the existing per-band failure rather than weakening it to pooled counts. Evidence: both retained profile-floor reports and `checks/after/checks/f7e325967ea1_after_semantic_gate.log`.

**The documented full-battery command should include an aggregate timeout appropriate for all 12 stages.** The packet instructions show `arcpuzzles check ... --battery` without `--timeout`, while the outer command defaults to 330 seconds and individual inherited stages can each budget up to 300 seconds. During review, an interrupted/outer-bounded invocation could leave confusing partial process/output behavior. Suggested change: show `--timeout 4000` in `DUTIES.md`, or have full-battery mode derive an aggregate timeout and terminate the entire descendant process tree on interruption.

**The override checker diagnoses root causes well, but its raw failure log is excessively repetitive.** The baseline produced 26,027 findings and a ~1.4 MB results file; after the useful grouped root causes, the log still printed thousands of near-identical seed lines. Suggested change: cap examples per normalized root cause in the human log, retain the exhaustive JSON artifact, and print counts plus minimized witnesses only.

**A missing semantic contract is only advisory in the baseline, even when the review goal is lesson quality.** This task had no `strict_canonical_like`, witnesses, or rivals, yet the semantic stage exited 0. Suggested change: full-review assignments should invoke semantic gate with `--require-contract`, or make “NO_CONTRACT” blocking for selected generators while preserving advisory behavior in broad catalog scans.

**Expose a public one-grid rule-evaluation command.** Verifying an exact counterexample outside the staged checker required directly using `RacketBridge`; `puzzle_generators.rule_wrap.wrap_rule` in the library tree imports `scripts.comment_solutions`, but `scripts` exists only in the prepared runtime layout. Suggested change: add `arcpuzzles apply-rule TASK_ID --input JSON` (or a documented library API) that prepares the runtime and returns the exact canonical Racket output with rule hash/provenance.

**Clarify self-check mutation scores.** The after report says only 19/57 destructive mutations were rejected, although the stage passes and several “mutations” (for example duplicating an empty row) can remain perfectly lawful for gravity. Suggested change: separate guaranteed-invalid probes from heuristic perturbations and report two rates, so reviewers do not mistake lawful mutation survival for a weak validator.

**The profile tools should print linked profile dimensions consistently.** The profile floor reports `(height, width, total palette)` while this review also needed cell count and occupied-column count to construct exact linked lessons. Suggested change: include both the compact gate tuple and a richer canonical-profile table when those observables are available.

**Audit target 761a24339019 shows a generic gap worth a targeted lint.** Seed 6/sample 6/easy puts a target at the right edge, so three of five exemplar offsets are out of bounds and the Racket output stamps only two cells. The summary promises stamping the shape at every target. Suggested change: for generators that declare exemplar/target semantics, support a witness or hook asserting every translated exemplar is fully in bounds and unobstructed; the generic shape/diversity gates cannot infer this.

Biggest avoidable friction: distinguish wrapper preflight failures

Changed-source approval gates and already-existing output paths produced wrapper output resembling payload/test failures even when the payload never ran. Print a one-line failure class (`preflight`, `approval`, `payload`, or `semantic`) plus the exact safe rerun command before the duplicated child output.

Notes-only peer audits must use a non-unchanged outcome, and evidence_paths must name direct archive members under checks/ rather than task files carried only in the source patch. Add one complete notes-only peer/results example showing those outcome and evidence-path rules so future agents can package successfully on the first pass.
